records.title: test(native-chat): fix flaky transcript watch-error initial-snapshot recovery test
records.body:
## Root cause

`transcript-watch-error.test.ts` > `still wins with a real initial snapshot once the transcript becomes readable` had a real ordering race with the watcher's own retry loop.

The test injects a tail-reader failure, waits for the `Transcript unavailable` frame, then did:

```ts
tailReaderState.failure = null                 // reads recover
await writeFile(filePath, claudeLine('u-recovered', ...))  // content lands
watchCallbacks[0]!('change', 'transcript.jsonl')           // poke the watcher
```

After the failed initial drain, `installTranscriptWatcher` keeps a capped rotation retry alive (`scheduleRotationRetry`, 25ms → 2s backoff), plus a 1s reconciliation tick. Any of those drains that lands in the window between "reads recover" and "content is on disk" succeeds against a **still-empty** file (`writeFile` also truncates first). Because `initialDrain` is still true, that drain legitimately emits the initial snapshot — an empty one — and flips `initialDrain` to false. The subsequent manual `change` callback then takes the append path, so `u-recovered` was delivered to `onAppend` and never reached `onInitialSnapshot`, and the `vi.waitFor` timed out.

The CI diff confirms this exactly. `onInitialSnapshot.mock.calls.flat(2)` was:

```
[false, 0, "Transcript unavailable", false, 0, undefined, undefined]
```

3 elements from the error frame (`([], false, 0, msg)`) + 4 from a **second, empty** snapshot (`([], hasMore, beforeOffset, undefined, lifecycle)`) = the 7-element `[ false, +0, …(5) ]` from the CI log.

## Verdict: test bug, not a product bug

Emitting an empty initial snapshot the moment the transcript becomes readable, then streaming `u-recovered` through `onAppend`, is correct: the client ends up with the identical transcript and is never stranded on the error frame. The watcher is not emitting a spurious or duplicate snapshot — coalescing is fine. The test was asserting on which callback happened to win a race that production does not order.

## Fix

Write the recovered line **before** clearing the failure, so no drain can ever observe a readable-but-empty transcript in any interleaving (while the failure is set, every read rejects; once cleared, every read sees the content). No timeout bumps, no retries, no skips.

The assertion is also strengthened rather than weakened: instead of flattening every call's args into one array and doing an `arrayContaining` membership check, it now asserts exactly two `onInitialSnapshot` calls and that the second one's message array is exactly `[{ id: 'u-recovered' }]`. That fails loudly on the empty-snapshot regression this flake was silently tolerating.

## Reproduction

Reproduced deterministically. In a scratch copy of the test I widened the race window by inserting `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 60))` between `tailReaderState.failure = null` and the `writeFile`, letting a rotation retry land in the gap. It fails 100% of the time with the byte-identical CI assertion:

```
AssertionError: expected [ false, +0, …(5) ] to deeply equal ArrayContaining{…}
+   false,
+   0,
+   "Transcript unavailable",
+   false,
+   0,
+   undefined,
+   undefined,
```

With the fix applied, the same scratch copy — 60ms delay after the `writeFile` *and* another 60ms after clearing the failure, so a retry drain deliberately wins the race ahead of the manual callback — passes 5/5.

## Loop evidence

- Fixed test file, 65 consecutive runs under 8 concurrent CPU hogs: **65 passed, 0 failed**.
- `pnpm test src/main/native-chat`: 83 files, 679 tests passed.
- `oxlint` clean, `pnpm tc` clean.

records.title: fix(packaging): ship agent-browser skill catalog
records.body:
## ELI5

The browser-automation helper we ship keeps its instruction manual in a folder next to
itself. We were shipping the helper but leaving the manual behind, so it kept answering
"I have no skills". This puts the manual next to the helper — in **both** places we copy
it: the desktop app and the headless `orcad` daemon.

## What Changed

Desktop bundle (`config/electron-builder.config.cjs`):

- ship `node_modules/agent-browser/skills/agent-browser` as `Resources/skills/agent-browser`
- ship `node_modules/agent-browser/skill-data` as `Resources/skill-data`
- both land beside the already-bundled `Resources/agent-browser-<platform>-<arch>` binary

Headless daemon (`config/scripts/build-orcad.mjs`):

- copy the same two directories into `out/orcad`, beside the agent-browser binary the
  script already copies there
- copy with `dereference: true`: the payload has no symlinks today, but the orcad deploy's
  SFTP walk skips symlinked entries, so this guards against a future pnpm layout shipping
  an empty directory

## Why

agent-browser resolves its version-matched catalog in this order:

1. `AGENT_BROWSER_SKILLS_DIR`
2. `<binary dir>/../skills`
3. `<binary dir>/skills`
4. `<binary dir>/skill-data`

Both packaging paths copy the binary and nothing else, so rules 2–4 all missed and
`agent-browser skills get core` answered "No skills found". Rule 4 has a subtlety worth
recording: `skill-data` on its own reports "Skills directory not found" — it is only read
once a sibling `skills/` directory anchors it. That is why both directories are shipped
rather than `skill-data` alone.

The first commit fixed only the Electron bundle. `build-orcad.mjs` copies the same binary
into `out/orcad`, which is what gets uploaded to a VPS, so a deployed daemon was still
skill-less. The second commit closes that half, which is what makes "Closes #17705"
honest.

The binary's own location is unchanged in both paths — `Contents/Resources/agent-browser-darwin-arm64`
is load-bearing and the issue's repro depends on it.

## Linked Issue

Closes #17705

## Visual Proof

`N/A` — packaging-only change with no UI surface. The observable difference is CLI output,
included under Testing.

## Testing

Empirical, against the real `agent-browser@0.27.0` binary. Staged the exact layout each
packaging path produces in a temp directory and ran the CLI:

```
# binary alone (what shipped before this PR)
$ ./agent-browser-linux-x64 skills get core
✗ Skills directory not found. Set AGENT_BROWSER_SKILLS_DIR or reinstall via npm.

# binary + skill-data, no skills/ anchor
$ ./agent-browser-linux-x64 skills get core
✗ Skills directory not found. Set AGENT_BROWSER_SKILLS_DIR or reinstall via npm.

# the layout this PR ships (binary + skills/agent-browser + skill-data)
$ ./agent-browser-linux-x64 skills get core
---
name: core
description: Core agent-browser usage guide. ...
$ ./agent-browser-linux-x64 skills list
  agentcore  core  dogfood  electron  slack  vercel-sandbox
```

The orcad half was staged from the real `node_modules/agent-browser` using the same
`cpSync` calls `build-orcad.mjs` now makes, so pnpm's actual on-disk layout (a symlinked
package root over hardlinked file contents) is exercised rather than a hand-built fixture.
Verified independently that the skill payload itself contains zero symlinks — `dereference:
true` is defensive, not load-bearing.

Automated:

- `vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts config/scripts/electron-builder-config.test.mjs` (37 passed)
- `vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts config/scripts/build-orcad.test.mjs` (3 passed; all 3 fail when the `build-orcad.mjs` change is reverted)
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --deny-warnings` (default + `config/oxlint-code-quality-native-plugins.json`) on the changed files
- `node config/scripts/check-reliability-gates.mjs`, `node config/scripts/check-max-lines-ratchet.mjs`

Platforms: verified on Linux. The desktop mappings are platform-neutral `extraResources`
entries asserted for mac/win/linux by the existing test; the orcad copy is
platform-neutral `cpSync`.

`build-orcad.test.mjs` derives its expected directory list from the desktop
`extraResources` rather than restating it, so an upstream rename cannot fix one packaging
path and silently leave the other shipping a directory that no longer exists.

- [x] I manually tested these changes locally
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below

records.title: [Feature]: LastPass integration for the embedded browser
records.body:
## Problem or use case

Users who rely on LastPass cannot use their saved credentials naturally inside Orca’s embedded browser. This is especially disruptive for remote browser sessions, where manually copying passwords or one-time codes between apps is slow and increases the chance of exposing credentials.

The need applies to both browser modes:

- **This device:** the page is rendered locally while traffic goes through the paired remote server.
- **Server (streamed):** the page is hosted on the remote server and displayed in Orca as a stream.

## Proposed solution

Add LastPass support to Orca’s embedded browser, ideally through supported LastPass extension integration or an equivalent native browser integration.

The solution should support, subject to LastPass capabilities and Orca’s security model:

- Sign-in and vault unlock within the browser profile.
- Credential autofill and save-password prompts.
- Consistent behavior for client-hosted and server-streamed browser pages.
- Clear handling of where the LastPass session and sensitive data live, without silently copying vault contents through Orca or the remote connection.

## Alternatives or additional context

The current workaround is to use the system browser or copy credentials manually. Neither works well for sites that must be opened in Orca’s per-worktree browser, and manual copying is particularly awkward for remote sessions.

This request is for LastPass specifically, but the design could leave room for other password managers later.

records.title: Document responsive viewport control and the browser passthrough in the orca-cli guide
records.body:
## ELI5

If you ask an agent to check your app at iPhone width in Orca's built-in browser, it renders at desktop width and reports success. Two reasons: the command that does the job, `orca viewport`, is missing from `orca --help`, and the flags that *look* right — `--mobile`, or `orca set device` — silently discard the width you asked for. This PR writes down which call actually works, plus the neighbouring traps, and fixes the one `orca exec` example in the guide, which was not a real command.

## What Changed

`skill-guides/orca-cli.md`, Built-In Browser section:

- **Added `orca viewport` to the typed command list.** It exists — `orca viewport --width <w> --height <h> [--scale <n>] [--mobile]` — but is absent from `orca --help`, so the guide is the only place an agent can find it.
- **Documented the `--mobile` trap.** With the mobile flag set, Chromium falls back to its 980 px default layout viewport and discards the requested width, while the command still reports it. `orca set device` implies the flag and hits the same wall.
- **Added the re-assert rule:** an override survives `goto` but is dropped by `reload`, and the failure is silent, so confirm with `eval innerWidth` before trusting a measurement.
- **Added a "Passthrough-only commands" block** for what has no typed equivalent: `set viewport 0 0` (the reset — typed `orca viewport` rejects 0), `pushstate`, `get styles`, `diff *`, `network route|har`, `vitals`, `set geo`, `set media reduced-motion`, `trace`/`profiler`/`inspect`. Points at `agent-browser --help` rather than duplicating it.
- **Noted the two dead ends** so agents stop retrying them: `record start` fails with a CDP `Target.createBrowserContext: Not allowed`, `react *` needs `--enable react-devtools`.
- **Noted that the passthrough tokenizes on spaces**, so multi-word arguments need the typed command.
- **Fixed the broken example:** `ORCA exec --command "help" --json` returns `Unknown command: help`. Replaced with `vitals`.
- Screenshot and SPA-navigation rules: `screenshot` honours the emulated viewport at exact CSS pixels but duplicated the page at scale 3; prefer `pushstate` over a hand-written `history.pushState`.

`config/scripts/orca-cli-skill-guidance.test.mjs`: three assertions in the existing style — the viewport trap, the passthrough surface, and a parity check that the generated bundle carries the same guidance.

`src/cli/bundled-skill-guides.ts`: regenerated with `node config/scripts/generate-bundled-skill-guides.mjs --write`.

No frontmatter change, so `skills/orca-cli/SKILL.md` is untouched.

## Why

The failure is silent, which is what makes it expensive. Every obvious path reports success and renders the wrong thing:

| Call | Reports | `innerWidth` | `min-width: 768px` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orca viewport --width 390 --height 844 --scale 3` | 390 | **390** | false ✅ |
| the same, plus `--mobile` | 390 | **980** | true ❌ |
| `orca set device --name "iPhone 17"` | 402 | **980** | true ❌ |

An agent has no way to tell the second and third rows from the first: `ok: true`, the requested width echoed back, no warning. And the row that works is invisible from `orca --help`, so the natural discovery path leads straight to the two that don't.

Two of the three rows are arguably a bug rather than a documentation gap — that's #17703, left to the maintainers, since whether `--mobile` should apply the requested width or refuse it is a product call. This PR makes the working path findable in the meantime.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #17703

## Visual Proof

N/A — agent-facing guide text, no UI or interaction surface. Evidence for each claim, on Orca 1.4.193 / Chromium 150 / macOS:

```
$ orca goto --url "data:text/html,<meta name=viewport content='width=device-width,initial-scale=1'><body>x</body>"
$ orca eval --expression "innerWidth+'x'+innerHeight+' dpr='+devicePixelRatio"
"1231x838 dpr=2"

# works
$ orca viewport --width 390 --height 844 --scale 3 --json
{"width":390,"height":844,"deviceScaleFactor":3,"mobile":false}
$ orca eval --expression "innerWidth+'x'+innerHeight+' dpr='+devicePixelRatio+' md='+matchMedia('(min-width: 768px)').matches"
"390x844 dpr=3 md=false"

# same call with --mobile: reports 390, renders 980
$ orca viewport --width 390 --height 844 --scale 3 --mobile --json
{"width":390,"height":844,"deviceScaleFactor":3,"mobile":true}
$ orca eval --expression "innerWidth+'x'+innerHeight+' md='+matchMedia('(min-width: 768px)').matches"
"980x2121 md=true"

# set device implies the mobile flag
$ orca set device --name "iPhone 17" --json
{"device":"iPhone 17","deviceScaleFactor":3,"height":874,"mobile":true,"width":402}
$ orca eval --expression "innerWidth+' md='+matchMedia('(min-width: 768px)').matches"
"980 md=true"

# reload drops the override; goto does not
$ orca viewport --width 390 --height 844 --scale 3 --json
$ orca eval --expression "innerWidth"     # 390
$ orca goto --url "<a different url>" --json
$ orca eval --expression "innerWidth"     # 390
$ orca reload --json
$ orca eval --expression "innerWidth"     # 1231

# reset has no typed form
$ orca viewport --width 0 --height 0 --json
{"error":"--width must be a positive number"}
$ orca exec --command "set viewport 0 0" --json
$ orca eval --expression "innerWidth"     # 1231

# the example that was in the guide
$ orca exec --command "help" --json
{"code":"browser_error","message":"Unknown command: help"}
```

`pushstate` doing a real Next.js soft nav (breadcrumb changes across a soft nav between two dynamic routes, client search state resets):

```
$ orca exec --command "pushstate /admin/eventos/<other-id>/inscritos" --json
{"url":"/admin/eventos/<previous-id>/inscritos"}      # result echoes the pre-nav URL
$ orca eval --expression "location.pathname"
"/admin/eventos/<other-id>/inscritos"
```

## Testing

- Ran the touched suite in isolation against the working tree: `config/scripts/orca-cli-skill-guidance.test.mjs` — 14 tests pass (11 pre-existing, 3 new). Confirmed all three new assertions fail against the unpatched guide and bundle.
- Ran `node config/scripts/generate-bundled-skill-guides.mjs` before the change (reported `src/cli/bundled-skill-guides.ts` stale), then `--write`, then re-ran the check clean — generated file in sync, generator idempotent over it.
- Verified every behavioural claim against a live Orca 1.4.193 embedded browser on macOS, driving a local Next.js 15 dev server and data URLs. Transcripts above.
- **Not run locally:** the full `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`. I did not install the repo's Electron toolchain, so I ran the affected test standalone instead of the whole suite. The change is guide markdown, one test file, and a regenerated string constant — leaving the rest to CI.
- **Platforms:** verified on macOS only. The guide text is platform-neutral and nothing here is guarded by a platform check.

- [x] I manually tested these changes locally
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below

## AI Disclosure

Written with Claude Opus 5 via Claude Code. The findings come from running the commands against a live Orca instance, not from model recall; every claim in the guide has a transcript above it.

## Review

- **Cross-platform:** guide markdown plus a generated string; no platform-specific code, paths, or shortcuts. The guide points at `agent-browser --help` rather than a bundled binary path, which would be OS-specific. Verified on macOS only; the `--mobile` behaviour is Chromium/CDP `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` semantics, so it should not be platform-dependent.
- **SSH / remote / local:** no change to transport or host resolution. The existing client-hosted vs server-hosted paragraph is untouched; the new rules concern the page's own viewport, not where it renders.
- **Agent / integration compatibility:** guidance only; no change to command surfaces, flags, or output shapes.
- **Performance:** none. One embedded string grows by ~2.8 KB.
- **UI quality:** N/A.
- **Security:** the section's untrusted-page-content rule is untouched and still asserted by the existing test. No credential, cookie, or secret examples added; `network route` and `inspect` are named but not demonstrated with payloads.
- **Backwards compatibility:** additive documentation. The only removal is a command string that never worked.

## Agent skill upstream boundary

- [x] Not applicable, or this change follows `docs/reference/agent-skill-sharing-upstream-boundary.md` and copies or mechanically translates no upstream skill-installer source, tests, fixtures, registry entries, path tables, comments, or documentation.

Not applicable: that boundary covers `vercel-labs/skills`, the skill installer. This change documents Orca's own typed commands and its `orca exec` passthrough. Command names were read from `--help` output and every documented behaviour was verified by running it; no upstream source, tests, fixtures, registry entries, or path tables are copied or translated.

## Notes

An earlier revision of this PR framed viewport control as passthrough-only and missed that `orca viewport` exists. @pullfrog caught it in review; the correction turned out to isolate the actual root cause — the mobile flag, not the command — which is now what both the guide and #17703 describe. Thanks.

## Author

GitHub: @Donivanes

## Checklist

- [x] This PR is small and focused
- [x] I explained what changed and why (including ELI5)
- [x] Before/after screenshots or videos attached for UI changes, or `N/A` with reason
- [x] Self-reviewed for correctness, security, and performance
- [x] Cross-platform, SSH/remote, and path/shortcut impact considered (or N/A)

records.title: [Bug]: bundled agent-browser ships without its skills, so `agent-browser skills get core` returns "No skills found"
records.body:
### Operating system

macOS

### Orca version

1.4.193

### Details

**Short summary:** Orca bundles the `agent-browser` binary but not its `skills/` directory, so the self-documentation the binary points every agent at resolves to nothing.

#### What happened

`agent-browser --help` opens with:

```
Start here (for AI agents):
  agent-browser skills get core --full

  Skills ship with the CLI (always version-matched) and include workflow
  patterns, ref/selector usage, and copy-paste examples. Prefer this over
  guessing commands from flag docs alone.
```

In the bundled copy that resolves to nothing:

```
$ /Applications/Orca.app/Contents/Resources/agent-browser-darwin-arm64 skills list
No skills found

$ /Applications/Orca.app/Contents/Resources/agent-browser-darwin-arm64 skills get core
✗ Skill not found: core

$ /Applications/Orca.app/Contents/Resources/agent-browser-darwin-arm64 skills path
/Applications/Orca.app/Contents/Resources/skills

$ ls /Applications/Orca.app/Contents/Resources/skills
current-manifest.json
release-mapping.json
snapshot-registry.json
```

`skills path` points at Orca's own skill-release metadata directory, which contains no agent-browser skills. The binary and the directory it resolves to are unrelated.

#### How can we reproduce it

1. Install Orca 1.4.193 (macOS).
2. Run `/Applications/Orca.app/Contents/Resources/agent-browser-darwin-arm64 skills list`.
3. Observe `No skills found`.

#### Why it matters

`orca exec --command "<agent-browser command>"` is a passthrough to this binary, and the `orca-cli` guide describes the passthrough as the route for "less common workflows" without listing what it reaches. The binary's own skills are the natural place for that detail, and they are exactly what's missing — so an agent has no in-product way to discover the passthrough surface. The practical consequences are in #17703.

#### Suggested fix

Ship the CLI's `skills/` payload alongside the binary in `Contents/Resources`, or point `AGENT_BROWSER_SKILLS_PATH` (or the equivalent) at wherever it lands, so `agent-browser skills get core --full` works from the bundled copy. If bundling them is deliberate scope-trimming, having `skills list` say so would be better than an empty result, since the binary's own help routes agents there first.

#### Anything else that might help

`package.json` pins `"agent-browser": "~0.27.0"`. Only the macOS arm64 build was checked; the same packaging step presumably covers the other platform binaries.

records.title: Remote Web UI terminal custom titles revert after snapshot, refresh, or restart
records.body:
## Problem

Renaming a terminal tab in the Remote Web UI updates only the current client. The next `session.tabs` host snapshot restores the old title, and the rename is also lost after refreshing either Web client or restarting the headless Orca host.

## Root cause

The Web renderer stores a rename in local `TerminalTab.customTitle` / unified-tab `customLabel`, but `session.tabs.setTabProps` currently carries only `color`, `isPinned`, and `viewMode`. The headless runtime therefore never updates the workspace session or the authoritative subscription snapshot with the custom title.

## Expected behavior

- A rename from one Remote Web UI client is published to every subscribed Web client.
- The custom title survives client refresh/reconnect.
- The custom title survives an Orca headless-host restart and cold session rehydration.
- Clearing a custom title restores normal generated/default-title resolution.

## Proposed scope

- Extend the existing `session.tabs.setTabProps` path with nullable `customTitle` (optional = unchanged, null = clear).
- Mirror the Web renderer rename action to the owning runtime host.
- Persist terminal `customTitle` in the headless workspace session and include it in emitted subscription snapshots.

records.title: feat(browser): auto-discover installed Chromium browsers for cookie import
records.body:
## ELI5

Orca can copy your logged-in sessions from another browser so you don't have to sign in again. Today it only offers a **hardcoded list** of browsers (Chrome, Edge, Arc, Brave, Comet, Helium). This makes Orca **auto-discover any installed Chromium browser** — Aside, Vivaldi, Whale, Dia, … — so it just shows up in the import picker with no code change per browser.

## What Changed

A macOS auto-discovery layer feeding the existing cookie-import pipeline:

- Enumerate installed browsers from the OS URL-handler registry (`LSCopyAllHandlersForURLScheme` via `osascript` — no bundled binary), then keep only candidates that own a Chromium cookie store (a `Local State` + a resolvable cookies DB). This cleanly excludes Electron apps (Slack/Discord/VS Code) that share the on-disk layout but aren't registered browsers.
- Resolve each to `{dataDir, keychainService}` via a ladder: known hardcoded entry (zero-config) → standard `<Browser> Safe Storage` convention → "needs setup" when neither matches (never guesses).
- New `browserFamily: 'custom'` + per-entry `sourceLabel`; a `browserSourceLabel()` helper so different custom browsers stay distinguishable in Settings.
- `detectAllBrowsers()` composes hardcoded + discovered, de-duped by canonical data root (hardcoded wins → keeps verified keychain). Wired through the detect/import IPC **and** remote RPC, threading an optional `customBrowserId` so custom browsers (all `family: 'custom'`) are unambiguous on import. Secret strip preserved on both surfaces (no `cookiesPath`/keychain leaves the main process).

macOS-first (consistent with the existing Arc/Helium entries); Windows/Linux enumeration are follow-ups. This is **generic Chromium auto-discovery** — there is no browser-specific logic (Aside is only used as the example in tests).

## Why

Every new Chromium fork currently costs a PR — Comet (#1923), Helium (#6768), Aside (#15452). Adoption of AI-native / niche browsers is growing and the long tail is unservable one-PR-at-a-time. Auto-discovery removes the treadmill: a user's browser appears because it's installed, not because someone added it.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #15458

Related: #15452 (adds Aside as a **hardcoded** entry). This PR generalizes that; the two compose cleanly (dedup precedence keeps the hardcoded entry's verified keychain when both are present), so they are not mutually exclusive.

## Visual Proof

Before → After (Settings → Browser → Session & Cookies, "Import Cookies" dropdown). The only change is that an installed Chromium browser ("From Aside") now appears alongside "From File…". 

**Before** — no auto-discovery (dropdown shows only "From File…"):

![Before – no auto-discovery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16c69b9b-8d44-47d0-b581-ae5de065d2b0)

**After** — Aside auto-discovered ("From Aside" appears):

![After – Aside auto-discovered](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3fba6ab-5b37-4bcb-9651-e776abe37242)

## Testing

- **Unit** (cross-platform, run in CI): installed-browser discovery + Chromium filter, resolution ladder (known/convention/needs-setup), dedup merge + precedence, candidate→DetectedBrowser, macOS query JSON parsing, `browserSourceLabel`, and the IPC handler (exposes `customBrowserId`, strips secrets; import matches custom by `customBrowserId`).
- **E2E** (`tests/e2e/browser-cookie-import-custom-discovery.spec.ts`): launches the app, navigates to Session & Cookies, opens the picker, hard-asserts "From Aside". Deterministic via an env-gated OS-query seam (ignored in packaged builds) + a seeded data dir; **macOS-only** (skips on the Linux e2e CI).
- `pnpm lint` clean; `tc:node` / `tc:cli` / `tc:web` clean.
- Platforms actually tested: **macOS** (real `osascript` enumeration verified: Aside/Comet/Chrome/Safari/iTerm, filtered correctly).

- [ ] I manually tested these changes locally (verified real-machine `osascript` enumeration + the picker via e2e; did not run a full packaged-app cookie copy)
- [x] Automated tests added/updated

## AI Disclosure

Claude (Anthropic), model **Claude Fable 5**, via Claude Code.

## Review

Self-reviewed for correctness, security, cross-platform, and remote/SSH impact — see Notes.

## Agent skill upstream boundary

- [x] Not applicable, or this change follows `docs/reference/agent-skill-sharing-upstream-boundary.md` and copies or mechanically translates no upstream skill-installer source, tests, fixtures, registry entries, path tables, comments, or documentation.

## Notes

Ensure no issues in: Security, Cross-platform support (Linux, Windows, Mac), Remote SSH, Mobile, general backwards compatibility, performance

- **Security:** the `ORCA_E2E_FAKE_HTTPS_HANDLERS` seam is gated behind `!app.isPackaged`, so a shipped app never honors it. The `osascript` query passes values as argv (never shell-interpolated) and is read-only. No `cookiesPath`/keychain identifier is exposed to the renderer or over RPC — only `customBrowserId` (a bundle id) is added. Profile paths keep the existing traversal guard. No SQL is built from new input.
- **Cross-platform:** macOS-only for now; `detectAllBrowsers()` returns the hardcoded set unchanged on Windows/Linux (their OS queries are follow-ups).
- **Remote/SSH:** additive/Rule-1 wire changes only — `'custom'` browserFamily and optional `customBrowserId` (validated as a plain string, not an enum). Old client omitting `customBrowserId` still imports via the family path; the detect/import RPC handlers were switched to the same `detectAllBrowsers()` as local.
- **Mobile:** no mobile surface touched.
- **Backwards compatibility:** additive; no changed stream opcodes or persisted-schema breakage.
- **Performance:** one extra OS query at detection time (settings-time, not a hot path).

## Summary

- Fixes local embedded-browser reloads that remained visually idle while Chromium was still loading.
- Keeps the existing browser navigation lifecycle as the source of truth and preserves Stop/Reload semantics.

## What was broken

The local webview `did-start-loading` handler is intentionally gated by `trackNextLoadingEventRef`. URL navigations arm that gate, but accepted reloads did not. A delayed reload therefore left the persisted tab state at `loading: false`, so the toolbar continued to show Reload.

## Fix

- Arm the existing local loading-event gate before calling `webview.reload()` / `reloadIgnoringCache()`.
- Set `BrowserPage.loading` to true immediately after an accepted reload.
- Clear the temporary gate for guest-missing and not-ready outcomes.
- On parked-pane reattach, reconcile `webview.isLoading()` only when the store already says a navigation is active, using a stable ref to avoid listener teardown/rebind races.
- Client-hosted and remote/server-hosted paths remain unchanged.

## Reproduction and proof

Added a deterministic local HTTP fixture whose second `/held` response waits on an explicit resolver barrier (no arbitrary sleeps). Baseline/reverted source stayed at Reload/non-spinning/loading=false after the reload request began. The candidate showed Stop, an animated Loader2, and loading=true until the barrier was released, then returned to Reload/loading=false with the reloaded body.

![reload-held.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92c14031-14c7-471e-a2af-bec6fbcdc79d)

## Tests

- `pnpm test src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane/navigate/browser-reload-action.test.ts src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane/navigate/use-browser-page-reload-actions.test.tsx src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane/assemble-chrome/browser-navigation-control-row.test.tsx src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane/ClientHostedBrowserPagePane.chrome-parity.test.tsx` (33 passed)
- `pnpm exec playwright test tests/e2e/browser-reload-feedback.spec.ts --config tests/playwright.config.ts --project electron-headless --workers=1` (passed)
- Existing browser reload/zoom E2E in `tests/e2e/browser-tab.spec.ts` (2 passed)
- `pnpm tc` and `pnpm tc:web` (passed)
- `pnpm run check:code-quality:changed` (passed)
- `pnpm typecheck:e2e` still reports unrelated pre-existing repository-wide typing errors.

## Tradeoffs

This is intentionally scoped to local embedded guests. It adds no timer, polling, duplicate navigation state, wire field, or remote protocol change. The only behavioral risk is the small accepted-reload window before Chromium emits lifecycle events; the gate and did-stop/did-fail cleanup keep the icon tied to actual navigation, while parked-pane reconciliation covers missed events.

records.title: [Feature]: Make orca-cli browser control work for remote/SSH (client-hosted) browsers
records.body:
### Problem or use case

Agents can drive Orca's built-in browser with `orca snapshot` / `orca click` / `orca tab create` when everything is local. On SSH / Remote Orca Server, that loop is not a first-class workflow yet, even though the user is often sitting in front of a **local** Orca window while the agent and web server run on the remote host.

Community report (WeChat, tests already passing locally):

- Local `orca-cli` browser control works.
- For remote, the **orca-cli skill** (and the CLI behavior it describes) needs to be updated so agents can actually control the browser the user sees.
- Concrete ask: *when connected to a remote server over SSH, can I debug a web service in my local browser after the port has been forwarded to my machine?*

Today the skill guide is still written as a local snapshot-interact-re-snapshot loop. Remote adds topology that agents currently guess at:

1. **Where the tab actually lives.** A remote workspace tab can be **client-hosted** (Chromium on the paired desktop the user is looking at) or **server-hosted** (on the execution host / offscreen). Commands against a client-hosted page need that desktop online; otherwise they fail with `browser_host_unavailable`.
2. **What `localhost` means.** If the user forwarded `remote:3000` → `local:3000` and opens the page in the *local* browser, `http://localhost:3000` is correct. If the agent opens the same URL in a *server-hosted* tab, `localhost` is the remote host (where the service already is) and the forward is irrelevant. Agents currently have no playbook for this.
3. **Wrong control surface.** On remote, agents still fall back to Playwright, a system Chrome CDP port, or `orca computer` on the desktop UI instead of `orca tab list` / `orca snapshot` against the worktree's embedded browser.

Related work (not a substitute for this issue):

- #6701 — browser / emulator on SSH workspaces (broader product)
- #17354 / #16502 — STA-5504: mark client-hosted placement and make host-unavailable failures actionable for CLI agents (open; Neil called this out as the in-flight PR)
- #14440 — client-hosted tunnel contracts (desktop tab, execution-host networking)
- #9055 — agents pick Chrome/CDP/`orca computer` instead of the embedded browser even locally
- #5610 — agent-browser vs Orca CLI as the control surface

### Proposed solution

Treat remote browser control as a supported `orca-cli` workflow, not a local-only skill with a footnote.

**Skill / agent playbook (`skill-guides/orca-cli.md` Built-In Browser):**

- Document SSH / Remote Orca Server as a first-class case: the agent runs on the execution host; the user may be looking at a client-hosted tab on the paired desktop.
- Tell agents to start with `orca tab list --json` and `orca snapshot --json` on the worktree, not Playwright / system Chrome / `orca computer`.
- Explain placement: client-hosted vs server-hosted, when each is appropriate (interactive debug the user can watch vs unattended automation), and that there is no silent failover.
- Explain **localhost / port-forward** semantics: use the URL that is valid *on the machine that owns the tab's network*. For "I forwarded the remote web server to my laptop and want to debug in the local Orca browser," that means a **client-hosted** tab at the forwarded local URL (or the remote host URL if the tab is server-hosted).
- Recovery: `browser_host_unavailable` → bring the desktop back, or explicitly `orca tab create --url …` for server placement. `browser_no_tab` / `browser_stale_ref` unchanged.

**CLI / runtime (follow-through after STA-5504):**

- Tab list/show/current should make placement visible enough that an agent can explain or wait, without forcing every command to branch on it.
- Client-hosted command failures should be structured (`browser_host_unavailable`, outcome-unknown after lost delivery) so agents do not retry mutations blindly.
- Opening a tab from a remote agent should be able to land in the browser the user is watching (client-hosted) when they asked to debug locally.

### Alternatives or additional context

- Shipping only #17354 (placement + errors) without updating the skill still leaves remote agents guessing localhost and falling back to Playwright.
- Telling users to open system Chrome at the forwarded URL bypasses Orca's worktree-scoped browser, so the agent cannot snapshot/click the same tab.
- Computer Use against the local desktop is the wrong surface for the embedded browser.

Suggested acceptance:

- [ ] From an SSH / remote worktree, `orca tab list --json` + `orca snapshot --json` drive the tab the user sees in the paired desktop browser.
- [ ] Agent can open a forwarded local URL in that client-hosted tab for interactive debug, and can open the remote-host URL in a server-hosted tab when no desktop is attached.
- [ ] `orca-cli` skill documents this topology, localhost rules, and `browser_host_unavailable` recovery.
- [ ] Agents do not need Playwright or system Chrome to complete the flow.

records.title: feat(browser): edit a page annotation's comment and intent inline in the tray
records.body: ## ELI5 When you annotate an element in the embedded browser and make a typo, the only way to fix it today is to delete the annotation and re-pick the element on the page. This PR adds a small pencil button to each annotation row in the tray: click it, fix the text or intent right there, save. The element you picked stays picked. ## What Changed - New store action `updateBrowserPageAnnotation(pageId, annotationId, patch)` next to the existing add/delete/clear actions. It no-ops (same state reference) when the id is missing and runs the merged annotation through the existing `sanitizeBrowserPageAnnotation`, so edits obey the same comment length budget as adds. - Each tray row gets a hover-revealed edit button beside the delete button. It swaps the row to an inline editor: a textarea seeded with the current comment, the intent toggle seeded with the current intent, and Save/Cancel. The screen submit shortcut saves, Escape cancels, Save is disabled while the trimmed comment is empty, and only one row edits at a time. If the annotation is deleted or the list cleared mid-edit, the edit state drops safely. - The annotate mode's window-level capture keydown listener gains an exemption for the edit container (marked `data-slot="annotation-edit"`), so Escape cancels only the row edit instead of tearing down the whole annotate session. A capture listener fires before descendant React handlers, so this cannot be solved with `stopPropagation` from inside the row. - Handler is threaded through the existing overlay props, so both surfaces that render the tray (browser pane and HTML doc preview) get the feature with no surface-specific code. - Four new machine-minted localization keys for the new strings (minted via the repo's extraction script, catalog checks pass). Deliberately untouched: annotation element targets, cross-navigation persistence, and `browser-annotation-output.ts` (the send/copy builder reads comment and intent live off the array, so edited text flows through with no change). ## Why Annotations queue up feedback for an agent; a typo or a wrong intent choice currently costs the whole annotation, including the picked element. Inline editing preserves the target and keeps the review flow moving. Editing lives in the tray row rather than re-opening the anchored composer because the compose popover's anchor geometry is only guaranteed while an add is pending; the inline row edit avoids that entire class of stale-anchor problems. ## Linked Issue Fixes #17501 ## Visual Proof Before and after screenshots attached (before: hover reveals only delete; after: hover reveals edit + delete; after: the row in inline edit mode). ## Testing - [x] I manually tested these changes locally - [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below Manually verified on Windows in the dev app: pencil appears on hover, editing seeds current values, save updates the row and the copied feedback, cancel and Escape leave the annotation unchanged, Escape does not exit annotate mode. Automated: 3 new store tests (update merges and sanitizes like add; nonexistent id is a strict no-op) and a new component test for the tray (seeded editor, save passes trimmed comment and chosen intent, cancel restores the read view, Escape regression). Full targeted suite: 83 tests across 12 files pass. Typecheck passes for node, web, and cli projects; oxlint clean on changed files; max-lines ratchet clean; localization catalog, extraction, and coverage checks pass. ## AI Disclosure Built with Claude Code (Claude Fable 5). records.title: [Feature]: Edit a browser annotation's comment and intent without deleting it
records.body:
### Problem

In the embedded browser's annotate mode, an annotation's comment and intent cannot be changed after it is added. The tray offers only delete and clear. Fixing a typo means deleting the annotation and re-selecting the element in the page, which loses the picked target and interrupts the review flow, especially when several annotations are already queued.

### Proposed solution

Allow editing an existing annotation's comment and intent inline in the annotations tray, keeping the element target untouched. Deleting should remain the only way to change which element an annotation points at.

### Scope notes

Element re-targeting, annotation persistence across navigation, and the send/copy prompt format are separate concerns and intentionally out of scope here.

records.title: perf(browser): use reverse guest tab lookup
records.body:
## ELI5

When a browser guest reports an event, Orca needs to answer “which tab owns this guest?” It used to look through every open tab until it found the matching WebContents ID. The browser manager already keeps the reverse answer, so this reads that map directly.

## What Changed

- Expose the existing WebContents-ID → browser-tab-ID map through `BrowserManager`.
- Use the direct lookup in CDP bridge state, CDP tab commands, and the agent-browser bridge.
- Keep strict and safe missing-tab behavior unchanged.
- Add lifecycle coverage for process swaps/unregisters and deterministic 1,000-tab lookup fixtures.

## Why

Guest-to-tab resolution runs on frequent CDP, navigation, permission, popup, and session lifecycle paths. A linear scan over the registered-tab map scales with the number of open browser tabs and repeats the same work for every event.

## Performance Measurement

Reproducible fixtures: run `pnpm test src/main/browser/cdp-bridge-state.test.ts src/main/browser/agent-browser-bridge-tab-routing.test.ts`. Each fixture repeats the lookup 1,000 times with 1,000 registered tabs and rejects any forward-map enumeration.

- Before: **1,000,000 registered-tab entries inspected** (1,000 lookups × 1,000 tabs) for a last-tab target.
- After: **0 entries enumerated**; each lookup is one reverse `Map.get`.
- Improvement: **100% removal** of measured tab-map enumeration, changing lookup work from O(number of tabs) to O(1).

Existing browser integration and lifecycle suites also cover active-page resolution, process swaps, stale guest cleanup, and missing IDs.

## User-Facing Trade-offs

None. Tab ownership, strict errors, safe null results, active-page selection, and cleanup semantics are unchanged. The reverse map is updated and cleared by the same registration lifecycle that owns the forward map.

## Summary

- Preserve visible structured Codex chat session identities in the durable agent-session store.
- Restore from that identity index when an older profile parser drops `contentType: agent-session` tabs.
- Remove the visibility reference on chat close while retaining the durable record and journal.
- Await handoff reveal persistence so a failed compatibility write is observable.

## Root cause

The workspace profile tab list was treated as the sole restoration identity for structured sessions. The pinned base release rejects the newer `agent-session` discriminator and salvages those entries away; after the base release rewrites the profile, re-upgrade can no longer discover the surviving records/journals.

This is a persistence ownership/lifecycle issue, not a reason to revert the structured-chat feature. The visible-tab reference now lives with the structured-session store, which older builds do not rewrite. Closed historical journals remain lazy and are not resurrected on startup.

## Regression coverage

- Automated target → pinned-base → target profile fixture.
- Verifies target parsing, legacy discriminator salvage, durable record/journal survival, and target re-upgrade recovery identity.
- Verifies deliberate close removes only the visible reference.
- Verifies runtime startup prefers the durable visible-session index after profile tab loss.

## Validation

- `pnpm tc`
- Focused Vitest suites (61 tests)
- Changed-code quality gate
- Oxlint
- Oxfmt

## ELI5

An older Orca build can erase structured-chat tabs it does not understand when it rewrites the profile. The visible chat IDs now live in the durable agent-session store, which the older build leaves alone, and that list is used when the app returns. Closing removes only the visible-tab pointer; the record and journal stay available, and open/close waits for the durable write.

## Performance Measurement

This is a persistence-compatibility fix, not a throughput optimization, so no speedup is claimed. In the deterministic target-to-pinned-base-to-target fixture, profile-only restoration returns 0 session IDs after the base round-trip, while the durable index restores 1 ID and preserves the journal; closing leaves the durable record and an empty visible index. No timing claim is made.

## User-Facing Trade-offs

There is no visible data-loss trade-off. Each visibility change now waits for one small durable whole-store transaction, which can add a little open/close latency; closed chats remain in history but are not resurrected. Stores without the new field retain the legacy profile fallback.

records.title: [Feature]: Built-in browser should diagnose and recover stopped worktree HTML previews
records.body:
### Operating system

Linux

### Orca version

1.4.190

### Details

## Summary

When an HTML preview server for the active worktree stops or is restarted on a different bind address, Orca's built-in browser leaves the old page visible and later falls back to a generic `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`. It does not explain that the worktree preview listener is gone or that the browser URL no longer matches the active listener, and it offers no worktree-aware recovery.

This makes in-Orca HTML acceptance testing feel as if the browser cannot open the application, even though the HTML itself is compatible.

## Why this HTML preview did not open

The failing tab still used `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`.

Two concrete conditions occurred during the same QA session:

1. The acceptance service was explicitly stopped while its previously rendered page remained visible in the browser tab. No process was listening on the port when the next navigation failed.
2. In an earlier run, the service was bound only to a non-loopback interface while the browser tab still used `127.0.0.1`. The loopback URL refused the connection; manually using the interface where the service was actually listening succeeded.

The browser gave the user no indication whether the cause was a stopped service, a stale worktree preview, or a bind-address mismatch.

## Control result: the HTML works in Orca

A controlled run kept the same application's acceptance server alive on runtime loopback:

1. Start the full app with isolated demo data on `127.0.0.1:<new-port>`.
2. Open it in Orca's built-in browser.
3. The page renders, seeded API data loads, navigation to another application route succeeds, and the browser console has no errors.

This rules out an HTML, CSS, JavaScript, or embedded-renderer compatibility failure. The usability gap is preview-service detection and recovery.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start an HTML dev or acceptance server in an Orca-managed worktree.
2. Open it in the worktree's built-in browser tab.
3. Stop the server while leaving the tab open.
4. Navigate within the cached page or reload it.
5. Observe a generic connection failure with no explanation that the worktree listener stopped.
6. Restart the server on the same port but a different local interface.
7. Observe that the stale browser URL still fails until the hostname is manually corrected.

## Expected behavior

Because the browser tab is already scoped to a worktree, Orca should:

- detect when the preview port no longer has a listener and say that the worktree preview service stopped;
- show the currently active listener or preview URL for that worktree when one exists;
- offer direct actions such as retry, open the active port, or return to the terminal that owns the server;
- distinguish a dead listener or bind-address mismatch from an HTML rendering failure;
- avoid leaving a cached page that looks usable until the next click fails without context.

## Impact

Without this diagnosis and recovery path, users must inspect processes and bind addresses manually and cannot rely on Orca's built-in browser for a continuous conversational HTML testing loop.

Related: #16274 covers the separate case of loopback tunneling for genuinely paired remote runtimes. This report is the local worktree preview lifecycle and error-recovery case.

records.title: [Bug]: DevTools opens on the host machine's display for remote and headless browser tabs
records.body:
### Operating system

Other

### Orca version

1.4.178-rc.2

### Details

**Summary.** `BrowserManager.openDevTools` resolves the tab's `webContents` and calls `openDevTools({ mode: 'detach' })` without branching on which browser backend is in use. On the offscreen backend the DevTools window therefore opens on the host machine's display, where a remote client cannot see it — so from the client's side the button appears to do nothing at all.

**Why I think this happens.** With the offscreen backend (`orca serve`, and remote workspaces generally), each tab is a hidden `BrowserWindow` in main, and the client only ever sees it through the CDP screencast. `startBrowserScreencast` streams the tab's own `webContents`; there is no path that streams a DevTools `webContents`. So the detached window has no route to the client, and nothing in `openDevTools` refuses or degrades when the backend can't display it.

**Honest caveat.** I found this by reading the code, not by reproducing it against a remote host — I don't have that setup handy. I'd rather flag it and be told I've misread than sit on it, so please treat the diagnosis as a hypothesis and the "button does nothing remotely" part as the claim worth checking first.

**A cheap improvement regardless of the fix.** Even if properly surfacing DevTools remotely is out of scope, disabling the control with a tooltip when the backend cannot display it would be better than a button that looks functional and silently opens a window somewhere the user isn't. A control that lies is worse than one that's greyed out.

Happy to open a PR for the disable-and-explain version if that's a direction you'd take.

records.title: Security: replace browser client localStorage bearer token with proof-of-possession
records.body:
## Summary

The supported browser client persists its runtime-scoped bearer credential in `localStorage`. Any JavaScript executing in the web client's origin can read and export it.

This is separate from the Expo mobile web QA path discussed in #17396. The affected implementation is the browser client served by Orca at `/web-index.html`.

## Evidence

[`src/renderer/src/web/web-runtime-environment.ts:18-36`](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/9e993dd1c06ebda52c47ad31a23e85e2994fbc1e/src/renderer/src/web/web-runtime-environment.ts#L18-L36) reads the complete runtime environment from `localStorage`.

[`src/renderer/src/web/web-runtime-environment.ts:48-50`](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/9e993dd1c06ebda52c47ad31a23e85e2994fbc1e/src/renderer/src/web/web-runtime-environment.ts#L48-L50) writes it back, while [`createStoredWebRuntimeEnvironment`](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/9e993dd1c06ebda52c47ad31a23e85e2994fbc1e/src/renderer/src/web/web-runtime-environment.ts#L56-L86) includes `deviceToken` in the stored endpoint.

## Impact

An XSS vulnerability or compromised same-origin script can export the long-lived bearer token and reuse it from another client, subject to endpoint reachability. The browser credential is runtime-scoped and therefore grants broader access than a mobile-scoped token.

Removing the pairing value from the address bar protects browser history and accidental sharing, but does not protect the copy persisted in `localStorage`.

## Suggested direction

Replace the exportable bearer credential with proof-of-possession authentication:

1. Generate a non-exportable WebCrypto signing key in the browser.
2. Register its public key during pairing.
3. Bind a fresh server challenge to the E2EE handshake transcript.
4. Have the browser sign the challenge and verify it using the registered public key.
5. Persist only the non-exportable `CryptoKey` handle, for example through IndexedDB.

This would **reduce persistent compromise; it would not solve XSS**. Malicious same-origin code could still ask the key to sign while it is executing, but it could not normally export the private key and retain access from another machine after the script is gone.

If that protocol change is not currently justified, shorter-lived credentials with rotation and an explicit browser-session lifetime would still reduce the exposure.

records.title: [Feature]: Element annotations (comments) on remote-runtime browser tabs
records.body: ## Problem or use case Annotating a page element and dispatching it to the agent is one of the fastest ways to steer UI work — "this button is misaligned" goes to the agent together with the element's DOM context. On a remote-runtime browser tab that workflow is unavailable: the annotate button is a permanently disabled placeholder. ``` aria-label: 'Browser annotations unavailable in remote runtime' tooltip: 'Browser annotations are only available in local browser tabs.' ``` — `src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane/stream-remote/remote-browser-page-toolbar.tsx` The cause is clear from the code: element grab injects an overlay into the guest page (`window.api.browser.setGrabMode`, with `injection-failed` among the reject reasons in `annotate/useGrabMode.ts`), and a remote pane is only a screencast image stream with no local guest to inject into. The pane's own comment states the boundary: > `// Why: markup snapshots the displayed screencast (no injection), so it works on remote panes even though element-grab doesn't.` > — `stream-remote/remote-browser-page-pane.tsx` I hit this running Orca on a headless Linux server (`orca serve`) with paired clients — every browser tab there is a remote-runtime tab, so annotations are simply never available to me. `ClientHostedBrowserPagePane` does not close the gap either: it never receives `elementTools`, so client-hosted pages have no annotate affordance. ## Proposed solution Make element grab work host-side and ship the result over the existing remote-browser channel, rather than requiring a local guest in the client renderer. The host owns a real `WebContentsView` for the page, so it can do the injection the client cannot: 1. `browser.setGrabMode` / `cancelGrab` already exist as RPCs. Route them to the runtime that owns the page instead of no-oping for remote panes. 2. The host injects the same grab overlay it uses locally, and hit-tests against real DOM. 3. The picked element's payload (`BrowserGrabPayload`) and its rects travel back to the client. The wire shape for this largely exists — `src/shared/browser-annotation-viewport-bridge.ts` already defines markers carrying `rectPage` / `rectViewport` / `isFixed`, which is exactly what a screencast client needs to draw the overlay in stream coordinates. 4. The client maps stream coordinates to page coordinates for the pointer hit-test, the same mapping the remote pane already performs for clicks and wheel events (`remote-browser-page-input-model.ts`). The existing annotation tray, send menu, and dispatch path can then be reused unchanged (`annotate/browser-page-annotation-tray.tsx`, `use-browser-page-annotation-send.ts`) — none of that is guest-dependent. Incremental fallback if the full round trip is too much: enable only the annotate intent (comment on a region) without DOM element extraction, so users at least get a positioned comment anchored to the page and dispatched to the agent. That is strictly better than a disabled button. ## Alternatives or additional context **Why markup is not a substitute** Markup/draw does work on remote panes and can be sent to the agent, but it produces a flat screenshot annotation with no DOM context — the agent receives a picture, not a selector. **UX note** Even before the feature lands, the disabled button's tooltip could point somewhere. "Browser annotations are only available in local browser tabs" tells the user what is not possible but not what to do instead; linking it to this issue would help. **Related issues** - #15476 — pasting images into the comment element in browser tab - #11360 — make browser annotation feedback compact by default - #8687 — keep annotations across page navigation - #14811 — floating annotations All four assume annotations are available; none covers making them available on remote-runtime panes. **Environment** - Orca v1.4.192 - Host: headless Linux server via `orca serve`

## ELI5

Every mounted terminal tab was rereading the entire unread-completion list whenever Zustand published any store update. With many tabs and markers, that made one harmless publication do the same long scan hundreds or thousands of times on the renderer thread.

This builds the list of owning tab IDs once for each immutable unread-map snapshot. Every tab then does one constant-time membership check. No notification, marker, tab, or feature is capped or disabled.

## User-visible problem

`SortableTab` stays mounted for every terminal and agent-session tab. Its selector called `hasUnreadAgentCompletionForTerminalTab`, which scanned all `U` pane markers for each of `T` tabs on every store publication—even when React ultimately rendered nothing. Accumulated sessions could therefore turn background status/title writes into synchronous O(T × U) input and status latency.

## Change

- Cache `ReadonlySet<tabId>` by `unreadAgentCompletionPanes` object identity in a `WeakMap`.
- Preserve truthy-marker filtering and the existing first-colon/no-colon ownership rule.
- Let old snapshots and their indexes be garbage-collected; retained palette snapshots can coexist safely.
- Reset the cache only in tests.

Production add, clear, close, hibernate, move, and purge paths already replace this map rather than mutating it in place; the test exercises add/clear through new snapshot identities.

## Deterministic before / after

Node 24.18.0, actual helper, mostly-absent lookups, three samples per case. Before uses `origin/main`; after uses a fresh marker-map identity for every sample so index construction is included.

| Mounted tabs | Pane markers | Before median | After cold median | Improvement |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100 | 1,000 | 9.46 ms | 0.15 ms | 63× |
| 100 | 10,000 | 128.29 ms | 1.39 ms | 92× |
| 500 | 5,000 | 273.84 ms | 0.70 ms | 391× |
| 1,000 | 10,000 | 1,245.73 ms | 1.30 ms | 958× |

The committed structural regression test is timing-independent: 2,500 tab lookups over one 1,000-marker snapshot caused 2,500 enumerations / 2,500,000 marker reads before and exactly 1 enumeration / 1,000 reads after.

Parity measurements at 1,000 lookups × 10,000 markers kept identical hit counts for absent, first match, last match, explicit `false`, and legacy no-colon keys. After times were 1.13–1.46 ms versus 1,110.50–1,330.56 ms before.

Low-cardinality guard: one tab with an early match did not regress cold construction—at 10,000 markers it measured 1.157 ms before and 0.999 ms after; an absent match measured 1.267 ms before and 1.012 ms after.

## Regression and compatibility proof

- Exact booleans remain unchanged for canonical, numeric legacy, no-colon, multi-colon, prefix-collision, falsy, missing, add, and clear cases.
- Adding or clearing one marker changes only its owning tab in the parity test.
- Duplicate tab IDs retain the prior existential behavior; the cache does not infer worktree or host ownership.
- Native, folder-workspace, WSL, direct-SSH, and paired/remote tab IDs remain opaque strings. There is no Git command, provider, process, RPC, stream, persisted-state, or remote-wire change.
- `WeakMap` avoids strong retention and supports multiple concurrently retained snapshots.

Electron CDP validation used an isolated profile and the intended branch identity. On two real rendered terminal tabs, adding an unread completion marker to the inactive tab visibly applied the amber unread treatment only there; the real clear action removed the store marker and the treatment from both tabs. The only console errors were the pre-existing exhausted GitHub API limit.

## Verification

- `pnpm tc`
- 78/78 related tests across terminal-tab status, SortableTab update-depth, Cmd+J live status, and recent tabs
- `pnpm run check:code-quality:changed` — 0 findings
- `pnpm run check:max-lines-ratchet`
- targeted `oxfmt`
- `git diff --check`
- independent review: no blocking correctness issue

## GitHub overlap and merge risk

Checked before editing. Merged PRs #13554 and #16173 cache/gate different unread projections; no active PR implements this per-tab index. Open PR #9318 is the only direct file overlap and still scans the marker map per tab, so this is not duplicate work.

- **Behavioral risk: low.** Pure renderer-derived cache; no source-of-truth or user-facing behavior changes.
- **Compatibility risk: low.** No platform, execution-host, Git, provider, or wire boundary is touched.
- **Textual/rebase risk: high.** #9318 rewrites the same status module and is currently stale/dirty. If it lands first, this must be rebased into its provider-aware resolver (likely indexing pane keys per tab, not only booleans) while retaining current false-marker semantics.
- **Backout:** revert this single commit; there is no migration or external state.

records.title: perf(browser): release popup origin bar contents
records.body:
<!-- orca-pr-loc -->
<!-- Programmatic LoC summary. Do not edit by hand; rewritten on every commit. -->

| | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 1 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​45 | 0 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​45 |
| Prod | 1 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​14 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​5 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​9 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

Each browser popup contains two mini browser pages: the site itself and Orca's origin strip above it. Electron closes the outer `BaseWindow` but deliberately leaves both child pages alive. Orca already closed the site page, but forgot the origin strip, so every popup could leave one hidden `WebContents` behind. This closes both children.

## What Changed

- Close the origin-bar `WebContents` after the popup content during normal window teardown.
- Close it on content self-destruction and fail-closed popup preparation paths too.
- Cache the bar contents while valid, because Electron's getter becomes empty after independent destruction.
- Cover normal close, content self-destruction, preparation failure, an already-destroyed bar, and 25 repeated popup lifecycles.

## Why

Electron 43's documented [`BaseWindow` resource-management contract](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v43.1.0/docs/api/base-window.md#resource-management) says closing the window does not destroy child `WebContentsView.webContents`; applications must close each child explicitly. Leaving the Orca-controlled bar alive accumulates renderer-side WebContents resources as users open OAuth/SSO and other browser popups.

## Linked Issue

N/A — found during the performance audit. An overlap search found no open issue or PR owning this lifecycle leak; the similarly worded popup issues found were unrelated.

## Visual Proof

N/A — popup appearance and interaction are intentionally unchanged. The invisible cleanup was verified through the rendered Electron surface and CDP target lifecycle:

- Baseline: 2 targets (`Orca` page + opener webview).
- Visible popup open: 4 targets; the added targets were the 500×400 popup content and the 500×34 origin strip displaying `http://127.0.0.1:8899`.
- Clicked the visible **Close popup** button: returned to the exact same 2 baseline target IDs, with neither popup target stranded.

## Measurement Proof

Deterministic red/green tests against the production boundary:

| Lifecycle | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Normal close | 0/1 origin bars closed | 1/1 |
| `prepareContent` failure | 0/1 origin bars closed | 1/1 |
| 25 repeated popup cycles | 0/25 origin bars closed | 25/25 |

The old implementation failed both one-cycle assertions with “expected once, received zero.”

## Testing

- [x] I manually tested these changes locally
- [x] Automated tests added/updated
- `pnpm test src/main/browser/popup-origin-bar-window.test.ts` — 19/19 passed
- `pnpm tc:node` — passed
- `pnpm run check:code-quality:changed` — 0 findings across 2 changed files
- `git diff --check` — clean
- Electron 43.1.0 on macOS via Playwright CDP — intended worktree/branch identity confirmed; popup opened and closed through its real rendered controls

Linux/Windows were not manually exercised. The changed path uses only Electron lifecycle APIs with no platform branch; CI covers the platform matrix.

## No-user-regression signoff

- Popup content still receives `close()` first, preserving its unload/opener notification semantics.
- The isolated Orca data-URL bar closes second; no popup layout, navigation, title, session, or origin-display behavior changes.
- Destroyed-content guards remain in place, including the Electron edge where a destroyed view's getter becomes empty.
- No IPC, remote wire, SSH execution, Git, filesystem path, workspace-kind, or provider behavior changes.

## Review

Independent lifecycle review found no merge blocker after the cached-WebContents guard was added. The implementation matches Electron's explicit ownership contract.

## Merge Risk

Low. This is a two-file ownership fix localized to popup teardown. The main risk is changing close ordering; the implementation deliberately retains the existing graceful content close first and only then releases Orca's origin strip. Automated coverage exercises every reachable teardown path.

## Agent skill upstream boundary

- [x] Not applicable.

records.title: fix(browser): accept an empty --value in cookie set and --pass in set credentials
records.body:
## ELI5
Setting a cookie to "nothing" and using a blank password are both real things the browser runtime already allows. The CLI was saying "you forgot to type something" and refusing. This teaches both commands that an empty value is a real value.

## What Changed
`cookie set` reads `--value` and `set credentials` reads `--pass` with `getRequiredStringFlagAllowingEmpty` instead of `getRequiredStringFlag`, so an explicit empty string is forwarded to the RPC. `--name` and `--user` still require a non-empty string, matching the schemas.

## Why
The server contract is deliberately asymmetric — `CookieSet.value` and `SetCredentials.pass` accept any string while `name` and `user` require a non-empty one (`browser-schemas.ts`). The CLI was stricter than the schema on the two fields where empty is meaningful. Clearing a cookie's value and token-only HTTP basic auth (empty password) were impossible from the CLI. Mirrors #15863 (storage set) and #16030 (fill/select), tracked separately per the note on #15810.

## Linked Issue
Fixes #17225

## Visual Proof
N/A — CLI arg-parsing behavior, covered by tests.

## Testing
New `src/cli/browser-cookie-credentials-empty-value.test.ts`: asserts `--value ""` reaches `browser.cookie.set` and `--pass ""` reaches `browser.setCredentials`, and that empty `--name` / missing `--pass` are still rejected before dispatch. The two empty-value cases fail without the fix and pass with it. `browser.test.ts` (33) still passes. oxlint + oxfmt clean, `tc:cli` passes.

## AI Disclosure
Written with AI assistance (Claude, model claude-fable-5). I reviewed the diff and test before submission.

## Review
Same two-line helper swap as the merged storage fix and #16030, applied to the last two fields in this family. Server contract unchanged. CLI only becomes less restrictive on existing params.
