- **Tests (`src/main/browser/browser-session-registry.test.ts`)**: Added comprehensive unit tests covering creation, deduplication, folder lookup, partition allowlist checks, storage clearance, and hydration from persisted disk metadata.

Multi-project workflows and agent runs frequently collide when projects share local ports and domains. records.title: [Bug]: browser fill/select reject --value "" though the runtime accepts empty values
records.body:
### Operating system

macOS (platform-independent — CLI layer)

### Orca version

main

### Details

**Short summary:** `orca browser fill --element X --value ""` and `orca browser select --element X --value ""` fail with `Missing required --value`, even though the runtime accepts an empty value. Filling a field with `""` clears it (a real operation, distinct from leaving it untouched), and selecting an `<option value="">` placeholder is common.

**What happened?** The CLI rejects `--value ""` before ever sending the RPC.

**How to reproduce:**
1. Attach a browser and get an element ref for a text input.
2. Run `orca browser fill --element <ref> --value ""`.
3. See error `Missing required --value` — the field is never cleared. Same for `orca browser select --element <ref> --value ""`.

**Root cause:** `src/cli/handlers/browser-interact.ts` reads `value` with `getRequiredStringFlag` (rejects empty), but the server schemas accept empty — `Fill.value = requiredStringAllowingEmpty(...)` and `Select.value` only checks `typeof === 'string'` (`src/main/runtime/rpc/methods/browser-schemas.ts`). Same shape as #15810 / #15863 for `storage set`. I have a fix ready.

records.title: fix(terminal): arm the restore baseline only on a snapshot that painted content
records.body:
<!-- orca-pr-loc -->
<!-- Programmatic LoC summary. Do not edit by hand; rewritten on every commit. -->

| | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 3 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​399 | 0 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​399 |
| Prod | 2 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​58 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​4 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​54 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## What

`setRestoredSnapshotBaseline` arms a baseline that permanently drops every delivery chunk at or below the snapshot's `seq`, on the model's claim that those bytes are already painted.

`reconcileChunkAgainstRestoredSnapshot` has recovery for a baseline that **under**-reports — a gap ahead triggers `force-fresh-restore`, and a `rawLength` mismatch re-restores. It has no path for a baseline that **over**-reports. Those chunks hit `if (meta.seq <= restoredSnapshotBaselineSeq) return { action: 'drop-duplicate' }` forever, and an idle shell never re-sends them, so the hole never heals.

This gates arming on whether the snapshot actually painted printable cells. A snapshot claiming `seq > 0` while painting nothing cannot be the rendering of the output it claims to cover, so the claim is disproven and the redelivery is the only remaining copy of those bytes.

Also adds `headless-terminal-dispose-write-ordering.test.ts`, pinning both halves of `disposeHeadlessTerminal`'s contract (a write queued before disposal still parses; a write issued after lands on a fresh emulator). Both halves were previously unpinned and silently reversible — the test is mutation-verified.

## Honest scope — please read before approving

- **This does not fix STA-4999.** That bug's pane shows a *truncated* buffer that ends mid-pad, not a blank one. Truncated is not blank, so this guard would not have caught it. STA-4999 stays open.
- **No field evidence that blank-with-`seq > 0` actually occurs.** This is a reachable-by-inspection hole in a function with a proven recovery asymmetry, hardened defensively. It is not a reproduction of an observed failure.
- **Known false positive.** The predicate is `stripAnsiEscapeSequences(...).trim()`, so a screen painted entirely as spaces on a colored background reads as blank. Such a snapshot would decline to arm and replay a bounded backlog instead. The trade is deliberate — replaying a bounded backlog is recoverable, dropping bytes permanently is not — but it is a real behavior change on that path.

## Testing

- `pty-connection-restored-baseline-shortfall.test.ts` — integration through `connectPanePty`: the inverse case recovered (chunk inside the window, chunk straddling the baseline, live chunk after it), plus a regression guard that a content-bearing snapshot still suppresses duplicates *and* still trims a straddling chunk.
- `restored-snapshot-coverage.test.ts` — predicate units.
- **Mutation-verified**: removing the guard fails both recovery tests and leaves the regression guard passing.
- 3,724 terminal-pane tests, 2 dispose-ordering tests, `typecheck:web`, `typecheck:node`, `oxlint` — all green.

Refs STA-5179

records.title: [Feature]: Add cua-driver as a computer-use provider (background input, Wayland, menu paths, page-level browser ops)
records.body:
### Problem or use case

> **Disclosure up front:** I work on [`cua-driver`](https://github.com/trycua/cua) (Cua AI, Inc.). This is a vendor proposal — read it with that in mind. It's MIT, same as Orca, and I've tried to write the tradeoffs section honestly rather than pitch. If the answer is "no thanks, we want this in-tree," that's a completely reasonable answer and I'd still be glad to have the gap list be useful.

## Summary

Orca's computer-use stack (`native/computer-use-{macos,linux,windows}` + `src/main/computer/`) is a clean, well-factored piece of work — the provider indirection in `ComputerProviderLifecycle` is exactly the right seam. This proposes adding a third provider behind that same seam:

```ts
type ComputerProvider =
  | MacOSNativeProviderClient
  | DesktopScriptProviderClient
  | CuaDriverProviderClient   // new
```

**Explicitly not proposing:** changing the `orca computer <verb>` CLI surface, the `skills/computer-use` contract, or removing the existing providers. The public surface stays byte-identical; `capabilities` starts reporting `true` for things that report `false` today. If it doesn't work out, delete one file.

## The gaps

Each of these is a thing agents hit in practice, not a spec-sheet diff.

### 1. Every action steals focus

`SyntheticMouseClickDelivery.swift` posts to the HID event tap, and the header comment explains why `CGEventPostToPid` was rejected. That's a correct read of the problem — pid-targeted mouse events arrive with no window association and AppKit never routes the press. But the consequence is that Orca's computer-use is a **foreground** driver: hence `window_not_focused`, hence `--restore-window`, hence the guidance in the skill guide to "restore/focus the window" when an action doesn't visibly change anything.

For an ADE running a fleet of parallel agents, this is the sharpest edge. Two agents driving two apps fight over the frontmost window, and the user can't use their own machine while either runs.

`cua-driver` solves this per-platform rather than giving up on it:
- **macOS** — SkyLight private SPI (`SLPSPostEventRecordTo`, `SLPSSetFrontProcessWithOptions`) for per-PSN delivery to a specific window without changing the front process.
- **Windows** — layered UIA + `PostMessage` chain.
- **Linux/X11** — AT-SPI + `XSendEvent`.
- `launch_app` starts an app *without* foregrounding it; `bring_to_front` is the explicit opt-in when you actually want focus.

Delivery mode is reported back per action (`delivery.mode: background | foreground | not_applicable | unknown`), so the agent knows which it got instead of guessing.

### 2. Linux is X11-only, and degrades silently-ish on Wayland

`native/computer-use-linux/runtime.py` gates on `XDG_SESSION_TYPE`:

```python
is_wayland = os.environ.get("XDG_SESSION_TYPE", "").lower() == "wayland"
has_hotkey     = shutil.which("xdotool") is not None and not is_wayland
has_screenshot = Gdk is not None and GdkPixbuf is not None and not is_wayland
...
raise RuntimeError("modified clicks require xdotool on an X11 session")
```

So on a default GNOME/Fedora/Ubuntu desktop (Wayland since 22.04), computer-use loses screenshots, hotkeys, and modifier-clicks. Given Orca ships a VPS/headless Linux story, that's a large slice of the install base.

`cua-driver` has a native Wayland backend (`CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`) plus a GNOME Shell helper extension (`winrects@cua`) for window geometry under the compositor's restrictions.

### 3. No menu-path invocation

There's no `AXMenuBar` traversal and no menu verb. `ComputerProviderCapabilities.supports.surfaces.menus/menubar` exist as flags, but the only way to reach a menu item is if the provider happens to surface it as a tree node and you click it — which means opening the menu, re-snapshotting, and clicking again, with focus churn at each step.

`cua-driver` has `invoke_menu`, which resolves an exact menu path one live native level at a time and invokes the final item through AX — no screenshot round-trip, no intermediate clicks. A huge fraction of real desktop tasks are menu paths.

### 4. Browsers are driven as pixels + AX, not as pages

The skill guide's browser advice is telling:

> "for Edge, Chrome, Safari, and similar browser windows, set the address/search field directly, then press Return. Do not assume raw typing went to the address bar." … "Page text fields can expose accessibility actions without moving DOM focus; if a click or `set-value` does not change the focused receiver, use `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` from a known focused field or window-local coordinates from a fresh screenshot."

That's a well-written workaround for not having page-level access. Since Orca is itself an Electron app and a lot of agent work is web work, this matters.

`cua-driver` binds a browser window to its DevTools endpoint (`browser_prepare`) and exposes typed page tools: `browser_navigate`, `browser_click`, `browser_type`, `browser_pointer`, `browser_dialog`, `browser_download`, `browser_set_input_files`, `get_browser_state`. Refs are exact and live; navigation invalidates them and the tool refuses a stale ref rather than clicking whatever moved into that position.

### 5. Element indexes are raw integers, so staleness is unenforced

`ComputerSnapshotData.focusedElementId` is a `number`, and actions take `--element-index <n>`. The guide is candid about the risk:

> "Element indexes are short-lived and go stale after delays, navigation, focus changes, scrolling, window changes, or app re-rendering."

The failure mode isn't `element_not_found` — that's the *good* case. The bad case is index 42 still existing after a re-render and now pointing at a different control. The agent gets `ok` and a wrong action.

`cua-driver` uses `element_token` — a snapshot-generation hash plus index, e.g. `s00007a3f:42` — validated on every use, with a distinct error: *"element_token is stale; call get_window_state again to refresh."* Structurally impossible to hit the wrong element from a stale ref.

### 6. Snapshots return prose, not structured elements

`renderSnapshot()` deliberately drops the elements array:

```ts
// Why: bridge elements can be large; keep them cached internally for actions
// instead of returning duplicated metadata in every agent-facing snapshot.
```

and the guide instructs the agent to parse indexes out of `result.snapshot.treeText`, warning that `elementCount` must not be used to infer them and that indexes may be sparse. So the agent's only machine-readable path to a target is string-parsing a rendered tree.

`get_window_state` returns **both** a structured `elements[]` array (preferred) and a Markdown rendering (back-compat). Payload size is handled with `max_elements`/`max_depth` bounds rather than by withholding the structure.

### 7. Verification is binary; there's no "probably did nothing"

`ComputerActionVerification` is `verified | unverified`, with `unverified` covering both "the AX call succeeded but we didn't assert" and "input was fired into the void." Those are very different confidence levels, and the guide has to spend a paragraph teaching the agent to tell them apart by reading `reason`.

`cua-driver` reports:
- `effect: confirmed | partial | unverifiable | suspected_noop | refused`
- `evidence[]: { kind: value_readback | window_change, … }`
- `escalation: { target: pixel | foreground | page | session, reason: route_unavailable | delivery_failed | effect_unconfirmed | suspected_noop | permission_required }`

`suspected_noop` is the one that matters most in practice — it's the difference between an agent retrying and an agent confidently continuing down a branch that never happened. `escalation` tells the agent *what to try next* instead of leaving it to infer.

There's also a standalone `verify_state` tool for deterministically checking bounded predicates against one exact window.

### 8. Smaller gaps

| | Orca today | `cua-driver` |
|---|---|---|
| Window move/resize | `supports.windows.moveResize` flag exists; no CLI verb | `set_window_frame` with independent geometry readback |
| Occlusion | Guide: on Linux/Windows screenshots "may come from the visible desktop region"; "trust the tree over potentially occluded pixels" | Per-window capture; `zoom` for cropped region capture with padding |
| Repeatability | — | `start_recording` / `stop_recording` / `replay_trajectory` — replay a run by re-invoking every turn's tool call |
| Human observability | — | Agent cursor overlay (`set_agent_cursor_*`) so a watching human sees where the agent is acting |
| Agent transport | CLI only — the skill shells out to `orca computer …` | MCP stdio + local HTTP w/ bearer token, **and** a CLI |
| Lifecycle | Stateless per call | `start_session`/`end_session` with cleanup hooks, authenticated transport lease, `revoke` |
| Diagnostics | `capabilities`, `permissions` | `doctor`, `diagnose`, `health_report` |
| macOS TCC identity | Grants attach to Orca/terminal | Signed `CuaDriver.app` (`com.trycua.driver`) — grants attach to a stable identity, survive Orca updates |

### Proposed solution

### Integration shape

1. `src/main/computer/cua-driver-provider-client.ts` implementing the same interface as `MacOSNativeProviderClient` / `DesktopScriptProviderClient` — talks MCP stdio to a `cua-driver` child, same as `sidecar-client.ts` forks the Node sidecar.
2. `shouldUseCuaDriverProvider()` gated behind a setting, **off by default**, preferred over the existing providers only when the binary is present and `doctor` passes.
3. Map `cua-driver`'s richer result vocabulary down to `ComputerActionMetadata`/`ComputerActionVerification` so nothing downstream changes; optionally widen the Orca types later if the extra states prove useful.
4. Keep `app_blocked` enforcement in the Orca wrapper, above the provider.
5. `capabilities` starts reporting the newly-true flags. The skill guide needs no rewrite — same verbs, same flags, more of them work.

Binary distribution is the real open question, and I don't want to hand-wave it. Options, roughly in order of how much I'd expect you to like them: (a) opt-in, user installs it themselves, Orca detects and offers it; (b) Orca offers install via `cua-driver`'s own installer/updater; (c) bundled. (a) seems like the obvious starting point.

### What a provider swap must not regress

Genuinely — these are good and `cua-driver` does not have equivalents today:

1. **The password-manager blocklist.** `BLOCKED_APP_FRAGMENTS` (1Password, Bitwarden, Dashlane, LastPass, NordPass, Proton Pass) → `app_blocked`. `cua-driver` has consent/policy/authorization layers but no app blocklist of this kind. This should stay enforced in Orca's provider wrapper regardless of backend, and I'd like to upstream the idea.
2. **Zero-install Windows.** `runtime.ps1` needs no binary — just PowerShell + UIAutomation. `cua-driver` is a ~60 MB binary.
3. **The permission setup UX.** `ComputerUsePane` / `ComputerUseSkillSetupPanel` / the macOS permission helper are better onboarding than a CLI prompt.
4. **WSL-managed sessions** and the `ORCA_CLI_COMMAND` / `orca-ide` resolution logic (including the GNOME Orca screen-reader collision handling — nice catch).

### Alternatives or additional context

### Open questions for maintainers

- Is a third provider behind `ComputerProviderLifecycle` acceptable in principle, or is out-of-tree/binary dependency a hard no for this surface?
- Would you rather have some of the above upstreamed into your own providers instead? Background input on macOS and Wayland support are both self-contained and I'm happy to help either way — the goal is that the gaps close, not that a particular binary ships.
- Does `ComputerProviderCapabilities` need a version bump if a provider reports capabilities the current flags can't express (menu paths, page-level browser ops, recording)?

Happy to prototype (1)–(3) behind the flag as a draft PR if there's appetite. If not, no hard feelings — closing this as "we'll build it ourselves" is a fine outcome and the gap list stands on its own.

records.title: fix(win32): hide the console window for agent-browser and git helpers
records.body:

| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 3 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​217 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​1 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​216 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## Problem

A GUI Electron process that spawns a console-subsystem binary without `windowsHide` gets a real console window: it flashes and steals foreground. For the git status poll that is once per poll (#10488).

W1 (#15749) routed most child processes through `runProcess`, which sets the flag once for everything. Six call sites still spawn directly and were missed:

- `src/main/browser/agent-browser-bridge.ts` — stale-session close, main command exec
- `src/main/git/runner.ts` — `execFile`, two `spawn`s, and `gitExecFileSync` (every synchronous git call)

Diagnosed by @OrcaWin in #14589. The SSH and cookie-import sites that PR also covered are already fixed on `main` by the W1 migration, and it now conflicts because `agent-browser-bridge.test.ts` was split up since.

## Change

Add the flag at the six sites, then stop relying on review to catch the seventh: a ratchet scans every file importing `child_process` and fails on a call whose options omit `windowsHide`.

- Allowlist starts at the **76** files that still offend and can only shrink. It doubles as the W4 worklist for routing those calls through the chokepoint, where the flag stops being a per-call-site decision.
- Comments are stripped before scanning — `runner.ts` documents its own wrapper as `execFileSync('git', ...)` in a doc comment, and counting that as a call would have parked the file on the allowlist forever, pre-approving a real regression in it. (Caught by testing the guard against a reverted fix.)
- A vacuity check fails if the scan ever collapses to nothing.

## Verification

Typecheck, lint, full unit suite. Guard verified non-vacuous by reverting one fix and watching it name the file.

## Risk

None identified. `windowsHide` is inert off Windows, and no call site changes behaviour beyond not opening a window.

Credit: @OrcaWin (#14589).

records.title: fix(browser): store an empty value in storage set commands
records.body:
## ELI5
Saving an empty text value into the browser's storage from the command line was blocked, even though the app itself is happy to store an empty string. This lets `--value ""` go through.

## What Changed
`orca storage local set` and `orca storage session set` now read `--value` with `getRequiredStringFlagAllowingEmpty` instead of `getRequiredStringFlag`, so an empty string is accepted. `--key` is unchanged and still must be non-empty.

## Why
The runtime's `StorageKeyValue` schema (`src/main/runtime/rpc/methods/browser-schemas.ts`) deliberately validates `key` as a non-empty string but `value` as *any* string, so `setItem(key, "")` is a supported operation distinct from an absent key. The CLI used `getRequiredStringFlag`, which rejects `""`, so the empty-value case failed with `Missing required --value` before ever reaching the runtime — and there is no other CLI way to store an empty value (`storage clear` wipes everything). This matches the existing convention: computer-use `set-value` already uses `getRequiredStringFlagAllowingEmpty` for the same reason.

## Linked Issue
Fixes #15810

## Visual Proof
N/A — CLI-only behavior with no UI/interaction change.

## Testing

- [x] Automated tests added/updated

Verified fail-without/pass-with by reverting only the source. Ran `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `typecheck:tsc:{node,cli,web}` (all clean), plus adjacent CLI suites (52 passing). Tested on macOS; change is platform-independent.

records.title: fix(terminal-pane): gate remote pane spawns on the first session.tabs snapshot
records.body:
## Summary

**What**

A runtime-owned pane with **no PTY binding** now waits for its worktree's first accepted `session.tabs` snapshot before connecting its transport (timer-polled at 200ms — hidden tabs get no animation frames — bounded at 10s). Panes carrying a preserved sleep-resume PTY handle are exempt; local and SSH panes are never gated.

**Why**

#15622 — opening a paired-runtime worktree restores persisted PTY-less terminal rows, and each pane's mount connected its transport immediately; on a remote runtime that connection **creates a shell**, so every stale row respawned as a live terminal. The first authoritative snapshot resolves the ambiguity: it either attaches the pane to the host's existing PTY (the connect path then reattaches instead of spawning) or drops the stale row — but only if the pane hasn't already spawned beside it.

The gate lives at the single connect chokepoint (`runDeferredConnect` inside `connectPanePty`), so both mount paths (TerminalPane + the lifecycle hook) get it, and the bounded wait preserves today's behavior when the runtime is unreachable. The sleep-resume exemption matters because that path *is* an intentional cold-spawn of a preserved handle — the existing remote-attach suite caught it before shipping (`cold-spawns slept remote runtime PTYs instead of reattaching the preserved handle` now passes unchanged).

The snapshot-accepted check reuses `getLatestWebSessionTabsPublicationEpoch` from `web-session-tabs-sync` — the same acceptance record the tab reconciliation trusts.

**Testing**

- New `runtime-pane-spawn-gate.test.ts` (6 cases): local/SSH never gated; existing PTY binding never gated (reattach path); PTY-less runtime pane defers until snapshot accepted then proceeds; bounded wait expires so an unreachable runtime gets a pane; mid-wait snapshot wins; **sleep-resume preserved-handle panes are never gated**. 6/6.
- Full `terminal-pane` suite: **3695 passed, 1 skipped, 380/380 files** — including the remote-runtime attach suite that pinned the slept-resume semantics.
- `pnpm run typecheck` clean.

Fixes #15622

records.title: fix(cmd-j): host-qualify browser and simulator tab candidates (STA-4965)
records.body:
<!-- orca-pr-loc -->
<!-- Programmatic LoC summary. Do not edit by hand; rewritten on every commit. -->

| | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 16 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​1497 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​21 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​1476 |
| Prod | 23 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​712 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​136 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​576 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

Cmd-J treated a worktree ID as globally unique, but it is only unique inside one execution host. If two hosts published the same ID, Orca could duplicate, hide, or misroute browser and simulator results. This change makes a unified tab carry its owning host and makes candidate construction, activation, reuse, and metadata lookup use `(execution host, worktree)`.

## Current-Main Decision

Latest inspected `origin/main` is `a157f4cfec`; the only post-rebase commit is unrelated, and the affected Cmd-J surfaces remain byte-identical to the proven-red merge base `012e9f410c`, so the report is not superseded.

Invariant: same-ID sibling hosts retain separate correct tabs, each appears once, and selection activates its owning host.

Injected identities:

- `local|repo-shared::/workspace`
- `runtime:host-b|repo-shared::/workspace`

The deterministic fault injection aggregates both hosts under one bare worktree bucket. Independent oracles assert exact candidate ownership and the selected/rendered host plus backing state.

## Red / Green / Revert Proof

- Affected baseline `012e9f410c`: **4 failed, 24 passed**; browser and simulator tabs were routed through both owners and ambiguous unstamped tabs duplicated.
- Candidate: **28/28 passed**.
- Candidate with only the reported browser/simulator filters disabled: **the same 4 failed, 24 passed**.
- Restored candidate: **28/28 passed**.
- Review counterexamples went red before their fixes: **4/40**, **4/16**, **1/6**, **1/7**, **1/12**, **1/13**, four additional **1/6** cases, including SSH/runtime aliases, folder reuse, repo/review metadata, local creation stamping, filtered-host ambiguity, scoped open-tab ambiguity, and legacy local fallback.
- Exact current focused result: **17 files, 239/239 passed**.

## What Changed

- Add optional `Tab.executionHostId`, persist it, and validate it in workspace sessions.
- Stamp local creation and paired-runtime browser/editor/terminal mirrors with the owner.
- Keep manual emulator launches local and reuse exact host-stamped simulator tabs before worktree hydration.
- Treat physical SSH ownership and its `runtime:<environment>` paired alias as one boundary.
- Share one ownership predicate across browser, simulator, generic workspace, and open-tab candidate builders.
- Compute legacy ambiguity from the unfiltered topology, so host filters cannot make unknown ownership look known.
- Host-qualify activation, dedupe, simulator reuse, worktree/repo lookup, rendered repo badges, and review-cache metadata.
- Preserve hostless legacy local worktrees through a local-only lookup fallback while keeping ambiguous remote ownership fail-closed.
- Fail closed for missing, conflicting, or ambiguous owners.
- Centralize the repeated active-worktree host fallback.
- Seed the E2E browser URL and dismiss the optional first-use markup hint through a bounded two-second wait; only Playwright TimeoutError is treated as absence, while strict-locator and lifecycle errors rethrow.

No polling, TTL, cleanup sweep, new stream opcode, required wire field, or provider-specific path was added.

## Why This Boundary

The aggregate maps intentionally remain keyed by bare worktree ID and can contain sibling-host publications. Re-keying only one map or patching the two reported readers leaves generic tabs, activation, simulator reuse, metadata, and future tab types inconsistent. `Tab` is the first shared object that knows both what the tab is and which runtime owns it, so optional `Tab.executionHostId` is the durable boundary. Unknown legacy ownership stays unknown rather than silently routing local.

Rejected alternatives:

- Re-key every aggregate map: larger state migration and still leaves old/publication ownership implicit.
- Separate browser/simulator filters: duplicates policy and misses generic, activation, and reuse paths.
- Infer from the selected UI host or fall back local: recreates the misrouting.
- Rewrite simulator resolution or merge unlike active-tab helpers: saves little and raises regression risk.
- Extract the one-off E2E hint handling: adds indirection without consolidating a repeated contract.

## Diff Size

The LoC bot labels `config/reliability-gates.jsonc` as production. The actual split is:

- shipped renderer/shared source: **+412/-136, net +276**;
- reliability evidence manifest: **+300/-0, net +300**;
- tests: **+1497/-21**.

The runtime change is still cross-cutting, but 42% of the reported production additions are evidence, not shipped logic. Three architecture reviews found no safe material consolidation beyond the active-host fallback centralized here; broader reductions would move or duplicate ownership policy rather than remove it.

## Electron Proof

The paired journey uses a real host runtime plus a separate Electron client, proves a real mirror stamp, then injects the deterministic same-ID sibling. Browser and simulator are exercised separately. Each local/remote row appears once; selection updates the owning execution host plus browser workspace or simulator group/tab; the rendered tab is active; and backing owner tuples match.

After the final hint-wait hardening, a fresh build passed the exact journey: **1/1 in 19.8s** (**25.8s total**). A fresh OpenCode regression reviewer independently reran the exact head and got **1/1 in 21.7s** with the same ownership and uniqueness oracles intact.

## Validation

- Head: `11da4fd9f2732ba3e4ebbbcd81dea5b98f0f13ab`

records.title: fix(browser): fail closed on wedged cookie CDP mutations
records.body:
## Summary

- give a CDP command a 10-second deadline and a bounded 1-second settlement grace
- treat only a fulfilled reply during that grace as proven completion; rejection or silence retires the exclusively owned debugger target
- permanently quarantine the stable Electron Session after ambiguous retirement, so later same-partition imports fail fast without mutating the jar
- require an Orca restart to recover an ambiguously retired partition; other partitions remain independent

## Why

The per-partition lock correctly serialized imports, but a `debugger.sendCommand` promise that never settled held it forever. A plain `Promise.race` would restore liveness by releasing the lock while the original CDP mutation could still finish late and overlap a newer import. This change keeps the stable Electron Session as the authoritative partition identity and fails closed whenever retirement cannot prove completion.

## Evidence

- Baseline `012e9f410c`: deterministic oracle red. After 60 seconds, both same-partition imports remained pending and the only command was the first wedged `Network.setCookie`.
- Candidate: first call returns after target retirement and bounded grace; queued same-partition imports fail fast; no second target or mutation starts even if the injected promise later settles ambiguously.
- Fix disabled: the same oracle returns to the baseline red signal.
- Late completion: quarantine remains fail-closed because target destruction or debugger-promise rejection is not proof that Chromium cannot still mutate the Session.
- Grace rejection: a command that rejects after its deadline still retires and poisons the Session; the queued import never starts.
- Native clear/snapshot: an ambiguously retired `Network.getAllCookies` returns the same restart-required classification and discards pending staging state.
- Partition isolation: another Electron Session continues importing while the first is quarantined.
- Real Electron: the production `openCookieClearStore` path executes an injected wedged `Network.setCookie`, destroys its hidden target, rejects both queued and post-completion mutations, and verifies no recovery cookie entered the real jar.

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/main/browser` — 76 files, 803 tests passed
- `pnpm run typecheck`
- `pnpm run lint`
- rendered Orca dev smoke through Playwright CDP: intended worktree identity, normal visible welcome surface, zero renderer console errors

## Remaining gap

Chromium does not expose a safe way to force a real internal `Network.setCookie` implementation to hang. The Electron fixture injects the fault at the production debugger method boundary while retaining the real Session, target lifecycle, CDP command name, recovery write, and cookie jar.

records.title: fix(terminal): seed list preview from daemon snapshots after restart (STA-4326)
records.body:
<!-- orca-pr-loc -->
<!-- Programmatic LoC summary. Do not edit by hand; rewritten on every commit. -->

| | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 1 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​225 | 0 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​225 |
| Prod | 2 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​114 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​19 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​95 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

After Orca restarts, `orca terminal list` said a still-running agent pane had never produced output, while `orca terminal read` of the same pane showed the live TUI. List was looking at a blank in-memory notepad this process never wrote to. It now copies a small screen snapshot from the daemon that kept the pane alive, once, when listing rediscovers that pane. That listing snapshot is a short preview only — it does not steal the deeper scrollback `terminal read` and legacy worker reveal still fetch.

## What Changed

- `listTerminals` seeds a **listing-only** preview from a 24-row provider snapshot for never-attached local daemon PTYs. It does **not** write the shared restore tail.
- `lastOutputAt` is not invented from that snapshot. Snapshot bytes are historical screen state, not a recency event.
- If the daemon snapshot cannot be consulted, list adds optional `activityObservation: "unverifiable"` and leaves `lastOutputAt` null. That is not idle and not exited.
- Seed is once per PTY, capped at the 200-row listing limit, 24 rows, 750ms timeout. Attached PTYs that already ingested live bytes are not round-tripped.
- Recovered legacy workers skip the listing seed so their own 120-row provider read still runs.

## Why

`onPtyData` was the only writer of `lastOutputAt` / `preview`. A pane whose PTY survived restart is discovered only through controller inventory, so this main never attached and never ingested a byte. `terminal read` already fell back to the provider snapshot; `terminal list` did not. Callers treat a null `lastOutputAt` as idle/dead and conclude a live worker is finished.

A first version of this seed wrote the shared restore tail. That spent the one-shot restore budget at 24 rows, so the legacy provider-reveal never issued its own 120-row fetch and the revealed worker showed a truncated scrollback. Listing preview and restore tail are different products with different depths; they stay separate.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #14523
Linear: [STA-4326](https://linear.app/stably/issue/STA-4326)

## Visual Proof

N/A — CLI listing contract in the main process. No layout, chrome, or renderer styling change.

## Testing

- [ ] I manually tested these changes locally
- [x] Automated tests added/updated

Commands:

```
pnpm vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/runtime/orca-runtime.test.ts -t "fences provider resume and reveals one exact live legacy worker without stealing focus"
pnpm vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/runtime/terminal-list-inventory-activity-seed.test.ts
pnpm typecheck
node config/scripts/check-changed-code-quality.mjs -- 4e058d4a52ea4653a5cf86fac271c8010334361e
```

Legacy-worker reveal (`serializeProviderBuffer` at 120 rows), unmodified expectation:

- **Pre-fix:** FAIL. `toHaveBeenCalledWith('pty-legacy', { scrollbackRows: 120 })` received `{ scrollbackRows: 24 }`, number of calls: 1.
- **Post-fix:** PASS.
- **Neutered** (listing seed wrote the restore tail again from shared inventory): FAIL, same 24-vs-120 assertion.

Listing seed suite (5 tests):

- **Pre-fix (STA-4326):** 3 failed / 1 passed. Inventory-discovered PTY listed `preview: ""`; `activityObservation` absent.
- **Post-fix:** 5 passed, including a new assertion that a later `read` still fetches at 120 rows.
- **Neutered** (list seed call removed, tests kept): 4 failed / 1 passed (attached live-bytes row still passes).

Covered: (a) never-attached PTY reports the provider screen through `list`; (b) attached PTY with live bytes is unchanged and does not call `serializeProviderBuffer`; (c) missing snapshot is `activityObservation: unverifiable` with `lastOutputAt` still null; (d) four unattached rows seed once, the attached row is skipped, and a second `list` does not round-trip again; (e) listing seed does not consume the restore-tail budget.

`pnpm typecheck` passed. Changed-code quality gate passed since `4e058d4a52ea`.

## Review

**`lastOutputAt` after this change:** epoch ms of the last byte this main ingested via `onPtyData`. Null means this main has not ingested live output — not idle, not exited, and never a synthesized snapshot timestamp. A seeded listing `preview` is retained screen. `activityObservation: "unverifiable"` means the provider snapshot could not be asked; inventory still proved the PTY live.

SSH-scoped PTYs are not seeded here (they have their own lease/reattach path). Folder workspaces use the same inventory record. New optional JSON field only; old clients ignore it. No new stream opcode.

records.title: fix(codex): include verified selected home in resume discovery snapshot (STA-4919)
records.body:
<!-- orca-pr-loc -->

| Prod | 2 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​55 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​13 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​42 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

When Orca resumes a Codex session, it looks at two lists of account homes that were built a moment apart. If antivirus briefly locked the selected account's files during the first look, that account disappeared from the scan list even though the second look then found it. Another account that happened to have a copy of the same session could win, so the pane resumed under the wrong login. This PR takes both looks as one snapshot and keeps the selected account in the scan list only after that snapshot actually verified it.

## What Changed

`prepareCodexSessionResumeForLaunch` no longer builds `trustedHomes` from discovery and then, separately, resolves the selected home. Both reads now go through `snapshotCodexResumeHomes`, which unions the **verified** selected home into the trusted list.

Discovery still omits homes whose ownership is `indeterminate` or `untrusted`. Selection still throws on a still-unreadable selected home (STA-4422) and still returns null for a proven untrusted home. The selected path is added only because that second read verified it — never because verification was skipped.

## Why

`getHostCodexHomePathsForSessionDiscovery()` silently omits a home whose ownership read comes back `indeterminate` (transient `EBUSY`/`EPERM` while a scanner holds the marker). `resolveSelectedHostAccountCodexHomePathForResume()` then runs microseconds later and can succeed for that same home.

The legacy session-id rescan iterates only `trustedHomes`. If the selected account is missing from that list, a competing alias in another account wins and the session resumes under the wrong credentials.

STA-4422 already refused resume when the selected home was still unreadable at selection time. It did not close this discovery-then-selection window.

## Linked Issue

Fixes [STA-4919](https://linear.app/stably/issue/STA-4919/fix-transient-ownership-read-race-between-trustedhomes-discovery-and)

Related: STA-4910, PR #15046, STA-4422, STA-4607.

## Visual Proof

N/A — this is a main-process resume-ranking correctness fix. There is no renderer UI change. The regression is covered by a unit test that reproduces the wrong-account resume with a competing alias.

Asserts the resume lands on A, not B. Also asserts a genuinely untrusted home stays excluded.

1. **Pre-fix FAIL** — snapshot without the union: `expected trustedCodexHomes to include homeA` (selected was A; A was missing from the scan list).
2. **Post-fix PASS** — 4 tests passed.

records.title: [Bug]: Embedded browser file inputs never open a native file picker (ChatGPT / any site)
records.body:
### Operating system

macOS (darwin)

### Orca version

1.4.185 (`orca status --json` → `runtime.appVersion`)

### Summary

In Orca’s **embedded browser**, clicking an `<input type="file">` (or site UI that triggers one, e.g. ChatGPT’s paperclip / “+”) does **nothing** — no macOS file dialog appears. Agent path `orca upload --element <ref> --files <paths>` works; interactive UI upload does not.

### Why it matters

Users cannot attach files on chatgpt.com or any other site from the in-app browser. Only workaround is external Chrome/Safari or CLI `orca upload`.

### Reproduction

1. Open a browser tab in Orca.
2. Go to a page with a plain file input, e.g. a local `http://127.0.0.1:.../` page containing `<input type="file">`, or https://chatgpt.com and click attach.
3. Click **Choose File** / paperclip.
4. **Expected:** native macOS open-file dialog.
5. **Actual:** no dialog; input stays “No file chosen”.

Confirmed with CDP:

- `Page.setInterceptFileChooserDialog({ enabled: true })` + click → `Page.fileChooserOpened` fires (browser *can* see the chooser intent).
- With intercept off + click → no dialog surfaces to the user (native picker path broken/silent for this guest).

### Likely cause

Guest `webContents` always attaches the debugger for anti-detection (`injectAntiDetection`), but there is **no handler** that bridges `Page.fileChooserOpened` → `electron.dialog.showOpenDialog` → `DOM.setFileInputFiles`. Offscreen / embedded guests also make Chromium’s own native picker unreliable.

Agent upload works because it calls `DOM.setFileInputFiles` via agent-browser directly, skipping the UI chooser.

### Suggested fix

In guest policy setup (`injectAntiDetection` / `attachGuestPolicies`), after `Page.enable`:

1. `Page.setInterceptFileChooserDialog({ enabled: true })`
2. On debugger `message` === `Page.fileChooserOpened`:
   - `dialog.showOpenDialog` (respect `mode === "selectMultiple"`)
   - `DOM.setFileInputFiles({ backendNodeId, files })`
   - on cancel: `files: []`
3. Parent window: `BrowserWindow.fromWebContents(guest)` → else focused / first window
4. Mirror the intercept enable in `CdpWsProxy.attachDebugger` so agent CDP sessions don’t leave chooser state inconsistent

### Notes

- Do **not** recommend end users patch `app.asar` + ad-hoc resign; that breaks Team ID / Electron Framework loading on macOS.
- Happy to test a build that includes the bridge above.

records.title: feat(browser): add a real profile-reset operation, wired to nothing
records.body:
<!-- orca-pr-loc -->
<!-- Programmatic LoC summary. Do not edit by hand; rewritten on every commit. -->

| | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 1 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​182 | 0 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​182 |
| Prod | 1 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​49 | 0 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​49 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

"Clear browser profile" only deleted cookies. Everything else a site can store stayed behind, so the documented clear-and-retry workaround could not reset the affected profile. This PR adds the complete internal reset operation; **nothing calls it yet**, on purpose.

## The defect

`clearDefaultSessionCookies` calls `clearStorageData({ storages: ['cookies'] })`. A measured profile retained 445MB after that cookie-only clear, including Local Storage, IndexedDB, Service Workers, Session Storage, Trust Tokens, DIPS, Shared Storage, and Network Persistent State.

This is separate from Google sign-in. That redirect defect was fixed by #15221.

## Why this is wired to nothing

A reset is destructive and irreversible. This PR adds no UI, IPC verb, RPC method, preload surface, or existing-call-site change. `resetBrowserProfilePartition` appears only in its module and tests, so this branch is a user-visible no-op. Exposure and confirmation belong in the follow-up PR.

## What the operation does

**Rotates Electron's media-device identity before the full clear.** Electron only rotates its persisted media-device ID salt when `clearStorageData()` includes cookies, so the reset first calls `clearStorageData({ storages: ['cookies'] })`.

**Uses `clearData()` without a filter for the full reset.** Electron 43's unfiltered `clearStorageData()` clears Chromium's full StoragePartition mask, including Session Storage and Shared Storage. It still bypasses Chromium's BrowsingDataRemover, so it does not reach Trust Tokens, DIPS/BTM records, or persisted network history. `clearData()` enters BrowsingDataRemover with every real data type enabled, which covers those surfaces and delegates the ordinary partition storage clear too.

**Deletes staged import files.** `clearPendingCookieImport` removes both metadata and the staged SQLite database plus its sidecars, so startup cannot replay an old import over the reset partition.

**Clears imported-source metadata before storage.** A partial reset must not advertise an import whose data may already be gone.

**Reloads every live context in the partition after deletion or a partial-clear failure.** Contexts are enumerated from Electron's global WebContents list and filtered by Session identity. This includes popups and offscreen guests that Orca's tab registry omits, while leaving other partitions untouched. Reload runs in `finally` because a rejected browsing-data clear may already have removed some state.

**Serializes with cookie imports.** The body uses the existing per-Session mutation lock. Electron returns one Session wrapper per partition, so native imports, file imports, and resets share the same owner. The lock releases through `finally`, including when deletion rejects.

## Known gap before exposure

The import source-badge write still occurs outside the import mutation lock at three call sites, after the import function returns. A reset could land in that narrow window and then have the badge rewritten. Because this operation is unreachable here, closing that call-site transaction boundary remains a prerequisite of the exposure PR rather than a behavior regression in this one.

## Compatibility and scope

The operation is partition-generic, so default, isolated, and imported profiles take the same path. It contains no path, shell, platform, workspace, provider, IPC, RPC, or persisted-schema behavior; Windows, Linux, folder workspaces, git worktrees, SSH/offscreen guests, and mixed client/host versions therefore gain no new reachable behavior. The browser permission and auth-host changes in #15221, #15481, and #15542 are kept in memory and do not overlap this storage reset module.

## Testing

- 8 focused reset tests pass, covering media-device salt rotation, optionless full-data clearing, metadata/staged-file ordering, non-default partition forwarding, post-delete reload ordering, session-identity filtering, destroyed-context tolerance, partial-clear failure reload, lock serialization, and lock release after failure.
- The adjacent 8 cookie-import concurrency tests and 17 session-registry persistence tests pass: 33 focused tests total.
- Typecheck, focused formatting and lint, max-lines ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass. All 45 current CI checks pass; E2E is skipped because no E2E surface changed.
- Three deliberate mutations were caught: removing reload fails 2 tests; filtering `clearData` to cookies fails 1; moving the source clear after deletion fails 1.

Electron QA was run on `e2d70a23ef` and confirmed the intended result: browsing unchanged, the existing Session & Cookies control untouched, and no new reachable surface anywhere. Screenshots are in the QA comment below.



---

## Next steps — what follows this PR

This lands the engine. Nothing is plugged into it yet, and **the follow-up must ship all of the
below together**, because several items are preconditions for the others rather than a menu.

### 1. Close the transaction gap first — this is the blocker

The import writes its source badge **outside** the cookie mutation lock, at three call sites
(`browser-session-profile-ipc.ts` ×2, `orca-runtime-browser.ts` ×1), after `importCookiesFromFile`
has already released it. So a reset can complete, report success, and then have the imported badge
reappear when the in-flight import finishes.

The fix is to move that write inside the import's locked region so cookie work and source update are
one transaction. Until this lands, the reset is not race-safe — which is exactly why this PR is
wired to nothing rather than shipped with a button.

### 2. New IPC and RPC verbs, not a redefinition of the existing ones

The full reset must **not** ride `browser.profileClearDefaultCookies` or
`browser:session:clearDefaultCookies`. Mixed client/host versions are the normal state, and an older
client's trash control is gated on `profile.source`, labelled "Default cookies cleared.", and shows
**no confirmation dialog**. Redefining the existing verb would hand that client a full profile wipe
it cannot warn about.

Both boundaries need the new verb, or the local and remote paths disagree about what one name means.

### 3. Handle new client against old host explicitly

The new verb is simply absent on an older host. That must surface as "this host is too old to reset
the profile", **not** a silent fallback to cookie-only — telling a user the profile was reset when it
was not is worse than failing.

### 4. Then the user-facing surface

- **Enable the control unconditionally** — drop `disabled={!profile.source}`, which hides it from
  anyone who never imported.
- **Confirmation before the destructive call**, naming what is lost: signed-in sessions across every
  site in the profile, not just Google.
- **Surface failures** — the handler currently swallows them in a `catch` returning `false` and shows
  a success toast either way.
- **Fix the copy** — "Default cookies cleared." stops being true once it clears everything.

### 5. Fix the web client stub

`sessionClearDefaultCookies: () => Promise.resolve(false)` in `web-preload-api.ts` silently reports
failure on the web client. Whatever the new verb is, the web path needs a real implementation or an
honest unsupported state.

### Why this ordering

Shipping the button before items 1–3 would expose a destructive action that can be silently undone
by a concurrent import and that misbehaves against older hosts. A reset that reports success without
having reset is worse than no reset control at all — the current cookies-only clear already taught us
that, when "clear your profile and retry" was given as a workaround and did nothing.

records.title: fix(browser): name the requesting frame and the permission in denial notices
records.body:
<!-- orca-pr-loc -->
<!-- Programmatic LoC summary. Do not edit by hand; rewritten on every commit. -->

| | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 3 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​118 | 0 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​118 |
| Prod | 2 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​54 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​3 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​51 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

When Orca refuses a website some capability, it shows a small notice saying who asked and for what. Both halves could be wrong: it named the wrong site when the request came from an embedded frame, and it often described the capability using an internal codename instead of words.

## What Changed

Two independent defects in the same user-facing notice, both surfaced by the review of #15481 and deliberately left out of it.

**1. The notice named the wrong site.** `setPermissionRequestHandler` passed `webContents.getURL()` as the origin, which is the **top-level** document. A permission request from a cross-origin sub-frame was therefore attributed to the embedder — the user is told `https://news.example.com` asked for their location when the request actually came from an ad frame at `https://widget.example.net`.

Every `PermissionRequest` variant carries `requestingUrl` (`MediaAccessPermissionRequest`, `FilesystemPermissionRequest` and `OpenExternalPermissionRequest` all extend it), so the requesting frame is available at all three call sites. It now uses that, falling back to the top-level document only when absent.

**2. The notice showed raw Chromium permission names.** `humanizePermission` mapped exactly two permissions and returned the raw token for everything else, so users saw strings like `top-level-storage-access`, `idle-detection` and `display-capture` verbatim.

`top-level-storage-access` is the one that matters now: #15481 granted ordinary `storage-access` and deliberately left `top-level-storage-access` denied, which makes it the storage denial a user can still hit — and the only one they'd see, in its rawest possible form.

Added readable copy for the permissions users can actually reach. **The default still returns the raw token**, on purpose: inventing prose for a permission nobody has seen yet is worse than showing its real name.

## Scope

This does **not** fix Google sign-in — that was #15216, fixed by #15221. It does not change which permissions are granted or denied; the verdicts are identical before and after. It only changes what the user is told when a denial happens.

## Testing

Both halves verified red before the change; reverting both fixes fails both suites.

- **Sub-frame attribution**: a request carrying `requestingUrl: https://widget.example.net/embed` from a guest whose top-level document is `https://example.com/account` now reports the widget origin. Red before — it reported the embedder.
- **Fallback**: a request with no `requestingUrl` still reports the top-level document, rather than crashing or producing an empty origin.
- **Wording**: `top-level-storage-access` renders in words, and the notice is asserted **not** to contain the raw token.
- **Unmapped permissions** still name themselves — pins the deliberate fallback so a future refactor can't silently swallow an unknown permission into empty copy.

25/25 across both suites; typecheck clean.

records.title: fix(browser): apply the app-wide HTTP proxy to embedded browser sessions
records.body:
<!-- orca-pr-loc -->
<!-- Programmatic LoC summary. Do not edit by hand; rewritten on every commit. -->

| | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 11 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​1756 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​66 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​1690 |
| Prod | 16 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​740 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​152 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​588 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## Problem

Settings → HTTP Proxy configured Electron's `defaultSession`, but embedded Orca browser tabs navigate in dedicated `persist:orca-*` sessions. A hostname resolvable only by the configured proxy therefore worked from renderer/app traffic and failed visibly in embedded tabs, including restored and newly created profiles.

Proxy changes can also overlap. Without one per-session ordering/readiness boundary, an existing tab or a newly materialized partition can navigate while an older or incomplete `setProxy` call is still winning.

## Fix

- Apply the existing app-wide proxy policy to `defaultSession` and every app-owned browser session partition.
- Serialize proxy writes per Electron session and hold requests until the newest queued policy settles; failed or retired sessions stay fail-closed.
- Enqueue settings transitions synchronously so stale saves cannot overtake newer set/clear/reapply/bypass values.
- Await policy readiness for startup-restored and newly created browser profiles.
- Keep explicit settings above Chromium system proxy and environment fallback without changing the existing app-wide precedence policy.
- Preserve exact bypass rules and Electron's loopback exemption.
- Support credentialed proxy URLs without putting userinfo in Electron proxy rules or result metadata; credentials stay session-scoped and answer only matching proxy-auth challenges.
- Permanently retire deleted unique partitions, retaining their request and deny-by-default security policies so live pages and service workers cannot fall through to DIRECT or permissive defaults.
- Keep Electron imports out of the Node/serve runtime graph.
- Retry transient proxy-application failures with two immediate attempts and one final 100 ms delayed attempt; requests remain gated throughout and permanent failures remain bounded and fail-closed.

This does **not** change OpenCode or rate-limit behavior.

## Deterministic reproduction

The isolated rig uses a SOCKS5 proxy, a credentialed HTTP proxy, a direct loopback origin, and `proxy-only.invalid`, which resolves only inside the proxy. Orca runs with a unique user-data directory plus renderer/CDP ports and is driven through Playwright CDP.

On the baseline arm, renderer/default-session traffic returned `PROXY-OK` and produced matching proxy logs, while the same URL visibly failed in the embedded default partition, a newly created profile, and restored tabs. The revert arm reproduced that split again. The candidate makes renderer and embedded partitions converge on the same effective policy.

## Validation

The identical baseline/candidate/revert oracle covers:

- configured proxy, clear, and reapply;
- custom bypass add/remove;
- loopback staying direct;
- startup partition sweep;
- newly created profiles/partitions;
- delayed `setProxy` and concurrent settings transitions;
- credentialed proxy 407 → authenticated retry;
- deleted-partition readiness, including requests with no live `WebContents`.

The deterministic Electron proof was recorded on pre-rebase final head `41914d1913` (production proxy tree reviewed at `3ca0788963`, base `026389a3bc`): after the restart/startup partition sweep, the real embedded browser visibly rendered `PROXY-AUTH-OK` at `http://proxy-only.invalid/`; the rig logged the authenticated request and no direct origin request. The rebase onto `4065d053cf` preserved that behavior while integrating current-main document-preview session policies, as verified by range-diff, focused tests, and fresh CI.

Automated gates on the final rebased head:

- 179 focused proxy/browser/settings tests passed locally on rebased head `b68b495665`;
- `pnpm tc` and the changed-code quality gate passed on rebased head `b68b495665`; the earlier full `pnpm lint`, including localization and reliability gates, remains green for the proxy implementation;
- mutation proof: removing the delayed third attempt makes the new readiness/recovery test fail;
- original full local suite before the current-main parity correction: 62,959 passed, 13 failed, 260 skipped; the unrelated environment failures were missing @vscode/windows-process-tree and the existing 130k-pane timeout, while the deterministic export-parity expectation was corrected test-only in `41914d1913`;
- GitHub Actions run 33241519060 is fully green after retrying one infrastructure-only artifact-upload `ECONNRESET`, including Node 24 shards, typecheck, static analysis, macOS/Windows packaging, and changed-spec E2E;
- three fresh same-worktree Codex CLI reviewers using gpt-5.6-luna returned CLEAN on exact pre-rebase head `41914d1913`; range-diff and the fresh rebased validation found no proxy-semantic drift.

No mobile-facing surface, RPC/stream payload, Git/provider behavior, or persisted setting key changes. Session sweeps run only at startup and real settings transitions; identical settled configs do not repeat `setProxy`, and partitions apply in parallel.

Fixes #15342

## Visual proof

**Before** — embedded tab cannot resolve the proxy-only host:

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/827b9f0f-abfa-415f-b604-7a870edd1ed3)

**Visible Electron proof** — restored embedded tab visibly loads through the credentialed proxy after startup sweep:

![final startup partition sweep](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f9ce703-c20c-45a5-afb4-6077889ba1a9)

**Loopback** — custom bypass rules remain configured while the local origin stays direct:

![loopback stays direct](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/de97735e-d881-4d28-9dd8-7ef5f6932462)

records.title: fix(browser): grant storage-access so requestStorageAccess() stops rejecting
records.body:
<!-- orca-pr-loc -->
<!-- Programmatic LoC summary. Do not edit by hand; rewritten on every commit. -->

| | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 3 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​38 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​1 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​37 |
| Prod | 1 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​15 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​1 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​14 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

Websites sometimes have to ask the browser "may I use my own cookies and storage here?" Orca answered "no" to every site, every time, with no way for the user to say otherwise — and each refusal also burned the click the site was holding. Orca now answers yes, matching what Chrome answers under the same cookie settings.

## What Changed

- `storage-access` added to `AUTO_GRANTED_BROWSER_PERMISSIONS`, with a comment tying the grant to the conditions it depends on.
- `top-level-storage-access` deliberately left **out**, with a comment explaining why, and a test pinning the denial.
- Tests pin the grant on both the default and isolated-profile install paths, and pin that the user-visible denial notice stops firing.

## Why

`AUTO_GRANTED_BROWSER_PERMISSIONS` omitted `storage-access`, and `installBrowserSessionPartitionPolicies` denies anything not in that set. So every `document.requestStorageAccess()` in the embedded browser was refused, on every site. It was not silent: each refusal raised a user-facing notice — `https://www.google.com asked for storage-access, and Orca denied it.` — that the user had no way to act on. Worse, per the Storage Access API contract a **rejection consumes the caller's transient activation**, so Orca was also burning the user gesture the site was holding for whatever it meant to do next.

Note the shape of the bug: with **no** handler installed at all, Electron grants `storage-access` and defaults the check handler to true. Orca's deny-by-default installer had regressed this permission *below* Electron's own default.

The obvious objection is that granting it unconditionally is a privacy hole. For cookies, that objection assumes Orca blocks third-party cookies. **It does not** — nothing in `src/` blocks or partitions third-party cookies and no Chromium switch touches cookie policy, so Electron's default applies to every browser partition. This was confirmed at runtime, not just from source: a cross-site iframe read its `SameSite=None; Secure` cookie and sent it on a credentialed fetch **before** `requestStorageAccess()` was ever called, in builds both with and without this change.

Being precise about the blast radius, since it is wider than cookies alone: third-party **storage** partitioning is enabled by default and is independent of cookie policy, and the same permission lifts it for `localStorage`, IndexedDB, CacheStorage and friends when a site asks via the dictionary form, `requestStorageAccess({localStorage: true})` — Orca's handler sees only the permission name, never the call shape, so one grant covers both. So the frame does not "already have" everything this grants. It is still the right answer, because Chrome grants this same permission automatically under this same cookie policy — this is Chrome parity, not a widening past it. The comment records the conditions that would invalidate the reasoning.

### Why `top-level-storage-access` stays denied

These are not one decision. `requestStorageAccessFor()` becomes a distinct `TOP_LEVEL_STORAGE_ACCESS` request, which Chromium gates on **Related Website Sets** membership rather than on cookie policy — a permissive cookie setting never grants it there, it only ever acts as a veto. Orca has no Related Website Sets source, so granting it symmetrically would invent a permissive answer to a question the platform answers restrictively. It stays denied, deliberately and visibly, and a test pins it.

## Scope

This does **not** fix Google sign-in. That was a separate defect (#15216, fixed by #15221) where Orca cancelled its own navigations; sign-in completes end to end with this denial still in place, verified. This PR fixes an independent bug found while investigating that one.

## Testing

Unit coverage drives the **real handlers** installed by `installBrowserSessionPartitionPolicies`, not the pure predicate:

- `storage-access` granted through both the request and check handlers, on the default partition **and** on the isolated-profile path (`createProfile`), mirroring the `pointerLock` precedent — the default-partition suite does not reach that install path. Both verified red with the grant removed.
- The user-visible symptom is pinned: the denial-notification list is asserted *after* the new requests, so a regression that re-denied `storage-access` fails. Verified red pre-fix, in isolation.
- `top-level-storage-access` denied through both handlers. Green before and after **by design** — a pinning test, not evidence of this change, and not counted as such.

781/781 pass across `src/main/browser`; typecheck, oxlint and oxfmt clean.

**Empirical verification** (see QA comment below): in an isolated Orca dev instance, a genuinely cross-site iframe with a proven user gesture. Without the grant, `requestStorageAccess()` rejects with `NotAllowedError` and Orca raises its denial banner; with it, the promise resolves and no banner appears. This refutes the objection that Orca's handler is never consulted — the promise's resolution is live. It does **not** show that Chromium's cookie-unlocking plumbing is wired in Electron; that plumbing is moot here because third-party cookies already flow, which is exactly what the tripwire in the comment guards.

## Platform

The policy is pure and has no platform-specific behaviour, so macOS, Windows and Linux behave identically; the only platform branch in the permission path is macOS TCC media handling, which returns before the allow-set is consulted. Permission handlers are installed per-session in the host process and are not part of any client/host wire contract, so there is no remote or mixed-version surface.

records.title: [Feature]: User-declared custom Chromium browser for cookie import (stop one-PR-per-browser)
records.body:
## Summary

Replace the "one PR per browser" pattern for cookie import with a **user-declared custom Chromium browser** source: let a user point Orca at a browser's data directory from the picker, instead of every new Chromium fork needing a code change to `CHROMIUM_BROWSERS`.

## Problem

Each entry in `src/main/browser/browser-cookie-import.ts` `CHROMIUM_BROWSERS` differs only in ~5 strings (family, label, keychain service/account, data-dir roots). Every new fork — Comet (#1923), Helium (#6768), Aside (#15454 / PR #15452) — costs a full PR + review round, and the long tail (Vivaldi, Opera, Whale, Dia, …) is effectively unservable this way.

## Proposal

A "Add a browser…" affordance in Settings → Session & Cookies that lets the user:

1. Pick the browser's data root via a **main-owned native directory dialog** (mirroring `pickCookieFile`, so a compromised renderer can't supply arbitrary paths).
2. Infer the keychain service via the standard `<Browser> Safe Storage` convention, with a manual override field.
3. Persist entries as an optional `customBrowsers[]` in the existing `browser-session-meta.json` (additive → old files load unchanged).

`detectInstalledBrowsers()` folds these custom entries into the existing allowlist walk, so **the decryption path is reused entirely unchanged**. Cookie import stays exactly as it is today; only registration becomes user-driven.

## Explicitly NOT auto-scan

I considered scanning `~/Library/Application Support/*` for any dir with a `Local State` + cookies DB and rejected it: Electron apps (Slack, Discord, VS Code, …) share that layout, so it produces false positives and a keychain-access prompt per candidate. A user-declared entry avoids both.

## Scope / compatibility

- macOS first (same as the per-browser entries); Windows/Linux follow once a user's path resolves.
- `browserFamily` gains a `'custom'` value — additive/wire-safe like the existing families (validated as a plain string over RPC, not an enum).
- Security: new untrusted inputs are a user-chosen directory + a keychain string; mitigated by the native dialog, path confinement to the app-data root, the existing traversal guard, and passing the keychain name as argv (never shell-interpolated).

## Question for maintainers

Is this something you'd accept? I've just opened PR #15452 adding Aside via the existing pattern, and I'm happy to implement this generalization as a follow-up if you're open to it. Anything you'd want scoped differently (e.g. custom entries capped, or gated behind a setting)?

records.title: [Feature]: Add Aside browser to cookie import
records.body:
## Summary

Add support for importing cookies from **Aside** — a Chromium-based browser — alongside the existing Chrome / Edge / Arc / Brave / Comet / Helium / Firefox / Safari sources. Aside is currently reachable only via the "From File…" JSON path, not the auto-detected picker.

## Why

Users migrating from Aside to Orca have no way to bring their logged-in sessions across, forcing manual re-login on every site. This mirrors the previously accepted requests for other Chromium forks — Comet ([#1923](<https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/1923>)) and Helium ([#6768](<https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/6768>)).

## Verified on a real install (macOS, Aside 1.0.813.1)

* Data root: `~/Library/Application Support/Aside`
* Keychain: service `Aside Safe Storage`, account `Aside` (standard `<Browser> Safe Storage` convention)
* Cookies DB: `Default/Cookies` (legacy path; `resolveChromiumCookiesPath` already falls back to it)
* `Local State` `profile.info_cache` enumerates as expected

## Platform support

macOS only for now — Aside's Windows/Linux data-dir layouts are unverified, so those roots are omitted (per the lesson from stablyai/orca#14295).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Aside appears in Settings → Session & Cookies on macOS; absent on Windows/Linux with no error
- [ ] Profiles enumerate from Aside's `Local State`
- [ ] Cookies decrypt/import on macOS via the existing Chromium path
- [ ] SSH/remote path unaffected
- [ ] Tests cover the new browser family

records.title: feat(browser): add Aside as a Chromium cookie-import source
records.body:
## ELI5

Orca can copy your logged-in sessions from other browsers so you don't have to sign in again. It already knows about Chrome, Edge, Arc, Brave, Comet, Helium, Firefox, and Safari — this adds **Aside** to that list on macOS.

## What Changed

Registers Aside as a Chromium cookie-import source:

- `src/main/browser/browser-cookie-import.ts` — new `aside` entry in `CHROMIUM_BROWSERS` (macOS data root + keychain names).
- `src/shared/browser-workspace-types.ts` — `'aside'` added to the `browserFamily` union.
- `src/shared/constants.ts` — `aside: 'Aside'` in `BROWSER_FAMILY_LABELS`.
- `src/shared/browser-cookie-import-sources.ts` — Aside listed as a macOS-only picker source.
- Tests — new `browser-cookie-import.aside.test.ts` plus family/label guard updates.

Aside is Chromium-based and follows the standard conventions, so the existing macOS decryption path is reused unchanged — this is purely a browser registration. Unlike the Helium PR (#6768), no per-browser User-Agent case is needed; that synthesis was removed in #12849 (STA-3514).

## Why

Users migrating from Aside to Orca currently have no way to bring their logged-in sessions across, forcing manual re-login on every site. This mirrors the previously accepted requests for other Chromium forks — Comet (#1923) and Helium (#6768).

Verified on a real install (macOS, Aside 1.0.813.1):
- Data root: `~/Library/Application Support/Aside`
- Keychain: service `Aside Safe Storage`, account `Aside` (standard `<Browser> Safe Storage` convention)
- Cookies DB: `Default/Cookies` (legacy path; `resolveChromiumCookiesPath` already falls back to it)
- `Local State` `profile.info_cache` enumerates as expected

## Linked Issue

Fixes #15454

## Visual Proof

`N/A` — this adds a single label to the existing Session & Cookies browser-picker list (data-driven), with no layout, style, or interaction change. A live screenshot would require a packaged build on a machine with Aside installed; happy to attach one if a maintainer wants it.

## Testing

- Ran the touched suites: `browser-cookie-import.test.ts`, `browser-cookie-import.aside.test.ts`, `browser-cookie-import-sources.test.ts` — 34 tests green.
- Typechecked all three projects (`tc:node` / `tc:cli` / `tc:web`) — clean; the new `browserFamily` union member breaks no exhaustive switch.
- Changed-code quality gate (`check:code-quality:changed`) — 0 new findings.
- Verified the real Aside install's keychain service/account, data root, cookies path, and `Local State` on macOS. Did **not** run a full end-to-end import through a packaged build (no packaged run in this environment).
- Platform tested: **macOS** only (the change is macOS-only by design).

- [ ] I manually tested these changes locally (verified real-install facts + automated tests; did not run a full packaged-app import)
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below

## AI Disclosure

Claude (Anthropic), model **Claude Fable 5**, via Claude Code.

## Review

Self-reviewed for correctness, security, and cross-platform impact — see Notes below.

## Agent skill upstream boundary

- [x] Not applicable, or this change follows `docs/reference/agent-skill-sharing-upstream-boundary.md` and copies or mechanically translates no upstream skill-installer source, tests, fixtures, registry entries, path tables, comments, or documentation.

## Notes

Ensure no issues in: Security, Cross-platform support (Linux, Windows, Mac), Remote SSH, Mobile, general backwards compatibility, performance

- **Security:** no new untrusted-input path. Profile directory segments stay behind the existing `isSafeBrowserProfileDirectory` traversal guard (a new test rejects `../Outside`). Keychain service/account are static string literals — no interpolation. No SQL is constructed from any new input (SQL-injection N/A); no new renderer-reachable file reads. Decryption reuses the unchanged macOS Keychain path.
- **Cross-platform:** macOS-only by design. `winRoot`/`linuxRoot` are omitted, so `browserRootPath()` returns `null` and Aside is silently skipped on Windows/Linux (following the #14295 lesson against guessing unverified paths).
- **Remote SSH:** unaffected. Detection runs host-side; `browserFamily` crosses the client↔host boundary as a plain string (`browser-schemas.ts`, `requiredString`), not an enum, so adding `'aside'` is additive/Rule-1 safe. New client → old host fails cleanly (unknown family, no crash); new host → old client at worst shows a missing label for a persisted `'aside'` source (cosmetic).
- **Mobile:** no mobile surface touched.
- **Backwards compatibility:** additive only; no changed wire opcodes or published content.
- **Performance:** one extra allowlist entry in the detection walk; negligible.

## Checklist

- [x] This PR is small and focused
- [x] I explained what changed and why (including ELI5)
- [x] Before/after screenshots or videos attached for UI changes, or `N/A` with reason
