records.title: fix(browser): route every cookie-import write through CDP identities (STA-4300)
records.body:
<!-- orca-pr-loc -->
<!-- Programmatic LoC summary. Do not edit by hand; rewritten on every commit. -->

| | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 13 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​1417 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​50 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​1367 |
| Prod | 12 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​610 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​206 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​404 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

Some sites store a cookie that only works inside one specific parent site — a "partitioned" (CHIPS) cookie. When Orca imported cookies from Chrome, it wrote them through an Electron API that cannot express that "only inside this parent site" part, so the attribute was quietly dropped. The import said "success", the cookie was there, and the site still could not see it.

This routes every cookie-import write through CDP, which can express it. If we cannot read a cookie's partition faithfully from the source, we now skip that cookie and tell you — we never write a downgraded copy.

## What Changed

Both remaining user-data writes moved from `session.cookies.set()` to CDP `Network.setCookie`, through the identity machinery PR #14383 already built for the rollback path:

* `browser-cookie-import.ts` — `importValidatedCookies` (file / paste / Safari / Firefox) and the native Chromium import's in-memory load.
* `importValidatedCookies` no longer receives a `Session` at all. It takes a `CookieImportWriteStore`, which has no `set` on it, so the lossy write is not merely unused — it cannot be named. Same guard #14383 applied to the clear path.
* New `browser-cookie-source-partition.ts` reads partition identity **from the source**: Chromium's `top_frame_site_key` + `has_cross_site_ancestor` for the native path, and a `partitionKey` object for JSON exports.
* New `browser-cookie-import-write.ts` owns the write phase: plan → identity → write, with the skip decision in one place.
* `targetPartition` hardening: the native path's partition directory now comes from `targetSession.getStoragePath()` instead of `join(userData, 'Partitions', partitionString)`.
* Reporting: `partitionSkippedCookies` on the import summary, plus a warning toast.

The one attach change: `attachCookieClearSession` falls back to its own hidden window if it cannot lease the debugger of an existing tab.

## Why

Four P0s in this module came from one API boundary that cannot express cookie identity — STA-4013 → STA-4061 → STA-4090 → STA-4170. Each fix was correct and each spawned the next, because the lossy write stayed available. #14383 removed it from the *clear* path; this removes it from the *import* path, which is the last one that touches user data.

**Named user-visible harm for each behavior change** (nothing here changes without one):

| Change | Concrete harm it prevents |
| -- | -- |
| Route import writes through CDP | A CHIPS cookie from Chrome is imported unpartitioned. The import reports success, the cookie is in the jar, and the site cannot see its own session — the user re-authenticates with no error to explain why. Measured, see Testing. |
| Skip + report an unreadable partition | Same harm, but where we cannot even name the right partition. Guessing the ancestor bit files the cookie under a partition the site never reads, which is indistinguishable from losing it — except it looks like a clean success. |
| Read `partitionKey` from JSON exports | Chrome DevTools / Cookie-Editor exports carry `partitionKey`. The reader discarded it at parse time, so pasted exports lost CHIPS cookies the same silent way. |
| Derive the partition dir from `getStoragePath()` | `targetPartition` arrives from IPC and was pasted into a filesystem path unsanitized, so `persist:../..` resolved a `Cookies` DB outside `Partitions/` and staged a replacement over it. It also drifts if Chromium changes how a partition name maps to a directory. |
| Hidden-window fallback on debugger attach | CDP is now load-bearing for every write. Attaching to a live tab throws when DevTools already owns its debugger, so without this a user with DevTools open on that profile gets "import failed" instead of an import. |

**No `max-lines` disable was added.** `browser-cookie-import.test.ts` crossed the cap, so the new cases were split into `browser-cookie-import-partition-fidelity.test.ts` instead of suppressing it.

## Failure-mode table

Both write paths × cookie kind × outcome. **Every cell either preserves the cookie or reports it. No cell silently downgrades or silently loses a cookie.**

### Path A — validated import (`importValidatedCookies`: file, paste, Safari, Firefox)

Sources feed this path with a partition read each: JSON `partitionKey`, Firefox `moz_cookies.isPartitionedAttributeSet`, and Safari (no partition field exists in its format).

| Cookie | Write succeeds | Write rejected | CDP unavailable |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Ordinary | Written unpartitioned via `Network.setCookie`. Nothing to lose. | Run stops at the first rejection; every cookie this import wrote is removed and every replaced cookie is restored from its CDP identity; `ok:false`. | Attach throws at the snapshot (or, on an empty jar, at the first write). Nothing was written and nothing was removed; `ok:false`. Jar untouched. |
| `__Host-` | Written `hostOnly` at path `/`, which is what Chromium requires. Verified on real Electron. | As above. | As above. |
| Partitioned (CHIPS) | `partitionKey` carried to `Network.setCookie` and stored. Verified on real Electron. | As above. | As above. |
| Partitioned, source partition **unreadable** | **Skipped, never written**, and its domain is **excluded from the replace scope** so the existing session it never replaces is not erased. Counted in `partitionSkippedCookies`, logged by domain only, surfaced as a warning toast. | n/a — no write is attempted. | n/a. |
| Partitioned, unreadable, **client too old to report it** | Import **fails before the jar is touched** — no clear, no removal, no write — with a reason telling the user to update Orca. Only reachable from a remote client older than this change. | n/a. | n/a. |

`CookieImportMode` is `replace-imported-domains` at every call site, so a rejection always has the CDP restore behind it. Mutation set = restore set by construction: the removal plan and its identities are fixed together in `replaceCookiesForImportedDomains` (STA-4170's invariant), and this change does not re-read the jar anywhere.

### Path B — native Chromium import (`importCookiesFromBrowser`)

| Cookie | Write succeeds | Write rejected | CDP unavailable |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Ordinary | Written unpartitioned via `Network.setCookie`. | Counted in `memoryFailed`; the staged DB is registered so the cookie lands on the next cold start. If staging is unavailable, `restart-fallback-unavailable` warning. (Pre-existing behavior, unchanged.) | Attach throws during the clear, before any write; `ok:false` and the staging file is discarded. On an empty jar the clear does not attach, so the first write throws instead — every cookie is then counted failed and the staged replay covers them. |
| `__Host-` | Written `hostOnly` at path `/`. | As above. | As above. |
| Partitioned (CHIPS) | `partitionKey` read from `top_frame_site_key` + `has_cross_site_ancestor` and stored. Verified on real Electron. | As above. | As above. |
| Partitioned, source schema **cannot describe it** (partition site present, no ancestor column) | **Skipped everywhere.** Not written, **and not staged** — excluded from the staging DB, from `domainSet`, and from `imported`. Counted in `partitionSkippedCookies`. | n/a. | n/a. |
| Partitioned, unreadable, **client too old to report it** | Import **fails before the clear**, staging discarded, jar untouched. Only reachable from a pre-change remote client. | n/a. | n/a. |

Two cells deserve calling out as *deliberate* rather than incidental:

* **Absent `partitionKey` on a JSON cookie is read as unpartitioned, not as unreadable.** Every mainstream exporter omits the field for ordinary cookies; treating absence as unreadable would reject whole exports. Absence is a faithful read.
* **A source schema with no `top_frame_site_key` column at all is read as unpartitioned.** That schema predates cookie partitioning, so it genuinely has no partitioned rows.


### Three defects the review loop found in this PR, and their fixes

All three were introduced by the skip logic in this change, and all three are recorded here rather than quietly amended, because each is the same shape as the bug this PR is meant to end.

1. **A skipped cookie erased the session it never replaced** (validated path). `replaceCookiesForImportedDomains` received *every* importable domain, including domains whose only source cookie was skipped for an unreadable partition. So the import cleared the user's working cookies for that domain and then wrote nothing in their place — a strictly worse outcome than the downgrade this PR removes. Fixed by excluding unreadable-partition cookies from the replace scope. This is the mutation-set-wider-than-the-write-set failure STA-4170 was, in a new place.

2. **The staged cold-start replay re-introduced the downgrade** (native path). The first draft folded skipped cookies into `memoryFailed` so the staging DB would carry them, on the reasoning that staging copies the source's own partition columns verbatim. That reasoning was **wrong**: when the source schema has no `has_cross_site_ancestor` column, `buildChromiumCookieInsertParams` fills the *target's* column with the target's default, which is a guessed ancestor bit — exactly the silent misfile the write path refuses to make, arriving by the back door one restart later. Fixed by excluding unreadable rows from staging entirely, so the cookie is skipped in every channel and reported once.

3. **An older remote client would have rendered a skip as a plain success** (wire compatibility). `partitionSkippedCookies` is a new field on the import summary, and a client predating it ignores the field — so the host would skip cookies, the old client would show "Imported N cookies", and the loss would be silent again, over the wire this time. Remedied with capability negotiation: `browser.profileImportFromBrowser` takes an optional `supportsPartitionSkippedCookies: true`, current clients send it, and a host that would have to skip a cookie for a client that did **not** declare support **fails the import before touching the jar** — no clear, no removal, no write — with a reason telling the user to update Orca, rather than publishing a loss the client would render as success. The local Electron IPC path sends no flag and stays permissive, because main and renderer are always the same build. `importCookiesFromFile` has no remote RPC, so it carries no wire exposure.

Every fix is mutation-proved: reverting any one of them fails its test and only its test. I re-ran each mutation myself rather than taking the reviewer's word for it.

### Firefox source-model correction from final review

Firefox records two independent facts:

* `originAttributes.partitionKey` is dFPI / Total Cookie Protection storage isolation that Firefox imposed on an ordinary cookie. Its components can include port or ancestor context, so component count is not a CHIPS discriminator. Chromium re-derives its own third-party isolation after import; writing this cookie unpartitioned is faithful.
* `moz_cookies.isPartitionedAttributeSet` records whether the server sent `Partitioned`. That is the real CHIPS signal. Firefox records no Chromium cross-site-ancestor bit, so this identity cannot be rebuilt and the cookie must be skipped and reported.

Final readiness caught that the earlier implementation inferred CHIPS from `originAttributes` component count. That could skip ordinary dFPI cookies and silently downgrade real Firefox CHIPS cookies. Fixed in `adf4e62b32`: the importer schema-probes and selects `isPartitionedAttributeSet`, ignores `originAttributes` shape for CHIPS classification, imports flag-zero dFPI rows, and skips flag-one CHIPS rows. The regression contains both row types. `f2d8b46a08` also carries the old-client reporting capability into this Firefox path, so an older remote client fails before the target jar is read, cleared, or written.

**Safari stands as originally argued.** ITP is browser-imposed and is not recorded in `Cookies.binarycookies` at all, so there is no server-declared partition identity to drop and nothing to guess.

The one cell this change does **not** improve, stated plainly: `importValidatedCookies` still strips non-printable bytes from cookie values before writing. That is pre-existing, orthogonal to partition identity, and changing it risks turning a currently-imported cookie into a rejected one (STA-4240 territory). Left exactly as it was.

## Linked Issue

Fixes STA-4300 — https://linear.app/stably/issue/STA-4300/p1-route-all-cookie-import-writes-through-cdp-identities-ends-the

## Visual Proof

**Before/after captured end to end on real Electron (macOS): https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/14729#issuecomment-5301076955**

Driven through the real UI — Settings → Browser → Session & Cookies → Import Cookies → From File… — with a cookie JSON containing one ordinary cookie plus one CHIPS cookie whose `partitionKey` has `topLevelSite` but no `hasCrossSiteAncestor`.

* **BEFORE (`main`)** — only the success toast: "Imported 2 cookies from file into Default." The partial-partition cookie is silently downgraded and lands in the jar unpartitioned. No warning of any kind.
* **AFTER (this branch)** — the new warning toast renders alongside the success toast, and the jar contains only the readable cookie. `importedCookies: 1, partitionSkippedCookies: 1`.

Jar contents were verified on both instances, so the screenshots are backed by the actual cookie store, not just the toast text. The only automation seam was the native file-open dialog; no product code was modified to capture this.

Known cosmetic nit, deliberately left: the string reads "1 cookies" for a singular count. That matches the convention of every pre-existing toast in this module ("Imported {n} of {m} cookies", "None of the {n} cookies"), and fixing only this one string would make it the odd one out while touching four locale catalogs. Worth a separate sweep across the module's strings if wanted.

## Testing

Desktop main-process change. Not mobile, not Windows/WSL, not SSH. Tested on macOS.

**The defect was reproduced first, on real Electron, by a separate agent before any fix was written** (`3983fcd5d5`, first commit on this branch). On `main` the import returns `ok:true` with `importedCookies: 2` and no warning, while the partitioned cookie comes back through `Network.getAllCookies` with `partitionKey: null`.

Real-Electron regression tests (spawn the electron binary, write through the real import, read the jar back through CDP — `session.cookies.get()` strips `partitionKey`, so it cannot observe this either way and any test asserting through it would be vacuous):

* `browser-cookie-import-partition-success.electron.test.ts` — native path, full import end to end, CHIPS partition intact.
* `browser-cookie-import-validated-partition.electron.test.ts` — validated path, full import end to end: CHIPS and `__Host-` CHIPS both stored partitioned, ordinary cookie unchanged, unreadable partition skipped and counted.

**Mutation-proved** — each mutation was applied, the test run confirmed failing, then reverted:

| Mutation | Result |
| -- | -- |
| Drop `partitionKey` from the built identity | `partition-success.electron` fails: `expected null to deeply equal { … }` |
| Restore the over-wide replace scope | the skipped-domain replace test fails, and only that one |
| Let unreadable rows back into the staging DB | the never-stages test fails, and only that one |
| Disable the client-capability guard | the blocked-client assertions fail, and only that test |
| Stop the renderer sending `supportsPartitionSkippedCookies` | the store's RPC-params assertion fails, and only that test |
| Infer Firefox CHIPS from `originAttributes` component count instead of `isPartitionedAttributeSet` | the Firefox source-partition and fidelity tests fail |
| Make the Chromium source read always return unpartitioned | `partition-success.electron` fails, same signature |
| Make the JSON partition read return unpartitioned | `validated-partition.electron` fails |
| Downgrade a legacy partitioned row instead of skipping it | Exactly 2 tests fail — the unit test and the integration test for that cell — and only those |

**Vacuous-test trap** (this module has been bitten three times): a store mock missing `writeCookieIdentity` throws a `TypeError` the per-cookie `catch` swallows, routing every write down the rejected path while the suite still looks green. Guards against it here:

* Every new test asserts the write was **attempted** — `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(n)` and the identity argument — not just the end state.
* `browser-cookie-import.test.ts` and `browser-cookie-import-partition-fidelity.test.ts` install `unreachableCookieSet`, which **throws** if `cookies.set` is called for any user cookie. Only the `__init` probe (no user data) is allowed through. If the lossy write ever returns, those suites fail rather than pass quietly.
* Skip paths assert the store was **not** called for the skipped cookie.

Also covered: the skip log line contains only the domain, never the cookie name or value.

Commands:

```
npx vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/browser src/main/runtime/rpc/methods/browser.test src/renderer/src/store/slices/browser.test
#   -> 48 files, 734 tests
npx vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts browser-cookie-import-toast
npx tsc --noEmit -p config/tsconfig.node.json
npx tsc --noEmit -p config/tsconfig.tc.web.json
npx oxlint && node config/scripts/check-max-lines-ratchet.mjs
npm run audit:code-quality:native && npm run audit:code-quality:type-aware
npm run verify:localization-catalog && npm run verify:localization-extraction && npm run verify:localization-coverage
```

All green.

- [x] I manually tested these changes locally
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below

## Review

* **Security** — strictly reduces attack surface: `targetPartition` no longer reaches a filesystem path from a caller-supplied string. Cookie values are never logged; the skip line carries only the domain.
* **Cross-platform** — no platform-conditional code added. Path handling moved from string concatenation to Electron's own `getStoragePath()`, which is more correct on Windows, not less. The Electron fixtures use the existing `xvfb-run` wrapper on Linux.
* **Remote SSH / mobile** — `browser.profileImportFromBrowser` gains one **optional** request field, `supportsPartitionSkippedCookies: true`. Additive and back-compatible per `docs/reference/remote-wire-compatibility.md`: an old host ignores an unknown key, an old client simply omits it, and no stream opcode was added. What the host *publishes* also changed — the summary carries a new optional counter — which is precisely why the host refuses to skip a cookie for a client that has not declared it can report one.
* **Backwards compatibility** — `partitionSkippedCookies` is a new optional field on `BrowserCookieImportSummary`. Older renderers ignore it.
* **Performance** — the validated path now opens the CDP store for every import that writes a cookie, where before it opened it only in replace mode. Since every call site uses replace mode, the only newly-affected case is an import into a jar with nothing to remove, which now attaches a debugger it previously skipped. One attach per import, and the native path already did this unconditionally.

## Notes on adjacent tickets

* **STA-4183 (P3) is _not_ subsumed** — the ticket suggested it might be. It is about the *clear* path's rollback restoring a stale value for a cookie that arrived at the same coordinate mid-clear. That is a snapshot-timing problem, not an identity-fidelity one: the rollback was already CDP-backed after #14383, and nothing here changes when the snapshot is taken relative to the removal. It should stay open.
* **STA-4240 (P3) is out of scope** as specified — one rejected write still aborts the whole validated import when cookies were replaced. That contract is preserved deliberately, because it is what makes the rollback correct.

## Author

records.title: Fix Windows horizontal computer-use scroll
records.body:
## ELI5

Windows heard `left` and `right` scroll requests but sent them through the up/down mouse wheel. This change sends those requests through Windows' horizontal wheel instead.

## What Changed

- Added the Windows `MOUSEEVENTF_HWHEEL` (`0x01000`) synthetic mouse-event flag.
- Kept `up`/`down` on the existing vertical wheel path and routed `left`/`right` through the horizontal wheel.
- Added a focused source guardrail for the constant, routing, horizontal signs, synthetic dispatch, and unsupported-direction error.
- Left `WM_MOUSEHWHEEL` out because this path does not post window messages. `ConvertTo-OrcaWheelParam` is likewise not used: it packs a delta into `wParam` for `PostMessage`, while this path passes signed `dwData` directly to `mouse_event`.

## Why

Windows previously reported successful synthetic horizontal scrolling while actually moving the vertical wheel. Per Microsoft's [`MOUSEINPUT` documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/ns-winuser-mouseinput), `MOUSEEVENTF_HWHEEL` uses a positive value for right and a negative value for left, so Windows now sends `right` as positive and `left` as negative.

That native sign convention is the inverse of Core Graphics' encoding in Orca (`wheel2` positive for left and negative for right), but the caller-facing meaning is the same: `left` moves left and `right` moves right. It also matches Linux's caller semantics through AT-SPI buttons 6 and 7.

## Linked Issue

None. Found during a computer-use mouse and scroll surface audit.

## Visual Proof

N/A — this is native synthetic-input routing with no rendered UI, and the macOS host cannot execute the Windows runtime.

## Testing

- [ ] I manually tested these changes locally — Windows runtime testing was not possible on this macOS host.
- [x] Automated tests added/updated.

Passed:

- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm verify:computer-native`
- `pnpm vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts config/scripts/computer-use-windows-horizontal-scroll.test.mjs` (1 test)

`pnpm verify:computer-native` ran the macOS provider tests, Linux syntax and renderer checks, native argument guardrails, and macOS helper bundle/signature check. It skipped the Windows PowerShell parse check because `pwsh` is unavailable, as well as Windows handshake/snapshot tests and Linux provider imports on this host.

The source guardrail was mutation-verified against the real runtime. Replacing both horizontal routes with `$MouseEvents.Wheel` failed with `AssertionError: expected ... to contain '$mouseEvent = $MouseEvents.HorizontalWheel'`; restoring the implementation returned the runtime SHA-1 to `a650f3184b951942d287c02288a91e110672fcc9`, left only the intended two paths in `git status --porcelain`, and the test passed again.

## AI Disclosure

N/A — internal contributor.

## Review

The change is Windows-only and does not alter schemas, remote wire behavior, macOS/Linux input, SSH/folder-workspace behavior, mobile, security boundaries, or Git/provider behavior. The dispatch remains a constant-time synthetic input call with the existing unsupported-direction failure intact.

## Checklist

records.title: feat(computer-use): support macOS middle click and stop the silent left-click fallback
records.body:
## ELI5

`orca computer click --mouse-button middle` worked on Windows and Linux but was rejected on macOS. Worse, on macOS one specific form of the command quietly performed a **left** click and reported success. This makes middle click work on macOS and stops the silent downgrade.

## What Changed

**1. macOS middle click now works.** `MouseButtonSelection` gains a `middle` case mapped to the `otherMouse*` CGEvent family. macOS has no dedicated middle-button event type — it rides `otherMouseDown`/`otherMouseUp` with the button number carried by the `mouseButton:` constructor argument. Verified that argument is honored for exactly those types:

```
left:   type=1  buttonNumber=0
right:  type=3  buttonNumber=1
middle: type=25 buttonNumber=2
```

so no extra `mouseEventButtonNumber` write is needed.

**2. The button is validated before the accessibility fast path, and that path is skipped for buttons it cannot express.** Previously `click(params:)` read the raw string unvalidated and `performClickAction` only special-cased `right`, falling through to `AXPress` for everything else. So:

```
orca computer click --app X --element-index N --mouse-button middle
```

(no modifiers, click count 1) performed an **AXPress** — a left click — and returned `path: "accessibility"` with a success envelope. Any unrecognized button string did the same thing. Only coordinate-based or modified/multi-click middle clicks reached the validator and errored honestly.

The Windows and Linux providers already had this guard; macOS was the outlier. A source-guardrail test now pins the invariant on all three.

**3. Testability.** The button enum moves into `OrcaComputerUseMacOSCore` so it can be unit-tested — `main.swift` is an executable target with everything `private` and is not reachable from the test target. `main.swift` keeps only the CoreGraphics mapping.

**4. Docs.** `skill-guides/computer-use.md` never mentioned `--mouse-button` at all, so agents on Windows and Linux — where it already worked — had no way to discover it. Added, and `bundled-skill-guides.ts` regenerated.

No wire, schema, or capability changes: `mouseButton: z.enum(['left','right','middle'])` and the CLI/provider validators already accepted `middle` end to end. This only makes the macOS provider honor what the rest of the stack already promised.

## Why

Middle click is the one button with desktop workflows that have no keyboard substitute — closing a non-active tab, opening a background link (which fires `auxclick`, not `click`, so `Ctrl+click` is not a blanket substitute), and X11 primary-selection paste. A user asking for a middle click and silently getting a left click is worse than an error, because the agent reads `path: "accessibility"` as confirmation and moves on.

## Linked Issue

No pre-existing issue — found during a capability audit of `orca computer`'s mouse surface. The middle-click issues in the tracker (#1898, #2346, #8860, #10142) are all about the terminal/tab UI, a different subsystem.

## Visual Proof

N/A — no UI surface changes. The behavior change is in a CLI action result, shown above as the `path` value and covered by the new e2e assertion.

## Testing

Automated:
- **Swift unit** (`ActionArgumentValidationTests`): default/accept/reject cases for every button, and that only `middle` lacks an accessibility action. 75 tests pass via `swift test --package-path native/computer-use-macos`.
- **Source guardrail** (new `config/scripts/computer-use-mouse-button-routing.test.mjs`): pins the `otherMouse*` mapping, the validate-before-AX ordering, and the middle exclusion on all three platforms. **Mutation-verified non-vacuous** — reverting the gate in the real source fails the ordering test, and remapping `middle` to `leftMouseDown` fails the mapping test; source restored and checksum-confirmed.
- **CLI routing**: asserts `--mouse-button middle` reaches `computer.click` instead of being dropped.
- **Provider validation**: asserts an unknown `mouseButton` is rejected before the bridge launches.
- **Real-desktop e2e** (`computer-mac.e2e.ts`): a middle click on a TextEdit element must report `path: "synthetic"` with `fallbackReason: "actionUnsupported"` — this is exactly the assertion that fails on the old code, which reported `accessibility`.

Gates run locally on macOS: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm verify:computer-native` (exit 0 after `pnpm build:computer-macos`), and all 22 computer-use vitest files (155 tests).

Note: `tests/` is not covered by any tsconfig, so `pnpm typecheck` does not see e2e files. I typechecked `computer-mac.e2e.ts` explicitly against an extended config — clean.

Platforms actually exercised: **macOS** (built and unit/guardrail tested). Windows and Linux are unchanged by this PR; their guardrail assertions are read-only source checks. The macOS e2e runs in CI on `macos-15`; I did not run it locally because it drives real clicks and takes over the desktop session.

- [x] I manually tested these changes locally
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below

## Review

- **Security**: no new input surface; this narrows one, since an unvalidated button string previously reached the AX path.
- **Cross-platform**: macOS-only behavior change. Windows/Linux already supported middle click and already had the AX guard; the new test pins all three so they cannot drift apart again.
- **Remote SSH**: no SSH path exists for computer-use — the only remoting is WSL, which routes to the Windows provider and is untouched.
- **Mobile**: not applicable.
- **Backwards compatibility**: strictly additive. `middle` previously errored on macOS (or silently mis-clicked); no caller can be depending on either. No wire or capability change, so mixed client/host versions are unaffected.
- **Performance**: none — one enum switch on an already-existing path.

## Checklist

- [x] This PR is small and focused
- [x] I explained what changed and why (including ELI5)
- [x] Before/after screenshots or videos attached for UI changes, or `N/A` with reason
- [x] Self-reviewed for correctness, security, and performance
- [x] Cross-platform, SSH/remote, and path/shortcut impact considered (or N/A)
- [x] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` pass (or CI will cover; local preferred)

records.title: fix(browser): install anti-detection before the first guest document
records.body:
## Problem

On a cold app start, the first embedded-browser guest can commit before Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument has been registered. The first document then exposes the unmodified Electron surface even though later navigations receive the anti-detection script.

## Reproduction

1. Launch a clean dev profile.
2. Open the first browser tab directly to a page that probes the anti-detection surface.
3. Inspect the guest before any reload: navigator.webdriver is false, but chrome.csi and chrome.loadTimes are undefined.
4. Reload the same guest: chrome.csi and chrome.loadTimes are functions.

Observed on both the merge-base of PR #14685 and its HEAD, so this predates that PR. The relevant installation path currently starts Page.enable and Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument asynchronously without blocking the first navigation.

## Expected

The anti-detection script is installed before the first guest document can run page JavaScript, including on a cold app start.

## Scope

Track and fix the injection lifecycle separately from #14681 / #14685; do not couple it to the identity-signal alignment change.

records.title: refactor(browser): split browser and browser-IPC modules under the max-lines budget
records.body:
<!-- orca-pr-loc -->
<!-- Programmatic LoC summary. Do not edit by hand; rewritten on every commit. -->

| | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 6 | +16 | −11 | +5 |
| Prod | 42 | +3515 | −2929 | +586 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## What

Splits the five oversized `src/main/browser` modules and `src/main/ipc/browser.ts` into focused modules, removes their `eslint-disable max-lines` suppressions, and prunes the six corresponding entries from the `max-lines` ratchet baseline (341 → 335).

No behavior change.

## Why

Each of these six files carried a file-level `max-lines` suppression and had grown to 377–654 counted lines against a 300-line budget. Per `AGENTS.md` → "Do Not Disable Max Lines", the fix is to split, not to suppress; `config/max-lines-baseline.txt` is a shrink-only ratchet.

## How it was split

| Target | Was | Now | Extracted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ipc/browser.ts` | 654 | 181 | `browser-grab-ipc`, `browser-guest-view-ipc`, `browser-renderer-trust`, `browser-session-profile-ipc`, `browser-tab-registration-wait` |
| `browser/cdp-ws-proxy.ts` | 607 | 237 | `cdp-client-response-writer`, `cdp-debugger-channel`, `cdp-dom-focus-replay`, `cdp-page-capture-commands`, `cdp-page-navigation-commands`, `cdp-synthetic-session-registry`, `cdp-target-discovery` |
| `browser/browser-screencast-stream.ts` | 573 | 131 | `…-stream-types`, `…-debugger-command`, `…-frame-metadata`, `…-cdp-events`, `…-device-metrics`, `…-frame-pacer`, `…-snapshot-capture`, `…-viewport-fit` |
| `browser/browser-guest-ui.ts` | 529 | 157 | `browser-guest-renderer-target`, `browser-guest-context-menu`, `browser-guest-grab-shortcuts`, `browser-guest-wheel-zoom`, `browser-guest-shortcut-dispatch` |
| `browser/browser-session-registry.ts` | 489 | 295 | `browser-session-meta-store`, `browser-session-persisted-profile-validation`, `browser-session-cookie-staging`, `browser-session-partition-policies` |
| `browser/snapshot-engine.ts` | 377 | 143 | `snapshot-ax-tree-walk`, `snapshot-cursor-interactive-elements` |

`cdp-ws-proxy.ts` is decomposed into collaborating objects rather than free functions, because its state is genuinely per-connection. Every collaborator is a `private readonly` instance field built in the constructor with live closures over `this` (`() => this.client`, `() => this.port`, `() => this.stop()`), so per-connection state stays per-connection.

`browser-guest-ui.ts` was renamed to `browser-guest-shortcut-forwarding.ts`: after the split it exports exactly one function, `setupGuestShortcutForwarding`, so the old name no longer described its contents (`AGENTS.md` → "name files after what they actually contain").

No barrel exports; every new module owns real logic and importers point at the owner.

## Verification

- `npx oxlint` (whole repo) — clean
- `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet` — passes; baseline 341 → 335
- `pnpm typecheck` (node + cli + web) — clean
- `pnpm test` — full suite green; the only failures are pre-existing load-induced timeouts in files this branch does not touch, each verified passing when re-run serially
- No new runtime import cycles (type-only edges excluded — they are erased at compile time)
- Diff grepped to confirm no `eslint/oxlint-disable` directive was added anywhere
- `src/main/browser` suite: 40 files / 637 tests green, zero skips

**IPC surface proved intact.** The channel registration set was extracted from the original and from the new modules and diffed: identical sets *and* identical per-channel counts. All 23 registered handlers remain trust-gated (22 → 22 `isTrustedBrowserRenderer` call sites), and `trustedBrowserRendererWebContentsId` remains a single module singleton — the split did not fork the trust state.

**Independent adversarial review** of every file, each instructed to refute the "pure move" claim. Beyond reading, reviewers ran a multiset diff of every string/numeric literal and every comparison/logical operator (`??`, `?.`, `===`, `!==`, `&&`, `||`, …) between the original and the union of the new modules — confirming no `??` silently became `||`, no bound or error string changed.

Specific invariants confirmed rather than assumed:
- **No per-stream, per-guest, or per-connection state became module-level.** The only module-level containers in the guest split (`CONTROL_MODIFIERS`, `MAC_COMMAND_MODIFIERS`, `WHEEL_ZOOM_BLOCKING_MODIFIERS`, `recentGuestWheelZoomByGuest`) were already module-level in the original.
- **`isSnapshotStale` reads `getSeq()`, a live closure, not a captured number** — had `seq` been passed by value across the new module boundary, the initial-snapshot fallback would have raced every live frame.
- **`isClosed`/`isStopping` are live thunks**, so guards inside already-armed `setTimeout` callbacks still observe a `stop()` that happened after the timer was armed.
- **Listener pairing is identical** in membership, handler identity, and order — including that the screencast message handler is built once per stream and stored in a const, so `removeListener` still receives the same reference.
- **Frame pacer timing preserved verbatim**: the throttle disjunction, the non-sliding flush deadline, the retry re-entrancy guard, and the `ackPending = false` default (`finish()` must not ack, `stop()` must).
- **Ctrl+Tab state machine** transitions, guards, relative ordering, and the load-bearing absence of `preventDefault` on the keydown branch are unchanged.
- `configuredPartitions` moved from a `private readonly` instance field to a module-level `const`. The owning class is unexported with a single construction site, and two existing tests pin both halves of the semantics — one proves it still dedupes *within* a module instance, a later test reusing the same partition string proves state is still fresh *between* tests. Both pass.

## Pre-existing issues found and deliberately NOT changed

- `browser-guest-wheel-zoom.ts`: `consumeRecentGuestWheelZoom` returns `false` on a direction mismatch without deleting the stale WeakMap entry, so a zoom-in-then-zoom-out inside the 250 ms window leaves the old entry to expire on its own.
- `snapshot-cursor-interactive-elements.ts`: in the injected page script, the trailing `if (found.length >= 50) return` is a no-op (last statement in the function); the cap is actually enforced by the two `forEach` guards at the call sites.
- `snapshot-ax-tree-walk.ts`: `ordinal()` computes `s[(v - 20) % 10]`, which indexes negatively for `v < 20` and silently relies on the `|| s[v] || s[0]` fallback chain.
- `browser-session-cookie-staging.ts`: `clearPendingBrowserCookieImport` unlinks `stagedPath + suffix` after deleting the key, so a non-string persisted value would build a garbage path.
- `ipc/browser.ts`: `browser:acceptDownload` is `removeHandler`'d but never registered (preserved verbatim in `browser-guest-view-ipc.ts`).

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

If you had more than one passkey registered, signing in just silently did nothing. Now Orca asks which account you meant.

## What Changed

`browser-webauthn-access.ts` returned a credential only for the single-account case:

```ts
callback(details.accounts.length === 1 ? details.accounts[0].credentialId : null)
```

Its own comment said this was "until Orca has account-picker UI". This adds that UI: the offered accounts are presented, the chosen `credentialId` is returned, and `null` is returned only on genuine user cancel.

## Why

Any discoverable-credential assertion offering **two or more** accounts was cancelled with no UI and no error surface. A user with two Google identities, or one account with several registered passkeys, silently failed to sign in with no indication why.

**Explicitly out of scope:** `isUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable()` returns `false` in Orca and `true` in real Chrome — measured on the same Mac. That is an **Electron limitation** (no platform-authenticator delegate; `entitlements.mac.plist` has no `keychain-access-group`) and is not fixable here. Orca's WebAuthn surface remains HID-gated (`FIDO_HID_USAGE_PAGE = 0xf1d0`), i.e. USB security keys.

Fixes #14680

The picker dialog rendered in an Orca guest, driven directly over CDP:

![WebAuthn account picker rendered in Orca](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1b557c4a-0648-4ffe-aaed-aa67dc239c97)

A selection was driven through the preload IPC path and closed the dialog. **Not exercised:** a real multi-account assertion from a physical USB FIDO key — that needs hardware, so the dialog was driven directly instead. Stated plainly rather than implied.

records.title: fix(browser): move the Google cookie clear into Settings, behind a confirmation
records.body:
<!-- orca-pr-loc -->
<!-- Programmatic LoC summary. Do not edit by hand; rewritten on every commit. -->

| | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 13 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​960 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​14 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​946 |
| Prod | 24 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​603 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​55 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​548 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

Orca tells you "Google cookies were not imported — sign in to Google directly in Orca." If that sign-in still misbehaves, you may have stale Google cookies left over from an older Orca that did transplant them. The remedy now lives where destructive things belong: Settings → Browser, on the profile row, behind a confirmation that says exactly what it deletes. The toast just tells you where to go.

## What Changed

**1. The skipped-Google-cookies toast is informational.** No action button. New copy: *"Google cookies were not imported. Sign in to Google directly in Orca on {host}. If sign-in does not work, clear this profile's Google cookies from Settings → Browser."* It never claims the cookies came from an earlier import.

**2. "Clear Google cookies" lives on the browser profile row in Settings**, in an overflow menu, behind a destructive confirmation: *"This signs you out of Google in the {profile} browser profile on {host}. Cookies for other sites are kept."* The clear is domain-scoped to the `google.com` family and remove-only — entries are derived from cookies that already matched the family, and the store type admits only `get`/`remove`, so a `set` cannot appear on the path. It takes the same lock owner an import takes, so the two cannot interleave. Wired through IPC for local hosts and `browser.profileClearGoogleCookies` for runtime hosts.

**3. The profile-wide trash button is confirm-gated.** It calls `clearDefaultSessionCookies()`, which deletes *every* cookie in the default profile and signs you out of every site — previously one click, no confirmation, unrecoverable. It also resets the profile's import source and pending-import record, so Orca forgets which browser the cookies came from. The confirmation now names both losses: *"This deletes every cookie in the {profile} browser profile on {host}, signing you out of every site in it, including Google. Orca also forgets which browser these cookies were imported from, so you would have to import them again."* The store additionally refuses the clear outright when the selected host is neither local nor a runtime, instead of falling through to local IPC and wiping this computer's cookies.

## Why the earlier design was withdrawn

An earlier revision of this PR put a one-click "Clear Google cookies" button in the toast, shown when the source browser had skipped Google cookies **and** the destination profile held `google.com` cookies. Two reviewers blocked it, correctly: that gate cannot establish provenance.

Imports never write Google cookies — `browser-cookie-import.ts` filters source-bound Google names and then the whole non-transplantable family before anything is written. So a true probe almost always means the user's **own live session**, created by signing into Google in Orca exactly as the toast instructs. The toast was offering a one-click delete of a working session.

The design principles point the same way: a skipped-item disclosure belongs in an informational surface with a single OK and zero actions; a destructive clear belongs in a deliberate settings surface with copy naming the concrete consequence; and a destructive action hosted in a notification is only defensible when it is gated on a deterministic error code rather than an inferred signal. Decisively, provenance has to be stamped at write time, and when that marker is **absent** the non-destructive branch is the correct one. The withdrawn gate did the inverse — it read "cookies present, provenance unknown" as licence to delete. A confirmation would not have fixed that; it would only have made the user co-sign the guess.

Two commits on the old branch (`keep the recovery toast when the clear fails`, `guard the clear action against stacked confirmations`) existed only because a destructive action inside a transient toast is awkward. That scaffolding is gone rather than further patched.

**4. Two on-disk leaks fixed on the same paths.** `clearDefaultSessionCookies` and `deleteProfile` both dropped the staged cookie-import metadata pointer without unlinking the staged file — a complete SQLite copy of that profile's jar, Google rows included, left in `cookie-import-staging/` with no sweeper to reclaim it. Both now route through `clearPendingCookieImport`, which unlinks the file and its WAL/SHM. **This changes what "Clear profile cookies" and "Delete profile" remove from disk**, which is product scope beyond confirm-gating and is called out here deliberately.

**5. A cleared Google session no longer comes back at the next launch.** The staged restart-replay is a copy of the live jar keeping *only* the google.com rows, snapshotted at the start of an import and registered at the end, then copied back over the jar at startup. A clear could therefore be undone silently. Two paths now cover it: a clear strips the family from an already-registered staged DB, and registration compares a monotonic per-partition clear mark against the one taken at snapshot time. The mark is deliberately not a live-jar probe — after a clear the user's own Google tab can sign back in, so "the jar has Google cookies now" cannot distinguish *never cleared* from *cleared and repopulated*, and getting that wrong would let the replay overwrite the fresh session with the stale one.

## Notes

- `disabled={!profile.source}` is **not** restored on the trash button: keying it off import metadata is a bad proxy for "this profile has cookies" and re-breaks the case this PR set out to fix. The confirmation is the guard.
- A green test previously pinned the always-enabled trash button (`keeps the default cookie clear action enabled without import source metadata`). A passing test that pins a footgun is itself a finding; it is replaced by tests that assert the confirmation and its copy.
- The staged-replay drop reuses the existing `restart-fallback-unavailable` warning code rather than adding a sibling. A new enum value reaching an older client falls through to the generic "warning this version of Orca does not recognize" string, so it would degrade the message for every mixed-version pair to sharpen it for a rare race. The two strings that code renders are reworded cause-neutrally ("were not kept for a retry" rather than "the restart fallback was unavailable"), which is a client-side catalog change and costs nothing on the wire; the code's declaration now records that it is broader than its name. The reword also fixes a pre-existing inaccuracy in the *original* caller: on the staging-unavailable path `removeTransplantableCookies` had already cleared the jar and zero cookies then loaded, so nothing "replaced" the previous cookies — they were simply gone.
- The Google confirmation says cookies for other sites are kept "though an import still waiting for a restart may have to be run again": if the staged replay cannot be edited it is discarded whole, because keeping it would hand the cleared session back.
- The Google clear uses `cookies.remove` per cookie rather than `clearData({ origins })`. `remove` may not reach partitioned Google cookies, so the clear can under-delete — but `clearData` with `origins` and third-party matching could reach cookies partitioned *under* google.com, which would falsify "cookies for other sites are kept". Under-deleting is the correct failure direction for a destructive action.
- `browser.profileClearGoogleCookies` is a new RPC method. An older runtime host answers `method_not_found`, the renderer catches it and reports "Failed to clear Google cookies." — honest, since nothing was cleared. No stream opcode changes, so no capability negotiation is required.
- The `ProfileDelete` params schema is renamed `ProfileTarget`; it is just `{ profileId }` and is now shared by a non-delete method.

## Reviewing this diff

`git diff origin/main` is misleading on this branch — `main` advanced repeatedly while it was in review, so that command renders main's newer commits as deletions. Use:

```
git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) HEAD
```

That is the only view that told the truth, and it is what caught three unrelated files that a `git add -A` had swept in from a parallel agent working in the same repo.

## Testing

- `node config/scripts/check-changed-code-quality.mjs` — 0 new findings (native, type-aware, React Doctor)
- `pnpm run typecheck` — clean (`node_modules/.bin/tsc` verified present)
- `vitest --config config/vitest.config.ts` over the affected suites — 233 test files, 2180 tests green
- `verify:localization-catalog`, `verify:localization-extraction`, `verify:localization-coverage` — all pass
- `oxfmt --check` — clean
- Mutation-checked: dropping the decline guard, removing the menu item, restoring a toast `action:`, and widening the clear's domain filter each turn a test red.

records.title: fix(browser): align anti-detection identity signals
records.body:
## ELI5

We were telling Google's sign-in page "I'm Firefox" while handing it Chrome-only APIs, and telling sites a permission would prompt when we were going to silently deny it. Both now tell one story.

## What Changed

**1. Chrome-only globals are no longer shipped under the Firefox auth UA.** `window.chrome`, `chrome.csi()` and `chrome.loadTimes()` are gated behind `!navigator.userAgent.includes('Firefox/')`. The guards were previously **existence** checks, never UA checks, while we present a Firefox UA on `accounts.google.com` / `accounts.youtube.com`.

**2. The `chrome.runtime = {}` stub is removed.** Real Chrome reports `chrome.runtime === undefined` on an ordinary page — measured. The stub added to look *more* like Chrome made us look *less* like it.

**3. `promptPerms` narrowed to `camera` / `microphone`.** Those two genuinely resolve through macOS TCC, so `'prompt'` is honest. `geolocation`, `midi`, `idle-detection` and `storage-access` are hard-denied by `browser-session-permission-policy.ts`, so reporting `'prompt'` sent sites down a "the user will be asked" branch that ended in a silent denial.

## Why

Measured against real Chrome 151, same Mac and page:

| probe | real Chrome | Orca (before) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `window.chrome.runtime` | `undefined` | `object` |

GH #12852 reports "Email signing fails at the anti bot verification" in the in-app browser. An identity that contradicts itself across layers is exactly what those checks key on.

The permission **policy** is deliberately unchanged — whether to grant `storage-access` is a separate product decision, and this PR only stops misreporting the current policy.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #14681

## Visual Proof

N/A — no visual surface; the change is observable only via JS APIs presented to pages. Live before/after measurements are in Testing.

## Testing

- [x] I manually tested these changes locally
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below

Extended the existing `runInNewContext` harness. **Verified non-vacuous:** reverting the production change turns **6 of 8** tests red (Chrome globals under a Firefox identity, stub alignment with an ordinary Chrome page, and the four preserved denied states).

Gates: 643 browser tests pass · `pnpm typecheck` clean · `oxlint` clean · `oxfmt --check` clean.

**Not verified:** a live Cloudflare Turnstile challenge end to end. The public demo uses an always-passes dummy sitekey, so it proves nothing. Since these stubs exist for Turnstile (#885), that gap is called out rather than glossed.

## Review

Security: only removes/gates signals presented to pages; it cannot widen what a site sees. Cross-platform: pure JS in the injected script, no platform branches. No IPC, path, or shell changes.

## Checklist

- [x] Scope kept tight — permission policy untouched
- [x] No `max-lines` disable or baseline bump

The anti-detection override resolved a bare object literal (`{ state, onchange: null }`), so the `PermissionStatus` prototype was gone — no `addEventListener`, no `removeEventListener`, no `instanceof`. Any site doing `query(...).then(s => s.addEventListener('change', ...))` threw a `TypeError`.

| `permissions.query()` returns | `PermissionStatus` | plain `Object` |
| `.addEventListener` on it | `function` | **undefined** |

records.title: fix(browser): report cookies an import could not decrypt
records.body:
## ELI5

If Orca can't decrypt your browser's cookies, it used to say "Imported 0 cookies" in green, like it worked. Now it tells you what went wrong.

## What Changed

Nothing distinguished **"decryption failed"** from **"no cookies present"**. A row that would not decrypt was folded into a generic `skipped` counter, and a profile whose rows all failed returned `ok:true` with `importedCookies: 0` and no warning — reaching `toast.success`. The two situations produced opposite result shapes and the worse one reported success.

The cause is now attributed at the point of failure, while the version prefix is still in hand, and surfaced as one `cookies-undecryptable` warning carrying a reason:

- **`app-bound-encryption`** — Chrome/Edge 140+ on Windows write `v20`, which only the writing browser can unwrap. The version gate is a **format** check (`/^v\d\d$/`), so `v20` passed it and failed inside AES exactly like corruption.
- **`linux-keyring-unavailable`** — `getLinuxEncryptionKey` derived the v11 key from an **empty password** when both `secret-tool` lookups failed. It therefore never returned `null`, which made the existing "Could not access encryption key" guard **unreachable on Linux**.
- **`unknown`** — any other cause still warns rather than reporting success.

## Why

**This supersedes #13193** (@manuaudio). That PR is a correct fix for the case it targets, and this one keeps its core insight — detect the `v20` prefix and report it rather than swallowing it. It differs in four ways:

1. **Covers every cause, not one prefix.** #13193 emits its warning only when `appBoundEncrypted > 0`, so a zero-import from any other cause still reached `toast.success`.
2. **Fixes the Linux path it does not touch.** `getLinuxEncryptionKey` derived the v11 key from an empty password, so it never returned `null` and the existing "Could not access encryption key" guard was unreachable on Linux (#14181).
3. **One warning shape carrying a reason** (`cookies-undecryptable` + `reason`) rather than a cause-specific code, so a future backend reports correctly without another union member and another toast branch.
4. **Adds the non-regression that matters** — v10 "peanuts" profiles must still import when the keyring is unavailable, because that is exactly when Chrome writes them. A hard failure there would break imports that work today.

The underlying defect is the missing distinction between "decryption failed" and "no cookies present", not one prefix.

Deliberately **not** a hard failure on Linux: Chrome falls back to the "peanuts" v10 key *precisely when no keyring exists*, so returning `null` would have broken imports that work today. A regression test pins that.

## Linked Issue

Refs #13192
Refs #14181

Neither is fully closed — this makes the failure visible; it does not add v20 or portal decryption support.

## Visual Proof

All three `cookies-undecryptable` states, rendered in a real Orca guest from this branch
(`e3ffb979dc`), CDP-attached with the CDP and renderer ports both verified by `lsof`+`ps` to
belong to this worktree.

**App-bound (Windows Chrome/Edge 140+ `v20`)** — the state that previously showed a green
"Imported 0 cookies from Google Chrome."

![proof83-app-bound.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e2806635-eeab-456e-98d0-faa388f519d7)

**Mixed cause** — this is the accuracy fix review found. The named cause carries its **own exact
count** and the remainder is reported separately, instead of the total being attributed to one
cause: "cannot decrypt **214** … app-bound encryption; **2 more** could not be decrypted for
another reason."

![proof83-app-bound-mixed.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e51d6edb-beea-4902-be6d-2a69487f2f08)

**Linux keyring unavailable**

![proof83-keyring.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be2f7222-701f-4db4-bdc1-834b24c006bc)

**Method, stated plainly:** the toasts were rendered by calling this branch's own
`emitBrowserCookieImportToast` with the summary shapes the import path produces, because the
real Windows `v20` and Linux keyring code paths cannot be exercised on macOS. The copy, the
per-cause counts and the component are the shipped ones; the summary was supplied rather than
produced by a live import. The main-process logic that builds those summaries is covered by
`browser-cookie-import-undecryptable.test.ts`, whose assertions go red against the pre-fix code.

An earlier capture posted here showed only the settings page with no toast — it was taken after
the toast dismissed, and was removed rather than left as false evidence.

## Testing

- [x] I manually tested these changes locally
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below

New `src/main/browser/browser-cookie-import-undecryptable.test.ts` — three cases: v11 with keyring unavailable warns instead of empty-success; Windows `v20` warns with `app-bound-encryption`; **v10 still imports** with the keyring unavailable (the non-regression that matters).

Verified non-vacuous by reverting the production fix and confirming the tests go red.

Gates: 455 files / 4,627 tests pass · `pnpm typecheck` clean · `oxlint` clean · `oxfmt --check` clean.

## Review

Cross-platform: the Linux path is the one behaviorally changed; macOS and Windows keep their existing key resolution. No shell, path, or IPC changes. Remote/SSH unaffected — this runs in the import path on the executing host. No wire-format change.

## Checklist

records.title: fix(terminal): keep unresolved snapshot-capability verdicts re-askable
records.body:

<!-- Programmatic LoC summary. Do not edit by hand; rewritten on every commit. -->

| | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 5 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​801 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​14 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​787 |
| Prod | 4 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​183 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​25 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​158 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

Orca saves memory by unloading terminal views that have been hidden for a while. It may only unload a pane when the terminal process can be reattached **and** a replay source will survive the unmount; otherwise the user loses scrollback and the shell can be orphaned.

When Orca could not determine that replay capability, it correctly kept the pane mounted—but after about 91 seconds of failed probes it stopped asking forever. One slow daemon startup could therefore make every local terminal permanently ineligible for eviction for the rest of the app session. This change keeps the conservative safety behavior and re-asks every five minutes, allowing a recovered daemon to make those panes safely evictable.

## What changed

1. The `1/2/4/8/16/30/30s` unknown-capability ladder now decays to a bounded five-minute re-ask instead of synthesizing a permanent `false` verdict. Unknown remains eviction-exempt throughout.
2. Superseded probe generations keep their caller's timer chain alive, and closed PTYs are pruned from retry state.
3. The ongoing collector now covers tabs, pane-layout leaves, and pending reconnects just like startup refresh. Its sorted PTY-set key is memoized and JSON-encoded, so ordinary layout churn does not restart the loop and newline-bearing folder/workspace IDs cannot collide.
4. Capability changes publish a small external-store revision consumed by the terminal parking effect. A quiet hidden worktree therefore re-evaluates parking when the daemon recovers; recovery is not dependent on unrelated React/store churn.
5. The existing all-exempt force-park diagnostic now reports counts by route (`fail-open`, `foreign-worktree`, `capability-unknown`, `split-pane`) in a counts-only crash breadcrumb. No worktree IDs or filesystem paths enter the breadcrumb.

The broader `terminal_parking_pass` instrumentation was split into #14660 and is intentionally not part of this focused fix.

## Why

**This fixes a real latent defect, not a defect observed firing in the crash sweep.** The retained field snapshot from the separately investigated leak showed the exemption system idle, and this change does not explain that leak or the renderer OOM cluster. The defect here is reproduced by focused unit/React gates.

The safety invariant remains: no pane may unmount unless both process reattachment and surviving replay are known. A failed, timed-out, missing, or `null` capability answer never becomes permission to evict.

## Honest limitation

A stale cached authoritative `true` remains unchanged from `main`. If a provider later loses replay without invalidating that cached result, it remains the pre-existing route by which a pane could be unmounted without restorable scrollback. The five-minute re-ask applies only to unresolved answers and does **not** narrow that stale-true window; provider-generation/liveness invalidation is a separate follow-up.

## Scope and compatibility

- Renderer-only policy and state propagation; no RPC, stream opcode, daemon payload, or other remote-wire change.
- Shared desktop path works for native, SSH, and folder workspaces; no platform-specific path or shortcut behavior.
- Resolver-free/degraded surfaces perform at most one bounded unresolved batch per five-minute window and never gain permission to evict.
- Steady-state healthy sessions resolve once and leave the retry set. The only continuing work is the bounded slow re-ask for unresolved PTYs.
- Mobile is unaffected.

## Testing

Focused post-rebase verification:

| Gate | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| `terminal-provider-snapshot-capability.test.ts` | 16 passed |
| `terminal-provider-snapshot-capability-resettlement.test.ts` | 4 passed |
| `use-terminal-provider-snapshot-capability.test.tsx` | 9 passed |
| `terminal-retention-exempt-growth.test.ts` | 1 passed |
| `terminal-cold-park-exempt-flip.react185.test.tsx` | 1 passed |

The gates cover the full retry ladder and slow re-ask, same-array-identity timer refires, superseded generations, closed-PTY pruning, collector parity for split leaves and reconnects, newline-bearing PTY IDs, React invalidation, retention bounds after recovery, and repeated park-verdict flips without a React #185 loop. Targeted standard and type-aware lint also pass.

CI on the previous pushed head passed typecheck, package (macOS and Windows), cross-version wire compatibility, Git compatibility, shell contracts, and all 32 test shards. The sole static-analysis failure was an unused test suppression, removed in the next commit; final CI will rerun on the rebased head.

## Adversarial review

Eight loops were run to clean:

- Loop 1 found the split-leaf collector case and route classification unpinned, plus render-path collection work outside memoization; fixed and tested.
- Loop 2 found incomplete memo dependencies and a generation-cancelled pass that could kill the degraded-startup timer chain; fixed and tested.
- Loop 3 found the central same-identity re-ask mutation unpinned and a closed-PTY retry-state leak; fixed with non-vacuous gates.
- Loop 4 independently re-applied the mutations and returned clean.
- Merge-gate loop 5 found the missing React invalidation, newline-delimited key collision, non-exhaustive route switch, path-bearing diagnostic payload, and overstated stale-true claim; fixed and tested.
- Merge-gate loop 6 re-derived the final behavior and returned clean after seven focused files / 94 tests.
- Final-readiness loop 7 found a test-isolation leak: the prefetch `renderHook` stayed mounted, so a later capability publication logged a real assertion error even while Vitest reported green; fixed by explicitly unmounting the hook.
- Final-readiness loop 8 re-audited pushed head `b6cca5a26c` and returned clean with no P0/P1/P2 findings.

Open-source precedent review supports the design: detach/unmount is safe only with process persistence plus replay, unknown capability stays mounted, and recovery is retried or event-driven instead of converting transient uncertainty into a durable verdict. The bounded re-ask and explicit React invalidation are conventional, focused mechanisms.

## Visual proof

Electron QA ran through Playwright CDP on a dedicated dev instance at reviewed head `cf11b9aeba` (the final rebase adds only the lint-suppression cleanup and new base commits). The parking delay was reduced to 2 seconds for exerciseability; capability and replay behavior were production paths.

- [Visible marker before park](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/24f80f9c-b29c-4b6b-80c1-8330d056e0a4)
- [Target parked before the daemon process restart](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9817cecf-cba7-42b1-93db-228c47db9ba8)
- [Revealed after restart, marker visibly preserved in scrollback](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b41dad0a-aa5a-4342-9bdf-d0ca35358b2b)
- [Full QA report and screenshots](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/14676#issuecomment-5300877084)

The passing rendered flow was park → terminate only the dedicated profile's daemon process → daemon recovery → reveal; the marker survived and was visible after scrolling to the top. Orca's explicit `pty.management.restart()` is intentionally destructive: it synthesized session exits and retired the parked tab, so reveal was impossible and that API cannot serve as session-preserving proof.

Live visual proof of “unknown capability stays mounted” remains blocked: the context-bridged capability IPC is immutable, and the dedicated daemon auto-respawned quickly enough that new PTYs resolved authoritative before force-park. This gap is stated rather than replaced with store inspection; the safety direction is covered by the focused unit/React gates.

## Follow-ups

- Invalidate cached authoritative results on provider-generation/liveness changes, using the remote-wire compatibility process if a new daemon lifecycle signal is required.
- Continue the separate field-OOM investigation; this PR does not claim to identify its retainer.
- Broader parking-decision instrumentation remains in #14660.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused fix with regression coverage
- [x] Security/privacy, performance, cross-platform, SSH/remote, folder-workspace, and wire-compatibility reviewed
- [x] Automated tests added/updated
- [x] Final rebased focused verification and Electron evidence complete, with the live unknown-capability visual gap documented above
- [ ] Final rebased CI complete
