records.title: fix(runtime): skip unchanged worktrees when publishing mobile session snapshots
records.body:
Fixes a renderer OOM on always-on runtime hosts with paired clients.

## Defect

`buildMobileSessionTabSnapshots` rebuilt per-worktree content for **every** worktree on every publication, and consulted its per-worktree cache only *after* the content was built:

```ts
const content = { ...three Maps + group projection + full tab array... }
const cached = mobileSessionSnapshotCacheByWorktree.get(worktreeId)
if (cached && jsonContentEquals(cached.content, content)) { ... }   // too late
```

The cache suppressed fanout and one allocation. It saved none of the work. Publication is triggered by a sync key including `agentStatusByPaneKey`, so this ran on every agent-status tick.

An agent tick legitimately changes exactly **one** worktree's snapshot. Pre-fix the renderer rebuilt all 222 to discover that — **221 of 222 rebuilds were redundant**.

## Fix

Two commits, reviewable independently.

**`68a7017c36` — refactor: make inputs explicit.** Introduces `MobileSessionWorktreeInputs` (24 fields) built once per worktree and threaded through the seven per-worktree builders, replacing wholesale `AppState`. Pure refactor, no behavior change. This is the enabling step: with `AppState` out of those signatures the compiler proves the input set is complete, which is what makes the skip safe.

**`9180807746` — fix: skip unchanged worktrees.** Reference-compares those explicit inputs and skips before building any intermediates. `jsonContentEquals` retained as a backstop on the non-skipped path.

## Measured — `buildMobileSessionTabSnapshots` in isolation, N=222, 897 tabs, 54 live agent statuses

Median of 3 runs, before `922268af10` vs after `9180807746`:

| metric | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| republish, nothing changed | 11.99 / 12.42 / 15.30 ms | **1.31 / 1.75 / 2.02 ms** | **~7x faster** |
| worktrees rebuilt on one agent tick | 220 of 220 | **1 of 220** | **221 -> 1** |
| allocation per republish | 1.96 / 1.97 MB | **0.54 / 0.55 MB** | **3.6x less** |
| snapshots actually changed | 1 of 220 | 1 of 220 | **unchanged** |
| cold build | 26.9 / 29.4 / 29.9 ms | 29.5 / 31.9 / 43.0 ms | slightly worse |


> **Scope of these numbers.** The benchmark calls `buildMobileSessionTabSnapshots` directly. It does NOT run `syncRuntimeGraph`, so the 787-tab flatten, the whole-graph rebuild, and the structured clone over IPC are absent from *both* columns. These figures are publication-**content-build** cost, not end-to-end publication cost.

Output is preserved: exactly 1 of 220 snapshots differs before and after. The fix removes work, not results.

At a realistic 20-30 pub/s this path drops from **24-36%** of one core to **3.5-5.3%**. At the 16 ms coalescing ceiling (~62.5 pub/s) gross allocation drops from **~7.2 GB/min to ~2.0 GB/min**.

## Field impact

Always-on Windows runtime host, 4 paired clients. Four renderer OOMs in two days across `v1.4.163` and `v1.4.164-rc.3`. Renderer store at the OOM: `tabsByWorktree 222`, `unifiedTabsByWorktree 224`, `terminalLayoutsByTabId 787`, `agentStatusByPaneKey 54`.

Pre-crash `usedHeapMB` oscillated `3795 -> 3858` against a 4,192 MB limit — 91-92% occupancy for the final 8 minutes. That is allocation outrunning GC, not retention: ~95% of the churn is reclaimed, leaving a slow net climb that parks the heap near its ceiling, where near-continuous mark-compact on V8's GC threads converts allocation pressure into >100% of one core. The reported lag is those GC pauses.

## What this does NOT claim

- **The heap-occupancy improvement is inferred, not measured.** A node harness has a different heap limit and no comparable retained set, so any occupancy figure from it would be an artifact. Confirming it requires running the fixed build under a real workload and sampling `usedHeapMB / heapLimitMB` from the `renderer_memory` breadcrumb.
- **Not the full 106% CPU.** `pr_refresh_queue` (~100 coalesced events/min, main-process) is an independent contributor this does not touch.
- **End-to-end improvement is ~1.8x, not 7x.** The 7x is the content build in isolation. Measured end-to-end through the real `syncRuntimeGraph` with a `structuredClone`-backed IPC mock, same scale, 3 runs: **21.3 ms -> 12.0 ms**. The split after this PR is ~2 ms content build and ~4-7.5 ms structured clone of a **374-906 KB payload (see below) that is byte-identical before and after** — this PR reuses cached snapshot objects but does not shrink what gets published. So the payload, not the build, is now the bottleneck; there is almost no headroom left inside this function. At 20-30 pub/s the path goes from 43-64% of one core to 24-36%.
- **The remaining cost is the payload clone, on timing rather than allocation-rate grounds.** Two independent harnesses measured the graph payload at **374 KB** and **906 KB**; the gap is snapshot content density (the larger models `agentStatus` with a 20-entry `stateHistory` and a `lastAssistantMessage` the code notes can reach ~8 KB), and the larger is the more realistic. At the coalescer ceiling of 62.5 pub/s that is ~23-57 MB/s, i.e. **~1.4-3.4 GB/min** — *smaller* than the ~7 GB/min this PR removes from the build side, so the payload is not the larger allocation contributor. The case for the follow-up rests on the end-to-end timing instead: after this PR the clone is **4.1 ms of a ~12 ms publication**, and Electron pays it on both serialize and deserialize. A follow-up PR (#12245) withholds unchanged snapshots, cutting an unchanged republish from 374 KB / 5.08 ms to **3.4 KB / 0.02 ms**. It depends on this one — the partition is an object-identity check that only works once unchanged worktrees return reference-identical snapshots, and merging it first would silently degrade to "everything always changed". Note a graph-level equality check would NOT help: the sync-key gate at `App.tsx:1213-1241` already suppresses no-op publications, and on an agent tick the graph genuinely differs by 1 of 220.
- **Cold build regresses slightly** (~29 -> ~32 ms, once per module lifetime) from building the explicit input keys.

## Known fallback

A worktree with a mounted `TerminalPane` always rebuilds: `buildMobileTerminalSurfaceTabs` reads live `PaneManager`/DOM state that no store reference can witness. `canReuseMobileSessionSnapshot` refuses to skip when either the previous or current publication saw a registered tab for that worktree (the `previous` half covers unmount). Only a handful are mounted at real scale. The benchmark fixture registers none, so the measured post-fix figure is mildly optimistic.

## Correctness notes for review

- `agentStatusByPaneKey` **is** read inside the build loop (`buildMobileTerminalSurfaceTabs`, via a local `paneKey`), so it is a genuine per-worktree input and is bucketed through a `tabId -> worktreeId` index. A grep for the bare identifier misses this site. Skipping on it would have pinned stale agent statuses on paired clients silently.
- Absent slices previously resolved to a fresh `[]` per worktree, which would have defeated reference equality and produced a ~0% skip rate. Now shared `EMPTY_WORKTREE_*` constants.
- Two invariants relied on and commented in code, flagged for reviewer judgement: browser workspaces stored under `browserTabsByWorktree[K]` have `worktreeId === K`; and an `agentStatusByPaneKey` key rejected by `parsePaneKey` can never be looked up, since every lookup key is `makePaneKey` output.

## Tests

`sync-runtime-graph-publication-cost.test.ts` counts per-worktree work via a slice read once per worktree; `.fails` markers removed. Note that metric is satisfied by the refactor alone, so the fix commit adds tests counting `tab.title` reads, which observe content builds directly: at 300 worktrees, unchanged republish **1200 -> 0** build units, one worktree changed **1200 -> 4**. Both verified failing without the skip.

## Validation

- runtime directory: 57 files / 558 tests PASS
- 8 out-of-directory importers of this module: 775 tests PASS
- `typecheck:web`, `typecheck:node`, `oxlint` PASS

Note: the `pnpm test` wrapper cannot run in this environment (`windows-native-registry` node-gyp rebuild needs Visual Studio); `pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts` is the repo-correct direct invocation.








## Final merge-readiness review — 2026-08-03

Reviewed exact head `27d470c2ac645cbcd4cf75c087ce6b3dc771a49d`. The final independent review returned **CLEAN**. GitHub reports a clean merge state and 42 completed checks with zero failures, including Windows packaging.

### Review fix

`27d470c2` corrected the publication-cost regression so it mutates one real `agentStatusByPaneKey` entry and proves exactly one of 300 worktree snapshots changes identity. The earlier test only changed the top-level map identity and therefore did not exercise the claimed behavior. The temporary incident document was also removed from the PR.

### Statistical benchmark

Identical SHA-256-verified uncommitted harness at baseline `3658165119`, this PR `27d470c2ac`, and the combined stack through #12245 at `5081a12ac2`. Each target used three independently started, rotated rounds with 50 warmups and 150 measured samples per round: **450 measured samples per target per metric**. Values are `median / p95 [bootstrap 95% CI for median]`.

| Metric | Baseline | #12207 | Combined with #12245 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Direct snapshot build | 1.382 / 2.053 ms [1.341, 1.421] | **0.135 / 0.189 ms [0.1348, 0.1360]** | 0.138 / 0.218 ms [0.1373, 0.1399] |
| Scheduled publication, excluding the deliberate 16 ms coalescing delay | 2.913 / 3.929 ms [2.860, 2.967] | **1.581 / 1.851 ms [1.575, 1.588]** | **0.277 / 0.379 ms [0.2758, 0.2792]** |
| `structuredClone` | 1.369 / 1.873 ms [1.363, 1.381] | 1.329 / 1.436 ms [1.327, 1.332] | **0.0466 / 0.0529 ms [0.0465, 0.0468]** |
| Payload bytes | 933,388 | 933,386 | **49,631** |

This PR reduces median direct-build time **90.2%** versus baseline. The combined stack reduces median scheduled-publication time **90.5%** and payload size **94.7%** versus baseline; compared with this PR alone, #12245 reduces scheduled time **82.5%**, clone time **96.5%**, and payload **94.7%**. Its 0.003 ms direct-build bookkeeping overhead is dwarfed by the transport reduction.

Every measured iteration changed exactly one status. Baseline and this PR published all 222 snapshots; the combined stack published the changed worktree and withheld the other 221. Payload content preserved the changed status, and there were zero measured publication failures.

Raw local artifacts remain uncommitted in the dedicated benchmark worktree under `.benchmarks/mobile-session-publication/` (`report.md`, `summary.json`, `execution.json`, and `raw/*.json`). Absolute wall times should be treated cautiously because an unrelated two-day-old Node/Vite repro remained at approximately one logical CPU throughout; rotated commit order, independent processes, warmups, and confidence intervals reduce but cannot eliminate that host-load noise. The relative effects are large and consistent.

### Validation gaps and merge order

- Merge **#12207 first, then #12245**. #12245 depends on the reference identity established here.
- The saved `low spec windows` environment was unavailable: `remote_runtime_unavailable: Could not connect to the remote Orca runtime.` Windows packaging CI passed.
- `$electron`, `$perf`, and `$orca-mobile-emulator-qa` were unavailable. This is not a visual change, so no screenshots were fabricated and no prohibited OS-level UI automation was substituted.
- This PR remains a draft and was not merged.

records.title: fix(browser): bound retained webview guests across worktree switches
records.body:
## Summary

After #12137 (STA-3228), every worktree visited with browser pages kept its Electron webview guests alive for the rest of the session, so guest-process memory grew linearly with worktrees visited. This adds a retention budget: hidden worktrees keep their live browser guests for instant revisits, but only the 4 most recently activated (`BROWSER_GUEST_HIDDEN_WORKTREE_RETENTION_LIMIT`). Beyond that, the least-recently-activated worktree's guests are fully destroyed through the sanctioned cleanup path (`destroyPersistentWebview`, via the new `destroyWorktreeBrowserGuests`) and the worktree is dropped from `mountedWorktreeIdsRef`, so its overlay surface unmounts cleanly and a revisit rebuilds from persisted tab state — a fresh mount and page load, not a blank pane.

Key properties:

- LRU order = worktree activation order; re-activating a worktree refreshes its recency.
- Only worktrees that actually hold live guests count toward the budget.
- Never evicted: the active worktree; worktrees whose browser is currently visible to a remote controller (automation-visible / mobile-driven); background measure windows and targeted background mounts; Activity-portal worktrees; and worktrees with eviction-exempt terminal ptys or pending spawn work (a surface unmount would orphan live shells). These stay retained even over budget.
- Eviction destroys-then-recreates; it never detaches a live guest (the STA-3228 blank-forever state).
- Explicit close, worktree sleep, and worktree removal cleanup paths are untouched.

## Screenshots

No visual change. The only observable behavior difference is that revisiting an evicted worktree reloads its browser pages once instead of resuming instantly. This change was authored by an agent worker that did not run the packaged app; validation was via the unit suites and static gates below.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [ ] `pnpm test` — full suite left to CI (local host runs Node 26 vs the repo's pinned Node 24, a known source of false reds). Targeted + adjacent suites pass locally: the whole `browser-pane` directory (35 files / 230 tests) including the new `browser-guest-worktree-retention.test.ts` and the extended `BrowserPaneOverlayLayer.test.tsx`, `browser-page-viewport.test.ts`, `browser-webview-cleanup.test.ts`, plus `terminal-hidden-worktree-retention.test.ts`.
- [ ] `pnpm build` — not run locally; renderer-only change, CI covers packaging.
- [x] Added or updated high-quality tests that would catch regressions, or explained why tests were not needed

New/extended coverage: over-budget eviction targets the LRU worktrees only; active worktree never evicted (even when it ranks past the budget); under-budget is a no-op; non-evictable worktrees stay retained over budget; only live-guest holders count; revisit rebuilds a fresh viewport instead of reattaching the stale shell; eviction unmount resets the `hasCommittedMount` latch; `destroyWorktreeBrowserGuests` destroys every page (including legacy tab-id-keyed guests) and leaves other worktrees alone.

## AI Review Report

Authored and reviewed agentically (Claude). Main risks checked:

- **STA-3228 regression (detached-but-alive guest):** the eviction effect destroys guests via `destroyPersistentWebview` first, then removes the worktree from `mountedWorktreeIdsRef` and bumps a revision so the next render unmounts an already-empty surface. No live webview is ever detached. The revisit path was traced through `ensureBrowserPageWebview` (`created: true` → initial navigation from the store-persisted URL).
- **Terminal interplay:** dropping a worktree from `mountedWorktreeIdsRef` also unmounts its terminal surface, so eviction is vetoed for worktrees with Activity portals, targeted background mounts, active measure windows, pending spawn work, or eviction-exempt ptys (a remount would respawn and orphan those live shells). Ordinary hidden worktrees are already cold-parked/watcher-covered; eviction returns them to the fully supported "not yet visited this session" state.
- **Loop/thrash safety:** the effect runs on activation/surface-set/portal changes; the revision bump is not in its deps, and re-runs treat evicted worktrees as unretained, so it is idempotent (including StrictMode double-invoke).
- **Per-worktree state reset on eviction:** `webviewRegistry`, `registeredWebContentsIds`, page viewports, live-URL cache, and explicit zoom clear via `destroyPersistentWebview`; slot viewport roots clear via the slot's unmount ref callback; the `hasCommittedMount` latch dies with the unmounted layer; `backgroundMountTabIdsByWorktreeRef` / `activationDeferredMountTabIdsByWorktreeRef` entries are deleted alongside the mounted-set entry (mirroring the existing removed-worktree pruning).
- **Cross-platform (macOS/Linux/Windows):** no shortcuts, labels, file paths, or shell behavior touched; the logic is id-based and identical on all platforms, and applies unchanged to SSH-hosted workspaces and folder workspaces (webview guests are always local Electron processes regardless of workspace host).

Flagged during review and fixed: `recency.includes` inside a filter (React Doctor performance warning on the new lines) → Set lookup. Both CI changed-lines gates (`check-changed-code-quality.mjs`, `check-react-doctor-changed.mjs`) were run locally against the merge base and pass with 0 blocking findings.

## Security Audit

No new input handling, command execution, path handling, auth, secrets, or dependency surface. The only IPC involved is the existing sanctioned `window.api.browser.unregisterGuest` call inside `destroyPersistentWebview`, now reachable from the eviction path with the same page-id arguments explicit close already sends — no new channels or payload shapes. Eviction strictly reduces lingering guest processes and clears their registry entries, so no destroyed guest remains reachable through stale renderer state.

## Notes

- **Cherry-pick target: v1.4.165 release** — this bounds a memory regression introduced by #12137, which shipped in the RC (relevant given the chronic renderer heap growth reports on 1.4.162–164).
- The budget is defined in exactly one place, with its rationale: `BROWSER_GUEST_HIDDEN_WORKTREE_RETENTION_LIMIT = 4` in `src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane/browser-guest-worktree-retention.ts`.
- Intended behavior change: a worktree evicted from the budget reloads its browser pages on the next visit (URLs and tab structure come from the store) instead of resuming instantly.
- Follow-up candidate: worktrees protected from eviction (e.g. automation-pinned) can hold guests over budget indefinitely; if that shows up in the field, a TTL like the terminal retention budget's could be layered on top of the count bound.

records.title: fix(browser): preserve tab zoom across parent-drift webview repair
records.body:
## Summary

Fixes a regression introduced by #12137: the parent-drift webview repair (same-tab teardown/rebuild with `preserveViewport: true`) unconditionally ran `forgetExplicitBrowserPageZoomLevel`, wiping the tab's user-set zoom. Since `browser-page-zoom.ts` is the only store of explicit zoom, BrowserPane re-seeded the next mount from the Settings default — so a user's per-tab zoom silently reset after a parent-drift repair (visible after switching away from the pane and back).

`destroyPersistentWebview` now forgets explicit zoom only when `preserveViewport` is not set: a real tab close still forgets, a same-tab rebuild keeps it.

## Screenshots

No visual change (the fix prevents an unwanted zoom reset; nothing new is drawn).

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [ ] `pnpm test` — ran targeted suites instead: `pnpm vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts` on `webview-registry.test.ts`, `browser-page-zoom.test.ts`, `BrowserPane.webview-preferences.test.ts` (39 passed)
- [ ] `pnpm build` — not run (renderer-only two-file change; lint + typecheck + targeted tests cover it)
- [x] Added or updated high-quality tests that would catch regressions, or explained why tests were not needed

Two new regression tests in `webview-registry.test.ts`: one asserting explicit zoom survives a `preserveViewport: true` rebuild, one asserting a real close still forgets it. Verified the survival test fails against the pre-fix code.

## AI Review Report

Reviewed every `destroyPersistentWebview` call site: `preserveViewport: true` is passed only by the parent-drift repair in `browser-page-webview.ts`; all real close paths (`BrowserPane.tsx` tab close / onDestroyWebview, `useIpcEvents.ts` page-close events, `browser-webview-cleanup.ts` worktree shutdown) use the default and still forget zoom, so the explicit-zoom map cannot leak entries for closed tabs. The partition-mismatch rebuild path intentionally still forgets (different session). Cross-platform: the change gates deletion of renderer-local state keyed by an internal tab id — no shortcuts, labels, paths, shell behavior, or Electron platform differences involved; identical on macOS, Linux, and Windows, and unaffected by SSH or folder-workspace modes.

## Security Audit

No input handling, command execution, path handling, auth, secrets, dependency, or IPC changes. The diff only makes an existing in-renderer `Map.delete` conditional on an existing boolean option; the IPC calls in `destroyPersistentWebview` are untouched. No follow-up needed.

## Notes

- Cherry-pick target: v1.4.165 release (regression introduced by #12137 which shipped in the RC).
- Diff intentionally kept minimal to the zoom path: a concurrent change is adding a guest-retention eviction budget that also touches `webview-registry.ts` / `BrowserPane.tsx`.

records.title: fix(browser): import __Host- cookies host-only so Chromium keeps them
records.body:
## Summary

The cookie file/JSON import path (`importValidatedCookies`) passed a `domain` attribute for **every** cookie. Chromium rejects any `__Host-`-prefixed cookie that carries a Domain attribute — the `__Host-` prefix requires the cookie to be host-only, `path=/`, and `Secure`. As a result, importing a cookie file silently dropped `__Host-` session cookies (e.g. GitHub's `__Host-user_session_same_site`), so users stayed logged out after importing.

The browser-native import path already shapes `__Host-` cookies host-only; this brings the file/JSON import path to parity: when the cookie name starts with `__Host-`, omit `domain` and force `path=/`. Normal cookies are unchanged.

## Screenshots

No visual change.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint` — exit 0 (oxlint + native/type-aware code-quality audits + verify steps)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — exit 0 (all three tsconfig projects)
- [x] `pnpm test` — the changed file's suite passes 26/26. The full local suite shows failures only in unrelated, environment-sensitive files (`pty.test.ts`, `codex-accounts/runtime-home-service.test.ts`, `codex/codex-real-home-path.test.ts`, `check-root-directory-entries`, relay/daemon socket tests). These key off real `HOME`/`ORCA_*` env and local filesystem state, the failing set varies run-to-run, and none touch cookie import. They reproduce identically without this change (those files are untouched here); CI's clean environment is the authoritative gate.
- [ ] `pnpm build` — not run locally (packaging is unaffected by this logic-only change); CI covers it
- [x] Added or updated high-quality tests that would catch regressions, or explained why tests were not needed

Added a regression test that imports a `__Host-` cookie alongside a normal domain cookie in one file and asserts the `__Host-` cookie is set with no `domain` and `path=/`, while the normal cookie keeps its `.domain`.

## AI Review Report

Reviewed the diff with an AI coding agent. Main risks checked:
- **Parity with the browser-native path** — the same `__Host-` shaping already exists there; this makes the file/JSON path consistent rather than inventing new behavior.
- **Normal cookies unaffected** — only names starting with `__Host-` skip the `domain`/override `path`; the test asserts a normal cookie still receives `.github.com`.
- **Detection correctness** — `__Host-` is matched by name prefix, matching Chromium's prefix rule.

Cross-platform: this is pure main-process cookie-shaping logic with no keyboard shortcuts, UI labels, filesystem paths, shell invocation, or Electron platform-specific APIs. Behavior is identical on macOS, Linux, and Windows.

## Security Audit

Cookie import already validates each entry (`validateCookieEntry`) and strips non-printable bytes before `cookies.set`. This change only removes the `domain` attribute (and forces `path=/`) for `__Host-`-named cookies — it does not broaden what can be imported, add command/path execution, touch IPC, or expose secrets. If anything it enforces the stricter host-only scoping the `__Host-` prefix is designed to guarantee. No follow-up needed.

## Notes

`importValidatedCookies` is the shared file/JSON import path (Settings "Import Cookies from file" and JSON import entrypoints). The browser-native import path already had this handling, so no change was needed there.

records.title: feat(browser): point a Design Mode annotation at a second element or spot
records.body:
## ELI5 When leaving design feedback in Orca's built-in browser, a note could only point at one element on the page. Instructions involving two things ("move this button below the pricing table") forced you to describe the second item in words, so the agent often changed the wrong spot. The annotation box now has a crosshair picker: click another element (or an empty spot) and an @ref1 tag drops into your comment, giving the agent exact locations for every reference. ## Summary A Design Mode annotation can only describe the one element it is attached to. But most instructions in a UI review are about two things — "move this button below the plan comparison", "match the width of that card", "this overlaps the sticky header". The second target has nowhere to live, so it reaches the agent as prose while the first arrives as an exact selector, and the second one is what decides where the change actually lands. This adds a picker to the annotation composer. Point at a second target and an `@ref1` token drops in at your caret, so you keep writing around it. Picking is position-aware: a click that lands on content references that element, while a click that misses every child of its container is a **spot**, carrying its offset and ratio inside that container plus the container's size. That makes "move it here" expressible for empty space, which previously had no representation at all. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6135408f-0eb6-4e6a-95b4-c9cd0714110d ## Motivation The annotation model is single-target: `BrowserPageAnnotation` holds one `payload.target`, and `useGrabMode` clears the current payload before awaiting the next selection. So relational feedback degrades to English at exactly the point where precision matters. The prompt now resolves every token: ``` **References:** - @ref1 — p "See the critical path without maintaining a second plan" — `article > .feature p` (at 120,640 900x64) - @ref2 — empty space inside `article.feature`, not an element: 17% across and 81% down that container, at offset x=52, y=254 within its 306x314 box (page x=372, y=1180) **Feedback:** keep this div bg color same as this @ref1, also change this div @ref2 color to blue ``` A spot names its container as context while stating that the container is not the target — without that, an agent edits the container instead of placing something into it. ## Changes - New `browser-annotation-references.ts`: token construction, label derivation, append/remove with renumbering, persisted-state clamp, caret-aware insertion, and unresolved-token stripping. - Guest picker reports the click point and hit-tests it against the element's children, so a gap inside any container counts as a spot. A leaf has no children to miss, so clicking text inside a `

` still references the `

`; hover extraction reports no click and always stays an element. - `BrowserAnnotationReference` carries identity, geometry and the optional click point — no HTML, styles or screenshot per reference, since these are prompt landmarks and a second full payload each would blow the annotation budget. Capped at 4 per annotation. - `BrowserPageAnnotation.references` is optional and clamped in the store, so annotations persisted before this change load unchanged. - Composer: crosshair pick control, reference chips with remove, a dashed outline plus `@refN` badge over a referenced element, and a marker with its container outlined for a spot. - `useGrabMode` is untouched — a reference pick is the existing `rearm()` routed by the composer, so there is still one picker implementation. - i18n strings across the five locales. ## Testing - `browser-annotation-references.test.ts` (new) and additions to `browser-annotation-output.test.ts`: element-vs-spot classification including the no-click-point fallback, label truncation of page-controlled text, the reference cap and renumbering, caret-aware insertion (at caret, over a selection, padding, out-of-range caret), token removal with renumbering, unresolved-token stripping that leaves ordinary `@mentions` and newlines alone, and prompt block ordering and fencing. - `pnpm test` — 800 tests across browser-pane, main-process grab, store and shared. `pnpm typecheck` (node, web, cli) and `pnpm lint` clean, including the max-lines ratchet and localization gates. - Verified on Windows against a local page: element picks, spot picks in a grid gap and in page background, scrolling between a pick and its target, `Esc` mid-pick, chip removal, the cap, and a `position: fixed` reference staying pinned while scrolling. ## Notes - No platform-specific paths and no new keyboard shortcut. References travel the same `browser.setGrabMode` / `awaitGrabSelection` IPC as the existing grab, with no new channel, so remote and SSH-backed browser pages are unaffected. Output is provider-neutral markdown. - The child hit-test runs once per pick and is capped at 200 children; overlay rendering is bounded by the 4-reference cap and only mounts while the composer is open. - References carry no HTML or attributes. Labels come from the same page-controlled strings the composer header already escapes, length-bounded before whitespace collapsing. Capturing the click point is wrapped separately, so an element that cannot be measured still yields a normal pick. - Adjacent open work that may want ordering against this: #11360, #8687 / #8830, #9224. X: [@PraveenKum27793](https://x.com/PraveenKum27793) Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) 🐋

records.title: fix(browser): keep browser tabs rendering across worktree switches (STA-3228)
records.body:
## Summary

Fixes STA-3228: a browser tab that was open in a worktree went permanently blank after switching to another worktree and back — the URL bar still showed the address, but the page area rendered nothing, and reload silently did nothing.

Two layered defects:

1. **Trigger** — `WorktreeSplitSurface` unmounted `BrowserPaneOverlayLayer` for hidden worktrees whenever a targeted background mount restriction existed (agent wake/resume sets one constantly). Unmounting the overlay pulls the persistent `<webview>` slot divs out of the DOM, and Electron destroys the guest the moment a `<webview>` leaves the DOM — defeating the design from #6408 that renders browser panes at worktree level precisely so guests survive switches.
2. **Permanence** — `ensureBrowserPageViewport` returned the cached viewport shell even after its slot root had been unmounted, so when the worktree came back, the webview subtree was never re-appended to the live DOM. The tab stayed blank forever and the reload button threw `The WebView must be attached to the DOM and the dom-ready event emitted before this method can be called` (observed in the renderer console during repro).

Fix:

- Keep `BrowserPaneOverlayLayer` mounted for hidden worktrees. Slots already park their pane subtrees when the worktree is hidden (`shouldMountPane`), so a background-woken worktree only pays for empty slot divs. `EmulatorPaneOverlayLayer` keeps the old gating — it doesn't use the persistent-slot pattern.
- Make `ensureBrowserPageViewport` detect a replaced slot root and drop the stranded shell so the caller rebuilds against the live root. This also self-heals any remaining path that unmounts slots (cross-worktree tab moves, surface eviction): the existing parent-drift check in `ensureBrowserPageWebview` then rebuilds the webview, turning "blank forever" into "reloads once".

## Screenshots

Repro on main (tab created, worktree switched away and back — blank, reload dead):

![before: blank browser pane after worktree switch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58bdb211-6747-4a9a-ac3a-81cb607cf7e7)

Same sequence with the fix (guest survives without reloading — same in-page JS timestamp, no new HTTP request; reload button works):

![after: page still rendered after worktree switch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac9cd479-27ec-46e1-bfc8-d0a2b9fdaf79)

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint` (oxlint + react-doctor changed-lines on touched files)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm test` (browser-pane suite 32 files/191 tests; `Terminal` substring sweep 462 files/5156 tests)
- [ ] `pnpm build`
- [x] Added or updated high-quality tests that would catch regressions, or explained why tests were not needed

New tests in `browser-page-viewport.test.ts`: cached-viewport reuse under a stable root, parked viewport preserved while the root is unregistered, and rebuild under a replacement root (asserts the stale shell is detached and the rebuilt shell is connected to the new root).

Live Electron QA (dev build, CDP): reproduced the blank pane + dead reload on unfixed code, then verified with the fix that (a) slot/shell/webview stay in the DOM while the worktree is hidden, (b) the page renders after switching back with the guest's state intact (unchanged in-page timestamp, no new server request), (c) reload issues a real request, and (d) a session-restored tab renders after app restart.

## AI Review Report

Reviewed the mount-gating change for perf regressions (background wakes previously skipped the overlay): slots park pane subtrees for hidden worktrees, so no webview guests or BrowserPane chrome mount from this change alone. Reviewed the viewport self-heal for interactions with `destroyPersistentWebview` (which removes the current viewport before `resolveContainer` rebuilds it) and the floating-panel slot registration (`FloatingBrowserSlot` mints new tab ids, so no cross-host root swap for a live id). Checked the no-root case keeps returning the parked viewport so hidden-state callers see unchanged behavior. Cross-platform: renderer-only DOM/React change, no shortcuts, labels, paths, or shell behavior touched; nothing platform-conditional on macOS/Linux/Windows is affected.

## Security Audit

No input handling, command execution, path handling, auth, secrets, or dependency changes. No new IPC: the change only alters when existing renderer components mount and how a renderer-side DOM cache invalidates. Webview partitions are untouched (partition mismatch still forces a rebuild via the pre-existing check in `ensureBrowserPageWebview`).

## Notes

- The surface-eviction path (a hidden worktree fully unmounting after long parking) still destroys guests by design; with the self-heal the tab now recovers with one reload instead of dying. If we want guests to survive that too, that's a follow-up.
- `EmulatorPaneOverlayLayer` may have an analogous issue on the same conditional; left untouched to keep this PR scoped (worth a separate look).

records.title: Mirrored terminal tabs permanently lose their pane binding (ptyIdsByLeafId wiped by pending-handle snapshots)
records.body:
# Mirrored terminal tabs permanently lose their pane binding (`ptyIdsByLeafId` wiped by pending-handle snapshots)

**Version:** Orca 1.4.163, macOS (Apple Silicon), three machines connected via Remote Orca Servers (Tailscale, port 6768)

## Symptom

A tab mirroring a remote host's terminal (tab id `web-terminal-<hostTabId>`, stored under `workspaceSessionsByHostId`) suddenly renders wrong on the viewing machine: content is either cut off ("I only see half of it") or squeezed into the top of the pane with a large empty area below, the TUI input line is missing, and keystrokes are silently dropped. The session on the host is perfectly healthy the whole time.

## Root cause (from reading the bundled sources)

Mirrored tabs do not own their pane binding — it is re-derived from every incoming `session.tabs` snapshot of the host, and only surfaces with `status === 'ready'` are considered (`buildMirroredTerminalTabs`). When the host briefly publishes a surface as `pending-handle` (typical triggers: app restart on the viewer, worktree switching in the sidebar causing a session-attach storm, or the daemon-generation situation after a self-update), `applyWebSessionTabsSnapshot` writes the layout with `ptyIdsByLeafId = {}` into the viewer's store.

Three details turn this into a one-way ratchet:

1. **No downgrade protection** — a "worse" snapshot overwrites a good binding unchecked.
2. **Orphan recovery only covers *missing* surfaces** — a surface that is *present but pending* wipes the binding silently, and afterwards there are no local rebind candidates left.
3. **`setHostWorkspaceSession` persists the empty state** without the restore guard that local workspace sessions have.

Only tabs in mirrored *sub*-workspaces (`::workspace:<id>`) are affected; main-worktree tabs survive.

Because the data stream (socket subscription held by handle) is decoupled from the binding, bytes keep arriving — but the entire size negotiation path (`ptyIdsByLeafId` → `setPanePtyFitBinding` → fit override → `pty.resize`) is dead. The host PTY stays at the host-side geometry (e.g. 61×178 on a 4K display, or the 24×80 spawn default) while the viewer pane is ~40×120, so xterm paints a grid addressed for a different geometry. Input fails silently at `if (!connected || !handle) return false`. All gates bail with `return` instead of blanking the pane, so the tab looks "almost normal" — which makes this very hard for users to diagnose.

Meanwhile `orca terminal list` *on the host* still shows the correct leaf↔terminal mapping the whole time — only the viewer's store has `{}`.

Approximate offsets in app.asar (1.4.163): `buildMirroredTerminalTabs` ~79304043, snapshot apply ~79350900, orphan recovery ~79290687, RPC method table ~8125439, store schema ~1419450.

## Repro

1. Connect machine A (viewer) to machine B (host) as a remote Orca server; open a mirrored sub-workspace with an agent tab.
2. On A, switch worktrees in the sidebar a few times (or restart Orca on A) while B briefly republishes the surface — `session-attach` storm in B's daemon log, tab recreation on A.
3. Observe `terminalLayoutsByTabId["web-terminal-…"].ptyIdsByLeafId` in A's `orca-data.json` flip from a valid binding to `{}` and never recover, while B's `orca terminal list` still knows the binding.

## Suggested fixes

- Treat `pending-handle` like *missing* for the purpose of binding retention: keep the last known binding until the surface either comes back `ready` (rebind) or is confirmed gone.
- Add the restore guard to `setHostWorkspaceSession` so a degraded snapshot cannot persist over a good state.
- On reconnect/`session.tabs.listAll`, prefer the host's authoritative leaf↔terminal mapping over the locally cached empty layout.

Happy to provide store snapshots, daemon logs, or test builds — this hits a three-machine setup daily.

records.title: fix(browser): remove unsafe window close bypass
records.body:
## Summary

- Keep the guest lifecycle cleanup and early `window.close()` guard from #11910.
- Remove the CLI-only guard bypass, its synthetic preload marker, and persisted `allowWindowClose` state.
- Apply the guard uniformly to every embedded browser webview and retain focused coverage for link-created and directly created tabs.

## ELI5

The first fix installed a child lock so web pages could not accidentally destroy their little browser window inside Orca. It also gave CLI-created tabs a secret key to bypass that lock. Adversarial testing showed the key did not cleanly close the Orca tab: it killed the browser engine underneath while leaving a dead-looking tab behind. That dead tab stayed on screen but every later operation failed with `Invalid guestInstanceId`.

This PR takes away the unsafe secret key. Every embedded browser tab gets the same child lock. We keep the important part of #11910 that throws away stale pointers when a guest really dies, so the original #11763 crash remains fixed. Removing the synthetic file-URL key also removes the path mechanism that caused the Windows black screen fixed in #12038.

## Screenshots

No visual change.

## Testing

- [ ] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [ ] `pnpm test`
- [x] Electron production bundle (`pnpm exec electron-vite build --mode e2e`)
- [x] Added or updated high-quality tests that would catch regressions
- [x] 283 focused Vitest tests
- [x] 2 focused Electron E2E tests covering link-created and directly created `window.close()` attempts
- [x] Changed-code quality gate
- [x] 61 reliability-gate manifest checks
- [x] max-lines ratchet

## AI Review Report

The review split #11910 into its independent lifecycle-cleanup and close-policy layers, traced all creation/restoration paths, and tested the claimed CLI self-close behavior instead of relying on the existing replaceability test. Calling native `window.close()` on a bypassed tab resolved, destroyed its Electron guest, left the `<webview>` connected, and made the next guest call fail with `Invalid guestInstanceId`. The bypass was therefore removed while the identity-guarded forward/reverse map cleanup was retained.

Cross-platform review covered macOS, Linux, and Windows Electron preload handling and file-URL semantics. The resulting implementation has no platform-specific marker or path conversion.

## Security Audit

The renderer can no longer use a synthetic preload value to opt a guest out of the main-process close policy. `will-attach-webview` strips any renderer-requested preload and always replaces it with the standalone sandboxed guard after validating the URL and registered partition. Node integration remains disabled, context isolation and sandboxing remain enabled, and no auth, secrets, dependencies, shell commands, or external input formats changed.

## Notes

This is a targeted partial revert of #11910, not a full revert. A full revert would reintroduce #11763's stale guest pointer and main-process crash.

records.title: fix(windows): keep browser close marker URL absolute
records.body:
## Summary

- Fix the all-black Windows window introduced in `v1.4.164-rc.0` by making the synthetic browser close-policy preload marker absolute under Windows file-URL rules.
- `createMainWindow()` previously constructed the `BrowserWindow`, then threw `ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH` while converting `file:///__orca_window_close_allowed__`, before the renderer document could load.
- Add a regression test that runs `fileURLToPath()` with Windows semantics and pins the resulting absolute path.

## ELI5

The previous browser fix needed a pretend “special permission sticker” for certain browser pages. It used the fake file address `file:///__orca_window_close_allowed__` as that sticker.

Mac accepts that address as an absolute path. Windows requires a drive letter such as `C:/`, so it threw an error while reading the sticker. Orca had already created its window but had not loaded the UI yet, leaving a real but completely empty black window.

This PR makes the sticker Windows-valid (`file:///C:/__orca_window_close_allowed__`) and adds a test that reads it using Windows URL rules.

## Screenshots

No visual change.

## Testing

- [ ] `pnpm lint`
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck`
- [ ] `pnpm test`
- [ ] `pnpm build`
- [x] Added or updated high-quality tests that would catch regressions, or explained why tests were not needed

Focused validation completed:

- `pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/window/createMainWindow.test.ts src/preload/browser-window-close.test.ts src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane/BrowserPane.webview-preferences.test.ts`
- `pnpm run typecheck:node`
- `pnpm run check:code-quality:changed`
- `pnpm run check:reliability-gates`
- `pnpm run build:electron-vite`

## AI Review Report

No findings remain. The review traced startup from `BrowserWindow` construction through the close-policy marker conversion and renderer load, and verified both raw-URL and normalized-path policy comparisons. Cross-platform review confirmed the marker converts to `C:\\__orca_window_close_allowed__` under Windows rules and remains a valid absolute POSIX path on macOS/Linux; no shortcuts, labels, shell behavior, SSH routing, or workspace-path behavior changes.

## Security Audit

The synthetic URL remains a policy marker only and is removed before the guest preload can run. The change does not broaden accepted navigation origins, add command execution, alter IPC authority, process user-controlled paths, touch auth or secrets, or add dependencies. The existing fail-closed webview policy remains intact.

## Notes

The cause was confirmed from `main.trace.ndjson`: `fileURLToPath()` raised `ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH` in `getPathFromURLWin32` immediately after the RC update. This is unrelated to GPU capability; the renderer was never loaded.

records.title: feat(browser): add Aside as a Chromium cookie-import source
records.body:
## Summary

Adds **Aside** (`at.studio.AsideBrowser`) to the browser cookie-import sources, so an Orca browser profile can adopt a logged-in Aside session the same way it already can for Chrome, Edge, Arc, Brave, Comet, and Helium. It shows up as **Import Cookies → From Aside** in the browser toolbar menu and in Settings → Browser → Session & Cookies. macOS only.

Aside is Chromium-based and follows every layout convention, so detection, profile enumeration from `Local State`, and the macOS PBKDF2/AES-128-CBC decryption path all reuse the existing code unchanged. Its Keychain entry uses the usual naming (`Aside Safe Storage` / `Aside`), unlike Helium. Its cookie DB sits at the legacy `<Profile>/Cookies` path rather than `<Profile>/Network/Cookies`; `resolveChromiumCookiesPath` already falls back, so no new code was needed, but a test pins the behavior.

Every constant — bundle id, `macRoot`, Keychain service and account, cookie DB location, `v10` encrypted-value prefix — was read off a real macOS install rather than inferred from the Helium entry.

Worth noting for reviewers: Aside would have been an instance of the bug fixed in #12849. Its `Info.plist` reports the product version (`1.0.728.1`), not the Chromium version (`150.0.7871.183`), and the framework plist repeats the same value, so the old import-time UA synthesis would have presented `Chrome/1.0.728.1` for exactly the same reason Arc presented `Chrome/1.x` in STA-3514. Since #12849 deleted that synthesis, this PR needs no UA handling at all; the profile keeps the engine-derived UA like every other source.

## Screenshots

<!-- Drag the "Import Cookies → From Aside" screenshot here. -->

Settings → Browser → Session & Cookies → **Import Cookies** now lists **From Aside** alongside the other detected sources.

## Testing

Rebased onto `main` at `38bde20121` and re-run there.

- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm test` — 72572 passed. The same 4 files / 7 tests fail on a clean checkout of `main` at the rebase base, with identical counts: the three `tests/e2e/cross-version-wire/*` suites (they materialize release checkouts through `resolveCommit`) and `config/scripts/renderer-boot-graph.test.mjs`. Nothing in this change touches either area.
- [x] `pnpm build` — `build:desktop` passes. `build:native → build:computer-macos` aborts on my machine because `swift-package` cannot load `BuildServerProtocol.framework`; that is a broken local Command Line Tools install and reproduces on a clean checkout of `main`.
- [x] Added or updated high-quality tests

New `src/main/browser/browser-cookie-import.aside.test.ts` mirrors the Helium suite: detection via the legacy `Cookies` path with the `Network/Cookies` probe deliberately missing, absence when the data dir is gone, multi-profile enumeration from `info_cache`, rejection of a profile selection that escapes the browser root, and the family-label mapping. Existing suites were updated for the new family and label.

Beyond the unit tests, the change was exercised against a real local Aside install with Aside running, so the source DB had uncheckpointed WAL: `detectInstalledBrowsers()` → `importCookiesFromBrowser()` imported **3808 of 3922 cookies across 765 domains with 0 decryption failures**, all loaded in-memory with no restart needed. Every one of the 114 skipped rows is a deliberate exclusion — 5 Google integrity cookies and 109 non-transplantable-domain cookies — not a decryption or parse failure.

## AI Review Report

Reviewed with Claude Code, reading the diff adversarially rather than for confirmation.

**Cross-platform (macOS / Linux / Windows).** `winRoot` and `linuxRoot` are intentionally omitted, so `browserRootPath()` returns `null` for Aside off macOS and `detectInstalledBrowsers()` skips it — the source can never be offered on a platform whose layout is unverified. `CHROMIUM_COOKIE_IMPORT_SOURCES` marks it `mac: true, win: false, linux: false`, so the pre-detection hint text agrees. All paths go through `path.join`; no separator is assumed. No keyboard shortcuts, accelerators, or shortcut labels are touched.

**Collateral risk to existing browsers.** The only shared mutation is one more entry in `CHROMIUM_BROWSERS` (`browser-cookie-detection-types.ts`), consumed by `detectInstalledBrowsers` (guarded by an `existsSync` on the resolved root), `selectBrowserProfile` (family lookup), and the Windows key lookup (family lookup, and Aside cannot be detected on Windows in the first place). No existing browser's detection or decryption behavior changes. Appending Aside last shifts the `+N more` count in the import-hint summary, which the updated renderer test covers.

**SSH / remote / folder workspaces.** Cookie import reads the local machine's browser data directory and Keychain; that is true for every existing source and this change does not alter it. Nothing here assumes a git worktree, so folder workspaces behave identically.

**Agents, integrations, git providers.** No provider-specific or agent-specific surface is touched.

**Performance.** One extra entry in a small array walked once during detection. No hot path, no new I/O outside detection.

**UI quality.** No new components, colors, or tokens. The new source renders through the existing `Import Cookies` submenu and the existing `BROWSER_FAMILY_LABELS` mapping, so light/dark and spacing follow the current design system unchanged.

## Security Audit

**Input handling.** No new parsing or file reads are introduced. Aside's `Local State` goes through the same `discoverProfiles` JSON read as every other Chromium source, and profile directories still pass through the existing `isSafeBrowserProfileDirectory()` traversal guard. A test asserts that an Aside profile selection of `../Outside` is rejected.

**Path handling.** The only new path input is the `macRoot` string `'Aside'`, a compile-time constant joined under `~/Library/Application Support`. No user-supplied segment reaches it.

**Command execution.** None added. The Keychain lookup reuses the existing `execFileSync('security', [...])` call with a fixed argument vector and no shell; only the service and account strings differ.

**Secrets.** No cookie values, Keychain material, or derived keys are logged. The existing diagnostics log counts and paths only, and this change adds no logging.

**IPC / dependencies.** No IPC surface changed; no dependency added or bumped.

No follow-up required.

## Notes

- **macOS only, by design.** `winRoot`/`linuxRoot` are omitted because those layouts were not verified on a real install. Someone with an Aside install on Windows or Linux can add them in a follow-up; nothing here blocks that.
- **Legacy cookie path.** Aside writes `<Profile>/Cookies`, not `<Profile>/Network/Cookies`. That needed no new code because `resolveChromiumCookiesPath` already falls back, but the test pins it so a future refactor of that helper cannot silently break Aside.
- **No visual change beyond the new menu entry.**

records.title: fix(accounts): open WSL Claude sign-in in Windows browser
records.body:
## Summary

Give WSL Claude sign-in a private, temporary browser opener when the selected distro has no opener on PATH. The shim writes one atomic URL handoff into the existing temporary config directory; the main process validates and opens it through Electron. Existing distro openers keep precedence, and no renderer, IPC, preload, or mobile surface changes.

Closes #11823.

## Screenshots

No visual change. The only user-visible change is a more specific existing failure-toast message when opener preparation fails.

## Testing

Focused Vitest validation passed: the three touched bridge/service test files passed 52 tests. `pnpm run typecheck:node`, `pnpm run typecheck:web`, changed-file `oxlint`, and changed-file `oxfmt --check` passed.

Post-fix WSL opener validation passed: the focused bridge suite passed 17 tests, including cleanup-failure handling.

Real Windows + WSL2 and browser-owner checks remain unrun in this environment.

## AI Review Report

Native host login, existing WSL openers, credential capture, persistence, rollback, IPC, preload, renderer, web, RPC, mobile, SSH, remote, macOS, Linux, and performance surfaces remain unchanged. The fallback is scoped to interactive WSL Claude account login and reauthentication.

## Security Audit

The handoff uses one bounded read, atomically claims and deletes the request before validation, accepts only exact HTTPS hosts `claude.com`, `platform.claude.com`, `console.anthropic.com`, and `anthropic.com`, and rejects userinfo, fragments, ports, localhost, suffix lookalikes, and arbitrary hosts. The shim uses a quoted heredoc, an atomic same-filesystem rename, mode 0700, and no stdin or output. PATH injection is limited to the interactive WSL login command.

records.title: fix(browser): scope JavaScript dialogs to their page
records.body:
## Summary

- Replace Electron's app-global native `alert` / `confirm` / `prompt` sheets for managed browser guests with an overlay rendered inside the originating browser page.
- Keep Chromium's blocking dialog callback intact, including prompt text, while routing open/close state through the page's existing renderer ownership mapping.
- Preserve automation: `orca dialog accept|dismiss --page ... --worktree ...` now resolves an already-pending scoped dialog directly, with the existing agent-browser path retained as fallback.
- Clean up pending dialogs on CDP resolution, navigation cancellation, guest replacement, and teardown.

## Screenshots

The page is dimmed only inside its browser viewport; Orca's worktree and browser chrome remain usable.

![Worktree-scoped browser alert](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dgk-dev/orca/pr-assets-dialog-scope/docs/pr-assets/worktree-scoped-browser-dialog.png)

Manual QA also switched to a sibling terminal/browser surface while the alert was pending: the overlay disappeared with its originating page and returned when that page was selected again. CLI acceptance completed in 148 ms without starting an agent-browser process, and the page observed the accepted result.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [ ] `pnpm test`
- [x] `pnpm build`
- [x] Added or updated high-quality tests that would catch regressions, or explained why tests were not needed

Focused validation on current `origin/main`:

- 189 dialog/controller/BrowserManager/IPC/renderer tests passed.
- Node and web typechecks passed.
- Changed files passed oxlint and oxfmt checks.

The full local suite was also exercised. It reached 41,919 passing tests but retained 6 failures in pre-existing PTY/shell-ready suites under a scrubbed test environment; none overlap this change. Re-running the PTY suite against the PR candidate passed all 400 tests, while one existing live-zsh non-ASCII-path case remained environment-sensitive. The dialog-focused suites are green.

## AI Review Report

Reviewed the complete main/preload/renderer path and the pinned Electron 43.1.0 implementation. The review specifically checked:

- preservation of Chromium's blocking callback and prompt value semantics;
- stale dialog IDs, page ownership, renderer hydration races, guest swaps, teardown, and CDP-driven closure;
- the existing CLI/AI accept-dismiss flow, including the startup deadlock that occurs if agent-browser is launched behind an already-blocking dialog;
- accessibility labels, keyboard acceptance/dismissal, bounded long content, localization, and inactive-page behavior.

The review flagged that the initial CLI fallback could block during agent-browser session startup. The implementation now attempts the pending BrowserManager dialog first and keeps agent-browser only as the fallback; regression tests cover both paths.

Cross-platform review covered macOS, Linux, and Windows. The overlay has no platform-specific paths, shell behavior, or modifier labels. Enter/Escape behavior is platform-neutral. The only Electron-specific dependency is the internal `-run-dialog` event used by the project's pinned Electron version; tests cover listener replacement, restoration, cancellation, and callback behavior.

## Security Audit

- No dependency, auth, secret, filesystem, path, or command-execution changes.
- Dialog IPC is limited to the trusted browser renderer and verifies page ownership before reading or responding.
- Responses include a per-dialog UUID so stale renderer actions cannot answer a newer dialog.
- Page-controlled message/default text and renderer-supplied prompt text are length-bounded; React renders text without HTML injection, and displayed origins use the existing safe origin parser.
- Teardown dismisses pending callbacks and restores Electron's original listener, avoiding a stranded blocked renderer.

No security follow-up is required.

## Notes

Electron does not expose a public JavaScript-dialog interception API. This uses its internal `-run-dialog` contract, which is explicitly typed by Electron and verified against the pinned runtime. If Electron changes that internal contract during a future upgrade, the controller tests should fail before release.

records.title: fix(browser): prevent window.close guest crashes
records.body:
## Summary

- Guard ordinary embedded browser guests against `window.close()` during document creation and after `dom-ready`.
- Clear both forward and reverse guest/tab registrations when a guest is destroyed.
- Preserve explicit CLI-created tab self-close behavior and add Electron regression coverage for the `target=_blank` flow.

## ELI5

An embedded browser tab is like a small browser window inside Orca. A link-created tab ran `window.close()`, and although the close was supposed to be blocked, Orca kept a pointer to the guest after Chromium had destroyed it. Clicking another tab made Orca use that dead pointer and crash. The fix blocks `window.close()` early for normal embedded tabs and removes stale pointers when guests are destroyed. CLI-created tabs intentionally keep their existing self-close behavior.

Fixes #11763

## Validation

- 268 targeted Vitest tests passed.
- Workspace-schema tests passed.
- `pnpm run typecheck` passed.
- `pnpm exec electron-vite build --mode e2e` passed.
- `SKIP_BUILD=1 pnpm exec playwright test tests/e2e/browser-tab.spec.ts --config tests/playwright.config.ts --project electron-headless --workers=1 --grep 'blocked window.close'` passed.
- Changed-file native/type-aware lint passed.

Full lint still reports two unrelated pre-existing duplicate-import warnings in `tests/tools/benchmarks/terminal-cold-park-resource-bench.mjs` and `tests/tools/benchmarks/terminal-cold-park-reveal-bench.mjs`.

records.title: fix(terminal): make snapshot capability lookup async
records.body:
## Summary

- Replaces render-time `sendSync` PTY snapshot-capability IPC with async `invoke`.
- Prefetches restored primary and split-pane PTY capability before cold activation unlocks, preserving daemon tab deferral.
- Makes healthy SSH capability definitive `false`, preventing repeated unknown retries.
- Fails open to eager mounting after one second if capability discovery is unavailable.

No visual change.

### Before / after benchmark

| 1.5s injected main stall | Synchronous baseline | Async candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Max renderer interval gap | 1465.1ms | 71.6ms worst of 3 |
| Max API call return duration | 1464.2ms | 0.2ms worst of 3 |
| Capability calls completed by renderer loop | 4 | 32 each run |

The same Electron oracle was red on the synchronous implementation and green on the final candidate in 3/3 runs.

## Screenshots

No visual change.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [ ] `pnpm test` — focused suites run instead: 9 files, 667 tests passed
- [x] `pnpm exec electron-vite build --mode e2e`
- [x] Added or updated high-quality regression tests
- [x] Main-stall Electron benchmark, 3/3 passed
- [x] Production daemon cold-activation restore E2E passed
- [x] Docker SSH renderer reload and full app restart restore E2Es passed
- [x] Reliability gate manifest passed

## AI Review Report

Reviewed the renderer-to-preload-to-main capability path, provider ownership, startup ordering, stale async responses, retry fanout, and cold restoration. The first async candidate exposed a regression that eagerly mounted all eight cold daemon tabs; the final implementation now prefetches persisted primary and split-pane identities before readiness and the production cold-activation oracle passes again.

Cross-platform review covered macOS, Linux, and Windows plus local daemon, SSH, paired web, git worktree, and folder-workspace state shapes. This PR adds no shortcut, label, filesystem path, shell, native module, or OS-specific behavior. Docker SSH validates the Linux relay/provider route; Windows desktop remains a stated reliability-gate coverage gap.

## Security Audit

No new command execution, filesystem mutation, auth flow, secret handling, dependency, or network surface. The IPC handler retains input type checks, deduplication, and a 512-ID bound. Async results are generation-fenced, and an unresponsive request fails open after one second without issuing later batches.

## Notes

This is defensive hardening against renderer coupling to any main-process stall. It is not claimed as the confirmed root cause of the reported production hard freeze, and it is intentionally separate from #11836.

records.title: [P1] fix(mobile): restore folder session tab snapshots
records.body:
## Summary

Restore usable Orca Mobile session tabs for folder workspaces while keeping every persisted session and PTY bound to the local, SSH, or relay host that owns it.

This head fixes the post-restart input failure found during native acceptance. Previously, reconnect could restore the folder tab and scrollback and report the terminal as ready, but typed input disappeared because the restarted runtime had discovered the surviving PTY without attaching to it. Activating the restored tab now reattaches its persisted session once for the current runtime generation before input is accepted.

Follow-up review found two concurrency problems in that recovery path. First, concurrent mobile or paired renderer/mobile activation could issue duplicate local reattachments or SSH `pty.attach` calls. Second, after those duplicate calls were coalesced, whichever caller entered first also decided whether the shared operation activated the host tab. A navigation-only caller entering just before a host-focus caller performed one successful reattach but could leave the prior host tab active.

The shared operation now owns only physical reattachment. After it completes, every caller rechecks its own folder mutation and SSH reconnect generation, then applies its own client navigation or host/headless activation intent. This closes the backend/session-entry blocker documented in #11751 and complements #11767 and #11647 without merging or broadening them.

## Before and after

Before, restored PTY inventory was treated as writable ownership, so input could fail after restart. The first attachment fix corrected that, and the first concurrency follow-up ensured concurrent callers shared one exact-surface reattach. However, the shared promise still captured the first caller's host-navigation flag. If phone-local navigation reserved the operation before a concurrent host-focus request, the host-focus waiter only updated client projections and `activeTabId` stayed on the prior tab.

After, exact-surface callers still share one local, direct-SSH, or relay reattach, but the shared materialization is navigation-neutral. Each waiter revalidates its own deletion/recreation and reconnect fences before it can publish navigation or activate the restored headless tab. Navigation-first and host-first calls both end on the requested host tab, stale callers cannot publish or focus, and paired renderer/mobile restoration still avoids focusing a renderer that has not adopted the runtime-owned tab.

## What changed

- Recover folder terminal tabs from persisted workspace sessions when an attached renderer omits the folder snapshot, including ordinary local terminals and runtime-owned SSH/serve terminals.
- Reattach inventory-restored runtime-owned terminals before returning a writable activation after runtime restart or reconnect.

## Latest fresh exact-head review fixes

A fresh review of `a9b9dfbe99b7b809a5e2435a6270fafa17a3173e` found two remaining P1 PTY ownership bugs.

### Host-aware reservation paths

Before, any workspace path beginning with two slashes looked like a Windows UNC path to the reservation key. On a POSIX or SSH filesystem, distinct paths such as `//Server/Share` and `//server/share` could therefore be lowercased to the same key and share one PTY.

After, the reservation uses the path rules of the host that actually runs the PTY. Native Windows, WSL, and known Windows SSH/relay hosts still fold equivalent drive and UNC spellings. Linux, macOS, known POSIX remotes, and unknown remotes keep leading-double-slash paths and Unicode spellings byte-for-byte distinct. Raw worktree IDs and their `worktree:` form still meet when they identify the same surface, and paired renderer/mobile callers still share one provider operation.

### Creator-only retirement before stale checks

Before, the runtime checked the workspace-inventory fence immediately after provider spawn, before installing creator-only cleanup. An adopted relay result that omitted the unrelated `isReattach` flag could be mistaken for a new PTY and shut down, while a genuinely new local result could leave its terminal handle, pending registration, or early-exit fence behind.

After, an idempotent retirement token is created immediately when the provider returns. The provider's claim disposition decides ownership: only a result proven newly created may be shut down or have its binding, lease, provider state, and ownership removed. Adopted, reattached, reused, and coalesced-waiter results are never retired. Runtime admission state is cleared exactly once, cleanup failures cannot replace the original error or block later rollback steps, all reservation waiters receive that original error, and retry starts with a clear reservation.

## Final fresh-review follow-up

A fresh same-model/xhigh complete review of the reviewed head `b7f31677c81bc988089e3cb8eb82e993ec58779f` found two remaining concurrency races in the restored-terminal path.

### Shared PTY reservation retirement

Before, the caller that physically created a coalesced PTY kept unconditional cleanup authority. If that creator became stale or its renderer was destroyed while the provider was still pending, it could kill the PTY after a live runtime or renderer waiter had already received the shared result.

After, creator and waiter calls receive independent one-use retirement claims only when a fresh spawn is shared. An abandoning caller releases its claim; the PTY is retired only after every participant abandons it, while the first live adopter cancels retirement for all peers. Creator-only cleanup remains unchanged, adopted/reattached results are never retired, and provider exit plus rejection/retry paths clear reservation state.

### Fresh materialization coalescing

Before, the shared materialization key did not include the folder-routing fence or SSH reconnect generation captured by the caller. A current activation could therefore join an older promise and inherit its obsolete rejection after reconnect or a folder host/path mutation.

After, materialization identity includes the captured folder-routing fingerprint and reconnect generation in addition to the existing host/workspace/session/tab/leaf surface. Same-freshness callers still perform one physical attachment, while a current caller starts one independent retry instead of inheriting a stale promise; the stale caller remains fenced from publication and host focus.

## Renderer creator/runtime waiter ownership follow-up

### Before and after

Before, a full runtime `createTerminal` request could become the waiter behind a renderer-created PTY after it had already prepared a fresh terminal handle and Claude Agent Teams launch identity. When the shared reservation resolved, the runtime waiter treated the creator result as its own spawn, rebound the live PTY to the waiter handle, replaced creator title/launch metadata, and leaked the unused waiter team; pre-spawn and post-await inventory or disconnect rejection could leak the same provisional team.

After, `createTerminal` checks both rejection fences while its team remains provisional, removes that team by its exact team ID/token, and branches on `spawnDisposition: awaited` before registration or publication. A live waiter adopts the already-registered creator handle, workspace, pane, title, launch metadata, and execution-host metadata without rewriting them; stale waiters release only their reservation claim, caller-supplied session identities are not cleared, and changed folder routes remain isolated from the old reservation.

records.body:
**Operating system:** macOS (Darwin 25.5.0, Apple Silicon - Mac Studio, M1 Max, 32 GB) **Orca version:** v1.4.162 (first observed on v1.4.161; retested and reproduced on v1.4.162) ### Short summary The whole Orca app crashes (main-process SIGSEGV, `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` / `KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS` at near-null addresses) when a page in the embedded browser calls `window.close()` in a tab that was opened by clicking an `http://` link in the chat pane, and the user then clicks another tab in the tab strip. The close attempt is (correctly) blocked, but the app appears to retain a dangling reference that the next tab-strip interaction dereferences. ### Reproduction steps 1. Serve this single file on localhost: ```html Orca window.close repro

This page calls window.close() 300ms after load.

Attempting close…

``` 2. In an agent chat, render a markdown link to that page and click it - Orca opens it in a new embedded browser tab. `window.close()` is blocked and the page stays visible. 3. Click another tab in the embedded browser's tab strip. 4. Orca crashes - the entire app, all worktrees. Reproduced five times today (four on 1.4.161 during normal use of our own web app, once on 1.4.162 with the minimal repro above). Notably, tabs created programmatically via `orca tab create --url ...` ARE allowed to self-close via `window.close()` and do not crash - the difference in close policy between CLI-created and link-click-opened tabs seems to be where the bad state originates. ### Crash evidence Five `.ips` reports, all `procName: Orca` (main process, not a renderer helper), SIGSEGV at near-null fault addresses: | Report (local) | Version | Fault address | Top frame | |---|---|---|---| | Orca-2026-07-31-115813 | 1.4.161 | 0x60 | `_v8_internal_Node_Print` (Electron Framework) | | Orca-2026-07-31-121459 | 1.4.161 | 0x10 | `_v8_internal_Node_Print` | | Orca-2026-07-31-121601 | 1.4.161 | 0x60 | `_v8_internal_Node_Print` | | Orca-2026-07-31-121708 | 1.4.161 | 0x18 | `v8::Isolate::InstallConditionalFeatures` | | Orca-2026-07-31-122552 | 1.4.162 | 0x10 | `_v8_internal_Node_Print` | Happy to attach the full `.ips` files on request. ### Impact Any web page calling `window.close()` - an ordinary thing for pages to do - can bring down the entire app when opened via a chat link.
