records.title: fix(browser): stop agent browser input from stealing the user's focus
records.body:
## The problem

While an agent drives the built-in browser, its keystrokes land in whatever the user is typing into.

CDP input only reaches an Electron `<webview>` guest while that guest holds native DOM focus. Without it Chromium routes the event to whichever surface actually has focus — the user's terminal — and the CDP call still resolves `ok`, so the agent never learns its input went somewhere else. It retries, and the user's prompt fills with fragments of the agent's typing.

The same root cause shows up as focus theft: `mousePressed` moves focus onto the guest and nothing gives it back, so the user's cursor silently jumps out of the terminal they were working in.

## Why main can't fix it

`webContents.focus()` is a no-op for a `<webview>` guest — the guest is a DOM element owned by the host renderer, so only the renderer can focus it. Confirmed by measurement: text reached the page only when a human physically clicked into it. `Page.bringToFront`, `tab switch --focus`, and bringing the app to the foreground all failed to make input land.

## The fix

Route the focus handoff through the host renderer.

```
main (cdp-ws-proxy)                renderer (BrowserPane)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
input command detected
  → 'begin' + guestId ───────────→ save document.activeElement
                                    focusWebviewNow()
  ← granted / refused ───────────  did the guest actually take focus?
  forward CDP input ─────────────→ guest holds focus → input lands
  → 'end' ───────────────────────→ restore the saved element
```

Main cannot see whether the guest took focus — only the pane hosting it can — so the pane answers the borrow and main acts on the answer:

- **granted** → forward the input.
- **refused** → fail the command. A guest can refuse focus while staying perfectly alive: a hidden or detached pane still answers CDP, so forwarding would put the keystroke back in whatever the user is typing into. Failing is what lets the agent learn its input did not land, instead of getting the `ok` that hid this bug in the first place.
- **silence** → fail it too. The host renderer accepted the announcement, so no answer means no pane is holding this guest — it is mounting, unmounting, or being swapped out — and none of those can take focus. The wait is bounded at 250 ms, which is slack for a busy renderer rather than an expected pause; a mounted pane answers immediately and never reaches it.

Only a guest with **no host renderer at all** — offscreen, headless — skips the borrow and forwards straight through, exactly as it did before this handoff existed.

Scope is deliberately narrow:

- `Input.insertText` / `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` always borrow — key events reach nothing without focus.
- `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` borrows only for `mousePressed`. Moves, wheels and releases never take focus, so borrowing for them would create the very focus hop this prevents.
- `Runtime.evaluate`, screenshots, and read-only traffic are untouched.

The renderer listener is intentionally **not** gated on the pane being active. Agents drive background tabs while the user works elsewhere — that is exactly when the leak happened. Panes filter by guest `webContents` id so only the addressed one reacts.

Also included: `orca tab create` never sent `activate`, even though `TabCreate` documents *"User-initiated opens focus the tab; agent/automation opens stay background."* Every agent-created tab surfaced the browser pane and took focus. It now mirrors `tab switch` — `--focus` is opt-in.

## How this was verified

Measured per command by focusing a probe input in the page, firing the command, then reading the field back. A command is "leaking" when the field stays empty and the text appears in the user's terminal instead.

| Command | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `inserttext` / `type` / `keypress` | leaked into the user's terminal | lands in the page |
| `mouse down` / `up`, `click` | stole focus, never returned | focus returns to the user |
| `tab create` | surfaced the pane, took focus | stays in the background |
| `eval`, `screenshot`, `mouse move` | already fine | unchanged |
| `snapshot`, `set device`, `goto`, `tab switch`, `tab close` | already fine | unchanged |

Every command an agent session had actually issued was measured, not just the suspected ones — the innocent ones were confirmed innocent so the fix could stay minimal.

Reproduced in the failing configuration — browser as a **background** tab while the user typed in a floating terminal — before and after. Focus stayed with the user and the input reached the page.

The refused-focus case is covered by tests rather than by hand: it needs a guest that stays alive while its pane cannot hold focus, which the suites drive directly through the borrow reply.

## No visual change

This changes focus behavior only. No UI is added, removed, or restyled, so there are no screenshots to attach.

## Tests

`cdp-ws-proxy` suites updated and extended: the mock now carries a host renderer that answers borrows the way a mounted pane does, and the input paths assert the borrow is announced (`ui:browserAgentInput` / `begin`) instead of the old native `webContents.focus()`.

`cdp-ws-proxy-focus-borrow.test.ts` covers what main does with each answer — forwards on a grant, fails the command on a refusal (key events and `Input.insertText` both), fails on silence, and skips the ask entirely when the guest has no host renderer. `browser-focus.test.ts` covers the pane side: a failed focus is reported as such, and still unwinds its borrow so later restores are not swallowed.

980 tests pass across `src/main/browser`, `src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane` and `src/cli/browser.test.ts`, on top of the current `main`.

## Code review summary

- **Cross-platform** — No platform branches. `hostWebContents`, `send`, and DOM focus are Electron/DOM APIs available on macOS, Linux, and Windows. Verified on macOS; the logic contains nothing OS-specific.
- **SSH / remote / local** — Remote panes stream a viewport instead of hosting a local `<webview>`, so they never take this path; the web preload API gets a no-op stub for both directions. Offscreen/headless guests have no host renderer, so they skip the borrow entirely rather than waiting on an answer that cannot come.
- **Agents / integrations** — Only the agent-browser CDP path is affected. No agent, git provider, or integration-specific behavior is touched.
- **Performance** — Input now waits for the pane's answer instead of a fixed frame, so the common path got *faster*: the old 16 ms per key event and per mouse press is gone. A guest whose pane never answers pays the 250 ms bound before failing, and one with no host renderer pays nothing. Wait-polling and read-only probes (`Runtime.evaluate`, screenshots, mouse moves) are untouched.
- **UI quality** — No visual change. Focus visibly returns to where the user left it rather than parking on the browser pane.
- **Security** — The IPC carries a phase string, a numeric guest id and a numeric borrow id outbound, and a borrow id plus a boolean inbound. No new privilege, no page content, no user data crosses the boundary.

## Testing notes

- Verified on macOS with a local worktree and the desktop `<webview>` path.
- Remote/SSH and headless paths are covered by construction (stub + skipped borrow) but were not exercised on real remote hosts.
- Rebased onto current `main` (`54a9b58`). `browser-pane/` was refactored substantially in the meantime; there were no textual conflicts and the suites above pass on top of it.

records.title: fix(browser): recover embedded guests after lifecycle loss
records.body:
## Summary

Builds on the host-retention fix merged in #12137 and closes the remaining embedded-browser lifecycle gap: when tab chrome/model survives but its Electron guest is crashed, detached, or missing from the runtime registry, Orca now converges to a live registered guest or a truthful retryable error surface instead of a permanent blank viewport.

- Repairs healthy guests with missing registry ownership in place, preserving live DOM and unsaved page state.
- Reloads crashed renderers in place, preserving `webContents` identity while requiring a new renderer process and repainted DOM.
- Uses bounded guest replacement only as the final fallback, preserving URL/history, profile/partition, zoom, and the replacement viewport without duplicate guests or reload loops.
- Bounds replacement handoff at 8 seconds; a stalled teardown becomes a retryable error, and Retry starts a fresh replacement instead of waiting forever.
- Covers system resume, renderer reload/hydration, hidden tabs, parked worktrees, local `file://` pages, registry disagreement, redirects, and explicit recovery failure/retry.

## Relationship to #12137 / STA-3228

#12137 fixed the worktree-switch trigger by retaining browser overlay hosts and repairing stranded viewport shells. It merged while this combined candidate was being prepared, so this PR is rebased on that fix rather than duplicating it. This is the single remaining follow-up: it handles guest/process/registry loss after the host survives and adds an integrated worktree-retention + guest-recovery oracle.

## Deterministic reproduction

The byte-identical Electron oracle (SHA-256 `5f8272e96a7041d42db14de57744d939006a9d7cbb9c8b5aecc3e8eaa2d5329d`) force-crashes a real local `file://` guest while keeping tab chrome/model alive, then checks two independent signal groups:

1. guest DOM paint plus URL/form state;
2. runtime registry membership plus `webContents` and renderer-process identity.

- Current `main` `cd68a8b00c`: **fails** after 10 seconds because chrome survives but the guest DOM never repaints.
- Candidate `4958840738`: **passes** with the same `webContents` ID, a new renderer PID, restored DOM paint, and a live registry entry.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] 13 focused Vitest files: 417/417 passed
- [x] Full local Vitest sweep: 4,076 files and 43,548 tests passed; two relay tests pass with Codex-injected `GIT_CONFIG_*` variables removed, and three root-directory guard tests require Bash associative arrays unavailable in macOS Bash 3.2
- [x] Fresh Electron E2E build and recovery suite: 6/6 passed, repeated twice after the final integration fix
- [x] Headed minimize/restore: 1/1 passed with painted pixels and registry identity
- [x] Forced-headed combined worktree-switch/park/crash/recovery oracle: 1/1 passed

## AI Review Report

Fresh independent correctness/security, adversarial architecture, and performance/resource reviewers ended **CLEAN** on the final patch. Review covered parent-drift replacement, unregister/re-register ordering, bounded retries, duplicate-guest prevention, URL/history/profile/partition/zoom preservation, focus, multiple tabs/workspaces, local versus remote panes, resume scaling, listener/timer cleanup, and viewport/webContents retention.

The final rebase integrated newer main browser-retention and zoom work. Conflict resolution preserved explicit `preserveZoom` behavior plus guest-budget eviction and connected-root replacement coverage, and updated the parent-drift and async-destroy test contracts.

## Security Audit

The repair IPC accepts only trusted Orca renderers, validates argument shapes, resolves an existing live Electron `webview`, and requires its `hostWebContents` to be the invoking renderer before reattaching policies and registering the exact `webContents` ID. No command execution, dependency, credential, secret, or new path-interpretation surface is added.

## Gaps / risks

- Actual macOS sleep was not automated because it could sever the shared development session; minimize/restore, resume delivery, renderer loss, and worktree parking are covered separately.
- No native-Windows validation claim; CI provides Windows packaging/type/test coverage once this head runs remotely.
- GPU/compositor-only blanking with a healthy renderer and healthy registry is outside this deterministic failure oracle.
- Remote/paired browser pages use a separate lifecycle and are intentionally unchanged.

records.title: [Bug]: Closing all terminals clears center panel file browser; must re-open workspace to browse files
records.body:
### Operating system

_Unknown_

### Orca version

_Unknown_

### Details

**Short summary:** Closing all terminals/agent windows in a workspace clears the center panel file browser even though the workspace is still selected. The UI shows "Select a workspace to browse files", and the user must re-click the workspace and open a terminal before they can browse files or use Git.

### What happened?

The user closed every terminal or agent window in the current workspace. They still considered themselves in that workspace (nothing else was open), but the center panel already showed the empty state **"Select a workspace to browse files"**.

To browse files or use Git again, they had to click the workspace again and open a terminal — which is inconvenient when they only want to browse files (no terminal needed).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a workspace in Orca (with terminal and/or agent windows).
2. Ensure the center panel can browse files / show Git for that workspace.
3. Close all terminals and agent windows in that workspace.
4. Observe the center panel empty state: "Select a workspace to browse files".
5. Try to browse files or use Git without opening a new terminal.

### Expected behavior

- Closing terminals/agent windows should not deselect the active workspace for file browsing / Git.
- As long as a workspace remains selected/active, the center panel should keep offering file tree, editor, and Git for that workspace — even with zero open terminals.

### Actual behavior

- After the last terminal/agent window is closed, the center panel switches to "Select a workspace to browse files".
- The user must re-select the workspace and open a terminal before browsing files or using Git.

### Additional context

User report:

> There might be an interaction issue that could be improved. When I close all the terminal or agent windows in the current workspace, theoretically I am still in the current workspace but with nothing open. However, the center panel already displays "Select a workspace to browse files" at that time. I need to click on the workspace again to open a terminal in order to browse files or use Git. This can be inconvenient if all one wants to do is simply browse files.

![User report](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/5052cf925675e949c399878d5739a7cb07f71654/image-e92327de-af58-4226-85a0-8c309b78f487.png?raw=true)

**Likely area:** workspace selection / panel empty-state logic treating "no open panes/terminals" as "no active workspace", instead of preserving the selected workspace for file browser + Git.

records.title: fix(browser): clear grab mode operation queue on teardown
records.body:
Follow-up to review feedback on #11661 (already merged).

## Problem

`grabModeOperationByPageId` holds the pending promise chain that serializes grab mode operations per browser page. Two teardown paths cleared `grabModeIntentByPageId` but left the operation queue intact:

- **`registerBrowserHandlers()`** — on handler re-registration (e.g. workspace restart), a pending chain from the previous session survives in the map. The next `queueGrabModeOperation` for that page chains behind it, so if the stale promise never settles (an in-flight `executeJavaScript` whose guest was destroyed), new operations are silently stuck forever.
- **`browser:unregisterGuest`** — if an operation is still in flight against a guest that is mid-destroy, the chain stays alive. A `browserPageId` reused by a new tab then queues behind that stale promise.

## Fix

Clear/delete the operation queue alongside the existing intent cleanup in both paths.

This is safe with the existing teardown in `queueGrabModeOperation`: its `.finally` only removes the map entry when it still identity-matches its own `completion` promise, so a late-settling stale operation cannot clobber an entry created by a subsequent operation.

## Validation

- `npx vitest run src/main/ipc/browser.test.ts` — 20 passed
- `npm run typecheck:node` — clean
- `npx oxlint src/main/ipc/browser.ts` — clean

records.title: fix(browser): resolve grab mode race conditions and teardown
records.body:
## Summary
Resolves race conditions in grab mode (element selection) that prevented users from enabling/disabling the feature reliably. Fixes improper cleanup when disabling grab mode before selection completes.

## Problem
Grab mode operations were susceptible to race conditions when:
- Rapidly toggling enable/disable requests
- Disabling before the guest finished registration
- Page switching during pending enable operations
- Stale operations completing after being superseded

## Solution
**IPC serialization**: Queue grab mode operations per page to ensure they execute sequentially, preventing overlapping requests from interfering.

**Intent tracking**: Assign generations to each grab mode request so cancelled intents are ignored even if their async operations complete later.

**Registration wait**: When enabling grab mode without a ready guest, wait up to 1 second for guest registration to arrive (common on fast file:// pages).

**Teardown on disable**: When disabling grab mode without an active operation, execute cleanup script on the guest to tear down the armed overlay.

**Error classification**: Distinguish "injection-failed" (script execution failed) from "not-ready" (guest unavailable) to show users the correct error message.

## Key Changes
- `browser-manager.ts`: Execute guest cleanup when disabling without active operation
- `browser.ts`: Add operation queuing, intent tracking, and registration waits
- `useGrabMode.ts`: Track arm generation, set armed state immediately, handle superseded requests
- `browser-grab-types.ts`: Add 'injection-failed' reject reason
- i18n: Add localized error messages for all rejection reasons

## Testing
Comprehensive test coverage added for:
- Waiting for authorized registration with live old guest
- Registration timeout after 1 second
- Cancelling pending enable prevents activation
- Coalescing cancelled enable into later enable
- Serializing mode changes to prevent stale operations
- Distinguishing injection failure from readiness
- Rapid toggle/cancel during pending enable
- Page switch cancellation
- Screenshot stale-ness after restart

Those live reads publish immutable, monotonically revisioned repository snapshots containing repository identity, status, upstream state, conflicts, a worktree-graph placeholder, and per-projection freshness. Retention is bounded to 64 repository scopes, four variants per projection, 1,000 entries and ignored paths, and 64 Ki code units.

Per-caller status cancellation remains isolated, the last live status lease owns underlying cancellation, mutation invalidation fences old generations and suppresses stale publication, provider replacement isolates relay incarnations, and settled status or upstream results are never returned from a cache. Exact Git 2.25-compatible commands and SSH RPC payloads are unchanged.

The publication audit measured approximately +0.7 µs / +1.6 KiB sampled allocation for an empty status result, +3.5 µs / +16 KiB for 100 entries, and +29 µs / +151 KiB for the 1,000-entry retention bound. Callers still receive the exact original mutable result; retained entries are separate frozen copies.

Automatic Checks queries the exact host-owned snapshot seam before falling back to its existing fresh status/upstream path: desktop IPC for locally owned worktrees and background `git.repositorySnapshot` RPC for active runtime-owned worktrees. It admits only complete, current-generation, exact-branch projections; stale, failed, truncated, branch-mismatched, ambiguous-upstream, unsupported-runtime, and manual-refresh cases still execute fresh work.

| Settled active poll followed by automatic Checks | Before | Current |
| ------------------------------------------------ | -----: | ------: |
| Native/WSL physical status loads                 |      2 |       1 |
| Native/WSL physical explicit-upstream loads      |      2 |       1 |
| SSH `git.status` RPCs                            |      2 |       1 |
| SSH `git.upstreamStatus` RPCs                    |      2 |       1 |

The desktop path retains sender-scoped host-to-renderer subscriptions for both normal and `reuseLineStats` identities. `invalidated` events advance mutation/provider fences without launching work; `ready` is emitted only after the requested status and configured or explicit upstream projection is admissible. Checks then performs a memory-only projection query and coalesces events around an in-flight read.

SSH provider incarnation rebinding fences late old-provider events. Explicit unsubscribe, sender destruction/reload, visibility or context change, connection replacement, and handler disposal release exact listeners. Active runtime environments now resolve the exact worktree selector, native versus exact WSL identity, current SSH-provider incarnation, status identity, and optional push target through a query-only background RPC. Runtime snapshot subscriptions are now retained for automatic runtime-routed SSH Checks, as described below. The first bounded mobile consumer is retained after that section.

The subscription tranche adds 5,192 raw / 1,010 gzip bytes to Electron main and 1,019 / 177 to preload versus the prior checkpoint. All renderer entry raw sizes and JS/CSS counts remain unchanged.

Independent review corrected ambiguous embedded-upstream admission, late cross-context read completion, renderer send-failure/SSH-rebind cleanup, partial subscription cleanup when a sibling registration remains pending, project-level Windows/WSL runtime rebinding, background RPC classification, and the web preload fallback contract.

The Delete Worktree dialog is the next bounded snapshot consumer. Its warning-only dirty probe queries the exact normal and `reuseLineStats` status identities, admits only complete fresh status/repository/conflict siblings with matching identities, and selects the newest status projection revision. Missing or stale upstream data is intentionally irrelevant; cold, stale, failed, truncated, mismatched, unsupported, and runtime-routed reads retain the fresh fallback, while main-side deletion keeps the authoritative preflight.

| Settled active poll followed by Delete Worktree warning | Before | Current |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | -----: | ------: |
| Native physical status loads                            |      2 |       1 |
| Exact-distro WSL physical status loads                  |      2 |       1 |
| SSH `git.status` RPCs                                  |      2 |       1 |

The Delete Worktree tranche leaves Electron main and preload byte-identical. Renderer index changes by +63 raw / -67 gzip bytes with unchanged 292 JS / 2 CSS reachability; popout and web raw bytes and file counts are unchanged. The following runtime-query tranche leaves main, preload, index, and popout raw bytes unchanged; its explicit inert web API fallback adds 296 raw / 137 gzip bytes with unchanged reachability.

## Runtime-routed Checks revision stream

Automatic runtime-routed SSH Checks now keeps its existing three-second visible fallback until the normal and `reuseLineStats` streams represent the same live provider incarnation and a ready event drives an admissible current-context snapshot read. After that admission, idle snapshot polling stops; any incarnation mismatch, invalidation, replay, disconnect, error, visibility/context change, or malformed/inadmissible snapshot immediately fails open.

| One visible idle minute after readiness | Before | Current |
| --------------------------------------- | -----: | ------: |
| Normal identity snapshot RPCs / owner reads | 20 / 20 | 0 / 0 |
| `reuseLineStats` fallback RPCs / owner reads | 40 / 40 | 0 / 0 |
| Physical status / upstream producer work | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |

Independent review reproduced and corrected a cross-socket ordering gap where one stream could advance to provider incarnation 5 while its sibling remained at 4. The retained implementation pairs both live incarnations before admission, preserves the fail-open loop, passes 220 focused tests across 16 files plus type/lint/format/max-lines/build/budget gates, and records exact A/B evidence in `tools/benchmarks/results/phase2-runtime-checks-repository-snapshot-revision-stream-2026-07-30.md`.

## Initial mobile diff review

The first automatic mobile diff-review load now queries the exact default
`git.repositorySnapshot` projection published by mobile Source Control before falling back to
its existing fresh `git.status` request. Admission requires complete, untruncated,
current-generation status, repository-identity, and conflict siblings with one matching identity;
upstream data is ignored because this surface needs only entries, head, branch, and conflict state.

| Settled Source Control status followed by diff review | Before | Current |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -----: | ------: |
| Native/exact-WSL physical status loads                |      2 |       1 |
| SSH `git.status` provider/mux requests               |      2 |       1 |

Only the first connected load for a client, host, and worktree context may use the projection.
Initial disconnected states preserve that opportunity; later reconnects, mutation reloads, retries,
explicit refreshes, reconciliation, PR preparation, and every later diff-review load remain fresh.
The separately bounded Source Control remount consumer is described below.
Old-runtime, disconnected, missing, malformed, stale, truncated, generation-mismatched, and
identity-mismatched projections immediately retain the existing fallback and unavailable copy.

The mobile consumer adds no Electron renderer code. The mobile RPC allowlist changes Electron main
by 0 raw / -1 gzip byte versus the prior checkpoint; preload and the complete renderer tree are
byte-identical, with unchanged 292/77/33 JS reachability for index/popout/web.

## Initial mobile Source Control remount

The first connected automatic load for each mounted mobile Source Control client and default
status-identity context now queries the runtime-owned `git.repositorySnapshot` projection before
its existing fresh `git.status` fallback. Admission additionally requires a fresh configured-upstream
projection with non-negative integer counts, a nonempty name when upstream exists, and the exact
configured no-upstream shape. Status, repository identity, and conflicts remain complete,
untruncated, current-generation, and identity-equal; upstream shares the generation without assuming
the status identity.

| Source Control → diff review → Source Control remount | Before | Current |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -----: | ------: |
| Native/exact-WSL physical status loads                |      2 |       1 |
| SSH `git.status` provider/mux requests               |      2 |       1 |
| Read-only owner snapshot queries                     |      1 |       3 |

Cold, rejected, malformed, stale, old-runtime, or unavailable projections pay one best-effort query
and retain the fresh selector-retrying path. Disconnected-first and StrictMode preserve/coalesce the
single opportunity; reconnects and every explicit, retry, refresh, forced, mutation, branch,
reconciliation, and PR safety load stay fresh. Render-current client, connection, identity, mount,
and generation guards suppress late commits. The parser now lives at an acyclic Source Control domain
boundary shared with diff review.

This mobile-only tranche leaves Electron main, preload, and all renderer trees byte-identical, with
the same 779-record manifest and zero missing paths, missing edges, escaping paths, or static cycles.

## Workspace Space Manager snapshot reuse

After automatic Workspace Cleanup warms the existing repository owner without populating renderer `gitStatusByWorktree`, Space Manager now queries the exact normal and `reuseLineStats` projections before its existing six-worker fresh-status fallback. It selects the newest admissible status revision and applies status, repository identity, conflicts, and configured-upstream evidence only while the analyzed row, branch, connection/provider incarnation, runtime target, mount, and missing-status claim remain current.

| SSH provider/mux `git.status` work                     |      2 |       1 |
| Configured-upstream computation embedded in status     |      2 |       1 |
| Separate upstream work                                 |      0 |       0 |
| Repository-owner memory reads                          |      0 |       2 |
| Desktop runtime RPCs                                   |      0 |       0 |

Cold, stale, malformed, truncated, identity-mismatched, old-runtime, disconnected, or ambiguous projections retain the existing fresh path. Independent review corrected two liveness boundaries before publication: a fresh fallback can finish its own identity/upstream writes after claiming the missing status entry, and a connection-only SSH provider replacement aborts the old request and schedules a new one with the replacement connection. Folder/main exclusions, explicit refreshes, active polling, mutations, Workspace Cleanup reads, and authoritative deletion preflights are unchanged.

Electron main and preload remain byte-identical. The final renderer index changes by +67 raw / -169 gzip bytes, popout by 0 raw / -47 gzip, and web by 0 raw / +5 gzip, with unchanged 292/77/33 JS reachability and unchanged CSS counts.

## Source Control automatic-upstream snapshot reuse

After a settled active poll while Explorer, Checks, or an editor already keeps Git status interactive, switching to Source Control now queries the exact normal and `reuseLineStats` owner projections before the existing fresh upstream fallback. The consumer selects the newest admissible status revision and applies configured-upstream evidence only while worktree, path, branch, push target, SSH provider incarnation, runtime target, visibility, and mount remain current.

| Settled poll followed by Source Control tab switch | Before | Current |
| -------------------------------------------------- | -----: | ------: |
| Native/exact-WSL physical status work              |      1 |       1 |
| Configured-upstream computations                   |      2 |       1 |
| Separate native/exact-WSL upstream work            |      1 |       0 |
| SSH provider/mux `git.status` work                 |      1 |       1 |
| SSH provider/mux `git.upstreamStatus` work         |      1 |       0 |
| Repository-owner memory reads                      |      0 |       2 |

Runtime routing changes total Git RPCs from two to three (`git.status` 1→1, `git.upstreamStatus` 1→0, `git.repositorySnapshot` 0→2) while reducing physical runtime upstream work from one to zero. Cold, stale, malformed, truncated, branch-mismatched, old-runtime, disconnected, failed, or otherwise inadmissible projections retain the fresh path; explicit refreshes, mutations, reconciliation, polling, Workspace Cleanup, review-safety reads, and deletion preflights remain unchanged.

Independent review replaced literal-only A/B counters with call-instrumented measurements. The final ten-file focused suite passed 123 tests, the relevant host/routing suite passed 154 tests, and the broad renderer suite passed 1,913 tests; web/node typechecks, lint/format, max-lines, production build, budgets, and complete manifest/path/static-cycle validation passed. Electron main and preload remain byte-identical; renderer index changes by +2 raw / +10 gzip bytes, with unchanged 292/77/33 JS reachability and unchanged CSS counts.

## Validation completed for this checkpoint

- 84 settled Orca orchestration tasks, including per-tranche strict A/B builds and independent checkpoint/evidence audits.
- Fresh exact-tree production builds and bundle-budget checks.
- Root Node/CLI/web typechecks and mobile typecheck across the broader stacked checkpoint.
- Aggregate lint/format checks plus targeted `oxlint --deny-warnings` and `oxfmt --check` for this tranche.
- Max-lines ratchet with no new bypasses.
- Complete renderer manifest/path/static-cycle validation for baseline and retained builds.
- Tracked and untracked whitespace checks.
- This tranche's focused acceptance set passed 75 tests.
- Its broad host suite passed 376 tests with one skip; its broad renderer suite passed 121 tests; the core IPC registrar suite passed two tests.
- The Delete Worktree status-projection suite passed 30 tests; its broad owner/native/WSL/SSH/removal/dialog suite passed 611 tests with two skips.
- The runtime-query tranche passed 106 focused tests and 91 web preload tests; its broad host suite passed 663 tests with one skip and its broad renderer suite passed 110 tests.
- The initial mobile diff-review tranche passed 22 focused mobile tests, 66 broader mobile route/Source Control tests, and 42 host/RPC tests; all affected typechecks and static gates passed.
- The mobile Source Control remount tranche passed 64 focused mobile tests, 1,083 broad Source Control/session tests, and 42 host/RPC tests; all typechecks, static gates, a fresh production build, budgets, and exact-tree validation passed.
- The Workspace Space Manager tranche passed 59 focused consumer tests, 46 snapshot/hook/refresh acceptance tests, 251 relevant host-boundary tests, and 1,871 broad renderer tests; web/node typechecks, lint/format, max-lines, a final production build, budgets, and exact manifest/path/static-cycle validation passed.
- The runtime Checks revision-stream tranche passed 220 focused tests across 16 files; node/web typechecks, targeted lint/format, max-lines, a fresh production build, budgets, and complete A/B manifest/path/reference/static-cycle validation passed.

## Known unresolved risks

- No packaged-ASAR launch matrix has yet run across macOS, Linux, and Windows.
- Linux glibc/native-module packaging compatibility still requires the real packaging gate.
- Mobile process-memory evidence still needs physical-device validation.
- Initial mobile snapshot reuse still needs live-device and packaged reconnect latency sampling.
- Lazy first-use latency and stale-chunk recovery need runtime smoke coverage.

- This intentionally large stacked checkpoint is behind current `main` and will need conflict/review decomposition before merge.

Preserve native, exact-distro WSL, SSH incarnation, runtime, folder-workspace, provider, explicit push-target, cancellation, mutation-fence, and Git 2.25 behavior. records.title: perf(terminal): size checkpoints with a bounded walk, emit with JSON.stringify
records.body:
## Description

Follow-up to #11422. That PR replaced `jsonUtf8ByteLength` + `JSON.stringify` with `BoundedJsonWriter`, a hand-rolled JSON emitter that counts UTF-8 bytes while writing. It achieved its goal of bounding the over-cap path, but it also made the path that runs on every checkpoint — the one where the payload fits — measurably slower.

This keeps the bounded walk and uses it only for **sizing**, then hands emission back to native `JSON.stringify`. An over-cap checkpoint is still never passed to `JSON.stringify`, so #11422's win is preserved and improved on.

## ELI5

Orca has to check a terminal snapshot isn't too big before saving it. #11422 made Orca write out the save-file by hand while measuring, which turned out to be slow for colorful terminal output. Now Orca measures by hand — that part is fast and can stop early — and lets JavaScript's built-in, much faster writer produce the actual file.

## Why the emitter was slow

`BoundedJsonWriter` batches unescaped runs into 16 KiB spans. Every character needing a JSON escape flushes the current span and appends the escape separately. Terminal ANSI is dense with `ESC` (`0x1b`, a control character escaped as `^[`), so on real agent-TUI scrollback the span batching almost never engages and the writer degenerates into two small string appends per escape.

## Measurements

Node 24 / macOS, median of 9 warmed runs with `--expose-gc`, driven by SGR-styled scrollback with multibyte content. `PRE` is `main` before #11422, `MERGED` is `main` today, `FIXED` is this PR.

**Passing path — checkpoint fits under the cap. This runs on every checkpoint tick.**

| content | size | PRE | MERGED | FIXED | vs MERGED |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| plain ASCII | 1MB | 2.6ms | 4.4ms | 3.6ms | **0.83x** |
| plain ASCII | 5MB | 12.9ms | 17.0ms | 12.6ms | **0.74x** |
| light ANSI | 1MB | 3.0ms | 5.5ms | 3.8ms | **0.69x** |
| light ANSI | 5MB | 13.5ms | 25.4ms | 14.4ms | **0.57x** |
| agent-TUI ANSI | 1MB | 4.3ms | 10.0ms | 5.4ms | **0.54x** |
| agent-TUI ANSI | 5MB | 20.2ms | 86.2ms | 20.8ms | **0.24x** |

**Reject path — payload over a 256 KiB cap.**

| | PRE | MERGED | FIXED |
|---|---|---|---|
| agent-TUI ANSI, 10MB payload | 16.4ms | 1.7ms | **0.3ms** |

At realistic 5MB checkpoints this is at parity with pre-#11422 (0.97x–1.06x) and 1.4x–4.2x faster than `main` today. The 1MB rows carry more run-to-run variance and their absolute deltas are ~1ms. The reject path is ~55x faster than pre-#11422 and ~6x faster than `main`.

To be clear about the claim: this is not a win over pre-#11422 on the passing path. It restores that path to parity while keeping — and extending — #11422's early-exit benefit on the reject path.

## Proof of no regression

Differential fuzz of `stringifyWithinLimit` against `JSON.stringify` — **60,096 cases, zero divergence** on all three axes: exact output equality, acceptance at exactly the byte cap, and rejection at cap−1.

- 60,000 randomized nested values drawn from control characters, 1/2/3-byte UTF-8, paired surrogates, and lone high/low surrogates
- targeted cases straddling the 8 KiB chunk boundary (16382–32769 code units) for ASCII, 2-byte, 3-byte, surrogate-pair, lone-surrogate and control-character fills

```
checked 60096
{}          # no CONTENT, EXACT_LIMIT_REJECTED, or OVER_LIMIT_ACCEPTED findings
```

Test suites:

```
pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/daemon/
Test Files  77 passed | 2 skipped (79)
     Tests  1168 passed | 5 skipped (1173)
```

```
pnpm run typecheck        # passed: node, tc.cli, tc.web
pnpm run check:code-quality:changed
  code quality: 0 new finding(s) across 2 changed file(s).
  type-aware code quality: 0 new finding(s) across 2 changed file(s).
  React Doctor: 0 new finding(s) across 2 changed file(s).
```

## Two latent issues closed along the way

1. **Truncated-JSON hole.** `appendJsonValue` returned `false` for two different reasons — budget exceeded, and value not serializable — but `stringifyWithinLimit` discarded the boolean and returned `writer.result()`. The non-exceed `false` yielded a non-null, half-written string that would have been renamed into place as `checkpoint.json`. Unreachable today, but now structurally impossible: any `false` returns `null`.

2. **Restored the estimator cross-check.** #11422 dropped `throw new Error('Terminal checkpoint size estimator mismatch')`. Since output is native `JSON.stringify` again, the guard is cheap to keep, and it is the only thing that can catch a sizing bug before the bytes reach disk.

## Test changes

- `does not materialize and rescan a passing candidate` asserted `fullCandidateStringifies: 0, byteLengthCalls: 0` — it pinned the emitter design this PR reverses. Split into `reads each snapshot field once on the passing path` (the part that is still a real invariant) and a boundary test asserting acceptance at exactly the cap and rejection at cap−1.
- Added `sizes lone surrogates as JSON.stringify escapes them`. #11422's suite used only *paired* surrogates, so the 6-byte lone-surrogate cost had no coverage.
- Factored the duplicated expected-object literal into `expectedJson`.

Background daemon work only; no user-visible UI change, so screenshots are not applicable.

Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) 🐋

records.title: [Bug]: Google sign-in is impossible in the in-app browser — the UA laundering added in #885 is what Google rejects
records.body:
**Operating system:** macOS
**Orca version:** 1.4.161 (code path unchanged on current `main` @ 561e2d32c)


## Summary

Signing in to a Google account in Orca's in-app browser always fails with
`https://accounts.google.com/v3/signin/rejected` — *"This browser or app may not be secure. Try using
a different browser."*

The cause is Orca's own User-Agent laundering. `cleanElectronUserAgent()` strips the
`Electron/<ver>` and app-name tokens, which makes the UA indistinguishable from stock desktop
Chrome. Google rejects that. With the untouched Electron UA, Google sign-in works — including 2FA
and the OAuth consent/callback.

This is the opposite of the common folklore ("remove Electron from the UA to get Google login to
work"). I measured it both ways; the laundered UA is the one that fails.

## Regression origin

#885 ("improve Cloudflare Turnstile compatibility", fixes #107) added `cleanElectronUserAgent` to
the **default** session path in `browser-session-registry.ts` — its own summary lists *"Strip
Electron/app tokens from default UA even without imported sessions"*. Before that, the default
session used the untouched UA. Turnstile compatibility was the goal and I am not proposing to
regress it; Google sign-in is collateral damage.

## Evidence

Isolated harness, same Electron 43.1.0 binary Orca ships, one throwaway `userData` profile per run,
identical automation in every arm (native `webContents.sendInputEvent`, no CDP input). Verdict is
the URL class after submitting the account identifier.

| # | UA | `sec-ch-ua` | anti-detection script | CDP attached | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | untouched Electron UA | untouched | no | no | password page |
| 2 | untouched Electron UA | forged "Google Chrome" | no | no | password page |
| 3 | laundered | untouched | no | no | **rejected** |
| 4 | laundered | forged | no | no | **rejected** |
| 5 | laundered | forged | yes | yes + `Page.enable` + `Runtime.enable` | **rejected** |
| 6 | **untouched** | forged | yes | yes + both domains enabled | **password page** |
| 7 | Safari 18.5 UA, all `sec-ch-ua` stripped | — | no | attach only | **rejected** |

Rows 5 and 6 differ only in the UA. So the anti-detection script, the attached CDP debugger, and
the forged client-hints header are all irrelevant to this rejection — row 6 has all three and
passes.

Which token matters — it is not the word "Electron":

| UA | verdict |
|---|---|
| `… Chrome/150.0.7871.47 Electron/43.1.0 Safari/537.36` | password page |
| `… <app-name>/0.0.0 Chrome/150.0.7871.47 Safari/537.36` | password page |
| `… Chrome/150.0.7871.47 NeutralRuntime/43.1.0 Safari/537.36` | CAPTCHA (not rejected) |
| `… Chrome/150.0.7871.47 Safari/537.36` (laundered) | **rejected** |

Any extra product token is enough. A UA that is byte-shaped like stock Chrome is what fails.

### Controlling for order and for account state

Randomized blocked replication, 5 blocks, one laundered arm and one untouched arm per block, order
drawn per block (4 of 5 blocks ran the laundered arm **first**): laundered rejected 5/5, untouched
rejected 0/5.

Repeated with **non-existent** Gmail addresses (a different disposable address per block, so no
account state exists at all), 3 blocks: untouched UA reached "couldn't find your account" 3/3, i.e.
Google proceeded to account lookup; laundered UA was rejected 3/3 **before** the lookup.

Cumulative: Chrome-shaped UA rejected **12/12**. UA with any extra product token rejected **0/12**.

### End-to-end

With the untouched UA on the auth tab only (session left laundered, forged client hints,
anti-detection injected, CDP attached), a full sign-in completed by hand:

```
<relying-party>/sign-in
  → accounts.google.com/v3/signin/identifier
  → /challenge/pwd → /challenge/pk/presend → /challenge/selection → /challenge/totp
  → accounts.google.co.kr/accounts/SetSID
  → <relying-party>/documents          (session established, user rendered)
```

No `/v3/signin/rejected` anywhere. 2FA and the OAuth consent/callback both succeeded.

## What I am *not* claiming

I do not know Google's actual rule. I can only report that the UA string changes the branch. Google
does not document this check, and it has evidently changed before — the widespread advice to strip
the Electron token points at an earlier behavior. Any fix here depends on undocumented behavior that
Google can change again. Also note Google's OAuth policy still discourages embedded user-agents, so
this is a grey area regardless of what currently works.

All measurements are from one machine and one egress IP.

## Suggested fix

Make the laundering opt-out-able per browser session profile rather than unconditional, so #107 is
untouched by default:

- add `spoofUserAgent?: boolean` to `BrowserSessionProfile` (absent = today's behavior)
- resolve the session UA through a single helper that honors it
- expose it on profile creation (`orca tab profile create --no-ua-spoof`, plus the profile UI)

Deliberately **not** proposed: switching the UA by destination host, or switching it mid-session.
That desynchronizes the `User-Agent` header from `navigator.userAgent`, `navigator.userAgentData`
and `Sec-CH-UA*` across redirects and subresources, and Cloudflare treats a UA change during a
Turnstile session as a risk signal. The coherent boundary is a session partition whose identity is
fixed before its first navigation.

I have this implemented and passing (typecheck, `src/main/browser` + `src/cli` suites, oxlint,
oxfmt, max-lines ratchet) and can open the PR if the approach looks right — or adapt it if you would
rather surface the switch differently.

records.title: [Bug]: Mobile/remote browser screencast stops when host display turns off
records.body:
### Operating system

macOS

### Orca version

latest main

### Details

**Short summary:**  
When using the Orca mobile companion (or another remote client) to open the host browser, turning the host display off stops webpage rendering/screencast frames, even though the host is not fully asleep — terminals and other commands still accept input and execute.

**What happened?**  
Phone is paired to desktop Orca. Opening a browser pane on mobile relies on the host Chromium + `browser.screencast`. After the host display turns off (system still awake enough for PTY/RPC), the mobile browser stops updating / cannot usefully load pages. Agent terminals continue to work.

**How can we reproduce it?**  
1. Start Orca on a Mac (machine A) and pair the mobile companion.  
2. From the phone, open a worktree browser pane and load a page.  
3. Turn off / allow the host display to sleep (keep the Mac from full system sleep if needed so terminals still work).  
4. Observe that browser screencast/rendering stops while terminal commands still run.

**Anything else that might help:**  
Root cause appears to be compositor parking under display sleep / main-window background throttling. Guest webviews already use `setBackgroundThrottling(false)`, but CDP screencast still needs the display/compositor awake. Fix should gate `prevent-display-sleep` (and temporary main-window unthrottle) on active `browser.screencast` sessions only, so idle hosts still save power.

Related PR: https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/11491

records.title: fix(browser): keep host awake only while screencast streams are live
records.body:
Fixes #11492

## Summary

- Mobile/remote browser panes stream CDP screencast frames from the host Chromium. When the host display sleeps (or the main window is background-throttled), the compositor parks and frames stop — even though the main process, PTYs, and agent RPCs keep working.
- Add `BrowserScreencastAwakeService` (same `prevent-display-sleep` + macOS/Linux sleep-assertion pattern as agent-awake) and acquire it only while at least one `browser.screencast` session is active; release when the last stream ends.
- While a screencast is live, also temporarily set the authoritative main window's `setBackgroundThrottling(false)` so occlusion/display-sleep can't stall painting; restore the default throttle when idle.
- Electron power APIs are resolved lazily so incomplete `vi.mock('electron')` fixtures used by `orca-runtime` tests keep loading.

## Screenshots

No visual change.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint` — changed-file gates pass (`check:code-quality:changed`, `audit:code-quality:*`, `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check:reliability-gates`, localization/skill verifies). Full-repo `oxlint` currently fails on unrelated pre-existing `src/main/daemon/daemon-pty-router.ts` max-lines (304 > 300) on `main` tip; not introduced by this PR.
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm test` — fixed regression where static `powerSaveBlocker` import broke electron-mocked runtime suites; verified `orca-runtime*.test.ts`, `pty.test.ts`, `cdp-bridge-integration.test.ts`, SSH remote CLI/orchestration tests, plus screencast awake unit/integration tests (1406+ passing in the affected set). Full suite also surfaced unrelated flaky/env failures (managed-hook lock timing, WSL live relay, ephemeral-vm, SSH transport timeout) outside this change.
- [x] `pnpm build` — `pnpm run build:desktop` (typecheck + relay + cli + electron-vite + web) passes. Full `pnpm build` then fails on local macOS `build:computer-macos` Swift PackageDescription linker mismatch with Command Line Tools (environment), unrelated to this PR. CI package job on Ubuntu does not use that path the same way.
- [x] Added or updated high-quality tests that would catch regressions, or explained why tests were not needed

## AI Review Report

Reviewed the change for cross-platform compatibility, remote/mobile behavior, and power impact:

- **macOS**: Electron `prevent-display-sleep` + existing `MacosSystemSleepAssertion` (`caffeinate -i -s`), matching agent-awake.
- **Linux**: existing `LinuxLidSleepAssertion` + Electron blocker.
- **Windows**: Electron `prevent-display-sleep` only (same intentional omission of lid-plan mutation as agent-awake). No shortcut/label/path changes.
- **Headless / `orca serve`**: awake assertions still run; main-window unthrottle is skipped when no authoritative window exists.
- **Remote/SSH/local**: trigger is runtime `browser.screencast`, so mobile and remote browser panes benefit; local PTY/agent traffic is unchanged.
- **Performance**: idle hosts keep background throttling and may sleep; cost only while a screencast subscription is live.
- **Testability**: avoided static Electron named imports so runtime test mocks without `powerSaveBlocker` continue to load.
- No UI surface changes.

## Security Audit

No new IPC, command execution, path handling, auth, or secrets. The change only starts/stops OS power assertions and toggles Electron background throttling for an existing privileged main-process browser stream. Refcounted acquire/release and quit-time dispose avoid leaking blockers. Lazy `require('electron')` is confined to service construction defaults.

## Notes

- Browser guest webviews already call `setBackgroundThrottling(false)` permanently for screenshots; this PR gates *host* display-sleep prevention and main-window unthrottle on live screencast sessions so phone/remote browsing survives display-off without paying that cost when idle.
- Manual check: pair mobile → open browser pane → turn host display off → page should keep updating; close mobile browser pane → host may sleep/throttle again.
- First-time fork PR: GitHub Actions are in `action_required` awaiting maintainer workflow approval. Please approve `PR Checks` so CI can run on the latest commit.

records.title: fix(mobile): stop serving a pre-write host-list snapshot to loads issued after the write
records.body:
## Summary

Fixes the "Remove does not delete" half of #8791: removing (or renaming) a host committed to disk, but the home screen could immediately repaint the pre-write list, so the removed host's card came back.

Root cause: `loadHosts()` de-duplicates concurrent calls by handing back the in-flight pass. That de-dupe defeats the store's own `await hostListMutation` invariant — a pass that started *before* a write still holds the pre-write snapshot, and a load issued *after* the write commits (exactly the shape of `handleRemove` in `mobile/app/index.tsx`) was served that stale snapshot. Now every durable host write drops the shared pass (`mobile/src/transport/host-list-load-sharing.ts`), so the next load reads fresh; concurrent loads with no write between them still share one Keychain pass.

Note on scope: the freeze half of #8791 ("app frozen after tapping Remove") needs no code change — the host action sheet already sets `closeBeforePress` on Edit host + Remove since #8536. This PR extracts that sheet into `mobile/src/host-list-action-sheet-actions.ts` so the deferral is pinned by tests and can't silently regress.

<!-- user-visible-before-after:start -->
## What the user sees before and after

### Before

Removing or renaming a host writes the change, but the home screen can reload an older snapshot. A removed host card then reappears, making it look like removal failed.

### After

The next host-list refresh reads the newly saved state, so removed hosts stay gone and renamed hosts retain their new names.
<!-- user-visible-before-after:end -->

## Simulator validation

Manual iOS Simulator A/B on Lane A device `PR 8647 QA iPhone`: true merge-base `5d88c1093fd8a75c4e1c3a86c34bf4f704a9d6e8` versus exact head `fed029f1f6da37c0a45912afff3a228a18303347`.

### Before — parent resurrects the removed card

![Parent: removed Host 1 card repainted from a stale pre-write snapshot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e191016-8d74-490b-bf8e-e32116f7c73d)

Durable storage was already `orca:hosts=[]`, but the post-remove refresh reused the parked pre-write result and repainted Host 1 as disconnected.

### After — exact head keeps the card removed

![Exact head: Host 1 remains absent after the stale pass resolves](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97906350-1be9-4e7d-b124-c29f226adac4)

The same parked old pass resolved with the former host id, while the post-write refresh read `orca:hosts=[]`; the card stayed gone beyond 15 seconds.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm test`
- [ ] `pnpm build` (not run: mobile-only change, `mobile/` has no build script; Mobile Checks CI covers it)
- [x] Added or updated high-quality tests that would catch regressions, or explained why tests were not needed

Run in `mobile/` on node 24. Baseline at parent commit: 351 files / 2587 tests → with this change: 353 files / 2601 tests (+14). Non-vacuity proven both ways: the new host-store tests park a load mid-Keychain-read, commit a removal/rename underneath it, then assert a load issued after the write never sees the pre-write snapshot — they fail on the parent commit and pass here; the shared-pass test asserts de-dupe still works when no write intervenes.

## AI Review Report

Reviewed the stale-snapshot race end to end: writer paths (`mutateStoredHosts`, `persistHost` relay-upgrade + overlay-removal branches, `removeHost` overlay cleanup) all drop the shared pass after their durable commit; the late-settle case (a dropped pass resolving after its replacement started) is handled by only retiring the pass still on offer, with a test pinning it. Checked that the action-sheet extraction is behavior-preserving (same labels, ordering, live-state gating, `closeBeforePress` placement). Cross-platform: this is React Native (iOS/Android) code only — no desktop shortcuts, labels, paths, shell, or Electron surface touched; no platform-conditional logic involved.

## Security Audit

No new input handling, command execution, path handling, auth, or IPC. The change only affects when an in-memory promise cache is invalidated; credential reads still go through the existing SecureStore path and token cache, and write serialization via `hostListMutation` is unchanged. No new dependencies.

## Notes

Residual (pre-existing, not addressed here): `MobileEndpointSupervisor` persists via plain `saveHost` (`mobile/src/transport/mobile-endpoint-lifecycle.ts:92`), which *appends* a host that was removed mid-flight instead of throwing like `saveExistingHostRelayUpgrade` does — a background relay upgrade racing a removal can still resurrect the host through that path.

records.title: fix(computer-use): make modifier clicks interruption-safe
records.body:
## Summary

- add `orca computer click --modifiers <chord>` so agents do not need separate modifier-down/click/modifier-up scripts
- keep modified clicks interruption-safe on macOS, Windows, and Linux
- guarantee macOS synthetic hotkey cleanup when a later key event fails
- validate modifier-only chords at the CLI, RPC, provider, and native boundaries
- teach the bundled computer-use guide to forbid separate modifier-down/up scripting

The triggering incident sent Command down, Shift down, and then attempted a click. The click stalled at an accessibility boundary before the script reached its key-up statements, leaving the synthetic modifier state latched until reboot.

## Design fit

This follows the original computer-use contract from #1683: use the public Orca command instead of raw AppleScript, prefer semantic accessibility actions when they can express the operation, and confine synthetic input to provider-owned implementations. Modified clicks bypass the semantic press path because accessibility press actions cannot carry modifier state.

It also follows the later hardening direction in #1757, #2894, #3960, and #4705: validate untrusted action input at each boundary, keep synthetic input target-aware, bound external commands, fail closed on unsupported platform behavior, and exercise native behavior in the focused computer-use workflow.

Platform behavior:

- macOS attaches `CGEventFlags` directly to mouse events, so a modified click creates no modifier key-down state
- Windows submits modifier-down, click, and modifier-up events in one `SendInput` batch, with emergency releases if insertion is partial
- Linux uses one bounded `xdotool` sequence with reverse-order key-up events and a bounded `finally` release; it fails as unsupported outside X11 or without `xdotool`

## Screenshots

No visual change.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm test` — 3,867 files passed; 40,875 tests passed; expected skips only
- [x] `pnpm build`
- [x] Added or updated high-quality regression tests
- [x] Focused Vitest — 10 files, 93 tests
- [x] `swift test --package-path native/computer-use-macos` — 44 tests
- [x] `pnpm verify:computer-native`

## AI Review Report

Reviewed the change against the original implementation commit/PR and the subsequent Windows, validation, focus-safety, and runtime-hardening PRs listed above. The review traced CLI/RPC/provider authority boundaries, semantic-versus-synthetic routing, partial insertion, interruption cleanup, process timeouts, stale targets, and macOS/Linux/Windows behavior.

Findings fixed during review:

- the generic RPC optional-string schema could silently convert `modifiers: ""` into an unmodified click; the field now fails closed
- Linux modified clicks could attempt X11 synthesis under Wayland; they now return unsupported before sending input
- the focused computer-use CI job did not explicitly include the new native safety guard; its path filter and test list now do
- the shared validator accepted spellings the native parsers rejected; accepted aliases are now consistent across layers and chords are bounded to four modifiers
- source-safety tests now assert macOS mouse flag placement and the Windows partial-insertion release path more directly

No unresolved correctness or security finding remains in the reviewed diff. Windows PowerShell parsing, `Add-Type` compilation, and behavioral e2e are delegated to the PR's Windows native-smoke job because PowerShell is unavailable on the development Mac.

## Security Audit

- modifier values are whitelisted and bounded before reaching native providers
- the Linux command uses an argv array with fixed command structure; user text cannot become shell syntax
- the authenticated macOS provider boundary and desktop operation-file permissions are unchanged
- no modifier state or new sensitive data is persisted
- modified clicks do not broaden blocked-app policy or action authority
- cleanup covers normal completion, provider errors, timeouts, and Windows partial event insertion

## Notes

Live modified-input testing was intentionally avoided on the development machine after the incident. The PR workflow provides Linux and Windows native verification; scheduled permission-bearing runners retain the existing macOS e2e coverage.

records.title: perf(terminal): serialize checkpoints with one payload walk
records.body:
## Description
Serialize terminal checkpoints with a bounded JSON writer that accounts for exact UTF-8 bytes while emitting output. Passing candidates avoid a full-object `JSON.stringify` followed by `Buffer.byteLength`; over-cap JSON emission stops once the byte limit is exceeded and discards its bounded partial output. If the initial checkpoint is rejected, the existing fallback deliberately replays the full checkpoint so it can produce and size a trimmed candidate.

Warmed 100 MiB measurements were **253.7–330.2 ms before** and **247.4–253.6 ms after**. This is not presented as a dramatic speedup; the change primarily bounds JSON emission and removes the extra full-string byte scan for fitting candidates.

## ELI5
Orca now stops building checkpoint JSON when it reaches the size limit instead of building an oversized JSON string. If that first attempt is too large, Orca still reads the full terminal history on purpose so it can create a smaller checkpoint that fits.

## Review remediation

### What changed
- Replaced the false-positive total-code-unit assertion with a direct proof that an oversized checkpoint object is never handed to full-object `JSON.stringify`.
- Kept the exactness-parity tests and passing-path test unchanged.
- Clarified that JSON emission is bounded, while the rejection fallback intentionally performs a full checkpoint replay.
- Replaced implied dramatic performance claims with the measured warmed 100 MiB ranges: 253.7–330.2 ms before and 247.4–253.6 ms after.

### ELI5
The size-limited JSON builder stops once its bucket is full, so it never creates the giant JSON result. Orca may still reread the terminal data afterward because that replay is how it makes a smaller checkpoint worth saving.

### Proof of fix
RED phase: archived pre-fix production (`d0ce3c7ec3`) with the new test copied in.

```bash
temp_dir=$(mktemp -d /tmp/orca-pr11422-red.XXXXXX) && git -C /Users/nwparker/orca/workspaces/orca/prod-scan-07-29 archive d0ce3c7ec3 | tar -x -C "$temp_dir" && cp /Users/nwparker/orca/workspaces/orca/prod-scan-07-29/src/main/daemon/terminal-checkpoint-serializer.test.ts "$temp_dir/src/main/daemon/terminal-checkpoint-serializer.test.ts" && ln -s /Users/nwparker/orca/workspaces/orca/prod-scan-07-29/node_modules "$temp_dir/node_modules" && printf 'RED_TEMP=%s\n' "$temp_dir" && cd "$temp_dir" && pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/daemon/terminal-checkpoint-serializer.test.ts -t 'rejects an oversized escaped candidate without materializing it'
```

Result: **1 test file failed; 1 test failed, 2 skipped**. The intended assertion failed because pre-fix production passed the oversized checkpoint object to `JSON.stringify` (`expected true to be false`).

GREEN phase on pushed head `88ca338811`:

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/daemon/terminal-checkpoint-serializer.test.ts src/main/daemon/json-utf8-byte-length.test.ts src/main/daemon/terminal-checkpoint-writer-bounds.test.ts
```

Result: **3 test files passed; 9 tests passed**.

### Proof of no regression
The green command covers the serializer, exact UTF-8 byte estimator, and checkpoint writer fallback suites. The existing exactness-parity tests and passing-path test remain intact.

```bash
pnpm run typecheck
```

Result: **passed** across `config/tsconfig.node.json`, `config/tsconfig.tc.cli.json`, and `config/tsconfig.tc.web.json`.

```bash
pnpm exec oxlint src/main/daemon/terminal-checkpoint-serializer.test.ts
```

Result: **passed with 0 diagnostics**.

No user-visible UI change; screenshots are not applicable.


### Final review objections

#### What changed
- Added an over-limit multibyte serializer case where the complete JSON is 99 UTF-8 bytes over the cap while its UTF-16 code-unit length is one unit under the cap.
- Confirmed repo-wide that `json-utf8-byte-length` was imported only by its own test, then deleted both the dead module and its test.

#### ELI5
Some characters take more bytes to save than their JavaScript string length suggests, so the new test makes sure Orca measures the real saved size. The old measuring module was no longer connected to Orca, so it and its isolated test were removed.

#### Proof of fix
RED phase: archived head `88ca338811`, copied in the new test, and mutated `BoundedJsonWriter.append` in the temporary copy to compare and accumulate `value.length` instead of UTF-8 `bytes`.

```bash
temp_dir=$(mktemp -d /tmp/orca-pr11422-code-unit-red.XXXXXX) && git -C /Users/nwparker/orca/workspaces/orca/prod-scan-07-29 archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$temp_dir" && cp /Users/nwparker/orca/workspaces/orca/prod-scan-07-29/src/main/daemon/terminal-checkpoint-serializer.test.ts "$temp_dir/src/main/daemon/terminal-checkpoint-serializer.test.ts" && ln -s /Users/nwparker/orca/workspaces/orca/prod-scan-07-29/node_modules "$temp_dir/node_modules" && python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; p=Path("'$temp_dir'/src/main/daemon/terminal-checkpoint-serializer.ts"); s=p.read_text(); s=s.replace("if (this.bytes + bytes > this.maxBytes)", "if (this.bytes + value.length > this.maxBytes)").replace("this.bytes += bytes", "this.bytes += value.length"); p.write_text(s)' && pnpm --dir "$temp_dir" exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/daemon/terminal-checkpoint-serializer.test.ts -t 'rejects multibyte input whose code-unit length fits under the byte cap'
```

Result: **1 test file failed; 1 test failed, 3 skipped**. The mutation wrongly accepted and returned the direct over-byte-cap JSON, so `expect(serialized).not.toBe(expected)` failed.

GREEN phase on `4f28318842`:

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/daemon/terminal-checkpoint-serializer.test.ts
```

Result: **1 test file passed; 4 tests passed**.

#### Proof of no regression
```bash
pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/daemon/history-manager.test.ts src/main/daemon/history-reader.test.ts src/main/daemon/terminal-history-incremental-restore.test.ts src/main/daemon/terminal-checkpoint-writer-bounds.test.ts
```

Result: **4 test files passed; 95 tests passed**.

```bash
pnpm run typecheck
```

Result: **passed** across all 3 configured projects: node, tc.cli, and tc.web.

```bash
pnpm exec oxlint src/main/daemon/terminal-checkpoint-serializer.test.ts
```

Result: **passed with 0 diagnostics**.

Repo-wide import confirmation at `88ca338811`:

```bash
rg -n --hidden --glob '!node_modules' --glob '!.git' "(?:from|import\\()\\s*['\\\"][^'\\\"]*json-utf8-byte-length['\\\"]|jsonUtf8ByteLength" /Users/nwparker/orca/workspaces/orca/prod-scan-07-29
```

Result: the only import was `src/main/daemon/json-utf8-byte-length.test.ts:2`; all other matches were declarations or calls inside that same module/test pair. After deletion, a repo-wide search returned no matches.

## Scan provenance
Finding: **P2 — Terminal checkpoint serializer walks the full payload three times synchronously**. Severity: **P2**. Introduced by **#10647** (`ca5a821600`).

records.title: [Feature]: Make browser annotation feedback compact by default
records.body:
## Problem or use case

Browser design annotations send far more diagnostic context than a normal feedback turn needs. A one-sentence comment on one paragraph currently expands to roughly 38 lines of Markdown.

The useful context for most changes is:

* page file or URL
* element label and selector
* selected text or element text
* intent
* feedback

The current output also includes the browser tab ID, viewport, bounds, classes, nearby text and elements, computed styles, full DOM path, and an HTML snippet for every annotation. That context is useful when debugging a layout or selector problem, but it consumes agent context and makes the user's comments harder to scan during ordinary document review.

Example from a local HTML report in Orca 1.4.159:

```markdown
## Design Feedback: /Users/me/report.html

**URL:** file:///Users/me/report.html
**Browser tab id:** page-id
**Viewport:** 2279x1296

### 1. p "Recommended locking rule"
**Intent:** change
**Selector:** `p#locking-rule-copy`
**Location:** `main > #locking-recommendation > #locking-rule-copy`
**Bounds:** x=829, y=476, 622x58
**Text:** "Final run approval is the only irreversible point."
...
**Computed styles:**
...
**Full DOM path:** `body > main > article#locking-recommendation > p#locking-rule-copy`
**HTML:**
...
**Feedback:** Explain why this should be irreversible.
```

Adding `id="locking-rule-copy"` and `data-review-id="locking-rule-copy"` to the report made the selector cleaner, but did not reduce the payload. The report cannot control Orca's export format.

This request should not change how annotations work. Users should still be able to comment on any element in a page, not only predefined decision blocks.

## Proposed solution

Make the compact format the default for both Send and Copy, with full diagnostics available through an explicit `Include diagnostic context` or `Copy with diagnostics` action.

Suggested compact output:

```markdown
## Design feedback
**Page:** file:///Users/me/report.html

### 1. p "Recommended locking rule"
**Intent:** change
**Selector:** `p#locking-rule-copy`
**Text:** "Final run approval is the only irreversible point."
**Feedback:** Explain why this should be irreversible.
```

Suggested implementation on current `main` (`4543bb68263a89ab520cea62ca69d7ac78330dd3`):

1. In `src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane/browser-annotation-output.ts`, add an output mode such as `compact | diagnostic` to `formatBrowserAnnotationsAsMarkdown`. Default to `compact`. Keep the current formatter output unchanged under `diagnostic`.
2. Compact mode should emit the page once, then element label, intent, selector, selected text or text snippet, optional source file when available, and feedback for each annotation.
3. In `BrowserPane.tsx`, derive both prompts. Pass the compact prompt to the existing Send surfaces and clipboard handler by default.
4. In `BrowserAnnotationSendMenuContent.tsx`, offer an unchecked `Include diagnostic context` option that switches the prompt passed to `ReviewNotesSendMenuContent`. Add a `Copy with diagnostics` action beside the current compact Copy action.
5. Keep this choice local to the current action. It does not need a persisted setting or a new dependency.

### Acceptance criteria

* Sending or copying browser annotations uses compact output by default.
* Compact output preserves the page, arbitrary annotated element, selector, text, intent, and feedback.
* Selected text takes precedence over the element text snippet, as it does now.
* Diagnostic output remains available by an explicit action and retains the current metadata, computed styles, DOM path, and HTML.
* Both `file://` reports and normal web URLs format correctly.
* Annotation capture, on-page markers, and delivery to existing or new agent sessions remain unchanged.

### Tests

Extend `src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane/browser-annotation-output.test.ts` to cover:

* compact is the default
* compact includes page, selector, selected or element text, intent, feedback, and optional source file
* compact excludes browser tab ID, viewport, location, bounds, classes, nearby context, computed styles, full DOM path, and HTML
* diagnostic mode preserves the current detailed output
* empty annotations, backtick-safe formatting, newline collapsing, length limits, and surrogate-pair safety still pass in the relevant modes

Extend `BrowserAnnotationSendMenuContent.test.tsx` to verify that the unchecked state sends the compact prompt, enabling diagnostics sends the detailed prompt, and both BrowserPane send surfaces remain wired.

Add a focused BrowserPane interaction test or existing source-boundary assertion for compact Copy versus Copy with diagnostics.

## Alternatives or additional context

Related issues checked before filing:

* stablyai/orca#8687 covers retaining annotations across page navigation.
* stablyai/orca#8303 covered sending web annotations to an active agent.
* stablyai/orca#7346 covered selecting existing agent sessions from the design feedback Send menu.

None covers output size or diagnostic opt-in.

The current implementation has a single `browserAnnotationsPrompt` in `BrowserPane.tsx`, produced by `formatBrowserAnnotationsAsMarkdown(browserAnnotations)`, and uses it for both Send surfaces and Copy. The formatter currently hardcodes all diagnostic sections. That makes this a formatting and small UI-routing change rather than a change to capture or annotation targeting.

records.title: fix(browser): scope Cmd/Ctrl+F find to the focused split (#11348)
records.body:
## Summary

Fixes #11348.

In a terminal + browser split, pressing **Cmd+F (macOS) / Ctrl+F (Windows/Linux)** while the **terminal** was focused opened Find in the **browser** pane instead of find-in-terminal.

Root cause: the browser pane's renderer-path Find handler (`BrowserPagePane` in `BrowserPane.tsx`) is a **window-global, capture-phase `keydown` listener** that was armed on `isActive` — "am I the active tab within my own group?" — not on whether its split holds keyboard focus. `BrowserPaneOverlayLayer` computes `isActive` from `isWorktreeActive && isActiveInGroup`, which ignores `activeGroupIdByWorktree` (the focused split). So in a split the browser was `isActive` even while the terminal was focused, and its unscoped listener called `preventDefault()` + `stopPropagation()`, claiming the chord before the (correctly focus-scoped) terminal handler could act.

Fix: thread a focused-split signal (`isFocused`) from `BrowserPaneOverlayLayer` — derived from `activeGroupIdByWorktree[worktreeId]` — through `BrowserPane` → `BrowserPagePane`, and gate the renderer-path Find listener on `isFocused` instead of `isActive`. This mirrors how terminal leaves already gate global shortcuts via `focusedGroupId` in `TabGroupSplitLayout.tsx`. The IPC path (webview guest focused) is left on `isActive` — it only fires when the guest genuinely has focus, so it is already correct.

## Screenshots

No visual change. Behavior-only: the Find bar now opens in whichever split (terminal or browser) holds keyboard focus.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint` (oxlint + oxfmt ran clean via pre-commit; targeted lint of `browser-pane` clean)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` (`tsconfig.tc.web.json` clean)
- [x] `pnpm test` (browser-pane suite: 32 files / 181 tests pass)
- [ ] `pnpm build`
- [x] Added regression tests in `BrowserPaneOverlayLayer.test.tsx`: an active browser pane is `focused` when its own group holds focus, and **not** `focused` when another split (e.g. the terminal) holds focus (#11348).

## AI Review Report

Reviewed with an AI coding agent. Checks and outcomes:
- **Wrong-surface routing (the bug):** confirmed the browser's window-global capture listener was the interceptor and that gating on the focused split resolves it without disturbing the terminal's already-scoped handler.
- **Cross-platform (macOS / Linux / Windows):** the chord flows through `keybindingMatchesAction('browser.find', …)` which resolves `Mod` → `metaKey` on macOS and `ctrlKey` elsewhere — a single code path, so the fix applies uniformly. No `e.metaKey` hardcoding introduced; no platform-specific labels or paths touched.
- **Regressions to other call sites:** `BrowserPane` gained an **optional** `isFocused` prop defaulting to `isActive`, so the floating-browser call sites (`Terminal.tsx`, `FloatingBrowserSlot.tsx`) are unchanged. SSH/remote pane (`RemoteBrowserPagePane`) has no Find handler and is untouched.
- **Guest-focused find:** the IPC path is unchanged and still opens Find when the webview guest itself is focused.

## Security Audit

No new input handling, command execution, path handling, auth, secrets, dependency, or IPC surface. The change only narrows the condition under which an existing renderer keydown listener is registered (fewer events claimed, not more). No IPC channels added or modified. No follow-up needed.

## Notes

- Behavior is symmetric: Find now targets whichever split holds focus. Clicking into the browser (chrome, address bar, or guest) focuses its group via the overlay's existing `onPointerDown`/`onFocusCapture` → `focusGroup`, so Cmd/Ctrl+F opens the browser find bar as before.
- Related shape to #10288 (floating workspace shortcuts routing to the main workspace); this PR scopes only the terminal/browser split find path.
