records.title: [Feature]: Officially support opening local files in browser tabs
records.body:
### Problem or use case

Orca's built-in browser does not expose a consistent, documented way to open local files.

The current BrowserPane guidance accepts only HTTP(S) URLs or localhost addresses, while some existing file-preview flows can already render `file://` content. This creates an inconsistent experience: local rendering works in a few contexts, but users cannot reliably open a generated HTML file, Markdown document, PDF, image, or text artifact from the browser address bar or the New Tab UI.

This was observed on Orca 1.4.152, macOS 26.5.2, arm64.

### Proposed solution

Make local-file navigation an official browser-tab capability with a consistent entry point and explicit security model.

- Accept valid `file://` URLs and platform-appropriate absolute filesystem paths in the browser address bar.
- Add **Open local file** to the New Tab UI, backed by a native or Orca file picker.
- Safely preview common local formats such as HTML, Markdown, PDF, images, and plain text.
- Clearly distinguish web URLs, local files, and remote-workspace files in the tab UI.
- Preserve eligible local-file tabs in browser history and session restoration.
- In remote workspaces, explicitly let the user choose whether a path belongs to the local client or the remote host.
- Provide actionable errors for missing files, unsupported formats, malformed URLs, permission failures, and unavailable remote hosts.

Acceptance criteria:

- Entering a valid `file://` URL opens the referenced file.
- Entering a valid absolute path opens the referenced file without manually constructing a URL.
- New Tab includes an **Open local file** action.
- HTML, Markdown, PDF, image, and text files use an appropriate safe preview.
- Relative assets resolve only within an explicitly authorized directory or workspace root.
- HTTP(S) pages cannot read arbitrary local files through navigation, JavaScript, fetch, or iframes.
- Local HTML is sandboxed by default; scripts or broader filesystem access require a separate explicit trust decision if supported.
- Symlinks and `../` traversal cannot escape the authorized scope.
- Remote paths are resolved through the remote runtime and are never silently interpreted as local client paths.
- Restoring a tab reuses only previously authorized access and does not broaden filesystem permissions.
- Existing HTTP(S) and localhost navigation behavior remains unchanged.

### Alternatives or additional context

Orca already has partial local-file rendering behavior through some preview paths. This request is not based on the assumption that Orca cannot render any local file today.

The request is to turn that partial behavior into a unified, discoverable, officially supported browser feature with consistent New Tab/address-bar entry points, permission boundaries, local-vs-remote semantics, history restoration, and error handling.

Security should follow least privilege: selecting one file authorizes only that file unless access to its containing directory is explicitly required and communicated for relative assets. A local document must not implicitly gain access to parent directories, sibling projects, the user's home directory, or the entire filesystem.

records.title: Route browser tabs and terminal links by worktree owner, not global runtime focus
records.body:
## Summary

Fixes #10212.

While a remote runtime environment is focused (e.g. a paired Mac Mini runtime), browser routing used the **global** `activeRuntimeEnvironmentId` as the ownership signal instead of the owner of the worktree/pane the request came from. That broke three things at once, even for entirely local worktrees:

- **CLI browser tabs were rejected outright.** `orca browser tab create <url>` failed with "Browser tabs are unavailable while a remote runtime is active" — a guard from #1878 that predates headless remote browser panes (#5412). Tab close/setProfile were blocked too.
- **Cmd/Ctrl-clicking an http(s) link in a local terminal opened the system browser** instead of an Orca tab, because the terminal link paths (OSC 8, WebLinks addon, mouseup fallback) never passed a `sourceOwner` and the router inferred locality from the global focus flag.
- **Remote-hosted browser tabs were not operable by agents.** `browser snapshot/goto/click/...` resolved only against the desktop-local CDP bridge, so tabs the UI already creates on a remote host (via `createWebRuntimeSessionBrowserTab`) couldn't be driven from the CLI.

What this changes:

- **Terminal links** resolve ownership from the pane's live PTY transport → the worktree's explicit runtime owner → its SSH host → local (never the global focus), threaded through all three click paths. Local terminals open links in Orca again while a runtime is focused; genuinely remote/SSH terminals keep the external-browser behavior.
- **CLI tab create/close/setProfile** are ownership-aware: local worktrees get local webview tabs even while a runtime is focused; remote-owned worktrees route creation to the owning environment and mirror back into the desktop UI (same path as the UI's New Browser Tab action), with a `hostedRemotely` reply hint so main skips the webview registration wait/goto.
- **All `browser.*` RPC methods** retry target misses (`browser_no_tab`, `browser_tab_not_found`, `selector_not_found`) against the focused environment, which owns the remote-hosted tabs. `browser.tabList` additionally forwards when nothing local is live, so agents on the remote host can discover their tabs.

## Screenshots

No visual change.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint` — clean on all touched files. Note: `lint:switch-exhaustiveness` fails on `skill-freshness-group.tsx`, which also fails on the base commit (pre-existing, unrelated).
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm test` — 31,868 passed. The 8 failing files (43 tests: localStorage/environment related) fail identically on the base commit in this environment (verified via a separate base worktree); unrelated to this PR.
- [x] `pnpm build`
- [x] Added or updated high-quality tests that would catch regressions, or explained why tests were not needed

New coverage: terminal link source-owner precedence (pane PTY > explicit worktree owner > SSH > local, incl. local-under-focused-runtime regression), link open threading incl. the async preference hop, CLI tab create routing to the owning environment (+ local path), forwarding eligibility/timeout/error propagation, dispatcher-level forwarding, `tabList` proactive forwarding and degradation, web-session create return contract.

## AI Review Report

Reviewed the change for the main risks: ownership-resolution precedence (pane PTY wins over worktree owner so terminals actually spawned on the focused runtime in a local worktree still route remote), fallback safety (unknown worktree → local, matching pre-focus behavior), forward-loop risk between runtimes (remote servers never carry `activeRuntimeEnvironmentId`, so forwarded calls terminate), no behavior change when no environment is focused, and error-surface fidelity (remote failures propagate with their codes; list commands degrade to legacy local behavior).

Cross-platform compatibility checked: no keyboard shortcuts, path handling, or platform-specific UI was modified; the routing logic is platform-independent. `createWebRuntimeSessionBrowserTab` mirrors existing UI behavior on all desktop platforms. SSH-owned worktrees are explicitly classified and keep existing external-browser behavior per the SSH use case.

## Security Audit

No new input handling, command execution, or IPC surface: forwarding reuses the existing authenticated `runtimeEnvironments:call` channel (paired device token) with the same RPC method/params the caller was already authorized for. The renderer\u2019s remote-create path reuses the existing web-runtime-session RPC. No secrets, tokens, or user data are logged; forwarded params are validated again by the receiving runtime\u2019s zod schemas. Localization keys added for the two new user-facing error strings in all five locales.

## Notes

- `browser.tabSetProfile` on remote-hosted tabs returns a clear error (headless environments can\u2019t remount webviews for profile switches — pre-existing platform limitation), instead of the previous blanket "unavailable while a remote runtime is active" that also blocked local tabs.
- The old "Browser tabs/profiles are unavailable while a remote runtime is active" catalog strings are now unused in code; left in the locale files (harmless) to keep the diff focused.
- Follow-up worth considering: per-worktree host awareness in `browser.profile*` CLI listing while a runtime is focused (out of scope here).

## ELI5

With a remote runtime focused, local browser tabs and terminal links were blocked or mis-routed using global focus instead of the worktree that owned the request. Routing now follows the worktree’s owner so local and remote stay independent.

records.title: [Bug]: Browser tabs and terminal link clicks break for local worktrees while a remote runtime environment is focused
records.body:
### Operating system

macOS (reproduced here; the routing logic is platform-independent)

### Orca version

1.4.146-rc.0 (current main)

### Details

**Short summary:**
While a remote runtime environment is focused (e.g. a paired Mac Mini runtime), two related things break even for worktrees that are entirely local:

1. Agents cannot open links in the Orca browser via the Orca CLI. `orca browser tab create <url>` fails with `Browser tabs are unavailable while a remote runtime is active`.
2. Cmd/Ctrl-clicking an http(s) link in a terminal opens the system browser instead of an Orca browser tab, even though the terminal's worktree is local and `openLinksInApp` is enabled.

**What happened?**

- In a local workspace (repo and worktree owned by the local host), an agent asked to open a docs page in the Orca browser got the "unavailable while a remote runtime is active" error on every attempt.
- In the same configuration, Cmd-clicking a link printed in a local terminal opened the external system browser instead of an Orca tab.

**How can we reproduce it?**
1. Pair a remote runtime environment (Settings > Runtime environments) and focus it so `activeRuntimeEnvironmentId` is set.
2. Switch back to a worktree that is locally owned (no explicit runtime/SSH host).
3. Run `orca browser tab create https://example.com` → rejected with the error above.
4. Cmd-click an https link in a local terminal → opens in the system browser instead of Orca.

**Root cause (investigated):**

Routing decisions use the *global* runtime focus (`settings.activeRuntimeEnvironmentId`) instead of the owner of the worktree/pane the request came from:

- The renderer's `browser:requestTabCreate`, `browser:requestTabClose`, and `browser:requestTabSetProfile` IPC handlers blanket-reject whenever a runtime environment is focused (`isRuntimeEnvironmentActive()`). That guard predates headless remote browser panes (#1878 vs #5412) and blocks local tabs too.
- Terminal http-link paths (OSC 8, WebLinks addon, mouseup fallback) call `openHttpLink` without a `sourceOwner`, so it infers locality from the global focus flag.
- CLI browser automation commands (`browser snapshot/goto/click/...`) resolve only against the desktop-local CDP bridge, so remote-hosted tabs (which the UI already supports via `createWebRuntimeSessionBrowserTab`) can't be operated by agents driving the desktop runtime.

**Expected behavior:**

- Local worktree + focused remote runtime → local Orca browser tabs work (create/close/automate), and terminal links open in Orca.
- Remote-owned worktree → CLI browser commands route to the owning environment's hosted browser (mirrored into the desktop UI), matching what the UI's "New Browser Tab" button already does.

**Workaround:** switch the active execution host back to the local machine before opening links.

records.title: perf(terminal): avoid repeated pending drain snapshots
records.body:
## Description

- Replace the main-process local/daemon PTY renderer-delivery drain's per-flush `Map` snapshot and active/background partition with a map-backed intrusive queue.
- Keep one node per pending PTY across active, background, and ACK-blocked lanes while preserving authoritative `Map` order, active-first priority, two writes per flush, 16 KiB slicing, sequence metadata, hidden-output policy, renderer-credit gating, producer flow control, and final queued data before exit.
- Move pending-character accounting into the queue owner so enqueue, partial replacement, deletion, exit, and clear update the data, links, and total atomically.
- Harden synchronous reentrancy and lifecycle cleanup across renderer reload/crash, destroyed windows, provider teardown, active/hidden/interest changes, ACK/resync/heal/writeoff, partial drains, sentinels, exits, clears, and synchronous send failure.
- Leave relay and direct-SSH delivery code unchanged.

## ELI5

The old drain reread and reorganized the whole waiting list every time it was allowed to send two terminal chunks. The new drain keeps that waiting list organized as data arrives, so each flush can take the next eligible entries directly. It still uses the same two-chunk limit, timer cadence, ordering, credit checks, and exit behavior.

## Proof of zero regression

- Four adversarial design rounds with **GPT-5.6-Sol xhigh** and **Fable xhigh** ended `CLEAN`. The resulting design fixes queue/accounting ownership, live active reserves, round frontiers, settings invalidation, writeoff/credit wakeups, send-failure rollback, final-exit fencing, and cleanup before implementation approval.
- Adversarial implementation loops with both requested models ended `CLEAN`. GPT-5.6-Sol reviewed the implementation and its byte-identical rebase `CLEAN`; Fable also returned `CLEAN` on final exact head `ffc412ac73`. Together the reviews covered queue links and ownership, `Map` ordering, active/background/blocked transitions, ACK/resync/heal/writeoff recovery, hidden/readiness/settings gates, producer flow control, synchronous reentrancy, timers, send failures, exits, lifecycle cleanup, local/daemon/WSL integration, and unchanged relay/direct-SSH delivery.
- Final reviewed head `ffc412ac73` over base `559f04d297` is byte-equivalent to the prior reviewed implementation: both commits are `=` under `git range-diff`; binary diff SHA-256 is `530edc27644b040f8bf5a3d0ee51fab74a0574c9c6576840faf83cfd2e0a19cc`; stable patch ID is `410d00dde613f146b467eca3f83a6363c38d5b6d`.
- Frozen legacy-vs-queue differential oracles cover enqueue/update, partial drain, active priority, ACK gating and credit, hidden-interest changes, dropped sentinels, exits, clears, timer decisions, synchronous notification reentrancy, queue/accounting invariants, and bounded node churn.
- Focused four-file suite: **381 passed; 7 failed**. Related 20-file local/daemon/relay/SSH/renderer-credit slice: **744 passed, 6 skipped; 7 failed**. The exact seven failures are stale PowerShell spawn-argument fixtures and reproduce on untouched base `9ced27eca8` (**335 passed; the same 7 failed**).
- Full repository suite on final head: **3,327 files passed, 8 skipped, 4 failed; 35,478 tests passed, 60 skipped, 13 failed**. The seven PowerShell failures above and all six additional failures reproduce on untouched base behavior: five fail in isolated clean-base runs, and the sixth is a same-file mock-state leak that reproduces in the same clean-base combined run. The clean-base three-file reproduction matched all six exactly (**910 passed; the same 6 failed**).
- Fresh GitHub checks: **Windows terminal restart passed** and **packaged Windows crash-survival passed**. `verify` completed **35,507 passed, 84 skipped, 13 failed**; its failed-test names are exactly the same 13 clean-base-attributed tests above, with no drain-queue or differential-oracle failure.
- Full Node/CLI/web TypeScript check, touched ordinary and type-aware lint, formatting, max-lines ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. No max-lines bypass, threshold bump, or lint configuration change was added.
- Full `pnpm run lint` passed repository Oxlint, type-aware lint, styled-scrollbar checks, 48 reliability gates, max-lines, and bundled-guide verification, then stopped at the pre-existing released `orca-cli` revision-9 append-only manifest error.
- Main drift adjacent to provider shutdown was reviewed explicitly: local provider data remains live until physical `onExit`, final pending data still precedes `pty:exit`, daemon changes are spawn-only, WSL PTY routing is unchanged, and relay/direct SSH continue to bypass this queue.

## Proof of performance improvement

A deterministic production-limit oracle preloads **100 simultaneously pending, runnable, one-chunk PTYs** before the first flush and drains at the existing maximum of two writes per flush.

- Legacy snapshot selection: **2,550 pending-selection candidate visits** (`100 + 98 + ... + 2`).
- Intrusive queue selection: **100 selected-node visits**.
- Scheduled flush callbacks: **exactly 50 in both models** — one initial 2 ms flush and 49 one-ms continuations.
- The merged pending-character diagnostic path performs **zero full-map scans** during ACK updates; queue totals are checked against independent recomputation throughout the differential trace.

This claim is intentionally limited to selection traversal and pending-byte scan elimination for that main-process local/daemon workload. It does not claim measured wall-time, CPU, battery/power, OS wakeup, latency, throughput, memory, relay, or direct-SSH improvement; enqueue work and rare priority/policy invalidation relinks are outside the measured visit count.

records.title: fix(computer-use): settle Accessibility trust before failing on fresh helper processes
records.body:
## Problem

`orca computer permissions` reports `accessibility: granted` while every windowed action (`get-app-state`, `click`, …) fails `permission_denied` — the diagnostic says healthy while the tool is unusable. Filed as #9159, consolidated into #9458.

## Root cause (from the tccd IPC trace in #9458)

Every CLI invocation spawns a fresh, short-lived helper process. `tccd` answers a freshly spawned process with `preflight_unknown` / `do_not_cache` (`auth_reason=5`), so the first Accessibility answers a new pid sees can be **denied while the grant is real** — the same pid flips to granted moments later in the trace. One-shot checks therefore lose the race on every invocation:

- `AXIsProcessTrusted()` one-shots gate `buildSnapshot` and the permission-status printers.
- The AX window reads behind "app has visible windows but no accessibility window" hit the same uncached-denial window.

## Fix

- New `AccessibilityTrustSettling.settle`: probe immediately, then poll on 100 ms boundaries, capped at 1.5 s. Already-trusted processes pass on the first probe — **zero added latency on the happy path**; the cap only spends time in the exact state that used to hard-fail.
- Wired into: the `buildSnapshot` trust gate, both permission-status printers, and the "visible windows but no accessibility window" path — which now retries the actual AX window lookup (not just the trust bit) and reports how long reads stayed blocked if it still fails.
- Extracted `lookupUsableWindow` to dedupe the identical pre-/post-recovery lookup blocks.
- Deterministic unit tests for the settle policy via injected sleep (no timing flake).

## Validation

- `swift build` clean; full suite passes (37 existing + 4 new).
- The failure state reproduces 100% on one of our machines (every `get-app-state` → `permission_denied` with `permissions` → granted, matching #9458's trace signature). We could not E2E the patched binary against that machine's TCC state: a dev-built helper has a different code identity, so it gets a fresh TCC row rather than inheriting the raced one. Review therefore leans on the #9458 trace: answers change across probes within one pid, which is exactly what a bounded settle loop addresses. Happy to iterate if maintainers with a repro rig can run this against it.

Fixes #9458 (and the already-consolidated #9159).



## ELI5

macOS said Accessibility was allowed, but every computer-use click still failed right after a fresh helper start. The app now waits for that permission check to settle before giving up, so tools work once you have granted access.

records.title: feat(browser): choose where desktop browser tabs render
records.body: ## In plain English Interactive browser tabs opened from Orca Desktop render on that computer by default. Workspace-runtime browsing remains an explicit choice for remote/headless workflows. ## Summary - add an always-visible **Browser tab host** setting: **This computer** or **Workspace runtime** - apply one host policy to manual/keyboard tab creation, typed URLs, and routed links - default desktop clients to native local rendering while paired web clients remain runtime-owned - keep **Profile & Cookie Host** separate from tab execution - preserve the historical Shift escape hatch so runtime/SSH-owned links cannot be pulled into Orca merely by modifier inversion Explicit workspace-runtime selection remains authoritative and fails closed; Orca does not silently substitute local execution when explicit remote creation fails. ## Screenshots The body retains the related paired-session screenshot from #9758 as problem context: The setting and default were manually accepted on Linux in the equivalent feature build. records.title: Fix browser grab failing on Zone.js pages
records.body:
## Summary

Fixes issue #9947 where browser grab fails on pages using Zone.js-patched Promise. Zone.js replaces the global `Promise` with a non-native thenable; Electron's `executeJavaScript` boundary only unwraps native promises, so the wrapper object (with `__zone_symbol__*` fields) was serialized instead of the payload. Wrapping the promise-returning code in an async IIFE ensures it returns a native intrinsic promise that Electron always handles correctly.

## Screenshots

No visual change.

## Testing

- [x] Added high-quality regression tests thoroughly covering the ZoneAwarePromise scenario, including click, context menu, cancellation, and error paths
- [x] Tests verify the async wrapper produces a native promise, payloads cross the boundary correctly, and the raw Zone.js wrapper (regression case) is caught
- [ ] `pnpm build`

## AI Review Report

The fix is surgical: wrapping `AWAIT_CLICK_SCRIPT` in an async IIFE to ensure a native promise boundary crossing. Tests comprehensively model Zone.js's ZoneAwarePromise wrapper, verify all code paths (click, context menu, cancellation, rejection), and confirm serialization of the raw wrapper object is blocked.

Cross-platform verified: the fix is platform-agnostic—it addresses Electron's promise boundary and Zone.js behavior, not platform-specific paths, shortcuts, or shell behavior.

## Security Audit

No new attack surfaces. Error handling is preserved; input validation remains with `clampGrabPayload`. Tests verify correct boundary crossing for both valid payloads and error cases.

## Notes

This fixes compatibility with pages using Zone.js, primarily Angular applications. No impact on pages that don't patch `Promise`.

records.title: fix(session): preserve tab/editor/browser chrome when a repo's startup scan degrades
records.body:
Fixes #9972

Follow-up from the #9446 review.

## Problem
`hydrateWorkspaceSession` keeps persisted state for a worktree key when its repo is known but has no loaded worktrees and no authoritative detected scan (the #1158 graceful-degradation guard). The parallel hydrators — `hydrateTabsSession`, editor, and browser — lacked this guard and validated purely against `worktreesByRepo`, so a repo whose worktree fetch fails at startup (transient IPC/git error) had its unified-tab / editor / browser chrome dropped. Once `setHydrationSucceeded(true)` unlocks the session writer, that loss is persisted.

A terminal-free editor/browser workspace exposed a second edge: deriving degraded validity only from `tabsByWorktree` preserved its chrome in the parallel hydrators but still cleared the selected worktree.

## Fix
Extracted the #1158 validity computation into a shared `degraded-repo-worktree-validity` helper and applied it across all four hydrators. The workspace and tab hydrators now collect concrete persisted terminal, unified-tab, editor, and browser worktree keys, so terminal-free workspaces retain their selection without treating a stale selection-only ID as valid.

## Reliability contract
- **Invariant (`workspace-session.degraded-hydration-chrome-retention`):** a missing or non-authoritative repo scan cannot discard persisted terminal/tab/editor/browser state; an authoritative scan or removed repo still can.
- **Failure source:** #9972 / #1158 startup scan degradation.
- **Oracle:** deterministic full hydrate → persist → rehydrate tests cover mixed chrome and terminal-free editor/browser chrome; a negative test proves an authoritative empty scan removes the same state.
- **Gate:** no exact `config/reliability-gates.jsonc` entry exists; focused store tests are the executable gate, with live packaged startup fault injection remaining an accepted gap.
- **Provider/platform coverage:** the decision is pure persisted-state/catalog logic with no filesystem, process, path, Git, or local-host assumptions. Local, daemon, SSH, WSL, runtime, relay/mobile, macOS, Linux, and Windows routing/lifecycle behavior is otherwise unchanged.
- **Performance budget:** work is limited to existing startup/explicit rehydration calls and one linear pass over persisted workspace-key maps. It adds no polling, timers, IPC, provider inventory, subprocesses, store subscriptions, or render-path work.
- **Diagnostics:** existing authoritative worktree-purge diagnostics remain unchanged; deterministic tests identify degraded-retention versus authoritative-cleanup failures.
- **Residual gap:** no packaged-app fault-injection journey currently simulates a real startup scan failure.

## Verification
- `pnpm typecheck`
- 283 focused store/worktree tests
- changed-file `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check`
- `pnpm run check:reliability-gates`
- `pnpm run check:max-lines-ratchet`

records.title: Replicate hydrateWorkspaceSession's degraded-repo guard into tabs/editor/browser hydrators
records.body:
Follow-up from the #9446 review.

`hydrateWorkspaceSession` keeps persisted state for a worktree key when its repo is known but has no loaded worktrees and no authoritative detected scan (#1158 guard, src/renderer/src/store/slices/terminals.ts:2874+). The parallel hydrators — `hydrateTabsSession` (tabs.ts:1967), editor, and browser — lack this guard: they validate purely against `worktreesByRepo` and drop chrome for any unknown key. If a repo's worktree fetch fails at startup (transient IPC/git error), those hydrators discard its unified tab / editor / browser layout, and once `setHydrationSucceeded(true)` unlocks the session writer the loss is persisted.

Pre-existing gap (not introduced by #9446, which now prefetches all session-referenced non-runtime repos), but the fix is mechanical: extract the #1158 validity computation and share it across all four hydrators, with tests that a repo with a failed scan keeps its chrome through a full hydrate + persist cycle.

records.title: fix(browser): unstick Ctrl+Tab switcher when opened from a focused browser guest
records.body:
## Summary

Fixes the in-app browser's Ctrl+Tab tab switcher, which opened the MRU overlay but never committed or closed it, leaving it stranded on screen.

## ELI5

When you pressed Ctrl+Tab inside the built-in browser, the "switch tab" popup would appear and then get stuck open. Now it closes and switches tabs the way it should.

## Root cause & fix

In `setupGuestShortcutForwarding` (`src/main/browser/browser-guest-ui.ts`), the recent-tab-switcher chord handler called `event.preventDefault()` on the Ctrl+Tab keydown. In Electron, calling `preventDefault()` on the Tab keydown suppresses the subsequent Control keyup, so the overlay never received its commit keyup and stayed open. The fix removes `preventDefault()` from the keydown path (the commit keyup path still calls it), matching the existing main-window behavior in `createMainWindow.ts`.

## Evidence

Validated & rebased onto latest main during a bug-bash triage on 2026-07-23.

- Test files: `src/main/browser/browser-guest-ui.test.ts`, `src/main/browser/browser-manager.test.ts`
- On branch (fix present): 2 files passed, 79 tests passed.
- Fix reverted (test kept): 2 tests fail at `browser-guest-ui.test.ts:502` and `browser-manager.test.ts:2602`, both asserting `expect(keyDownPreventDefault).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`.
- Lint clean: `npx oxlint src/main/browser/browser-guest-ui.ts` reports no findings.

```
On branch (fix present):
  Test Files  2 passed (2)
  Tests  79 passed (79)

Fix reverted, tests kept:
  Test Files  2 failed (2)
  Tests  2 failed | 77 passed (79)
  - browser-guest-ui.test.ts:502  expect(keyDownPreventDefault).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
      -> expected not to be called, but called 1 time
  - browser-manager.test.ts:2602  expect(keyDownPreventDefault).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
      -> expected not to be called, but called 1 time
```

## Trade-offs

None — pure fix.

## Regression risk

Zero-regression: only the guest Ctrl+Tab keydown branch changes by dropping one `preventDefault()` call; the commit keyup path and all other input forwarding remain byte-identical, and the two updated unit tests prove both the fixed behavior and its absence when reverted.

_Credit to original author @Fazalkadivar21. Validated, rebased, and (where applicable) hardened via automated bug-bash review; original fix design preserved._

records.title: fix(browser): unstick Ctrl+Tab switcher when opened from a focused browser guest
records.body:
## Summary

Fixes #9937.

Ctrl+Tab from a focused in-app browser opened the MRU Switch Tab overlay but never committed or closed it, because guest `before-input-event` called `preventDefault()` on the Tab keydown and Electron then suppressed the Control keyup that should emit `ui:ctrlTabKeyUp`.

Stop preventDefault-ing that keydown in guest shortcut forwarding (same approach as the main-window path in `createMainWindow.ts`), so the existing IPC commit path can fire on modifier release.

## What changed

**Before:** Guest Ctrl+Tab keydown was `preventDefault()`-ed → guest keyups were dropped → overlay stayed stuck until focus left the browser tab.

**After:** Guest Ctrl+Tab keydown is forwarded without `preventDefault()` → Control keyup reaches the guest handler → `ui:ctrlTabKeyUp` commits/closes the overlay normally.

## Screenshots

No visual change (behavior-only fix for an existing overlay).

## Testing

- [ ] `pnpm lint`
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm test` (targeted: `browser-guest-ui.test.ts`, `browser-manager.test.ts` Ctrl+Tab cases)
- [ ] `pnpm build`
- [x] Updated unit expectations so guest Ctrl+Tab keydown must not call `preventDefault`

## AI Review Report

Root cause matches the documented main-window comment: preventing the held-chord keydown suppresses the modifier keyup and strands the overlay. Alternative approach in #9954 keeps `preventDefault` and blurs the webview so renderer DOM handlers own the rest of the gesture; this PR prefers the smaller change that removes the suppression trigger and stays consistent with `createMainWindow`.

Cross-platform: no new shortcuts/labels/paths; chord matching stays behind `matchesRecentTabSwitcherChord` / keybinding registry. Electron keyup-suppression after preventDefault is platform-independent (reported on Linux, same guest path on macOS/Windows). SSH unaffected (UI keyboard routing only).

## Security Audit

No new IPC channels or guest-supplied data paths. Change only removes `preventDefault` on an already-forwarded app chord; existing main→renderer `ui:ctrlTabKeyDown` / `ui:ctrlTabKeyUp` trust boundary is unchanged. Pages may observe Ctrl+Tab (previously swallowed); most pages ignore it.

## Notes

Related alternative: #9954 (blur webview + focus restore + E2E). This PR is the minimal main-window-aligned fix for the same root cause.

## Summary

Fixes #9937.

Fixed issue where the Ctrl+Tab tab switching overlay gets stuck when activated from within a browser window. 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e317b63e-673f-43bc-ac4e-da099ea48b8d


## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint`

- [x] `pnpm build`
- [x] Added regression tests:
    - New E2E spec `tests/e2e/browser-ctrl-tab-switcher.spec.ts` — reproduced the stuck overlay pre-fix (drives the real guest `before-input-event` path via `webview.sendInputEvent`), green post-fix: (1) opens from the guest and commits on modifier release; (2) advances while held, commits back to the browser tab, and returns focus to the guest page.
    - Unit: `RecentTabSwitcher.test.tsx` (webview blur on IPC open; focus-request restore on cancel), `browser-guest-ui.test.ts` (guest blur clears held-chord state).


## AI Review Report

Reviewed with Claude Code. The root cause was established empirically before writing the fix: an instrumented E2E run showed guest keydowns reaching `before-input-event` while every keyup after the prevented Ctrl+Tab keydown was suppressed, ruling out IPC wiring and renderer-listener explanations.

Risks checked:
- **Gesture correctness** — repeat keydowns, Shift-reversed direction, Tab-release-while-Ctrl-held (must not commit), Escape cancel, and window blur cancel all flow through the existing renderer handlers after the webview blur; no chord logic changed.
- **Focus lifecycle** — blur only fires when the switcher actually opened (guard on `switcherRef`) and the active element is a `<webview>`; restore targets the browser *page* id resolved from the tab (`activePageId`), matching what `BrowserPane` consumes. An earlier draft passed the tab id — the E2E focus-restore test caught it.
- **Stale state** — guest `blur` now clears `ctrlTabSwitching` so a later unrelated keyup can't emit a phantom `ui:ctrlTabKeyUp`; a phantom commit is additionally a no-op in the renderer (null switcher guard).
- **Non-browser guests** — simulator/emulator webviews still get the blur (commit works); source-restore is intentionally skipped when `activeTabType !== 'browser'`.

Cross-platform: explicitly checked for macOS, Linux, and Windows. No new chords or labels; matching stays behind `matchesRecentTabSwitcherChord`/the keybinding registry (`Ctrl+Tab` default on all platforms), the Chromium keyup-suppression behavior is platform-independent (bug reported on Linux, reproduced on macOS), and the change touches no paths, shell behavior, or platform-conditional Electron APIs. SSH use case unaffected — UI keyboard routing only.

## Security Audit

- **IPC**: no new channels; the fix consumes the existing main→renderer `ui:ctrlTabKeyDown`/`ui:ctrlTabKeyUp` events, which originate only from the main process's guest shortcut forwarding — guest page content cannot forge them and no guest-supplied data flows into the new code paths.
- **Input handling**: the renderer acts only on trusted store state (tab/page ids) plus `document.activeElement` tag checks; the guest keydown remains `preventDefault()`-ed, so pages still never observe the Ctrl+Tab chord.
- **Focus requests**: reuse the existing TTL-bounded `queueBrowserFocusRequest` path already used by the palette; ids come from the renderer store, not from guest content.






## ELI5

Ctrl+Tab from inside a browser tab could leave the tab switcher stuck on screen. Input is handled so the overlay closes when you release the keys, even when focus was in the browser guest.

records.title: Intermittent cross-worktree PTY teardown when opening an embedded browser
records.body:
## Summary

Opening an **embedded browser tab** inside Orca mass-killed **every agent PTY session across all worktrees** in a single ~1.5 s burst. The app did **not** quit, relaunch, crash, or reload — the main window stayed up the whole time. All running agents were lost mid-work.

This is **not** the auto-update path (stablyai/orca#8261): there was no update install, no relaunch, and the renderer process kept running continuously across the kill.

## Environment

* Orca **1.4.150** (build 1.4.150), macOS arm64, `/Applications/Orca.app` (packaged, not `--serve`)
* Shared local daemon (protocol v24), ~20 worktrees with live agent sessions

## Steps to reproduce (reported)

1. Have many worktrees open, each with a live agent terminal (Claude/Codex/etc.).
2. Open an **Orca embedded browser tab** (new web-page tab inside the app).
3. → All agent terminals across **every** worktree die at once; the app keeps running.

Reporter is confident the main window did **not** restart or flash and no update prompt appeared.

## Evidence (from `~/Library/Application Support/orca/logs`)

**daemon.log** — 25 sessions force-killed in ~1.5 s, spanning every worktree (session names redacted):

```
14:04:33.211  session-killed  <repo>/…@@…  immediate=true
14:04:33.300  session-killed  <repo>/…@@…  immediate=true
14:04:33.407  session-killed  <repo>/…@@…  immediate=true
...            (25 session-killed total, ~20 distinct worktrees)
14:04:33.721  session-killed  <repo>/…@@…  immediate=false   ← graceful close first…
14:04:33.927  session-killed  <repo>/…@@…  immediate=true     ← …then force-kill (two-phase)
14:04:34.417  session-killed  <repo>/…@@…  immediate=false
14:04:34.585  session-killed  <repo>/…@@…  immediate=true
14:04:34.9xx  session-exited  …  code=0     (for all)
```

The mixed signature — a **graceful** `immediate:false` **close-wave followed by forced** `immediate:true` **kills** — matches `runKillAllTerminalSurfaces()` (close terminal surfaces, then `killDaemonSessions()`), i.e. an app-surviving *global* daemon kill, **not** a per-worktree teardown (which force-kills only) and **not** `killAllPty()` (quit/updater only).

**Ruled out:**

* **Not the updater (**stablyai/orca#8261): no `updater.install` / `local_pty_kill_all` span anywhere near 14:04 (last update install was 07:59 UTC → 1.4.150); no relaunch.
* **Not an app quit / renderer crash / reload:** `renderer_memory` breadcrumbs are a continuous 60 s heartbeat straight through the kill — `14:04:04 → 14:05:04 → 14:06:04`, `usedHeapMB=631` flat, `browserWebviews=0`, `registeredBrowserGuests=0`, same process. A restart or reload would break the cadence and reset the heap.
* **Not a daemon restart:** no daemon `startup`/`shutdown` around 14:04; same daemon pid before and after.
* **Not a second/web client:** no new `client-hello`/disconnect near the kill — only the periodic `resolver-health-check` control client (5 min cadence). The 25 `kill` RPCs came from the desktop app's own daemon connection.

## Analysis / candidate mechanism

* The kill is an **app-surviving global daemon session kill**. In code the only match for "kill every daemon session while the app keeps running" is `runKillAllTerminalSurfaces` → `window.api.pty.management.killAll()` → `pty:management:killAll` (`src/main/ipc/pty-management.ts`), whose two-phase behavior matches the log signature.
* That function is currently only wired to **Settings → Manage Sessions → "Kill All Sessions"** (`useDaemonActions` / `ManageSessionsSection.tsx`) behind a confirm dialog — it is **not** on any browser path.
* The normal browser-open path does **not** touch terminals: `createBrowserTab` (`src/renderer/src/store/slices/browser.ts:486`) only appends a browser tab and reorders the tab bar (it explicitly preserves terminal ids), and the main-side browser guest lifecycle (`browser-manager.ts`, `orca-runtime-browser.ts`) never calls session/daemon kill.

So the **causal link between opening an embedded browser tab and the global kill is not yet explained by traced code** — the renderer emitted no breadcrumb for the triggering action, and the IPC/RPC that issued the kill isn't captured in the effect-span trace. Most likely culprits to investigate:

1. An error thrown during browser-guest attach that trips a renderer error boundary / recovery path which unmounts the terminal tree or invokes a kill-all recovery.
2. An accidental wiring or shortcut/command collision that reaches `runKillAllTerminalSurfaces` / `pty:management:killAll` on browser open.
3. A shared-state side effect in the browser slice that cascades into terminal-surface teardown.

An in-app repro with `pty:management:killAll` and `runKillAllTerminalSurfaces` instrumented (log the caller/stack) will pin it immediately.

## Impact

* **Silent, total loss of all running agents across every worktree** from a benign, common action (opening a web tab). No confirmation, no warning.
* Compounds with the frequent RC auto-updates (each of which also nukes all agents via stablyai/orca#8261): users on this channel are losing all agents repeatedly per day.

## Related

* stablyai/orca#8261 — auto-update install kills all active PTY sessions (distinct: that path quits/relaunches; this one does not).
* stablyai/orca#8459 — force-kills live daemon sessions without confirmation (same "global force-kill of live sessions" family).
* stablyai/orca#9749 / stablyai/orca#8457 — other mass-kill-of-live-sessions paths.

## Asks

* Add caller/stack logging to `pty:management:killAll` and `runKillAllTerminalSurfaces` so the browser-open trigger can be captured.
* Guard the global kill so it cannot fire from anything but the explicit Manage-Sessions action (and require confirmation).

records.title: [Bug]: Browser Grab fails on Angular/Zone.js pages with "Guest returned invalid payload structure"
records.body:
### Operating system

Windows

### Orca version

1.4.150.0

### Details

#### Short summary

`Grab Page Element` fails after clicking a normal visible element on an Angular 20 page that uses Zone.js:

```text
Grab failed: Guest returned invalid payload structure
```

The same Orca build successfully grabs an element from `https://example.com`, so this appears to be page-runtime/framework specific rather than a general browser-grab failure.

#### Environment

- Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit
- Windows version: 10.0.26200 (build 26200)
- Orca: 1.4.150.0
- Target application: Angular 20.3.25 with Zone.js enabled
- Page type: a private Angular application login page (the private IP, credentials, and cookies are intentionally omitted)

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Run or open an Angular 20.3.25 application with Zone.js enabled.
2. Open one of its pages in Orca's built-in browser.
3. Choose `Grab Page Element`.
4. Click a normal visible element on the page.
5. Observe `Grab failed: Guest returned invalid payload structure`.

Control check: repeat the same action on `https://example.com`; the grab succeeds.

#### Expected behavior

Orca should return the selected element payload and complete the grab on Angular/Zone.js pages.

#### Actual behavior

The click is captured, but Orca reports that the guest returned an invalid payload structure.

This is a normal selection, not a cancellation or teardown path.

#### Diagnostic evidence

On the affected Angular runtime, Zone.js has replaced the page-global `Promise` with a ZoneAwarePromise (minified constructor name `Z`). A minimal check using:

```js
const p = new Promise((resolve) => resolve({ page: {}, target: {} }));
```

produces:

```json
{
  "angular": "20.3.25",
  "promiseConstructor": "Z",
  "topLevelKeys": ["__zone_symbol__state", "__zone_symbol__value"],
  "wrappedKeys": ["page", "target"],
  "orcaWouldSeePage": false,
  "orcaWouldSeeTarget": false
}
```

`window[Zone.__symbol__('Promise')]` is present and points to the native Promise implementation.

#### Likely cause

The current grab flow calls:

```ts
await guest.executeJavaScript(buildGuestOverlayScript('awaitClick'))
```

The injected `AWAIT_CLICK_SCRIPT` creates its result with the guest page's global `new Promise(...)`. On a Zone.js page, that is a ZoneAwarePromise. It appears to cross the Electron `executeJavaScript` boundary as the wrapper object, whose direct keys are `__zone_symbol__state` and `__zone_symbol__value`, rather than as the resolved `{ page, target }` value. The main-side `clampGrabPayload` check then cannot find direct `page` and `target` fields and emits the reported error.

Relevant files:

- [grab-guest-script.ts](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/main/src/main/browser/grab-guest-script.ts)
- [browser-grab-session-controller.ts](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/main/src/main/browser/browser-grab-session-controller.ts)

#### Relation to the previous issue

This has the same final error text as #2783, but it is a different path from the cancellation case fixed by #3321:

- Orca 1.4.150.0 already contains the cancellation-marker guard.
- The error occurs after a normal element selection.
- The returned shape matches a ZoneAwarePromise wrapper rather than `{ __orcaCancelled: true }` or `{ message: "cancelled" }`.

#### Suggested fix / regression coverage

Please consider running the await-click code in an isolated world, or otherwise creating/returning the result through a trusted unpatched native Promise rather than the page-global Promise.

I would avoid fixing this by blindly unwrapping `__zone_symbol__value`, because page content is untrusted and can spoof those fields.

A regression test with a Zone.js/ZoneAwarePromise-patched page-global `Promise` should cover this case.

records.title: [Bug]: Ctrl+Tab Switch Tab overlay gets stuck open when focus is on the in-app browser tab
records.body:
### Operating system

Linux

### Orca version

1.4.150

### Details

# Summary

When focus is on an in-app browser tab and you press Ctrl+Tab, the Switch Tab (MRU) overlay opens as expected, but it does not switch to the selected tab. The overlay stays open indefinitely — it does not respond to key release, repeated Ctrl+Tab, or (as far as observed) Enter. The only way to dismiss it is to manually click over to another tab (e.g. a terminal tab) and press Ctrl+Tab again from there.

This does **not** happen when focus is on a terminal tab or other non-browser tab — Ctrl+Tab there opens and cycles the overlay normally.

# Expected behavior

Pressing Ctrl+Tab while focused on the in-app browser tab should open the Switch Tab overlay and switch to the selected tab on release/confirm, the same as it does from any other tab type.

# Actual behavior
- Ctrl+Tab opens the Switch Tab overlay while browser tab is focused.
- The overlay does not switch tabs and does not close on its own.
- It remains stuck open until you manually switch focus away from the browser tab (e.g. click a terminal tab) and press Ctrl+Tab again to dismiss it.

# Reproduction steps

1. In any worktree, open a terminal tab and a browser tab.
2. Click into the browser tab so it has focus.
3. Press Ctrl+Tab.
4. Observe: the Switch Tab overlay opens but does not switch, and stays open.
5. Manually click the terminal tab, then press Ctrl+Tab again — this dismisses the stuck overlay.
6. For comparison: repeat steps 2–4 while focus starts on a terminal tab (not the browser) — Ctrl+Tab works normally and switches tabs immediately.

# Additional notes

records.title: fix(browser): stop failing goto when a redirect or download aborts the load
records.body:
## What

Embedded-browser `goto` no longer reports a spurious failure when Electron `loadURL` rejects with `ERR_ABORTED (-3)` for a superseded or download-triggered load.

The abort path now distinguishes three outcomes:

- If another navigation is already loading, wait for it to stop and return its actual URL/title.
- If no replacement is loading, return the still-usable current page (the download-triggered case).
- If the page vetoed unload, the replacement failed, or the bounded wait timed out, fail closed.

Every non-abort `loadURL` error remains unchanged.

## Why

#9633 moved embedded `goto` from the daemon helper to direct `WebContents.loadURL`. Electron rejects with `ERR_ABORTED` when that load is superseded, even though the browser can continue to a usable replacement page. Surfacing that rejection directly caused successful SSO/login flows to report `Failed to navigate browser page ...: ERR_ABORTED (-3)`.

Testing against the pinned Electron 43.1.0 runtime also showed why a bare catch-and-ignore is unsafe:

- the rejected promise can settle before the replacement navigation lands, so immediately reading `getURL()` returns the old page;
- a page that blocks navigation in `beforeunload` also produces `ERR_ABORTED`, but the requested navigation did not happen.

The bridge therefore waits only when an aborted load has an in-flight replacement, uses `did-stop-loading` rather than polling, keeps the existing 30-second total budget, cleans up its timer/listeners on success, timeout, and destruction, and re-checks BrowserManager load state before reporting success.

## Tests

Added coverage for:

- superseding navigation abort → waits and returns the landed URL/title;
- download-triggered abort → returns the unchanged usable page;
- `beforeunload` veto → fails closed;
- failed replacement navigation → fails closed;
- replacement that never settles → times out, removes listeners/timer, and releases the command queue;
- ordinary non-abort navigation failure → still fails closed.

Verification:

- `agent-browser-bridge.test.ts`: 103/103
- related browser-manager/offscreen/runtime RPC suites: 83/83
- all TypeScript projects
- repository-wide oxlint (0 errors)
- oxfmt and `git diff --check`
- max-lines ratchet

A full local suite under unsupported Node 26 completed 33,665 passing tests; its unrelated failures were Node-24/environment-sensitive localStorage, inherited Git environment, and timeout tests. PR CI runs the supported Node version.

records.title: Remove host-blind lookups in SSH snapshot scoping, runtime events, and setup resolution
records.body:
## Context

Part of #9783 (follow-up from the #6030/#6031 supersession review; core multi-host state model landed in #6136). Same-id repos can legitimately exist on several execution hosts, and legacy projected setups reuse repo ids. Bare `repoId` or `setupId` lookups can therefore refresh, merge, or create on the wrong host.

This PR covers the renderer-side gaps (2–4). Gap 1 (`projectHostSetup` update/delete routing) still needs client/server host-perspective work and remains separate.

## Changed

- **Host-qualified refreshes:** `fetchWorktrees` accepts an explicit owner host and preserves it through runtime project refreshes, runtime change/activation events, SSH snapshot preparation, and SSH reconnects. Explicit owners remain authoritative if the repo catalog changes during an in-flight refresh.
- **Cross-host event isolation:** the worktree refresh queue keys by host and repo, so same-id events from two runtimes neither coalesce nor block each other.
- **SSH snapshot scoping:** snapshot merge, disconnect cleanup, and reconnect retry include only rows owned by the target SSH host. Legacy hostless rows are accepted only when the repo has one unambiguous owner.
- **Workspace creation:** target resolution pairs setups with repos by host plus repo id, preserves the resolved setup identity through composer state, and makes colliding legacy setup ids independently selectable in the Run on picker.
- **Option integrity:** host setup options require a matching repo on the same host; a same-id sibling repo can no longer make a stale setup appear runnable.
- **Performance:** refresh concurrency and per-host request coalescing remain bounded. Added host qualification is linear over already-enumerated repo/setup collections and constant-time on event queue operations.

## Review fixes added

The deeper review caught cases the first commit did not cover:

- runtime events fetched the correct repo catalog but then refreshed whichever host was focused;
- same-id runtime events were deduplicated across hosts;
- SSH snapshot preparation and reconnect refreshes were still host-blind;
- workspace resolution selected the correct setup but paired it with the wrong repo object;
- the composer discarded host identity after reducing the selection to a bare repo id;
- duplicate legacy setup ids produced duplicate UI keys/values and could not select the second host;
- explicit owner refreshes could fall back to local after an owner disappeared.

## Validation

Post-merge with current `main`:

- 7 affected Vitest files, **380/380 tests passing**
- `pnpm run typecheck:web`
- Oxlint on all 15 changed files
- `pnpm run check:max-lines-ratchet`
- `git diff --check`

A full-suite run during review completed 33,495 passing tests; its failures were unrelated local Node 26 / optional-native-package environment failures. The repository targets Node 24.

Credit: this lookup class was identified by @prateek in the #6030/#6031 stack.

records.title: fix(i18n): localize browser link-routing description
records.body:
## Summary

The **Link Routing** setting description (Settings → Workflow → Browser) was a hardcoded English template literal, so it bypassed the i18n catalog and stayed in English even when the UI language was set to a non-English locale — while its own title and every neighboring setting were already translated.

This routes the description through `translate()` with a `{{shortcut}}` interpolation (the platform keybinding stays a literal, uninterpolated value) and registers the string in every locale catalog.

Closes #9652

### What changed
- `src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-search.ts` — `getBrowserLinkRoutingDescription()` now calls `translate('auto.components.settings.browser.search.00f82a4c3d', <fallback>, { shortcut })` instead of returning a hardcoded template literal.
- `src/renderer/src/i18n/locales/{en,ko,ja,es,zh}.json` — added the new key. The key hash matches the repo's existing convention (`sha1(<relative file path>:<source string>)`, first 10 chars). `ko` is curated; `ja`/`es`/`zh` are included for catalog parity.
- `config/scripts/locale-ko-key-overrides.json` — added the curated Korean value so catalog regeneration (machine translation) preserves it.
- `src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-search.test.ts` — added a regression guard asserting the shortcut is interpolated (no raw `{{shortcut}}` leaks).

## Screenshots

> ⚠️ TODO (author): attach before/after screenshots of the Korean **Settings → Workflow → Browser → Link Routing** pane.

Before: description shown in English under Korean UI. After: description shown in Korean, with the platform shortcut label (`Shift+Ctrl+click` on Windows/Linux, `⇧⌘-click` on macOS) preserved.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm test` (scoped: `browser-search.test.ts` 2/2, `locale-ko-key-overrides` + `verify-localization-catalog` tests 4/4)
- [x] `pnpm build`
- [x] `pnpm verify:localization-catalog` (10,138 key references + es/ja/ko/zh parity verified)
- [x] `oxlint` clean on the changed files (pre-commit `lint-staged` oxlint + oxfmt passed)
- [x] Added a regression test for the interpolation behavior

Note: the full `pnpm lint` and `pnpm verify:localization-coverage` currently fail on `main` for reasons unrelated to this change (pre-existing `switch-exhaustiveness` errors in `skill-freshness-group.tsx` / `daemon-server.ts`, and unlocalized strings in the `ai-vault` session files). None of those files are touched by this PR.

## AI Review Report

Reviewed with an AI coding agent. Main checks:
- **Cross-platform (macOS/Linux/Windows):** the shortcut label is produced by the existing `getBrowserLinkRoutingShortcutLabel()` platform branch and passed as an interpolation value, so it stays literal and renders correctly per OS (`⇧⌘-click` vs `Shift+Ctrl+click`). No paths, shell behavior, keyboard-handling, or Electron main/renderer IPC were touched.
- **i18n correctness:** the new key follows the repo's hash convention (verified by reproducing an existing key's hash), placeholders (`{{shortcut}}`) are consistent across all five locales, and locale parity passes. The interpolation param name matches the placeholder.
- **SSH/remote & providers:** no runtime, process, git-provider, or network behavior involved — pure renderer copy.
- **Behavior:** no functional change beyond localizing an existing string; the fallback preserves the original English wording verbatim.

## Security Audit

No security-relevant surface. The change adds static i18n catalog data and one `translate()` call. No user input handling, command execution, path handling, authentication, secrets, dependencies, or IPC were added or modified.

## Notes

- `ja`/`es`/`zh` values are included to satisfy catalog parity; maintainers may prefer to regenerate them through the existing machine-translation pipeline. The `ko` value is curated and pinned via `locale-ko-key-overrides.json`.
- No changes to release/version files.
