records.title: Keep embedded browser commands on the registered Orca target
records.body:
## Summary
- make registered Electron webContents authoritative for embedded browser navigation and evaluation
- reassert the Orca CDP proxy on every helper-backed command so stale helper sessions cannot launch or control external Chrome
- fail closed on destroyed targets, stale debugger state, and helper-session cleanup failures

## Reproduction
A deterministic fake registers an Orca Electron webContents, initializes the helper, marks its session stale, and records helper calls without `--cdp`. Before this fix, `goto` and `evaluate` each produced one wrong-owner call:

```
--session orca-tab-tab-1 goto https://embedded.example/next --json
--session orca-tab-tab-1 eval document.title --json
```

The regression harness now proves both commands remain on the registered embedded target without launching a real browser.

## Validation
- real Electron E2E: create an actual embedded webview, initialize and terminate its real helper daemon, arm an external-launch sentinel, then verify `browser.goto` and `browser.eval` update the visible webview without launching the sentinel or recreating the helper
- browser slice: 28 files, 501 tests
- bridge suite: 95 tests
- full TypeScript typecheck
- touched-file oxlint
- reliability gates
- max-lines ratchet
- git diff --check

Fixes #9510

records.title: [Feature]: Context actions for commit files in Git History (Open Diff, Open in Browser, Copy path/hash)
records.body:
**Problem or use case**

When reviewing a commit in Source Control → Commits, there is no quick way to act on an individual changed file: opening its diff means expanding and clicking through, there is no way to open the file on the hosted remote (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket) at that commit, and copying the file path or commit hash requires leaving the panel.

**Proposed solution**

Add a right-click context menu to commit files in the Git History panel:

- **Open Diff** — opens the file diff at the commit, permanently.
- **Open in Browser** — builds the hosted URL (GitHub `/blob/`, GitLab `/-/blob/`, Bitbucket `/src/`) for the file at the immutable commit SHA and opens it in an Orca browser tab. Deleted files resolve at the parent commit path. If the commit is not reachable from any remote-tracking branch of `origin` (i.e. not pushed yet — the hosted URL would 404), the action shows a clear toast instead of opening the browser; if the repo has no supported hosted remote, a separate toast explains that.
- **Copy Relative Path** / **Copy Commit Hash** — clipboard actions with success toasts.

**Alternatives or additional context**

The hosted-URL resolution works for local, WSL, and SSH worktrees (the containment probe and remote URL read run on the host that owns the repo), and remote parsing supports HTTPS, SSH, and scp-like remote URLs. The SHA/host checks are validated at the IPC/RPC boundary.

records.title: [Bug]: Embedded browser commands can launch external Chrome instead of controlling the Orca webview
records.body:
### Operating system
macOS

### Orca version
current `main` (`d628c930`) / local branch `fix/orca-embedded-browser-no-agent-launch`

### Details
Short summary:
Browser automation commands that target an Orca-owned embedded browser tab can route through the external `agent-browser` helper instead of the registered Electron `webContents`. When the CDP handoff/session is stale, the helper can fall back to launching or controlling a separate local Chrome, so the command no longer affects the visible embedded browser in Orca.

What happened?
- An embedded browser tab is visible inside Orca.
- Commands such as `browser.goto` or `browser.evaluate` are expected to operate on that visible tab.
- On current `main`, `AgentBrowserBridge.goto()` delegates to `execAgentBrowser(sessionName, ['goto', url])`, and evaluate can also go through the helper path.
- If the helper's CDP target/session is stale, the operation may happen in a separate local Chrome/agent-browser target instead of the Electron webview.
- From the user's perspective, the embedded browser appears stuck or commands seem to affect the wrong browser.

Expected behavior:
For Orca-owned embedded browser tabs, commands that can be performed directly through the registered Electron `webContents` should stay in that webview. For example:
- `goto` should call `webContents.loadURL(url)` and return the webview URL/title.
- `evaluate` should use Electron debugger `Runtime.evaluate` against the registered `webContents`.
- These paths should not spawn the external `agent-browser` helper when a valid embedded tab target exists.

Why this matters:
The embedded browser is the UI the user sees and expects automation to control. Falling back to a separate local Chrome breaks that mental model and can make browser automation appear flaky or disconnected.

Suggested regression coverage:
Add tests that register a mock Electron `webContents`, run `evaluate()` and `goto()`, and assert that:
- `evaluate()` sends `Runtime.evaluate` through the `webContents.debugger` and does not call `execFile`/`agent-browser`.
- `goto()` calls `webContents.loadURL(url)` and does not call `execFile`/`agent-browser`.

A local branch has this shape after merging `main` into `fix/orca-embedded-browser-no-agent-launch`: keep embedded commands in registered Orca webviews and only use the external helper for commands that still require the agent-browser session/ref model.

records.title: fix(i18n): localize the Link Routing description in browser settings
records.body: ## Summary With a non-English UI language, the **Link Routing** description in Settings → Workflow → Browser rendered hard-coded English while every sibling string on the pane is localized. `getBrowserLinkRoutingDescription()` returned a bare template literal — because it interpolates the platform-specific shortcut label, the localization codemod never classified it as a candidate, so it never entered the catalog. This PR wraps the copy in `translate()` with a placeholder for the shortcut label and adds catalog entries for all five locales (`en`, `es`, `ja`, `ko`, `zh`), following each catalog's existing vocabulary. The same description feeds the pane's search entry, so settings search now matches the localized copy too. The entries originally shipped under the codemod's hash key with `{{value0}}`; after #10991 landed they were re-keyed to the hand-named copy-module convention — see **Update (2026-07-31)**. Three PRs independently fixed this bug; this one was kept, and #9681 (@Chang-Jin-Lee) and #9654 (@seandoesdev) were closed in its favour. From #9654 I ported the regression guard asserting the shortcut is actually interpolated — no raw `{{...}}` leaks into the rendered copy — generalized to `not.toMatch(/\{\{.+?\}\}/)` so it catches any placeholder name rather than one specific name. #9681 independently confirmed the same root cause and the same `{{value0}}` convention, which raised confidence in this approach. ## Update (2026-07-31) Two things happened after the sections below were written: 1. **#10991 landed on `main` and rewrote `getBrowserLinkRoutingDescription()`.** The description now has two variants — with the Shift-invert option on, the "always uses your system browser" sentence is dropped — and both variants were rebuilt as hardcoded English literals, which is exactly the regression class this PR's tests guard against. `origin/main` was merged into the branch (5e1c45fc9) and the localization re-applied onto the two-variant shape: the invert-off variant reuses the reviewed catalog values untouched, and the invert-on base sentence gets its own complete entry per locale (no suffix-stitching — sentence joining differs across locales, e.g. `ja`/`zh` join sentences without a space). 2. **The keys moved to the copy-module convention #10991 itself introduced** (73760e78a). The invert-on variant's text is byte-identical to the whitespace-compacted template head that produced `904ce58440` (per the derivation under **Notes**), so the codemod hash formula collides — it cannot key both variants. Rather than mixing one hash key with one hand-named key, both entries now follow the hand-named pattern of the #10991 copy module (`titleOrca`, `descriptionOrca`, `{{chord}}`): - `browser-link-routing-modifier-copy.ts` → renamed `browser-link-routing-copy.ts`, now carrying all Link Routing copy (description variants, shortcut label, modifier rows); - keys: `auto.components.settings.BrowserLinkRoutingSetting.description` / `.descriptionBase`, placeholder `{{value0}}` → `{{shortcut}}`; - catalog values moved verbatim in all five locales, so the reviewed translations are unchanged; - platform detection stays in `browser-search.ts` — the copy module keeps its resolved-arguments-only contract. Invert-on variant rendered output (the invert-off output is unchanged from the block under **Proof of fix**): ``` [en] Open http(s) links in Orca's built-in browser — from the terminal, markdown, and the editor. [es] Abre los enlaces http(s) del terminal, Markdown y el editor en el navegador integrado de Orca. [ja] ターミナル、Markdown、エディターの http(s) リンクを Orca の組み込みブラウザで開きます。 [ko] 터미널, Markdown, 편집기의 http(s) 링크를 Orca 내장 브라우저에서 엽니다. [zh] 在 Orca 内置浏览器中打开来自终端、Markdown 和编辑器的 http(s) 链接。 ``` Full gates at `73760e78a`: `pnpm lint` ✓ · `pnpm typecheck` ✓ · `pnpm build` ✓ · `pnpm test` 41,470 passed / 4 failed — all four unrelated to this diff: two in `src/relay/agent-exec-handler.test.ts`, which assert the exact spawned-process environment and fail identically on a pristine `origin/main` checkout under the same dev shell (it injects extra variables — e.g. `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` doubles under nesting); and two in `src/main/native-chat/transcript-watch-liveness.test.ts`, which pass 7/7 in isolation and fail only under full-suite parallel load. `verify-localization-catalog.mjs` ✓, and the Link Routing localization tests pass 15/15. ## ELI5 One line of text in the settings screen was written directly into the code instead of being put in the app's dictionary of translated phrases. Every other line on that screen was in the dictionary, so when you switched Orca to Korean, Japanese, Spanish, or Chinese, that one sentence stubbornly stayed in English. It got skipped because it has a keyboard shortcut glued into the middle of it, and the tool that collects text for translation didn't know how to handle that. Now the sentence lives in the dictionary too, with a slot where the shortcut goes — so it translates, and the shortcut still shows the right keys for your operating system. ## Proof of fix The pre-existing `browser-search.test.ts` could not catch this: English output is byte-identical before and after, so it passed on `main` either way. Added `browser-link-routing-localization.test.ts`, which switches the catalog through every non-English locale and asserts the copy actually changes and the platform label survives. Failing on `origin/main` (source + locales reverted to main, new test kept): ``` $ git checkout origin/main -- src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-search.ts src/renderer/src/i18n/locales/ $ npx vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-link-routing-localization.test.ts ❯ src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-link-routing-localization.test.ts (2 tests | 1 failed) 119ms × translates the description in every non-English locale on both platforms 31ms ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Failed Tests 1 ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ AssertionError: es/mac fell back to English: expected 'Open http(s) links in Orca\'s built-i…' not to be 'Open http(s) links in Orca\'s built-i…' // Object.is equality ❯ src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-link-routing-localization.test.ts:33:79 Test Files 1 failed (1) Tests 1 failed | 1 passed (2) ``` A second guard was added in `browser-search.test.ts` itself, so the file that previously *could not* fail on `main` now does. It switches to `ko` and asserts the rendered description equals the catalog entry with the shortcut interpolated: ``` $ git checkout origin/main -- src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-search.ts src/renderer/src/i18n/locales/ $ npx vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts \ src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-link-routing-localization.test.ts \ src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-search.test.ts × renders the Korean copy with the shortcut interpolated × uses the catalog key rather than an inline literal × translates the description in every non-English locale on both platforms Tests 3 failed | 3 passed (6) ``` With the fix restored, all six pass: ``` Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 6 passed (6) ``` Passing with the fix: ``` $ git checkout HEAD -- src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-search.ts src/renderer/src/i18n/locales/ $ npx vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts \ src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-link-routing-localization.test.ts \ src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-search.test.ts Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 4 passed (4) ``` The catalog key originally used here (`904ce58440`) is the one the codemod itself would generate — see **Notes** for the derivation, which is the load-bearing check on a PR like this. It has since been re-keyed to the hand-named convention (see **Update (2026-07-31)**). Both catalog gates are green: ``` $ node config/scripts/verify-localization-catalog.mjs Verified 10074 localization key references against en.json. Verified locale parity for es.json (10843 keys). Verified locale parity for ja.json (10843 keys). Verified locale parity for ko.json (10843 keys). Verified locale parity for zh.json (10843 keys). $ node config/scripts/audit-localization-coverage.mjs --check Localization coverage check passed with 0 allowlisted candidates. ``` Rendered output, all five locales × both platform branches: ``` [en] mac : Open http(s) links in Orca's built-in browser — from the terminal, markdown, and the editor. ⇧⌘-click always uses your system browser. [en] win : Open http(s) links in Orca's built-in browser — from the terminal, markdown, and the editor. Shift+Ctrl+click always uses your system browser. [es] mac : Abre los enlaces http(s) del terminal, Markdown y el editor en el navegador integrado de Orca. ⇧⌘-click siempre usa el navegador del sistema. [es] win : Abre los enlaces http(s) del terminal, Markdown y el editor en el navegador integrado de Orca. Shift+Ctrl+click siempre usa el navegador del sistema. [ja] mac : ターミナル、Markdown、エディターの http(s) リンクを Orca の組み込みブラウザで開きます。⇧⌘-click は常にシステム ブラウザを使用します。 [ja] win : ターミナル、Markdown、エディターの http(s) リンクを Orca の組み込みブラウザで開きます。Shift+Ctrl+click は常にシステム ブラウザを使用します。 [ko] mac : 터미널, Markdown, 편집기의 http(s) 링크를 Orca 내장 브라우저에서 엽니다. ⇧⌘-click을(를) 누르면 항상 시스템 브라우저를 사용합니다. [ko] win : 터미널, Markdown, 편집기의 http(s) 링크를 Orca 내장 브라우저에서 엽니다. Shift+Ctrl+click을(를) 누르면 항상 시스템 브라우저를 사용합니다. [zh] mac : 在 Orca 内置浏览器中打开来自终端、Markdown 和编辑器的 http(s) 链接。⇧⌘-click 始终使用系统浏览器。 [zh] win : 在 Orca 内置浏览器中打开来自终端、Markdown 和编辑器的 http(s) 链接。Shift+Ctrl+click 始终使用系统浏览器。 ``` ## Proof of no regressions ``` $ npx vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/renderer/src/components/settings/ Test Files 100 passed (100) Tests 610 passed (610) $ npx vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts config/scripts/locale-*.test.mjs config/scripts/verify-localization-catalog.test.mjs Test Files 7 passed (7) Tests 29 passed (29) $ npx tsc --noEmit -p config/tsconfig.tc.web.json # clean $ npx oxlint src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-search.ts \ src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-search.test.ts \ src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-link-routing-localization.test.ts # clean ``` No user-visible behavior changes beyond the fix. Under English the rendered string is byte-identical to before — the fallback preserves the original wording verbatim, so `translate()` returns the same characters. The only change any user sees is that the four non-English locales now render translated copy where they previously rendered English. The same function feeds the settings-search entry for this row, so search now matches on the localized copy too, which is the intended behavior for a localized description. ## Compatibility - **Platforms:** macOS / Linux / Windows — the shortcut label still comes from the existing `getBrowserLinkRoutingShortcutLabel()` platform branch (`⇧⌘-click` on macOS, `Shift+Ctrl+click` elsewhere) and is passed as an interpolation value, so it stays literal and is never translated. Per AGENTS.md the modifier is not hardcoded; the platform check is untouched. Verified by asserting both platform branches across all five locales, and that neither platform's label leaks into the other's copy. - **SSH / remote:** N/A — pure renderer copy. No process, path, git, or IPC behavior involved, so local, WSL, SSH, and relay runtimes are unaffected. - **Performance:** No hot-path change. One `translate()` call replaces one template literal, on a settings pane rendered on demand. The catalog entry adds ~140 bytes per locale, and the non-English catalogs are already lazy-loaded on language switch. ## Screenshots Before (Korean UI — the Link Routing description stays English): https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79ebc828-8046-4f1a-b7cf-607f669ae77b After (same pane — description localized, platform shortcut label preserved): The rendered-output block under **Proof of fix** covers the remaining four locales and both platform branches, which is not capturable in a single screenshot. ## Testing - [x] `pnpm lint` — the constituent gates covering this change all pass: `verify:localization-catalog`, `verify:localization-coverage`, and `oxlint` on the three changed files. The stale-base `lint:switch-exhaustiveness` caveat below is resolved — full `pnpm lint` is clean at 73760e78a (see **Update (2026-07-31)**). - [x] `pnpm typecheck` — all three projects clean at 73760e78a (see **Update (2026-07-31)**). - [x] `pnpm test` — scoped runs described below, plus the full suite at 73760e78a (see **Update (2026-07-31)**). - [x] `pnpm build` — passes at 73760e78a (see **Update (2026-07-31)**). - [x] Added or updated high-quality tests that would catch regressions — `browser-link-routing-localization.test.ts` fails on `main` and passes here; `browser-search.test.ts` gained a placeholder-leak guard ported from #9654. Commands actually run, in full: ``` node config/scripts/verify-localization-catalog.mjs node config/scripts/audit-localization-coverage.mjs --check npx vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/renderer/src/components/settings/ npx vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts config/scripts/locale-*.test.mjs config/scripts/verify-localization-catalog.test.mjs npx tsc --noEmit -p config/tsconfig.tc.web.json npx oxlint ``` `pnpm run lint:switch-exhaustiveness` reported one error in `src/renderer/src/components/skills/skill-freshness-group.tsx`, which this PR does not touch. It was an artifact of this branch's base being 499 commits behind `main`: `main` fixed that file in e133d93b7b. Resolved — `origin/main` was merged into the branch on 2026-07-30, and the command is clean at 73760e78a. ## AI Review Report Reviewed as maintainer with an AI coding agent, adversarially, against the three competing PRs for this bug. - **Cross-platform (macOS / Linux / Windows) — explicitly confirmed.** The shortcut label branches Mac (`⇧⌘-click`) vs non-Mac (`Shift+Ctrl+click`) in `getBrowserLinkRoutingShortcutLabel()`, and that branch is untouched by this PR. The label is passed as an interpolation *value*, so it is never sent through translation and cannot be corrupted by a translator. I verified interpolation on **both** platform branches in **every** locale — all ten combinations are in the rendered-output block under **Proof of fix** — and the test additionally asserts neither platform's label appears in the other's copy. Per AGENTS.md no `metaKey`/modifier is hardcoded. No paths, shell behavior, keyboard handling, or Electron platform APIs touched. - **Key-hash correctness:** the main risk on this PR, checked by reverse-engineering the codemod and re-deriving hashes from existing catalog entries. Two of the three competing PRs had keys the generator would not produce. Details in **Notes**. - **Translation quality:** each locale compared against sibling `browser.search` entries for house style and vocabulary. Korean particle handling was flagged by CodeRabbit and fixed in 1093c31d5 (`{{value0}}은 항상…` → `{{value0}}을(를) 누르면 항상…`), which reads correctly regardless of the trailing consonant of the interpolated label. - **Locale coverage:** all five catalogs carry a genuine translation, `zh` included — no English fallbacks left in non-English catalogs, which for this specific bug would have left the reported symptom visible to the user. - **Regression surface:** English output byte-identical; the settings-search entry consuming the same function was checked and its behavior change (matching localized copy) is intended. - **SSH / remote, providers, git version:** no runtime, process, network, or git-provider behavior involved — pure renderer copy, so none of these surfaces apply. ## Security Audit Thin surface, and honestly so: this is a string-catalog change plus one `translate()` call. No input handling, no command execution, no path handling, no authentication, no secrets, no dependency changes, no IPC. The interpolated value is a hard-coded platform label rather than user input, so `escapeValue: false` interpolation adds no injection surface. Nothing to follow up. ## Notes **Key-hash derivation — worth recording, because nothing in CI enforces it.** `localize-renderer-strings.mjs` derives auto keys as `sha1(":").slice(0, 10)`. The subtlety is *which* text. For a template literal, `stringParts()` emits the head plus every span, but `uniqueCandidates()` dedupes by `start:end:kind` — all parts share the same node range, so only the **head** survives — and `compactText()` (`/\s+/g → ' '`, then `.trim()`) runs before hashing. Two consequences: 1. The hash covers the **whitespace-compacted template head only**, so it is **independent of the placeholder name**. Renaming `{{value0}}` → `{{shortcut}}` does not change the key. 2. `verify-localization-catalog.mjs` never recomputes hashes — it checks key existence, placeholder consistency, and locale parity only. A wrong hash therefore passes review *and* CI, then orphans the entry (silently dropping every translation) the next time someone re-runs the codemod. Re-deriving over the `{{value0}}` keys already in this catalog confirms the form: restricting to keys whose head ends in whitespace (the only case where trimmed and untrimmed differ), the trimmed head reproduced **29/29** resolvable samples and the untrimmed head **0/55**. For this string that yields `904ce58440`, the key originally used here. `{{value0}}` is likewise the convention rather than taste — the codemod names interpolations positionally (`` `value${index}` ``), and across ~10.9k `auto.*` keys the placeholders are `value0` (769), `value1` (141), `value2` (30) and so on, with named placeholders only in the 218 hand-authored keys. **Superseded 2026-07-31:** this derivation is precisely why the hash scheme could not survive #10991 — the invert-on variant's text *is* the compacted template head, so its hash collides with `904ce58440`. Both entries now use hand-named keys in the #10991 copy-module convention, where named placeholders are the norm; see **Update (2026-07-31)**. The derivation above stays as the record of that constraint. Other notes: - Credit to @seandoesdev (#9654) for the placeholder-leak regression test, ported here and generalized to catch any placeholder name, and to @Chang-Jin-Lee (#9681) for independently confirming the root cause and the `{{value0}}` convention. - `config/scripts/locale-ko-key-overrides.json` was deliberately **not** touched. #9654 added an override entry for its key; that mechanism pins curated Korean against the machine-translation pass, and it is not needed here — only ~27% of the keys in this namespace carry one, and per the derivation above the hash does not vary with the placeholder name, so no regeneration path would clobber this value. - The stale-base caveat is resolved: `origin/main` was merged into the branch on 2026-07-30 (including the #10991 conflict — see **Update (2026-07-31)**), so the unrelated `skill-freshness-group.tsx` lint error no longer applies and `git merge-tree` remains conflict-free. - No platform-specific risks and no other follow-up work. Closes #9442 Closes #9652 Original patch by @m-a-king.

records.title: [Bug]: Link Routing description in Settings → Browser is not localized
records.body: ### Operating system macOS ### Orca version 1.4.146 ### Details Short summary: With a non-English UI language (e.g. Korean), the "Link Routing" description in Settings → Browser always renders in English, while every other string on the pane is localized. What happened? The Link Routing row's title is localized ("링크 라우팅"), but its description stays English: > Open http(s) links in Orca's built-in browser — from the terminal, markdown, and the editor. ⇧⌘-click always uses your system browser. Why (from reading the code): `getBrowserLinkRoutingDescription()` in `src/renderer/src/components/settings/browser-search.ts` builds this copy with a template literal (it interpolates the platform-specific shortcut label), so it never goes through `translate()` — the other five entries in the same file are all wrapped. The localization codemod that wrapped renderer strings only classifies string literals in user-visible positions (JSX attributes, `title:`/`description:` object properties, …), so a template literal returned from a plain function was never a candidate. The string is hard-coded English regardless of locale, and since it never enters the catalog, the translation pipeline can't pick it up either. How can we reproduce it? 1. Set the UI language to Korean (or any non-English locale) 2. Open Settings → Browser 3. The Link Routing description is English; every sibling description on the pane is localized

records.title: perf(mobile): route graph-sync snapshot fanout through the notify coalescer
records.body:
TITLE: perf(mobile): route graph-sync snapshot fanout through the notify coalescer
BRANCH: nwparker/perf-graph-sync-coalesce

## Description

Every `syncWindowGraph` call used to end with an unconditional `notifyMobileSessionTabSnapshots()` that re-serialized and re-fanned **every** worktree's mobile snapshot to **every** subscribed client — even when nothing a phone can see had changed. On a streaming agent (title/status spinner churn) this fires per graph sync, so a paired phone gets a full per-worktree stringify storm regardless of what actually changed.

This routes that fanout through the existing per-worktree `mobileSessionTabsNotifyCoalescer` and suppresses provably no-op work. All changes are in `src/main/runtime/orca-runtime.ts` (+ renderer revision reuse in `src/renderer/src/runtime/sync-runtime-graph.ts`):

- **Serve-hydrate fast path** — `hydrateHeadlessMobileSessionTabsFromWorkspaceSession` early-returns when `onlyServeOwnedTerminals===true`, there is no `offscreenBrowserBackend`, and the new `workspaceSessionHasServeOwnedPty` helper (next to `isServeOwnedPtyId`) finds no serve-owned PTY. That helper scans both `tab.ptyId` **and** every `terminalLayoutsByTabId[*].ptyIdsByLeafId` value — a strict superset of `hasServeOwnedPtyBinding`'s inputs — so it can never hide a real `orca serve` terminal (the common desktop case where the old loop built tabs only to drop them all).
- **Changed-worktree gating** — `syncMobileSessionTabs` now returns `Set<string>` of changed worktrees. `syncWindowGraph` (`orca-runtime.ts:3458`) schedules only those on the coalescer (50ms trailing edge, 250ms starvation cap) instead of the blanket fanout, kept after the leaves rebuild so the emit reads fresh leaf state. Gating is the union of stored-snapshot identity diff and a graph tab/leaf field diff (`collectMobileVisibleGraphChangedWorktrees`), a strict superset of `toMobileSessionTabsResult`'s graph-derived inputs.
- **Idempotent hydrate + content-based renderer revisions** — the headless hydrate keeps the existing snapshot object when the rebuilt serve/browser projection is structurally unchanged, and the renderer reuses its cached `(publicationEpoch, snapshotVersion)` for byte-identical per-worktree content so unchanged siblings don't mint fresh versions that would defeat the gate across the IPC boundary.

Removal frames still emit synchronously (with pending-notify cancel), runtime-initiated structural ops still emit immediately via `notifyMobileSessionTabsChanged(worktreeId)`, unsubscribe still `flushAll`, and the no-arg full-fanout path is untouched.

## Evidence

Independent end-to-end measurement (untracked deterministic vitest harness, fake timers + counters: renderer `buildMobileSessionTabSnapshots` → `OrcaRuntimeService.syncWindowGraph`, one subscribed listener that `JSON.stringify`s each emitted result; 6 worktrees, 120 graph re-syncs). BEFORE numbers came from re-running the same harness after `git stash` of the 3 tracked files.

| Workload (6 worktrees, 120 syncs) | Metric | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Steady desktop, nothing mobile-visible changes | emitted snapshots | 720 | **0** |
| | stringify bytes to phone | 414,624 B | **0 B** |
| One pane title changes every sync | emitted snapshots | 720 | **120** |
| | stringify bytes to phone | 415,663 B | **69,685 B** (~83% fewer) |

Honest scope: this helps the streaming-agent / title-spinner and idle-desktop cases the most — no-op syncs drop to exactly zero fanout, and real churn touching one worktree stops re-serializing the other five (720→120 emits). It does **not** reduce cost when content genuinely changes across many worktrees at once (every changed worktree still emits), and real changes always still propagate — the changed worktree emits every sync. The 50ms trailing edge now also applies to renderer-graph structural changes (desktop tab open/close reaching the phone), matching the already-accepted OSC-title window; the removal path stays immediate.

## Proof of no regressions

- **Typecheck**: `npx tsc --noEmit -p config/tsconfig.node.json --composite false` — exit 0, no errors.
- **Targeted tests** (vitest, `config/vitest.config.ts`): `graph-sync-mobile-snapshot-gating` + `mobile-session-tabs-notify-coalescer` + `mobile-subscribe-integration` + `sync-runtime-graph-key-reuse` + `web-session-tabs-sync` + `sync-runtime-graph(.test/browser/terminal-layout/scheduling)` + `rpc session-tabs(.test/move-validation)` = **206 passed, 2 skipped**; `orca-runtime.test` + `orca-runtime-terminal-cwd` = **761 passed**. New `graph-sync-mobile-snapshot-gating.test.ts` adds coverage for: serve pty via `tab.ptyId` and via layout-leaf-only map (superset proof), no-serve/no-backend skip, offscreen-backend browser tabs, changed-worktree-only fanout with silent sibling, renderer-reload epoch, restored-leaf pending-handle→ready flip, de-persisted serve/SSH tab drop, removal immediacy + pending cancel, and the 250ms starvation cap.
- **Lint**: `npx oxlint` on the touched files — exit 0, clean. `pnpm run check:max-lines-ratchet` — OK.
- **Behavior-equivalence (critical risk = phone goes stale on a real change)**: the fanout gate is a strict superset of `toMobileSessionTabsResult`'s graph-derived inputs (stored-snapshot identity diff ∪ graph field diff over `tab.title`, tab add/remove, `leaf.ptyId`, `leaf.connected`, `leaf.paneTitle`, leaf add/remove); false positives only cost a coalesced no-op emit. Non-graph inputs (OSC titles, PTY `agentStatus`, browser navigation) still emit via their own untouched paths. Renderer version reuse is content-based (`jsonContentEquals` over full projected tabs/groups/layout) and main keeps the stored version strictly monotonic, so a real change always crosses the web freshness gate.
- **Adversarial review**: 11 rounds run (GPT-5.6-Sol xHIGH). Earlier rounds surfaced and fixed real defects (IPC-boundary identity gate defeated by fresh clones, graph-only pending→ready staleness, mixed serve/renderer preservation dropping tabs, de-persisted serve/SSH tabs, serve-present no-op re-hydrate). The final **two** rounds were **clean** (2 consecutive), converging the loop, with typecheck + broad suites green. Independently re-verified: typecheck exit 0, 830 passed / 2 skipped.

## ELI5

Your phone used to get re-sent a fresh copy of **every** project's tab list every single time the desktop twitched — even when nothing you'd see had changed. Now the desktop only re-sends the one project that actually changed, and sends nothing at all when nothing changed. Real changes still show up on the phone, just without the wasteful spam.

Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) 🐋

records.title: fix(status-bar): tolerate missing provider snapshots
records.body:
## Summary

Fixes a status-bar crash that occurred when a rate-limit snapshot from an older main process omitted a provider key.

## ELI5

Sometimes the app's bottom bar asked for provider info that hadn't arrived yet and choked on the empty answer. Now it waits calmly instead of crashing.

## Root cause & fix

`isProviderConfigured` and `isProviderSnapshotPending` used a strict `provider === null` check, so an `undefined` snapshot (which happens when an older main process omits newly added provider keys) slipped past the guard and crashed on `provider.status`. The fix switches to a loose `provider == null` check so both `null` and `undefined` snapshots are treated as pending. Configured providers stay visible while their snapshot loads; unconfigured providers stay hidden. No provider payloads or IPC contracts change.

## Evidence

Validated & rebased onto latest main during a bug-bash triage on 2026-07-23.

- Test file: `src/renderer/src/components/status-bar/status-bar-provider-visibility.test.ts`
- Fix file: `src/renderer/src/components/status-bar/status-bar-provider-visibility.ts`
- On branch: all 29 tests pass.
- Reverting only the fix (keeping the new tests) reproduces the bug: 4 fail with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'status')`, including the older-main-process regression tests.
- Lint: `oxlint` on the fix source is clean; PR reports `pnpm typecheck` passing.

```
STEP 2a — on branch: Test Files 1 passed, Tests 29 passed.
STEP 2b — fix reverted: Tests 4 failed | 25 passed.
  TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'status')
  - getVisibleUsageProvider > creates a pending snapshot when an older main process omits a configured provider
  - isUsageEmptyState > treats provider keys omitted by an older main process as pending
```

## Trade-offs

None — pure fix.

## Regression risk

Zero-regression: the change only widens a null check to also catch `undefined`, so already-defined and `null` snapshots follow byte-identical paths. Behavior for configured, pending, and empty-state providers is unchanged and locked in by the passing 29-test suite. No IPC, payload, or platform-specific code is touched.

_Credit to @nsxdavid for the original fix. Validated, rebased, and (where applicable) hardened via automated bug-bash review; original fix design preserved._

records.title: fix: don't mint worktreeMeta from a sidebar sort-order snapshot
records.body:
## Summary

Stops a deleted or orphaned workspace from silently reappearing as a duplicate/"unknown" project whenever the sidebar snapshots its sort order.

**In plain terms:** the app was accidentally re-creating projects you had already deleted, just because it was saving the order they appear in the sidebar. It now only reorders projects that still actually exist.

**Root cause & fix:** Both `worktrees:persistSortOrder` (`src/main/ipc/worktrees.ts`) and `persistManagedWorktreeSortOrder` (`src/main/runtime/orca-runtime.ts`) looped over the renderer's `orderedIds` and called `store.setWorktreeMeta(...)`, which has no repo-existence check — it merges onto defaults and mints a fresh `instanceId` for any key. A stale id in the client's order (a repo removed elsewhere, or an already-orphaned id) therefore got re-created on every snapshot. The fix guards both call sites with an early `continue` on ids that have no existing `worktreeMeta`, so a snapshot can only reorder existing worktrees, never fabricate one.

**Trade-offs / regression risk:** None expected. Legitimate worktrees always have meta stamped before their order is snapshotted, so no real ordering is dropped. The guard only adds an early-`continue` on ids that lack existing meta — exactly the ids that previously would have been fabricated. Existing worktrees follow the identical `setWorktreeMeta` path as before.

Credit to @PannenetsF (Yunqian Fan) for the original fix. Validated and rebased onto latest main during a bug-bash triage on 2026-07-23; original fix design preserved.

## Screenshots

No visual change. The fix is entirely in the main process (IPC handler and runtime service); no renderer UI is touched. The observable behavioral effect is indirect: deleted/orphaned projects no longer resurface as duplicate/"unknown" entries in the sidebar after a relaunch.

## Testing

- [ ] `pnpm lint`
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck`
- [ ] `pnpm test`
- [ ] `pnpm build`
- [x] Added or updated high-quality tests for the change, or explained why not

Author-reported testing (I cannot run pnpm in this environment, so the unchecked boxes above reflect that the full gates were not confirmed as run):

- Added a guard regression test: `persistSortOrder only reorders existing worktrees and never mints meta for a stale id` in `src/main/ipc/worktrees.test.ts`.
- Author reports `src/main/ipc/worktrees.test.ts` passes on-branch (Test Files 1 passed, Tests 200 passed) and that reverting both fix files to `origin/main` fails the new guard assertion.
- Author reports `oxlint` on both source files and the test exits 0 (note: `pnpm lint` full run not confirmed, so left unchecked).

## AI Review Report

I reviewed this diff directly. The change is small and well-scoped: an identical early-`continue` guard added to two loops that call `store.setWorktreeMeta(...)`, plus one added unit test.

- **Correctness:** The guard `if (!store.getWorktreeMeta(id)) continue` correctly prevents minting new meta for ids without existing entries, which is the documented root cause. Both call sites (`worktrees.ts` and `orca-runtime.ts`) are guarded consistently.
- **Edge cases:** In `orca-runtime.ts`, the `updated` counter now only increments for ids that already had meta — this is the intended behavior (it should reflect actual reorders, not attempted ones). One minor consideration: the guard adds a `getWorktreeMeta` read per id inside the loop; for large `orderedIds` this is O(n) extra store reads, but sidebar orderings are small and this is negligible. Sort-order semantics (descending timestamps, `now - i * 1000`) are unchanged.
- **Cross-platform (macOS/Linux/Windows):** Confirmed checked. This is pure main-process JavaScript logic with no OS-specific code — no keyboard shortcuts, no shortcut labels, no filesystem path construction, no shell/command execution, and no Electron API surface that differs by platform. The worktree ids are opaque `${repoId}::${path}` strings compared by identity, not parsed as paths. No platform-specific behavior was touched.

No correctness or portability issues found beyond the negligible per-loop read noted above.

## Security Audit

Reviewed for security-relevant surface:

- **Input handling:** `orderedIds` from the renderer are treated as opaque keys and only used to look up / write store meta; the guard actually tightens input trust by rejecting ids that don't already exist. No new parsing or deserialization.
- **Command execution / shell:** None. No child processes or Git commands added.
- **Path handling:** None. Ids are compared by identity, not resolved as filesystem paths.
- **Auth / secrets / dependencies:** No changes.
- **IPC:** The existing `worktrees:persistSortOrder` IPC handler signature is unchanged; the change only makes it more conservative about what it persists.

No security concerns identified.

## Notes

- No platform-specific behavior; safe across macOS, Linux, and Windows, and unaffected by the SSH use case (main-process store logic only).
- Follow-up (optional, out of scope): the underlying `setWorktreeMeta` still has no repo-existence check of its own — this PR guards the two known callers rather than hardening the store itself, so any future caller must apply the same guard.

---

records.title: refactor(mobile): align browser keyboard with terminal via shared accessory bar
records.body:
## What

Align the mobile **browser tab**'s on-screen keyboard with the **terminal tab**'s so they look and lay out the same. Previously the browser used two fixed, non-scrolling rows (pointer modifiers + special keys) with their own key styling, while the terminal used a single horizontally-scrollable accessory bar — the two had drifted and duplicated styles.

## How

- New shared, descriptor-driven component `mobile/src/components/keyboard-accessory/MobileAccessoryKeyBar.tsx` with its styles as the single source of truth (moved out of `mobile-session-command-input-styles.ts`).
- Terminal session screen refactored to render its accessory keys (mode toggle, live-input toggle, Paste, built-in keys, custom keys, `+`) through the shared component — no behavior or appearance change. The keyboard-dismiss key stays inline/terminal-only (issue #5106).
- Browser dock now renders one shared scrollable bar above the type-on-page input. Pointer modifiers become sticky-active keys (reusing the terminal's active visual); special keys stay momentary. Built by a **pure, unit-tested** descriptor builder (`browser-keyboard-descriptors.ts`).
- Removed the browser-only `MobileBrowserKeyRow` and `MobileBrowserPointerModifiers` components.

## Visual (layout before / after)

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph Before["Browser dock (before)"]
    direction TB
    b1["Pointer modifiers row (fixed)"]
    b2["Key row: Enter / Backspace / Tab / Escape (fixed)"]
    b3["Type-on-page input + send"]
    b1 --> b2 --> b3
  end
  subgraph After["Browser dock (after) = terminal shape"]
    direction TB
    a1["Shared accessory bar (scrollable): modifiers + special keys"]
    a2["Type-on-page input + send"]
    a1 --> a2
  end
  Before -.align to.-> After
```

## Scope

Shell-only alignment. No terminal-specific behavior (live input, voice dictation, attach, custom keys) is ported to the browser — those have no browser analog or are separate features. The shared component accepts new descriptors, so browser buttons can be added in a follow-up PR without restructuring.

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` clean in `mobile/`.
- `pnpm test`: all pass, incl. 5 new descriptor-builder tests (order, modifier active state, momentary keys, glyph labels, disabled propagation). (2 pre-existing `happy-dom`-env errors in untouched terminal-webview tests are unrelated.)

## Screenshots needed (human visual check before merge)

Real device/simulator captures are not included yet — the browser-tab keyboard requires a paired desktop Orca session streaming a live browser, so it can't be captured in CI. Please attach:

- [ ] **Terminal tab** keyboard/accessory bar (baseline — should be unchanged)
- [ ] **Browser tab** keyboard bar (should be visually indistinguishable from the terminal's)
- [ ] Browser bar with a **pointer modifier selected** (active/highlighted state)
- [ ] Browser bar on a **narrow width** (confirm it scrolls horizontally like the terminal)

Repro: open a mobile session → Terminal tab (screenshot the accessory bar), then New Tab → Browser (needs a running desktop Orca with browser streaming) → focus the type-on-page input to reveal the bar → screenshot, tap a modifier, screenshot.

## ELI5

The mobile browser keyboard accessory matches the terminal's scrollable key bar instead of a separate fixed layout. Shared styling makes both tabs feel consistent and reduces duplicated UI code.

records.title: [Bug]: computer-use `permissions` reports accessibility granted while all `get-app-state` window reads fail permission_denied
records.body:
`orca computer permissions` reports `accessibility: granted` while every real `orca computer` window action fails `permission_denied`. The command you'd run to diagnose broken computer-use tells you it's healthy.

## Verified facts (no root-cause claim — see note)

Captured back-to-back on one machine, same moment:

1. `orca computer permissions --json` → `accessibility: granted`, `screenshots: granted`.
2. `orca computer list-apps` → **works** (enumerates running apps) — so some AX access is live.
3. `orca computer get-app-state --app <any windowed app>` → `permission_denied` for **every** app tried (Finder, TextEdit) — universal, not app-specific. Error text: *"…has visible windows but no accessibility window. …may need Orca Computer Use toggled off and on again in System Settings."*
4. A direct-exec of the helper binary in `--permission-status-file` mode also reports `granted` (attached and detached/`setsid` both).
5. Toggling the helper off/on in System Settings restored full function (previous session); it later regressed.

So: `permissions` and the helper's own status check agree on `granted`, `list-apps` confirms AX is partly live, yet reading any app's AX window tree is denied — and the diagnostic surfaces none of that.

## Note on root cause — I could not determine it, and retract an earlier guess

An earlier revision of this issue asserted the cause was the status probe launching the helper via `open -n` (LaunchServices) vs the runtime direct-exec'ing it, giving different TCC responsible-process attribution. **I tested that and it's wrong** — a direct-exec of the binary's status mode (attached *and* detached) also reports `granted`, so launch method is not the differentiator. I don't have a verified mechanism for why `list-apps`/`AXIsProcessTrusted` succeed while `get-app-state` window reads are universally denied; pinning it down needs instrumenting the live `--agent` process's AX calls at denial time and the Orca app's helper-spawn/entitlements design, which I can't do from outside. Leaving diagnosis to maintainers with that context.

## The user-facing ask (independent of mechanism)

Whatever the cause, `orca computer permissions` should reflect **real runtime capability**, not just the TCC-granted row: when the agent can enumerate apps but cannot read any AX window tree, `permissions` should report a degraded/actionable state (e.g. `granted_but_runtime_unavailable` with the "toggle off/on" hint the `get-app-state` error already emits) rather than a flat `granted`. Separately, the `get-app-state` "no accessibility window" → `permission_denied` mapping may be over-broad (it fires universally here) and could be worth distinguishing a true permission failure from a window-match failure.

## Environment

- Orca 1.4.143 (CLI `orca` → `/Applications/Orca.app/Contents/Resources/bin/orca`; production `Orca.app` running)
- macOS 26.3.1
- Helper: `/Applications/Orca.app/Contents/Resources/Orca Computer Use.app`
- Both `accessibility` and `screenshots` TCC rows show `granted`.

## Impact

`orca computer` agents/workflows are unusable (every window read denied) while `permissions` claims health and the one diagnostic command points the wrong way. Hit repeatedly during real multi-step automation.

records.title: computer-use spawns ~200 unmanaged helper processes/3h, causing 40-50GB+ memory usage and forced restarts
records.body:
## Summary

Orca's `computer-use` feature repeatedly spawns new child helper process instances instead of reusing an existing one. Each instance is explicitly excluded from RunningBoard/jetsam memory management, so macOS never proactively reclaims them. Over time this drives Orca's total memory footprint up to 40-50GB+ on a 16GB machine, ultimately triggering macOS's "Force Quit Applications — Your system has run out of application memory" dialog and requiring a full restart to recover. This has happened repeatedly (multiple restarts over the past ~24h).

## Environment

- Orca version: 1.4.142 (from a crash diagnostic captured during the incident window)
- OS: macOS 26.5.2 (Build 25F84)
- Hardware: MacBookPro18,1, 16 GB RAM, arm64e

## Evidence

**1. Force Quit dialog showing runaway memory**

Two separate screenshots (~2 hours apart) show "Orca (paused)" listed in Force Quit Applications at:
- 48.70 GB
- 54.83 GB

**2. `log show` reveals ~200 distinct unmanaged `computer-use` process instances spawned in 3 hours**

```
/usr/bin/log show --last 3h --predicate 'eventMessage contains "jetsam" or eventMessage contains "memorystatus"'
```

Filtering for unique `computer-use.<pid>.<pid>.<UUID>` identifiers in `runningboardd` log lines yields **200 unique instances** over a 3-hour window (~1 new instance every 54 seconds), each logged as:

```
runningboardd: (RunningBoard) [com.apple.runningboard:process] [app<application.com.stablyai.orca.computer-use.388334021.388334026.<UUID>(501)>:<pid>] Ignoring jetsam update because this process is not memory-managed
```

Sample of distinct UUIDs observed within the same parent coalition (388334021.388334026):

```
0045E532-E393-457E-907C-1F6720C77DCC
0202C128-C82A-4E56-B47B-8BBBC23294B8
02B243D4-5EAE-4B8D-922F-2079D074685E
0748271A-88D9-4F8A-90EF-8E3446AA3267
0CE1C91F-9AC6-4544-89A4-76651D8C12F9
10DFCDD4-150F-4CF3-8EFD-877F1E256572
... (194 more)
```

**3. Crash diagnostic flags excessive sustained disk writes from the main Orca process**

`/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/Orca_2026-07-16-214954_*.diag` (v1.4.142, PID 79823):

```
Event:            disk writes
Action taken:     none
Writes:           2184.27 MB of file backed memory dirtied over 9829 seconds (222.22 KB per second average), exceeding limit of 24.86 KB per second over 86400 seconds
```

Heaviest stack for the target process points into Electron's libuv write path:

```
uv_guess_handle + 48520 (Electron Framework + 32395452)
  write + 8 (libsystem_kernel.dylib + 18484)
```

7 separate Orca/"Orca Helper (Renderer)" `.diag` crash reports have accumulated in `/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/` over the past week.

## Expected behavior

`computer-use` helper processes should either be reused/pooled rather than spawned fresh every ~1 minute, or be properly registered with RunningBoard/jetsam so macOS can reclaim idle ones under memory pressure instead of accumulating unbounded.

## Actual behavior

Memory usage climbs unbounded during `computer-use` usage until the OS-level Force Quit dialog appears, requiring the user to manually kill Orca (and in this case, restart the machine several times) to recover.

## Impact

Multiple forced system restarts over ~24 hours due to total memory exhaustion, disrupting other running applications.

records.title: feat(computer-use): show a separate agent pointer on macOS
records.body:
Fixes #9126

## Summary

When Orca performs macOS Computer Use actions through Accessibility APIs or process-targeted Core Graphics events, the action succeeds without moving the native pointer, so the person watching cannot see what the agent is doing.

- Add an Orca-owned, click-through pointer overlay for click, secondary action, scroll, and drag operations
- Animate movement to the target, show a brief system-accent action/pressed state, support full-screen spaces and multi-display Quartz coordinates, and hide after 1.2 seconds of inactivity
- Keep the human's native macOS pointer untouched and preserve process-targeted input delivery to the selected application
- Keep the overlay outside Orca model screenshots by limiting both capture engines to the selected target window, without relying on legacy `NSWindow` sharing flags
- Authorize the exact shared dev launcher bundle id (`com.stablyai.orca.dev`) in addition to the existing per-worktree dev prefix, enabling live validation through the packaged helper

## Screenshots

Orca model screenshots intentionally omit this UI: both ScreenCaptureKit and the existing Core Graphics fallback capture only the selected target window, while the pointer is a separate helper-owned panel. This is a guarantee of Orca’s capture pipeline, not a claim that other screenshot or recording software cannot capture the overlay.

Manual visual validation was performed in the macOS dev build against Calculator. The agent cursor visibly moved through clicks on 7, 3, and All Clear while the Calculator display changed `0 → 7 → 73 → 0`; the native macOS pointer did not move.

## Testing

- [ ] `pnpm lint` — branch Swift files are outside the TypeScript lint paths; the current-main run stops on 2 untouched switch-exhaustiveness errors in `native-chat-session-option-labels.ts` and `skill-freshness-group.tsx`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [ ] `pnpm test` — 31,123 passed and 46 skipped; 23 unrelated local failures in untouched suites: 2 relay environment assertions caused by duplicated inherited Git config variables, 5 PTY shell-ready expectations, and 16 resource-sensitive relay/Git/SSH/OMP/node-pty timeouts or fd assertions while the dev app was running
- [x] `pnpm build` — desktop, web, universal macOS Computer Use helper, and notification helper
- [x] Added regression tests for pointer interpolation and Reduce Motion, Quartz-to-AppKit multi-display geometry, authenticated helper ownership, capture/input safety, and the shared dev launcher bundle id
- [x] `pnpm verify:computer-native` — 52 macOS Swift tests pass; Linux provider syntax/argument guardrails pass; app bundle/signature verification passes. Windows PowerShell parse/handshake checks were skipped locally because `pwsh` is not installed
- [x] Manual macOS dev validation against Calculator, including accessibility click actions and confirmation that the native pointer remains stationary

## AI Review Report

Reviewed the complete diff with Codex against the repository checklist:

- **Cross-platform (macOS/Linux/Windows):** the implementation is isolated to the macOS native Computer Use Swift package. No renderer shortcuts, shortcut labels, paths, shell behavior, or Electron platform branches changed. Linux and Windows providers are unchanged; Linux native guardrails pass locally, while Windows native checks remain for CI because PowerShell is unavailable on this Mac.
- **SSH/remote/local:** the overlay represents actions performed by the local macOS helper and adds no repository, filesystem, credential, or network assumptions. SSH and remote worktrees continue to use the same provider routing; no remote host behavior changes.
- **Agents/integrations/providers:** all agents using Orca's macOS Computer Use provider receive the same visible pointer behavior. No Codex-specific, integration-specific, GitHub-specific, or git-provider-specific path was added.
- **Performance and accessibility:** one panel/view is created lazily and reused. Movement uses at most 12 bounded interpolation steps; Reduce Motion jumps directly to the destination. Hide and pulse work is cancelable and coalesced, with no persistent timer or hot-path polling.
- **UI quality:** the cursor uses a high-contrast monochrome arrow and reserves the system accent color for transient action state, matching the style guide. The panel is non-activating, click-through, transparent, present across spaces/full-screen, and positioned with tested global-coordinate conversion.
- **Flagged and resolved during review:** native cursor warping was rejected because the agent needs a distinct pointer; input remains scoped with `postToPid`. The dev bundle authorization assertion was moved into the existing agent-entrypoint safety suite instead of being mixed into pointer behavior tests.

## Security Audit

- The overlay is a borderless non-activating panel with `ignoresMouseEvents = true`; its panel cannot become key or main and its view is excluded from the accessibility hierarchy.
- Model screenshots use an explicit selected-window capture scope. The helper-owned overlay is structurally outside both capture paths, and verification rejects reintroduction of legacy `sharingType = .none`.
- Mouse, scroll, Unicode, modifier, and key events are process-targeted through `postToPid(pid)`; verification rejects global event-tap posting and `CGWarpMouseCursorPosition`.
- The exact `com.stablyai.orca.dev` bundle id is added to the existing trusted dev-id set because the shared launcher uses that value; the existing peer command/path validation remains unchanged.
- An authorized, token-valid handshake claims helper ownership; closing that sidecar connection terminates the helper and releases the overlay. No new IPC methods, command execution, paths, secrets, dependencies, or persistent data were introduced.

## Notes

- This is intentionally macOS-specific. Linux and Windows Computer Use behavior is unchanged.
- The overlay is local UI even when the active Orca worktree is remote/SSH; it does not depend on remote display state.
- The existing `CGWindowListCreateImage` macOS 14 deprecation warning remains unchanged and is unrelated to this PR.

X (Twitter): [@dbachko](https://x.com/dbachko)

Generated with [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/)

## ELI5

When Orca’s agent clicks or drags on the Mac without moving your real mouse, you couldn’t see what it was doing. This adds a separate on-screen pointer overlay that shows agent actions so you can follow along.

records.title: [Feature]: Show a separate agent cursor during macOS Computer Use actions
records.body:
### Problem or use case

When Orca performs Computer Use actions on macOS, the action can be delivered through Accessibility APIs or process-targeted Core Graphics events without moving the system pointer. The action succeeds, but the person watching cannot see where the agent moved, clicked, scrolled, or dragged.

The visible indicator should be Orca's own agent pointer. It must not take over or move the native macOS pointer, steal focus, intercept input, or become part of screenshots sent back to the agent.

### Proposed solution

Render a separate, click-through pointer overlay from the macOS Computer Use helper:

- animate the agent pointer to click, scroll, and drag targets
- show a brief system-accent action/pressed state
- support global Quartz coordinates across multiple displays and full-screen spaces
- hide the pointer after a short idle period
- exclude the overlay from screen capture so model inputs remain unannotated
- preserve process-targeted input delivery to the selected application
- leave the user's native pointer untouched

### Alternatives or additional context

Moving the native pointer would make actions visible, but it would also disrupt the user's own cursor position and conflate the agent pointer with the human pointer. Annotating captured screenshots would expose the indicator to the model and change the visual input used for subsequent actions.

A GitHub issue/PR search did not find an existing request or implementation for this behavior.

records.title: fix(browser): local HTTPS Try HTTPS + cert proceed (#8454)
records.body:
### Description

Fixes #8454 — the built-in browser could not reach HTTPS-only local dev servers (e.g. `next dev --experimental-https`).

Two independent failures:

1. **Scheme-less loopback still defaults to `http://`** (no silent flip to HTTPS — that would break normal HTTP dev servers). After a **local HTTP failure**, the load overlay offers **Try HTTPS**.
2. **Self-signed / untrusted loopback certs** had no proceed path. Adds certificate-specific failure copy and **Proceed Anyway (Unsafe)** for `ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID` on eligible loopback hosts only (`localhost` / `*.localhost` / `127/8` / `::1`).

Approval is temporary and narrow: one WebContents × secure endpoint × leaf SHA-256 × error, in-memory only. A session `webRequest` gate contains Chromium’s certificate-cache so trust cannot leak to sibling tabs/assets/WSS. Desktop webviews and SSH/headless offscreen pages both supported (`browser.certificate.proceed` + `browser.certificate-trust.v1`).

**Credit:** Design + core implementation from [@AmethystLiang](https://github.com/AmethystLiang) in #9070. This PR rebases that work onto current `main`, resolves conflicts (markup mode, clicked-link frame routing, removed `serveSimStateWatcher`), and adds adversarial hardening (below). Supersedes #9070.

### Evidence (of fix — tests/commands before→after)

**Before (main / this worktree pre-fix):**
```text
$ pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/shared/browser-url.test.ts -t "normalizes manual local-dev"
✓ normalizes manual local-dev inputs to http
  localhost:3000 → http://localhost:3000/   # documents forced-http contract
# no certificate-error handler, no Try HTTPS, no Proceed Anyway
```

**After:**
```text
$ pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts \
  src/shared/browser-url.test.ts \
  src/main/browser/browser-certificate-trust-controller.test.ts \
  src/main/browser/browser-manager.test.ts \
  src/main/ipc/browser.test.ts \
  src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane/browser-load-failure-overlay.test.tsx \
  src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane/browser-notices.test.ts \
  src/renderer/src/components/tab-bar/tab-create-entry-classifier.test.ts \
  src/main/runtime/orca-runtime.test.ts \
  src/main/runtime/runtime-rpc.test.ts \
  src/renderer/src/store/slices/browser.test.ts \
  src/renderer/src/runtime/sync-runtime-graph-browser.test.ts

Test Files  11 passed (11)
     Tests  923 passed (923)
```

Still: scheme-less `localhost:3000` → `http://…` (intentional). New coverage for eligibility, HTTPS recovery URLs, grant isolation, conflicting-leaf proceed rejection, and overlay actions. Real-Electron e2e suite added at `tests/e2e/browser-local-https-certificate-trust.spec.ts` (not run in this agent pass; unit mocks alone do not replace packaged validation).

### ELI5

Typing `localhost:3000` still goes to plain HTTP first (most dev servers are HTTP). If that fails, a button lets you try HTTPS. If the HTTPS cert is self-signed and local, Orca shows a clear warning and a one-time “I understand, open it” button for **that tab only** — not a global “ignore all certs” switch.

### User-regression-tradeoffs

Ideally **zero** for normal workflows:

| Area | Tradeoff |
|------|----------|
| HTTP localhost | Unchanged default (`http://`) |
| Explicit `https://` | Still preserved |
| `file://` / UNC / absolute paths | Unchanged |
| Public HTTPS untrusted certs | Still blocked (no proceed) — intentional |
| Non-authority cert errors (date, name, etc.) | No proceed — intentional |
| Cross-tab trust | Blocked by request gate after grant |
| Persisted exceptions | None (cleared on tab close / process exit) |

### Adversarial review findings fixed (vs #9070)

- Pin accepted cert identity at **grant** time so a sibling tab with a different leaf cannot `proceed()` successfully after the first approval
- Drop stashed load errors on **navigation commit** so later `ERR_ABORTED` cannot restore an old overlay over a good page
- `registerGuest` IPC rejection → `false` so did-attach/dom-ready retry is clean
- Advertise `browser.certificate-trust.v1` whenever a browser backend can host pages (desktop or headless), not only offscreen
- E2E test server counts only `/` as document requests (favicon/probes 404)

records.title: Hidden Codex terminal can jump to scrollback top after reveal snapshot replay
records.body:
## Summary

In Orca 1.4.138 on macOS, a floating Codex terminal that has been hidden for a while can jump abruptly to the very top of its normal-buffer scrollback shortly after being revealed.

The terminal is initially interactive after reveal: wheel/trackpad scrolling works normally for a short period, then the viewport jumps to line 0 without a keyboard shortcut.

## Reproduction

1. Run Codex TUI in a floating terminal.
2. Hide or switch away from that terminal long enough for hidden Codex output to accumulate.
3. Reveal the terminal.
4. Scroll up/down with a mouse wheel or macOS trackpad.
5. After hidden-output snapshot replay finishes, the viewport may jump to the top.

The long-hidden condition is important; normal scrolling in a continuously visible terminal does not reproduce it.

## Root cause

applyMainBufferSnapshot() captures the scroll intent, queues several asynchronous xterm writes (including ED2 + ED3 + CUP and the serialized snapshot), then calls enforceTerminalWriteScrollIntent() immediately:

- src/renderer/src/components/terminal-pane/pty-connection.ts:5985 captures the intent.
- :6013 queues the normal-buffer clear.
- :6028 queues the snapshot.
- :6067 restores the viewport before xterm has parsed those writes.

xterm.write() parses asynchronously. After the premature restore runs against the old buffer, the queued clear/replay can later leave the reconstructed buffer at viewport line 0.

The normal foreground-output path already avoids this race: writeForegroundTerminalChunkWithIntent() enforces scroll intent from its onParsed callback (pane-terminal-output-scheduler.ts:863-872). Snapshot replay bypasses that ordering.

## Minimal reproduction

Using Orca current scroll-intent code with real @xterm/headless:

```text
immediate after replay writes are queued: viewportY=76, baseY=101, parsed=false
after xterm parsing completes:             viewportY=0,  baseY=501, parsed=true
```

Moving the same enforcement into the final write callback preserves viewportY=76 with baseY=501.

## Test gap

The existing test "preserves a scrolled-up viewport after hidden-backlog snapshot replay" makes the terminal write callback synchronous (pty-connection.test.ts:11571-11575). It therefore passes even though real xterm parsing is asynchronous.

## Expected behavior

Hidden snapshot replay is an internal content-recovery operation and should preserve the conventional terminal follow-output / scroll-lock state machine:

- If the viewport is at the bottom (`followOutput`), replay should finish at the latest output bottom.
- Once wheel/trackpad/scrollbar navigation moves the viewport away from the bottom (`pinnedViewport`), replay and new output must not steal that historical viewport.
- Scrolling back to the bottom should restore `followOutput`.
- Replay may refresh content and grow the scrollback range. It must not independently change the follow/pinned state.
- If the exact historical anchor was pruned, clamp to the nearest retained content; do not reset to line 0 merely because replay parsing completed later.

This matches common terminal behavior: output follows only while the viewport is at the bottom; explicit history navigation engages scroll lock. Typing/input-driven "snap to bottom" behavior is a separate policy and is not part of this bug.

## Suggested fix

- Finish parsing the replay writes before enforcing scroll intent; do not enforce against the pre-replay buffer.
- At replay completion, honor the latest scroll-intent generation. A wheel/trackpad/scrollbar action that occurred while recovery was in flight must win over an older captured intent.
- Preserve a logical history anchor where possible instead of blindly transferring an absolute `viewportY` across a cleared/rebuilt buffer.
- Add asynchronous regression coverage for:
  - `followOutput` remaining at the latest bottom;
  - `pinnedViewport` retaining history;
  - user navigation away from and back to the bottom while replay callbacks are pending.

## Environment

- Orca 1.4.138
- macOS 26.5.1 (Apple Silicon)
- Codex CLI 0.144.5
- xterm normal buffer (alternateScreen=false, mouse tracking disabled)

records.title: fix(browser): gate certificate proceed on runtime capability; dedupe cert-error helpers
records.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to the certificate-trust feature (issue #8454). Hardens the "Proceed Anyway (Unsafe)" affordance and dedupes the certificate-error helpers.

- **Gate proceed on runtime capability.** A remote runtime that predates `browser.certificate-trust.v1` cannot honor a proceed request, so `RemoteBrowserPagePane` now hides the proceed affordance until the connected runtime positively advertises the capability (probed via `runtimeEnvironmentSupportsCapability`). The error page still renders — only the unactionable "Proceed Anyway" button is suppressed. Desktop/built browsers advertise the capability whenever they can host a page, so the local HTTPS-dev-server case keeps its proceed button.
- **Single certificate-error normalizer.** Extracts `normalizeCertificateError` into `src/shared/browser-certificate-errors.ts` so the main-process certificate-error handler and the renderer overlay can never silently diverge on challenge matching (`browser-certificate-identity.ts` re-exports it for existing importers).
- **Centralize load-error redaction.** Both the `did-fail-load` path and the synthesized certificate failure now build load errors through one `BrowserManager.buildLoadError`, so Kagi session-token redaction can't be forgotten by a future call site.
- **Fail-closed logging.** The trust controller's catch now logs before answering `false`, so a throw during challenge recording no longer presents as "the cert prompt never appears" with no trace.

## Screenshots

No visual change in the supported case. In the unsupported-runtime case the "Proceed Anyway (Unsafe)" button no longer appears on the load-failure overlay.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint` (oxlint on changed dirs — no new findings)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` (web + node projects — clean)
- [x] `pnpm test` (`browser-certificate-trust-controller.test.ts`, `runtime-rpc-client.test.ts` — 34 passed)
- [ ] `pnpm build`
- [x] Existing unit tests cover the trust-controller fail-closed path and the capability-probe cache; the gating is a thin prop guard over already-tested surfaces.

## AI Review Report

Reviewed correctness of the capability gate, the helper extraction, and the logging change.

- Verified passing `certificateFailure={null}` suppresses **only** the proceed button — the overlay body is driven by `loadError`, so the error page still renders.
- Confirmed `browser.certificate-trust.v1` is a conditional capability (advertised whenever `canBrowse`), matching `browser.headless.v1`, so desktop/built browsers keep proceed while pre-feature remote runtimes hide it.
- Checked the `useEffect` probe has complete deps and a `cancelled` guard against out-of-order resolution.
- Confirmed all `normalizeCertificateError` importers still resolve after the move.
- Cross-platform: change is browser-pane/main-process logic with no new shortcuts, labels, paths, or shell invocations; no platform-specific branches touched.

## Security Audit

- Load-error redaction is now centralized, reducing the chance a future call site leaks a Kagi session token from an untrusted URL.
- The capability gate fails closed (defaults to unsupported, `.catch` → unsupported), so a probe error hides proceed rather than exposing an unactionable bypass.
- No new input handling, command execution, auth, or secret paths introduced. IPC surface is the existing `status.get` capability probe.

## Notes

The proceed affordance for the **local** webview pane (`BrowserPagePane`) is intentionally left ungated — the local runtime always owns its browser pages and advertises the capability.

records.title: [Bug]: Agent can miss the worktree-scoped Orca browser and choose the wrong control surface
records.body:
### Operating system

macOS

### Orca version

1.4.137

### Details

#### Summary

A coding agent running in an Orca-managed worktree can fail to select Orca's embedded-browser control path even when the user explicitly says "Orca browser." It may choose generic Chrome/CDP automation and then Orca desktop computer control before discovering `orca tab list`. In the observed case, the embedded browser and worktree targeting were healthy once the correct CLI surface was used.

This is distinct from browser command parity (#5705), general capability diagnostics (#5709), and browser/worktree visibility in the UI (#5095): the failure is choosing and discovering the correct control surface in an actual agent session.

#### What happened

- A supported coding agent was launched inside an Orca-managed worktree.
- That worktree already had an authenticated Orca browser tab open.
- The user explicitly asked the agent to drive the existing Orca browser tab.
- The agent invoked a generic browser automation skill and searched for a Chrome CDP endpoint.
- After correction, it inspected Orca's desktop UI using `orca computer`, which reflected whichever workspace was visible.
- Only after inspecting CLI help and running `orca tab list --json` did it find the correct worktree tab and control it successfully.

#### Expected behavior

When an agent running inside Orca is asked to use an Orca browser tab, the Orca-native route should be reliably discoverable and preferred. `orca tab list --json` and `orca snapshot --json` should be the initial path; attaching to Chrome or scanning the desktop UI should not be necessary.

#### Reproduction

1. Make both Orca's `orca-cli` skill and a generic browser-automation skill available to a supported coding agent.
2. Start the agent in an Orca-managed worktree with an Orca browser tab already open in that worktree.
3. In a long-running conversation where generic browser tooling may have been used earlier, ask the agent to drive the Orca browser tab that is already open and verify a page.
4. Observe that the agent may choose generic browser automation or computer-use instead of `orca tab list`.
5. Run `orca tab list --json`; the correct worktree tab appears and subsequent Orca browser commands work.

#### Confirmed during debugging

- The Orca-managed terminal had `ORCA_WORKTREE_ID` set.
- The installed `orca-cli` skill explicitly routes "Orca browser" requests to the Orca CLI and distinguishes the embedded browser from Chrome and desktop UI control.
- A generic browser skill can contain broader preference wording that competes with this routing.
- The live CLI correctly listed the open tab with the exact worktree binding.
- Focused CLI tests for browser targeting passed: 182 tests across `src/cli/browser.test.ts` and `src/cli/index.test.ts`.
- No backend browser-control or tab-discovery failure was found.

#### Possible direction, not an assumed fix

Consider giving agents a small session-scoped capability hint when Orca launches them. For example, when `ORCA_WORKTREE_ID` is present, an "Orca browser" request could be directed first to `orca tab list --json` and `orca snapshot --json`, with generic Chrome/CDP automation and `orca computer` explicitly identified as different surfaces.

An evaluation with competing browser skills in a long-running session may also be useful. Updating skill copy alone may not be sufficient because tool/skill selection remains model-dependent.

The reproduction has been anonymized; private URLs, local paths, page names, and session identifiers are intentionally omitted.
