records.title: [Bug] Sandboxed containers (with sshd) + browser mode: port forwarding not working
records.body:
<kbd>[![kenev](https://cdn.discordapp.com/avatars/109100933165662208/2ce062cc5951d81c113311702b4e18ef.webp?size=40)](https://discord.com/channels/1492228674081263786/1520558755970814053/1520558755970814053)</kbd> [kenev](https://discord.com/channels/1492228674081263786/1520558755970814053/1520558755970814053)  `via Discord`

Usually, I'm developing inside containers to obtain a sandbox environment. Looking at the docs, i think Orca doesn't support this out of the box.

The ideal architecture I want is like this:

Mac Orca -> remote linux machine -> container on the linux machine (this is where i want orca to connect)

Currently, what I've tried is roughly:

Mac Orca → SSH to remote Linux machine → `ProxyCommand` / `docker exec` → `sshd` inside a container

This works well for terminal access. Orca can connect to the container over SSH and it works.

The problem I hit was browser/design mode: if a dev server is running only inside the container, Orca needs to port-forward that service back to my local Mac. I don’t want to rely on Docker `ports:` mappings because they’re static, host-level.

The question is:

How are people achieving sandboxing in Orca with docker containers?

And how do you handle dynamic port forwarding for browser/design workflows?

I opened an issue describing the problem here: https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/6498

And I made a PoC PR that proves one direction locally: https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/6499

The PoC keeps the existing `ssh2` forwarding path, but for system SSH / `ProxyCommand` targets it uses managed `ssh -N -L` forwarding. It worked on my local setup, but I’m curious whether this is the right direction or if there’s a better abstraction for container-based sandboxing.

records.title: Fix browser pane stuck in HTML fullscreen (#6442)
records.body:
## Summary

Fixes #6442. A web app in an Orca browser pane could **enter** HTML fullscreen but not **exit** it: `requestFullscreen()` resized the host `BrowserWindow` into native fullscreen, and `exitFullscreen()` had nothing to restore — leaving the pane stuck fullscreen (only escapable via the native macOS control).

## Fix

Set `disableHtmlFullscreenWindowResize=true` in the `<webview>`'s `webpreferences` so HTML fullscreen is contained to the `<webview>` element rather than resizing the OS window. Exit then works and `fullscreenchange` fires with `document.fullscreenElement === null`, as guests expect.

This is the minimal approach (option 1) from the issue. Tradeoff: fullscreen fills the pane rather than the whole screen, but exit is reliable.

Note: the `webpreferences` key must be **camelCase** (`disableHtmlFullscreenWindowResize`) — Electron spreads the key verbatim into `WebPreferences`, so a lowercase key is silently ignored.

## Testing

- `pnpm typecheck:web` ✅
- `oxlint` on the changed file ✅
- Manual: repro HTML from the issue — Enter then Exit returns the pane to normal size and logs `exited OK`.

records.title: [Bug]: Browser pane ignores exitFullscreen() — web content gets stuck in fullscreen
records.body:
### Operating system macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 15 / Darwin 25.5.0) ### Orca version v1.4.101 (root cause also confirmed in the `main` source at v1.4.102-rc.0) ### Details **Short summary** A web app running in an Orca browser pane can **enter** HTML fullscreen but cannot **exit** it. `element.requestFullscreen()` works (the pane fills the whole screen), but a subsequent `document.exitFullscreen()` (and `webkitExitFullscreen()`) is ignored — the pane/window stays stuck in fullscreen. The only way out is the native macOS control (`Ctrl`+`Cmd`+`F` or the green traffic-light button). This affects **any** site that offers a fullscreen toggle (image/video viewers, slide decks, dashboards, etc.). **What happened** 1. Open any page in an Orca browser pane (mine was a local static page, but it reproduces on any site using the Fullscreen API). 2. Web content calls `documentElement.requestFullscreen()` → the browser pane goes fullscreen, covering the whole display (menu bar and Orca chrome disappear). ✅ as expected. 3. Web content calls `document.exitFullscreen()` (e.g. user presses the page's own exit button / `Esc` handled by the page) → **nothing happens**; the pane stays fullscreen. ❌ Expected: `exitFullscreen()` returns the pane to its normal size and fires `fullscreenchange` with `document.fullscreenElement === null`, exactly like a real browser. **How to reproduce** Save this as `fs-repro.html` and open it in an Orca browser tab. Click **1 (Enter)**, then **2 (Exit)**. The log will show `still full-screen` after step 2. The same file exits correctly in Safari/Chrome **and in cmux** (another Electron app with an embedded browser), so this is specific to Orca's webview fullscreen handling. ```html 


```

**Likely root cause (from the source)**

Browser panes mount an Electron `` tag in `src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane/BrowserPane.tsx` (around line 3612):

```ts
webview = document.createElement('webview') as Electron.WebviewTag
webview.setAttribute('partition', webviewPartition)
webview.setAttribute('allowpopups', '')
```

The `` sets `partition` and `allowpopups` but:

- does **not** set `webpreferences="disablehtmlfullscreenwindowresize=true"`, and
- there are **no** `enter-html-full-screen` / `leave-html-full-screen` listeners on the webview (none in `BrowserPane.tsx`) or in the main process (none under `src/main`).

So guest content falls through to Electron's default HTML-fullscreen handling, which resizes the **host window** into native fullscreen on enter. On exit there is nothing to restore the webview/window, so the pane stays stuck. (`grep -rn "disablehtmlfullscreenwindowresize\|enter-html-full-screen\|leave-html-full-screen" src` returns nothing on `main`.)

**Suggested fixes**

1. *Minimal* — make exit reliable by preventing the guest from resizing the host window:
   ```ts
   webview.setAttribute('webpreferences', 'disablehtmlfullscreenwindowresize=true')
   ```
   HTML fullscreen then fills the `` element instead of the OS window, and `exitFullscreen()` works. (Tradeoff: fullscreen fills the pane, not the whole screen.)

2. *Full whole-screen support* — listen for `enter-html-full-screen` / `leave-html-full-screen` on the webview's `webContents` (or as DOM events on the ``): on enter, expand the webview to cover the window (and/or set window fullscreen); on leave, restore the pane bounds. This gives true whole-screen **with** a working exit.

**Environment**

Electron `^42.3.3` (per `package.json`). Happy to open a PR for whichever approach you prefer.

records.title: fix(browser): keep webview guests alive across worktree switches
records.body: Electron `` guests are destroyed when their DOM parent is removed. When switching worktrees, `BrowserPane` chrome unmounts and previously tore down the webview, forcing a reload on return. Introduce persistent page viewports inside overlay slots so webviews stay in a stable parent without keeping the full React chrome mounted. On worktree switch, park hidden viewports instead of destroying guests; explicit close paths still call `destroyPersistentWebview`. Fixes stablyai/orca#6385 ## Summary - **Fix:** Browser tabs no longer reload when switching between worktrees/projects. A page you left open (e.g. a long-running QA session) keeps its loaded document, scroll position, and in-page state when you switch away and back. - **How:** Each browser page gets a persistent viewport shell under its worktree-level overlay slot. The `` guest lives in that stable DOM parent and is registered in the existing `webviewRegistry`. When `BrowserPane` chrome unmounts on worktree switch, the viewport is **parked** (`display: none`) instead of destroyed. React chrome (toolbar, address bar, find bar, overlays) continues to mount/unmount normally via `shouldMountPane`. - **Why not “keep everything mounted”:** We deliberately do **not** keep the full `BrowserPane` React subtree mounted for inactive worktrees. That caused performance issues (React reconciliation, event listeners, layout work for every hidden browser). Only the lightweight viewport shell + webview guest persist; the heavy chrome unmounts. - **Performance tradeoff:** Inactive worktrees still hold live webview guests (same memory/compositor cost as an open tab in a normal browser). We avoid the extra cost of repeatedly destroying/recreating guests and re-running full page loads. Hidden guests are parked and non-interactive (`display: none`, `inert`, `pointer-events: none`). ## Screenshots Behavior change only, same browser UI as before. Verified on macOS that pages render correctly after the fix (Google homepage and loaded sites display in the browser pane; no blank/white regression). No visual change to layout or chrome. ## Testing - [x] `pnpm lint` - [x] `pnpm typecheck` - [x] `pnpm test` — browser-pane suite: 112 tests passed (`src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane`) - [x] `pnpm build` — not run end-to-end in this session - [x] Added or updated high-quality tests that would catch regressions, or explained why tests were not needed **Manual verification (macOS, local dev):** - Open browser tab, load a real page (google.com / custom site). - Switch to another worktree, then switch back. - Confirmed via Electron CDP: same `getWebContentsId()` before and after switch (no guest recreation); URL and title preserved. - Confirmed viewport shell is visible and sized when active (`display: flex`, non-zero container rect). **New tests:** `browser-page-viewport.test.ts` covers viewport creation under slot root, chrome inset sync, layout show/hide, and park behavior. ## AI Review Report Reviewed the full diff with focus on Electron webview lifecycle, overlay-slot anchoring, and worktree switch paths. **Risks checked:** - **Webview reparenting:** Electron destroys guests on DOM parent change. Viewports are created once under the overlay slot root and never moved; `destroyPersistentWebview` only runs on explicit close. - **Blank-page regression:** Initial navigation must happen while the viewport shell is visible. `applyBrowserPageViewportLayout` is called in the webview lifecycle effect before `webview.src` is set, and again in a `useLayoutEffect` keyed on `slotViewportReady`. - **Focus on macOS:** `moveFocusToRendererBeforeWebviewDetach` runs before parking to avoid macOS reactivating the previous app when a focused webview is hidden. - **Drag/drop:** File drop handlers moved to native listeners on the persistent container via refs so they survive chrome unmount. - **Overlay stacking:** Page overlays (find bar, failure UI, annotations) portal into the persistent container; toolbar stays in React chrome with `pointer-events-auto`. **Cross-platform (macOS, Linux, Windows):** - No platform-specific code added. Uses standard DOM APIs (`ResizeObserver`, `inert`, `display`, `pointer-events`) available in Electron’s Chromium on all platforms. - No keyboard shortcut, menu accelerator, or path-handling changes. - Electron `` OOPIF behavior is the same across Orca’s desktop targets; the persistent-parent pattern applies uniformly. - Remote/SSH browser path (`RemoteBrowserPagePane`) is untouched. **Not flagged / verified:** - `BrowserPaneOverlayLayer` slot viewport ref registration is keyed by workspace tab id, matching existing overlay architecture. - `webview-registry.ts` teardown now also removes orphaned viewport shells on explicit close. ## Security Audit - **No new IPC surface.** Existing `registerGuest` / `unregisterGuest` paths unchanged. - **No command execution or shell invocation** added. - **No auth/secrets handling** changed. - **DOM/event handling:** Native drag/drop listeners on the viewport container only handle existing workspace file MIME types; same logic as before, moved to survive unmount. - **Input isolation:** Parked/inactive viewports use `inert`, `pointer-events: none`, and `display: none` so hidden guests cannot receive input. - **No new dependencies.** No security follow-up identified.

records.title: [Feature]: Expose Orca browser tabs through a public CDP attach command
records.body:
### Problem or use case

This is related to #5610, but it may be worth tracking as a general Orca CLI/browser enhancement rather than only as an `agent-browser` provider integration.

Orca already appears to have the internal pieces:

- `AgentBrowserBridge` creates a per-tab CDP proxy for Orca browser commands.
- `CdpWsProxy` serves `/json/version` and `/json/list` on an ephemeral localhost port.
- Orca passes that proxy to its internal `agent-browser` invocation with `--cdp <port>`.

The missing public surface is a CLI/RPC command that starts or pins that proxy and returns an attach descriptor for external browser automation clients.

The agent-browser provider proposed in #5610 may also return a CDP WebSocket URL internally. This issue is about making that attach descriptor a stable Orca CLI/RPC primitive, so non-agent-browser clients do not need to implement or shell through the provider contract just to discover the same endpoint.

### Proposed solution

Add a command such as:

```sh
orca tab cdp --page <browserPageId> --json
```

or:

```sh
orca browser attach --worktree active --json
```

Example JSON shape:

```json
{
  "host": "127.0.0.1",
  "port": 54321,
  "cdpUrl": "ws://127.0.0.1:54321",
  "webSocketDebuggerUrl": "ws://127.0.0.1:54321",
  "browserPageId": "page_123",
  "worktreeId": "repo::/path/to/worktree",
  "profileId": "default",
  "capabilities": {
    "singleTarget": true,
    "supportsJsonVersion": true,
    "supportsJsonList": true,
    "supportsTargetCreate": false
  }
}
```

### Alternatives or additional context

## Why this matters

Some tools can use an `agent-browser` provider/plugin. Others only know how to attach to a browser through Chrome DevTools Protocol configuration: either a full CDP WebSocket URL or a `host:port` endpoint that supports standard discovery.

Today Orca exposes high-level browser commands (`snapshot`, `click`, `fill`, `goto`, `exec`) but not the lower-level attach descriptor needed by generic CDP clients.

## Acceptance criteria

- Orca can expose the selected browser tab's CDP proxy through a documented CLI/RPC command.
- The command supports active worktree/tab defaults and explicit `--worktree` / `--page` targeting.
- The JSON output includes both `host`/`port` and full CDP URL fields where possible.
- The output documents endpoint capabilities, especially whether it is single-target or browser-level.
- The proxy lifetime is explicit: either held until command exit, leased with a TTL, or released by a close command.
- SSH/remote usage is documented, including whether callers need port forwarding.
- Concurrent callers and stale tabs are handled safely.

## Follow-up / full browser-level endpoint

The existing internal proxy appears to be single-tab. That may be enough for clients that attach to one existing target, but not for clients that expect a browser-level DevTools endpoint with target creation.

A fuller version could expose a browser-level endpoint that maps:

- target list -> Orca browser tabs
- target create -> `orca tab create`
- target attach -> selected Orca tab CDP proxy
- target close -> `orca tab close`

That would make Orca's embedded browser usable by a broader set of external browser automation clients, without requiring every client to implement an Orca-specific provider.

records.title: Add an in-place screenshot markup tool to the browser pane
records.body: ## What this adds A screenshot-markup tool for the in-app browser pane. A new **Draw** button freezes the visible page into a still image and overlays a drawing surface for pen, highlighter, arrow, rectangle, ellipse, and text (color, thickness, font size, undo/redo, plus a select tool to move/restyle/re-edit shapes). **Copy markup** then puts the annotated PNG on the clipboard to paste into your agent. It's fully **opt-in** and additive — nothing changes unless you click the new button, and no existing flow is touched. ## Why When steering an agent against a live page, "make this look like X" is far faster to express by drawing on a screenshot than by typing it out. This turns the browser pane's existing "grab element → feedback" idea into a freehand markup pass, delivered through the same clipboard path the terminal already uses for pasted screenshots — so it works for local and remote/SSH agents alike. ## A note on scope (sorry for the surprise) This is a sizable, unsolicited contribution and I didn't open an issue first — apologies for dropping it without a heads-up. It's deliberately self-contained (all renderer-side, new modules under `browser-pane/markup/`, one small wiring change in `BrowserPane.tsx`) and opt-in, so it should be low-risk to evaluate or set aside. **I'm very happy to split it into smaller PRs, rework the UX, or close it** if it doesn't fit the roadmap — just say the word. ## How it works - The drawing layer is a renderer-side `` overlay — it never touches the page. Only the base image is environment-specific: local panes use `webview.capturePage()`, remote panes snapshot the displayed screencast ``. Compose + delivery are shared. - The composite is always a PNG within the clipboard handler's limits, copied via the existing `clipboard:writeImage`; pasting into the agent reuses Orca's clipboard-screenshot flow (which writes the temp file on the correct host for local or remote agents). - Drawing model, compositing, shape rendering, hit-testing, and text metrics are isolated, unit-tested modules; the editor logic is split into focused hooks. ## Testing - Unit tests for the drawing model (incl. undo/redo snapshots), compositing budget, shape rendering, hit-testing, and text metrics. - `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm test` pass locally. ## Compatibility / review notes - **Cross-platform (macOS/Linux/Windows):** renderer/canvas only; no platform APIs or paths. Undo (`Cmd/Ctrl+Z`) is platform-guarded via `navigator.userAgent`. - **Local / remote / SSH:** environment-agnostic by design — only the base-image capture branches (local webview vs remote screencast frame); delivery reuses the terminal's existing local/remote clipboard-image path. - **Agents / integrations / git providers:** provider-neutral; only adds a renderer tool and reuses the clipboard. - **Performance:** the overlay mounts only while active; the frozen base image and canvases are released on exit. No new IPC, polling, or watchers. - **Security:** no new IPC surface; the composite goes through the existing, size-limited PNG-only `clipboard:writeImage` handler. - **UI quality:** shadcn primitives + design tokens; verified across the draw/select/edit flows in light and dark. ## Screenshots X: @1shiharat

records.title: [Bug]: Orca embedded-browser cookie/session limitation? Cannot log to Auth0 apps.
records.body:
### Operating system

macOS

### Orca version

1.4.95

### Details

 Summary:
 Logging in through Auth0 Universal Login fails in Orca's embedded browser, both manually and via CLI automation. The same credentials and same URLs work fine in a normal desktop browser (Chrome/Safari).

 Steps to reproduce:
 1. Open an Orca browser tab to an app that delegates auth to Auth0 Universal Login.
      2. Get redirected through /auth/login → Auth0 /authorize (302) → /u/login (200). The login form renders correctly.
    3. Enter valid credentials and submit (manually, or via orca fill + orca click on Continue).
    4. Result: Auth0 returns its generic "Oops!, something went wrong" page with invalid_request: ... we couldn't find your session .... Never reaches the app.

 Auth0 tenant log for the failed attempt:
 type: "w"
 description: "A user has attempted to access a login page directly. This is not supported
 unless an 'Application Login URI' is set for your application, or a 'Tenant Login URI'
 is set for your tenant."
 user_agent: "Chrome 1.152.0 / Mac OS X 10.15.7"

 Diagnosis / evidence:
 - The redirect chain is structurally correct — /authorize is hit before /u/login (confirmed via orca network), so it is not a client-initiated "direct" navigation to the login page.
 - orca cookie get shows the Auth0 cookies (auth0, auth0_compat, did, did_compat) are present in the jar on dev-...us.auth0.com, all with SameSite=None; Secure.
 - Despite being present, the Auth0 transaction/session is not recognized on the login POST → Auth0 treats it as a sessionless "direct access." This strongly indicates the SameSite=None; Secure session cookie set by /authorize is not being sent back on the subsequent cross-document login POST inside Orca's webview.
 - This is not a port/callback-allowlist issue (no "Callback URL mismatch"; the login form renders) and not a credentials issue (verified working in a normal browser).
 - Failure is identical on localhost and on the deployed HTTPS env, and identical for manual vs. automated input → the variable is the Orca browser itself, not the app.

 Impact:
 Any app behind Auth0 Universal Login (and likely other SPA-based OIDC providers relying on SameSite=None transaction cookies) cannot be logged into or automated through Orca's embedded browser. This blocks end-to-end UI testing of authenticated flows.

 Likely root cause to investigate:
 Cookie policy in the embedded webview — SameSite=None; Secure cookies not being persisted/sent on cross-site requests in the automation context (third-party-cookie blocking, partitioned/CHIPS handling, or the webview not treating the navigation chain as same top-level site).

records.title: Add default browser action for terminal links
records.body:
## Description

Adds an **Open in Default Browser** item to the terminal right-click context menu when the cursor is over an `http`/`https` link. The item reuses the existing terminal link hit-testing (`getTerminalHttpLinkForMouseEvent`) to detect the URL under the pointer and routes it through the shared `openHttpLink` funnel with `forceSystemBrowser: true`, so it behaves exactly like Shift+click's system-browser path (including the loopback worktree-label rewrite for local dev-server links). Orca's default click behavior may open links in the embedded browser; this gives users an explicit, discoverable way to open a specific link in their OS default browser.

The item only appears when a link is actually under the cursor, and is separated from the rest of the menu.

### Scheme safety

The URL is scheme-restricted at two independent layers, so a terminal emitting hostile text (e.g. `file://`, `javascript:`, `smb://`, `vscode://`) can never reach `shell.openExternal`:
1. **Renderer** — `extractTerminalHttpLinks` only yields candidates that parse via `new URL()` **and** have protocol `http:`/`https:`.
2. **Main** — the `shell:openUrl` IPC handler re-validates the protocol before `shell.openExternal`.

## Evidence

- **Unit tests** (`terminal-url-link-hit-testing.test.ts`): hit-testing returns the URL under the cursor, returns `null` outside the link, resolves wrapped URLs from mouse coordinates, and **returns `null` for `file:`/`javascript:`/`smb:`/`vscode:` schemes**.
- **Component test** (`TerminalContextMenu.test.tsx`): the "Open in Default Browser" item is absent when no link is under the cursor and present (and fires its callback) when a link is set.
- **Live Electron check**: right-clicking a rendered `https://` link shows the item at the top of the menu; right-clicking empty space does not (screenshots attached in the takeover comment).
- `pnpm vitest` (14 tests), web typecheck, oxlint on touched files, and the localization catalog check all pass.

## ELI5

When you right-click a web link in the terminal, there's now an "Open in Default Browser" button. It only shows up when you're actually pointing at a link, and it only ever opens normal `http`/`https` web links — never anything sketchy the terminal might print.

## Trade-offs

- The menu item routes through the same code path as Shift+click, so any future link-handling logic (remote-runtime, localhost labels) stays consistent — no second code path to maintain.
- To keep `TerminalContextMenu.tsx` under the `max-lines` lint after adding the item, the quick-command row was extracted into `TerminalQuickCommandMenuItem.tsx` (behavior-preserving, no `eslint-disable`).
- New label translated in all five locales (en/es/ja/ko/zh).
- **No regressions**: existing terminal link click/Shift+click behavior is untouched; the added right-click work is deferred until the menu actually opens (skipped on the Windows right-click copy/paste path).

records.title: [Bug]: macOS computer-use get-app-state can time out on AccessKit-backed apps
records.body:
### Operating system

macOS

### Orca version

Not specified

### Details

Short summary:

`orca computer get-app-state --no-screenshot` can time out against a native macOS app that exposes a valid accessibility tree through AccessKit.

What happened?

The target app remained running and direct macOS AX traversal of the same app succeeded, but Orca returned:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "runtime_unavailable",
    "message": "The Orca runtime closed the connection before responding. Restart Orca and try again."
  }
}
```

How can we reproduce it?

1. Run a native macOS app with an AccessKit-backed accessibility tree.
2. Run:

```sh
orca computer get-app-state --app <app-name> --no-screenshot --json
```

3. Observe that the request may time out / close the runtime connection even though the target app is still alive and its AX tree is readable through direct macOS AX APIs.

Anything else that might help:

Sampling `orca-computer-use-macos` during the hung request showed time spent under:

```text
Provider.observe
Provider.buildSnapshot
TreeRenderer.render
isSecureTextElement
traitsFor
stringAttribute / boolAttribute / frame
AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue
```

This suggests the provider may be doing repeated serial AX attribute probes per element, including unsupported attributes. Some AccessKit-backed elements appear to respond slowly enough that the total snapshot exceeds the request timeout.

Possible fix direction:

- Cache AX attributes per element during one snapshot render.
- Use `AXUIElementCopyAttributeNames` to avoid probing attributes the element does not advertise.
- Only run secure-text heuristics for text/input-like roles.
- Avoid repeated role/title/description/value/frame/action reads for the same element.
- Return a partial/truncated snapshot on slow AX reads instead of failing the entire request.

records.title: feat(browser): built-in password manager for the embedded browser (autofill + save)
records.body: ## Summary Adds a built-in password manager to Orca's embedded `` browser: an encrypted credential vault, login-form detection, **click-to-fill**, **save-on-submit** capture, and a settings management UI. Enabled by default. This is **Spec 1 (core)** of a planned three-part feature. The two follow-ups — **import from other browsers** and an **OS-keychain bridge** — are intentionally out of scope here and will land as separate PRs that plug into the same vault. ## How it works - **Vault** (`src/main/browser/credential-vault.ts`) — credentials encrypted with Electron `safeStorage` (OS-backed key), persisted to a dedicated `userData` JSON file via atomic write (`0600` + temp-then-rename). Matching is by hostname (http/https kept distinct). One shared vault across all session profiles. - **Bridge script** (`src/shared/browser-password-bridge-script.ts`) — injected into an isolated world (`1208`, mirroring the existing annotation bridge at `1207`). Detects login fields, tags them, and emits detect/capture events via the established `console.debug(prefix+token)` → `console-message` channel. Re-detects on SPA navigation (debounced MutationObserver) and scroll/resize. - **Click-to-fill (security keystone)** — a small key affordance appears over the username field only when a matching credential exists. On selection, the renderer requests `browser:credentials:fill` with **IDs only**; the password is decrypted **in the main process** and injected straight into the guest's isolated world (dispatching real `input`/`change` events). **Stored plaintext never crosses into the renderer** — the only renderer-bound plaintext is the explicit per-row *Reveal* action in settings. - **Save-on-submit** — the just-typed password is held in a transient `useRef` (never React state, never rendered) and forwarded to main to encrypt only on explicit confirm. New → "Save"; changed → "Update"; identical → silent. - **Settings → Privacy & Security → Passwords** — master toggle (default on), searchable saved-logins list with per-row reveal/edit/delete, manual "Add login", and a clear warning that disables saving when `safeStorage` is unavailable (e.g. a Linux box with no keyring) — it never falls back to storing plaintext. ## Security model - Every credential IPC channel is gated by the existing `isTrustedBrowserRenderer` guard. - Stored passwords are decrypted only in main and injected main→guest; the renderer receives a boolean from `fill`, never the password. - Injected credential values are `JSON.stringify`-escaped; field selectors use `CSS.escape`; the per-tab token lives only in the isolated-world closure (the page's main world can't read or forge it). - `safeStorage`-unavailable never persists plaintext (vault refuses; UI disables add + edit-save). ## Cross-platform / SSH - `safeStorage` across macOS (Keychain) / Windows (DPAPI) / Linux (libsecret), with the no-keyring case handled. - No hardcoded modifier keys; paths via `path.join`. - The web/SSH preload client gets safe no-op stubs (autofill simply disabled there), so the remote path isn't broken. ## Scope (this PR) In: vault, detection, click-to-fill, save-on-submit, settings management UI, default-on toggle. Out (future specs): import from other browsers; OS-keychain read/sync; cross-frame/iframe login forms; auto-fill-on-load; auto-submit; master password; passkeys/TOTP/generation. ## Testing - Unit tests: vault encrypt/decrypt round-trip + hostname matching + new/updated/unchanged save logic + safeStorage-unavailable refusal (with a persistence-layer assertion that nothing is written); bridge script detection/capture/fill under happy-dom; pure message parser; fill controller; IPC trusted-guard coverage across channels (incl. reveal + mutation rejection). - `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint` clean; full `pnpm test` suite passing (the implementation was built test-first, task-by-task, with per-task review). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## ELI5 Embedded browser gets a built-in password manager: encrypted vault, click-to-fill, save on login, and settings UI. Import from other browsers and OS keychain are later follow-ups.

records.title: Harden mobile session tab sync: snapshot ordering, terminal create rollback + idempotency
records.body:
## Summary

The mobile file-tab close fix landed separately on main (a8feafe92), so this PR drops that overlap and keeps the remaining #5910 sync hardening that isn't on main yet:

- Mobile rejects strictly-older session-tab snapshots (by `publicationEpoch`/`snapshotVersion`) and tombstones just-closed tabs, replacing the 300ms blind refetch that raced closes back open.
- Terminal creation rolls back a half-created tab when its surface never publishes, and dedupes retries via a `clientMutationId` idempotency key.

## Screenshots

No visual change (state-sync / behavior fix).

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` (node/cli/web)
- [x] `pnpm test` for the changed areas (orca-runtime 463 + the mobile snapshot-gate helper). The remaining local failures are unrelated Windows/locale environment tests (symlink privileges, WSL, locale-dependent labels) and are green on CI.
- [x] `pnpm lint` — oxlint, styled-scrollbars, and localization pass (the type-aware switch sub-check needs CI tooling locally; no switch statements changed)
- [ ] `pnpm build` (not run locally)
- [x] Added unit tests: snapshot reconciliation, create idempotency, create-rollback

## AI Review Report

Reviewed for correctness and regressions. Checked: out-of-order/equal-version snapshot handling plus tombstone TTL (an equal-version poll must still let tombstones expire), create rollback distinguishing reply-stage vs surface-timeout failures, and retry idempotency releasing on settle so failures stay retryable. Cross-platform (macOS/Linux/Windows): no hardcoded paths or shortcuts; logic is runtime-agnostic. Verified the change leaves the renderer-authoritative merge and headless/SSH terminal preservation intact, and does not duplicate a8feafe92's close routing.

## Security Audit

No new input handling, command execution, path handling, or secrets. The one new RPC field, `clientMutationId`, is length-capped (≤128) and used only as an idempotency key.

Rebased onto main after a8feafe92. Out of scope, left as follow-ups: pruning serve-owned terminals whose PTY has died, and a unified tab-readiness/generation protocol.

records.title: fix(jira): send non-browser User-Agent to avoid XSRF 403 on issue search/create
records.body: ## What this fixes Connecting a Jira Cloud site succeeds, but **no issues ever load** — every preset (Assigned / Reported / All Open / Done) and any JQL search shows *"No Jira issues found."* The same breakage silently affects creating issues, editing fields, commenting, and status transitions. ## Root cause Jira Cloud's XSRF filter rejects **POST/PUT** REST calls that carry a **browser `User-Agent`**, responding `403` with body `XSRF check failed` — even under valid API-token (Basic) auth. Orca issues Jira requests via Electron's `net.fetch`, which rides the Chromium stack and sends a Chrome `User-Agent`. That's why the failure looked so selective: - **GET** calls (`/rest/api/3/myself` during connect) are exempt from XSRF → connecting worked, so the UI reported "connected." - **POST** calls (`/rest/api/3/search/jql`, issue create, update, comment, transitions) all tripped the filter → 403. `searchIssues` treats a non-401 error as a soft failure and returns `[]`, so the 403 surfaced to users as an empty backlog rather than an error. ## The change Send an explicit non-browser `User-Agent` (`Orca`) on Jira REST requests, in both auth helpers (`jiraRequest` and `requestWithCredentials`) in `src/main/jira/client.ts`. This is the reliable, documented workaround for this Atlassian behavior; `X-Atlassian-Token: no-check` was tried and does **not** resolve this particular case. ~9 lines + a regression test. No API surface, type, or UI changes. ## Testing - New unit test asserts a non-browser `User-Agent` is set on outgoing Jira calls (`src/main/jira/client.test.ts`) — `12/12` pass in that file. - Verified live in a dev build against a real Jira Cloud site: before the change, all presets returned `403 / "XSRF check failed"`; after, issues load correctly across projects. - Full gate green locally: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`. ## AI code-review summary - **Cross-platform:** No platform-specific code; the header is set uniformly for macOS/Linux/Windows. No path, keyboard, or OS-API assumptions touched. - **SSH / remote runtime:** The change is in the local-runtime Jira client path; it adds a request header only and doesn't assume local-only execution. Remote-runtime RPC callers are unaffected. - **Git-provider compatibility:** N/A — Jira integration only; no source-control/review code touched. - **Risk:** Minimal. A static request header; no behavior change for already-working GET calls. Worst case is a server that dislikes the UA, which is far less likely than the current browser-UA rejection. ## Notes / possible follow-ups (not in this PR) - The `User-Agent` value is a plain `Orca`; happy to enrich it with the app version (e.g. `Orca/`) if preferred. - Separately, `searchIssues` masking a real error as an empty result made this hard to diagnose — surfacing search failures in the Tasks panel would be a worthwhile follow-up. Glad to open a PR for that if of interest. ## Screenshots Before: connected but every preset shows "No Jira issues found." After: issues populate across projects. (Adding before/after screenshots to the PR conversation.) --- 🐳 Submitted by the **Orca Whisperer** — chased this one from "connection bug" through XSRF to a one-line fix. ---

records.title: fix(daemon): reap dead terminal sessions and clear stale checkpoint flags
records.body: ## Summary The terminal **daemon** never reaped dead terminal sessions, leaking xterm scrollback for the lifetime of the (long-lived, survives-renderer-reload) daemon process. **Primary leak — `TerminalHost.sessions`:** sessionIds are minted fresh per pane and never reused, but the map only deleted entries on the same-id re-create path and full daemon dispose. On natural exit or kill, the dead `Session` stayed in the map, each pinning a `@xterm/headless` emulator with ~5000 rows of scrollback. Nothing reads a dead session's emulator (`getSnapshot` / `takePendingOutput` / `getForegroundProcess` / `listSessions` all skip `!isAlive`), so it was pure retained memory. This is exactly the "TerminalHost dead-session cleanup" that `Session.handleSubprocessExit`'s comment already anticipated but was never built. Fix: wire a `Session` `onExit` hook to `TerminalHost.reapSession`, which disposes the emulator and removes the entry. Fires on natural exit and the kill-timeout `forceDispose` path; the immediate-kill path reaps inline (and now disposes its emulator for symmetry). `reapSession` no-ops on live/unknown sessions. **Secondary leak — `DaemonPtyAdapter.sessionsNeedingFullCheckpoint`:** the cold-restore reanchor path adds a sessionId to this Set, removed only when a full checkpoint actually completes. A cold-restored session that exited before its first checkpoint stranded a permanent entry. Fix: delete it in the `exit` event handler and the non-`keepHistory` shutdown path, next to the existing sibling deletes. No visual change. ## Evidence **Leak reproduced (before fix).** `terminal-host-session-reaping-leak.test.ts` spies on `HeadlessEmulator.prototype.dispose`; on the unfixed code the emulator is never disposed when a session exits or is killed: ``` × disposes the emulator and reaps the session when its subprocess exits × does not retain dead-session emulators across many create/exit cycles × reaps a session killed immediately (forceKill path) AssertionError: expected "dispose" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times ``` And the checkpoint-flag leak: ``` × clears the pending full-checkpoint flag when a session exits AssertionError: expected true to be false // flag stranded after exit ``` **Resolved (after fix).** ``` ✓ terminal-host-session-reaping-leak.test.ts (3 tests) ✓ daemon-pty-adapter.test.ts › sessionsNeedingFullCheckpoint cleanup ``` **No functional regression.** The full daemon suite stays green, including the existing retention tests (`terminal-host.test.ts` "does not list exited sessions" / "skips forceKill on already-exited sessions" — their assertions are timing-agnostic and still hold): ``` Test Files 35 passed | 1 skipped (36) Tests 557 passed | 2 skipped (559) ``` Plus `oxlint` clean and node typecheck (`tsgo -p config/tsconfig.node.json`) passes. ## Testing - [x] `pnpm test` (daemon suite, 557 passing incl. new regression tests) - [x] `pnpm typecheck` (node project) - [x] `pnpm lint` (oxlint clean; pre-commit hook clean) - [x] Added regression tests that fail before the fix and pass after ## AI Review Report Found by an adversarial multi-agent memory-leak audit (collection-growth / dispose-never-called lenses) and verified by reading every post-exit reader of a session (all skip `!isAlive`) and every exit path (`handleSubprocessExit`, `forceDispose`, `forceKillAndDisposeSubprocess`). Key risks checked: (1) disposing the emulator too early — ruled out because no reader touches a dead session's emulator; (2) recycled-PID SIGKILL — `reapSession` uses `Session.dispose()`, which skips `forceKill` once `_state === 'exited'`; (3) mutating the session map during `host.dispose()` iteration — avoided by not firing the hook from `forceKillAndDisposeSubprocess`. Cross-platform: daemon PTY logic is shared across macOS/Linux/Windows; no platform-specific branches touched. ## Security Audit No input handling, command execution, auth, secrets, or IPC surface changes. Pure lifecycle/resource cleanup in the terminal daemon. Reaping reduces retained memory; tombstone/kill semantics are unchanged. ## Notes Highest-impact of the leak series — terminal scrollback is the largest per-entity payload and the daemon outlives renderer reloads. Reaping is deterministic on the dominant natural-exit and graceful-kill paths. Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) 🐋 ---

records.title: fix: dismiss stuck browser address bar autocomplete on webview click
records.body: ## Summary Clicking the loaded page in a browser tab could leave the address bar history dropdown stuck under the toolbar, with no way to dismiss it except refocusing the address bar and pressing Escape. The dropdown now closes when you click into the page, switch away from Orca, or press Escape. records.title: Browser & editor tab pin/color not persisted on remote-server (Orca server) worktrees
records.body:
## Summary

Terminal tab **pin** and **color** now round-trip through the headless host for remote-server ("Orca server") worktrees (persisted via `session.tabs.setTabProps`, survive snapshot rebuilds + server restart). **Browser** and **editor** tabs were intentionally left out of that work and still lose pin/color on remote-server worktrees.

This is a follow-up scoped out of the terminal/tab capability audit — the audit and fixes focused on terminal tabs, where the reported bugs were. It is **cosmetic / lower-severity**: pin/color on a browser or editor tab reverts on the next host snapshot and is not persisted across restart or surfaced to other (e.g. mobile) clients.

## Why it happens

The client unified-tab builders for browser/editor hardcode the props instead of deriving them from a host-authoritative source:

- `src/renderer/src/runtime/web-session-tabs-sync.ts`
  - `buildBrowserUnifiedTab` → `color: null`, `isPinned: false`
  - `buildEditorUnifiedTab` → `color: null`, `isPinned: false`

Unlike `buildTerminalUnifiedTab`, these map from `BrowserWorkspace` / `OpenFile` source objects that don't carry color/pin, and there's no host push path for them.

## What "done" looks like

Mirror the terminal-tab approach (already merged) for browser/editor tabs:

1. Carry `color` / `isPinned` on the browser/editor session-tab representation (or thread them via the existing `session.tabs.setTabProps` RPC, which is tab-id scoped and already handles any tab type host-side via `setMobileSessionTabProps`).
2. Populate them in the host snapshot builders for browser/editor tabs.
3. Map them in `buildBrowserUnifiedTab` / `buildEditorUnifiedTab` instead of hardcoding `null` / `false`.
4. Mirror the client pin/color actions for browser/editor tabs (TabBar pin already calls `setWebRuntimeTabProps`; verify it fires for non-terminal tabs and that the color setter path covers them).

Note: the host method `setMobileSessionTabProps` is already type-agnostic (matches by top-level tab id), so most of the remaining work is client-side plumbing + snapshot population.

## Severity / priority

Cosmetic, single-client revert. Safe to schedule as backlog.

Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) 🐋

records.title: Support direct agent-browser control of Orca browser tabs in addition to Orca CLI browser commands
records.body:
## Summary

Orca browser tabs can currently be automated through the Orca CLI browser command surface (`orca snapshot`, `orca click`, `orca fill`, `orca exec --command ...`). Add a way for users/agents to control the same Orca browser tabs directly with `agent-browser` as an additional path, not a replacement for the Orca CLI.

## Motivation

Agents that already have the `agent-browser` skill installed expect to use commands such as `agent-browser snapshot`, `agent-browser click @e1`, and `agent-browser --provider <name> ...`. Today, those commands do not know how to discover Orca browser tabs unless routed through `orca` commands.

This would let agents use the familiar `agent-browser` workflow against Orca's embedded browser while preserving the existing `orca` CLI workflow.

## Proposed shape

Implement an Orca-owned `agent-browser` provider plugin or equivalent provider entry point. agent-browser already supports `browser.provider` plugins that return a CDP URL. Orca already has an internal CDP proxy for browser tabs via the existing AgentBrowserBridge/CdpWsProxy path.

A possible flow:

1. User/Orca configures an `orca` agent-browser provider, for example `AGENT_BROWSER_PROVIDER=orca` plus an `AGENT_BROWSER_PLUGINS`/`agent-browser.json` entry.
2. `agent-browser --provider orca snapshot` invokes an Orca provider command.
3. The Orca provider command talks to the running Orca daemon/runtime, resolves the active worktree/browser page, ensures a CDP proxy exists, and returns `browser.cdpUrl`.
4. agent-browser connects to that CDP endpoint and runs its normal snapshot/interact workflow.

## Requirements / acceptance criteria

- Existing Orca CLI browser commands continue to work unchanged.
- The new path is clearly documented as an additional direct `agent-browser` integration.
- Users can run direct `agent-browser` commands against an Orca browser tab after setup, ideally with `agent-browser --provider orca ...` or plain `agent-browser ...` when Orca configures the default provider.
- Targeting should handle the active Orca worktree/browser tab and ideally support explicit browser page/worktree selection.
- The integration should consider SSH/remote runtime cases; a remote agent may not be able to reach a desktop-local `127.0.0.1` CDP proxy without forwarding or daemon brokering.
- The provider/attach lifecycle should avoid racing with existing Orca CLI browser commands and should clean up stale sessions/proxies.

## Notes

This likely does not require changes in agent-browser core. The cleanest first implementation may be in Orca: add a provider command that implements `agent-browser.plugin.v1` with `browser.provider` capability and returns the CDP URL for an Orca browser tab. A follow-up agent-browser docs/skill update could advertise the Orca provider once the Orca side exists.

records.title: [Bug]: Logitech MX mouse back side button does not work in the built-in browser
records.body:
## Operating system
macOS

## Summary
Logitech MX mouse back/forward thumb side buttons do nothing in Orca's built-in browser, even though they work in Chrome/Safari on the same Mac.

## Root cause (investigated)
This is **not** an Orca-specific bug — it is a macOS + Electron limitation, confirmed by instrumenting every input channel (guest `before-mouse-event`, `app-command`, guest DOM `mousedown`/`mouseup`/`auxclick`/`pointer*`, and `before-input-event` on both the guest and the host window). When the side buttons are pressed, **no event of any kind reaches the app** — no mouse button, no keyboard, no DOM event.

Why:
1. **macOS gives no navigation semantics to mouse buttons 4/5.** They arrive only as raw `NSEvent otherMouseDown` with `buttonNumber` 3/4, which most apps ignore.
2. **Logi Options+ default "Back/Forward" does not send a raw button** — it synthesizes a macOS 3-finger swipe gesture (`NSEventTypeSwipe`). Only apps implementing `swipeWithEvent:` (Chrome, Safari) receive it. That's why it works in Chrome.
3. **Electron does not forward that swipe to the renderer**, and Chromium does not convert it into a DOM event, so the `<webview>`/renderer sees nothing.
4. **Electron's `app-command` event (`browser-backward`/`browser-forward`) is Windows/Linux only — not emitted on macOS.** Electron's only macOS navigation event is `swipe` (trackpad-only).

This matches the upstream consensus: VS Code closed the equivalent request (microsoft/vscode#116507) as **as-designed**.

References: Electron docs (`app-command` = Windows/Linux, `swipe` = macOS); microsoft/vscode#116507; SensibleSideButtons technical writeup; Chromium `render_widget_host_view_cocoa.mm`.

## Fix
Since raw mouse buttons cannot be captured in-process on macOS without a native CGEventTap (Accessibility/Input-Monitoring permission, local-session only — incompatible with the SSH use case), the chosen approach is to support the **standard history keyboard shortcuts** and let users map the side buttons to them:

- Add `browser.back` / `browser.forward` keybindings:
  - macOS: `⌘+[` / `⌘+]`
  - Windows/Linux: `Alt+Left` / `Alt+Right`
- Wire them through both paths used by other browser shortcuts: the guest `before-input-event` (page focus) and a renderer-local keydown handler (host-chrome focus) → `webview.goBack()` / `goForward()`.

User step (one-time): in **Logi Options+**, set the back/forward buttons to **Keystroke Assignment** `⌘+[` / `⌘+]`. This also benefits keyboard users, who now get history navigation in the browser pane.

## How to reproduce
1. Open the built-in browser, navigate to a second page via a link.
2. Press the Logitech MX back side button → nothing happens (before the fix).

records.title: fix(web): guard secure-context-only crypto in browser client
records.body: ## Problem A user reported the web client (Orca in the browser) throwing **`crypto.randomUUID is not a function`** and failing to work reliably. The web client is frequently served over **plain HTTP on a LAN**, which is **not a secure context**. In that case the browser leaves `crypto.randomUUID()` and `crypto.subtle` **`undefined`** (only `crypto.getRandomValues` is available). Electron always runs in a secure context, so unguarded `crypto.*` calls pass locally and in CI but crash in the browser — which is why this slipped through (the default vitest env is `node`, where `crypto.randomUUID` exists globally). ## Reproduction Added `non-secure-context-crypto.repro.test.ts`, which recreates the exact non-secure-context global shape (`getRandomValues` present, `randomUUID`/`subtle` undefined) and drives the real call sites. Against the **pre-fix** code it fails with: ``` TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'digest') at hashOrcaHookScript src/renderer/src/lib/orca-hook-trust.ts:6 ``` With the fix, it passes. ## Fix Route the three unguarded renderer call sites through non-secure-context-safe code: | Site | Before | After | |------|--------|-------| | `worktree-creation-flow.ts` | `crypto.randomUUID()` | `createBrowserUuid()` | | `launch-agent-background-session.ts` | `globalThis.crypto.randomUUID()` | `createBrowserUuid()` | | `orca-hook-trust.ts` | `crypto.subtle.digest(...)` | guard `crypto.subtle`; fall back to a JS hash (`tweetnacl`, already bundled) | The hook-trust change keeps `crypto.subtle` as the primary path so existing stored trust hashes stay valid on Electron/HTTPS, and only falls back off a secure context. `createBrowserUuid()` / `mintStablePaneId()` already existed and were the intended pattern — these sites just weren't using them. ## Scope / what this does NOT cover The reproduced crashes are on **action paths** (creating a worktree, launching an agent, hook-trust during launch). The reporter also mentioned **"sessions are empty and one project is missing"** on load. I traced the passive session/repo hydration path (web RPC ids use a counter, not crypto; tab hydration already uses `createBrowserUuid`) and did **not** find a crypto cause there. That symptom may be a cascade from a thrown exception during launch, or a **separate bug**. Recommend asking the reporter to retest loading after this lands; if sessions are still empty, I'll open a separate investigation into the web hydration path. ## Testing - New repro test (`non-secure-context-crypto.repro.test.ts`) — 3 passing, demonstrably fails on pre-fix code - New `orca-hook-trust.test.ts` — covers both the secure path and the non-secure fallback - Existing `ensure-hooks-confirmed.test.ts` — 16 passing - `typecheck:web` and `oxlint` clean Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) 🐋 ---

records.title: Support browser panes on headless remote Orca servers
records.body:
## What & why

Closes #5321.

Headless `orca serve` couldn't create or render browser panes — every pane was backed by an Electron `<webview>` that only exists inside a renderer window, so a windowless host threw *"Browser tab creation requires a desktop renderer."* Remote-owned workspaces also silently fell back to a **local desktop** browser tab, creating confusing split ownership.

This makes a headless server host its own browser panes by adding a main-process **offscreen** browser backend, reusing the existing CDP screencast/input pipeline. The key realization: `orca serve` is the full app running with no window, and Electron is Chromium — so the main process can create an invisible `BrowserWindow` and stream it, with no extra browser to install.

## How it works

- **Backend seam** (`browser-backend.ts`): today's renderer/`<webview>` path is unchanged; a new `OffscreenBrowserBackend` creates a hidden `BrowserWindow` per page and registers its `WebContents` so automation, screencast, and input all resolve uniformly. Profile → Electron partition keeps cookies/logins persistent.
- **Routing** (`orca-runtime-browser.ts`): `browser.tabCreate` / `tabClose` go to the offscreen backend when there's no authoritative window; the old "not supported" throw is removed.
- **Honest capabilities** (`orca-runtime.ts`, `protocol-version.ts`): advertise `browser.screencast.v1` when either a renderer or the offscreen backend can serve pages, plus a new `browser.headless.v1` when headless-only — only when actually available.
- **No silent local fallback** (`store/slices/browser.ts`): a remote-owned workspace stays remote-owned; it no longer opens a tab on the user's laptop.
- **Linux display** (`ensure-virtual-display.ts`): Chromium on Linux needs a display server even for offscreen rendering. On a headless Linux serve with no `DISPLAY`, Orca starts **Xvfb** before app-ready and switches to software rendering; if it can't, browser panes are cleanly reported unsupported (no crash). The offscreen backend is gated on display availability so the capability stays truthful. `xvfb` (deb) / `xorg-x11-server-Xvfb` (rpm) added to the Linux package deps.

## Cross-platform behavior

| Surface | Behavior |
|---|---|
| macOS / Windows / Linux **desktop** | Unchanged |
| macOS / Windows as a remote `orca serve` | Browser panes now work headlessly; no extra setup |
| Linux as a remote `orca serve` | Works headlessly; Orca auto-starts Xvfb (or cleanly reports unsupported if missing) |
| Client (desktop **or** mobile) | Remote-workspace browser panes run on the remote machine, not locally. Mobile needs no app-store change — it already speaks the protocol. |

## Verification

- **Spike (headless Linux, Docker):** confirmed Electron `--headless` segfaults on a browser window and that a virtual display (Xvfb) is genuinely required.
- **End-to-end integration (headless Linux, Docker, no `DISPLAY` set):** the *real* shipping modules started Xvfb themselves, created an offscreen page, streamed non-blank frames, and cleaned up. ✅
- **Package names verified** against real Debian and Fedora images (Fedora has no `xvfb` package — it's `xorg-x11-server-Xvfb`; using the wrong name would make the RPM uninstallable).
- Unit tests added for backend routing, capability reporting, and the Xvfb logic; tests encoding the old behavior were updated. Typecheck (node/cli/web) + lint clean.

## Not in this PR (follow-ups)
- Idle-timeout teardown of offscreen windows beyond per-page close.
- A full UI-level run with a live paired client rendering the pane (backend + stream + provisioning are verified end-to-end; the client render path was code-traced as local-handle + screencast driven).

Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) 🐋

records.title: Support browser panes on headless remote Orca servers
records.body:
## Problem

Headless remote Orca servers (`orca serve`) cannot currently create or render browser panes.

Today browser panes are backed by Electron renderer/BrowserView state. When a remote runtime has no attached desktop renderer window, `browser.tabCreate` fails with:

> Browser tab creation requires a desktop renderer; headless orca serve does not support browser panes yet.

This is correct for the current architecture, but it means remote servers/cloud VMs are not fully first-class for workflows that need browser tabs.

## Current behavior

- Local desktop workspaces can use browser panes.
- SSH/local-client workflows can use browser panes through the local desktop renderer.
- Headless remote Orca servers can handle projects, files, git, terminals, tasks, and other runtime RPCs, but not browser panes.
- The client should not fall back to a local browser tab for a remote-owned workspace because that creates confusing split ownership.

## Desired behavior

Remote hosts should own browser panes for remote-owned workspaces.

For headless remote servers, Orca should provide a server-side browser backend so users can create, view, and interact with browser tabs from the remote host, without requiring a visible Electron renderer on that machine.

## Proposed direction

Implement a headless browser backend for remote runtimes:

1. Add a Playwright/Chromium-backed browser service inside `orca serve`.
2. Advertise an explicit capability such as `browser.headless.v1` when the server can launch/manage headless browser pages.
3. Keep using the existing runtime browser RPC shape where possible:
   - `browser.tabCreate`
   - `browser.screencast`
   - `browser.goto`
   - `browser.click`
   - `browser.type`
   - `browser.scroll`
   - tab close/list/current APIs
4. Route browser RPCs to either:
   - renderer-backed Electron backend, when an authoritative renderer window exists
   - headless Playwright backend, when running as headless `orca serve`
5. Stream browser frames over the existing/extended screencast event channel.
6. Forward UI input events from the client to the remote browser page.
7. Persist browser profiles/cookies/download state on the owning host.

## UX requirements

- Do not create local fallback browser tabs for remote-owned workspaces.
- If a host does not support browser panes, hide or disable browser actions with clear copy.
- Capability reporting must match actual support. A headless server should not advertise browser pane support unless it can actually create/render browser pages.
- Browser session ownership should be consistent with the workspace host model: the machine running the workspace owns the browser.

## Why this matters

This is important for making remote servers, VMs, and future Orca cloud environments first-class. A cloud/remote workspace should not require the user's local desktop renderer to provide browser functionality.

records.title: fix: replace per-5s full-buffer terminal checkpoints with an incremental log
records.body:
Addresses #5096 ("Terminal Cursor and Orca slows down heavily") — the daemon-side root cause. A renderer-side `SerializeAddon` call-site audit is a tracked follow-up.

## Problem

During an active agent session, every PTY chunk marks the session dirty, so the terminal-history checkpoint fires every 5 seconds for as long as output flows. Each tick:

1. Serialized the daemon emulator's **entire retained buffer** (up to 5,000 rows) synchronously on the daemon event loop — the same loop that forwards PTY output for **all** terminals — with up to 4 sessions serialized back-to-back per tick.
2. Shipped the ~0.3–0.5MB snapshot over the NDJSON socket (JSON encode/decode on both sides).
3. Stringified and rewrote the full `checkpoint.json` on Electron main, which also services keystroke IPC.

Serialize cost is proportional to buffer content, so it ramps over the first ~5k rows of a session and then stays maximal — matching the report that lag grows "after working long enough" and disappears when history is cleared (compacting an agent session emits clear-scrollback, emptying the buffer being serialized).

## Change

Periodic ticks no longer serialize anything. Instead:

- Daemon sessions record every output chunk, resize, and clear as **pending records** (2MB cap, adjacent output coalesced; on overflow, records are dropped and flagged — the next tick re-anchors with one full snapshot, which subsumes everything dropped).
- A new `takePendingOutput` RPC (protocol v13) drains them per tick; the history manager appends framed batches to a per-session `output.log`. Per-tick work is **O(new bytes since last tick)** instead of O(entire buffer).
- Full snapshots now happen only on: clean disconnect (unchanged — full 5k-row restore depth is preserved for normal quit/reboot), pending-buffer overflow, or the log reaching its 5MB cap (one serialize per ~5MB of output, which compacts the log into a fresh checkpoint generation).
- Cold restore replays the checkpoint base + log tail through a scratch headless emulator, producing the same `TerminalSnapshot` shape the renderer already consumes. Post-crash restores are now **byte-exact to ~5s before the crash** instead of up-to-5s-stale snapshot content.

## Benchmark metrics

All numbers from the env-gated harness in `src/main/daemon/headless-emulator-snapshot-cost.bench.test.ts` (`ORCA_TERMINAL_PERF_BENCH=1`), M-series macOS. Windows/older hardware scales these up.

**1. Why it lagged — full-snapshot cost vs buffer fill** (the old per-tick work):

| Buffer fill | Serialize (median) | Snapshot size | Main-process stringify |
|---|---|---|---|
| empty | 1.6ms | 0 B | 1.9ms |
| 1k rows | 26.8ms | 95 KB | 2.9ms |
| 5k rows (daemon cap) | 94.8ms | 483 KB | 10.5ms |
| 50k rows (renderer-scale, for reference) | 1,182ms | 4.9 MB | 127.9ms |

**2. The user-visible stall — worst chunk-to-chunk output delay on a simulated daemon loop** (5k-row buffer, chunks streaming every ~2ms, checkpoint landing mid-stream):

| Scenario | Worst output gap | Per-tick checkpoint cost |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline (no checkpoint) | 19.7ms (timer jitter) | — |
| Old design: full serialize per tick | **273.6ms** | 271.1ms |
| New design: incremental take per tick | **12.7ms** | **0.22ms** |

The stall lands directly on PTY output forwarding in the old design and is eliminated (indistinguishable from baseline jitter) in the new one — **~1,200× less work per tick**.

**3. Renderer regression gate** — new e2e spec `tests/e2e/terminal-history-size-typing-latency.spec.ts` measures keypress→echo latency at 0 / 10k / 50k rows of terminal history (fails if medians exceed 250ms). On this change: 13.2 / 15.3 / 40.6ms medians — flat within bounds. (Methodology note: this spec polls only the trailing buffer rows; polling via full-buffer `getTerminalContent` self-inflicts a ~1.2s serialize per poll at 50k rows and measured 492ms medians — itself a demonstration of the root cause.)

## Crash-safety design

- **Framed log** (`u8 kind + u32le length` records under a magic/version/generation header): a torn final append is detected and truncated at the last complete frame — never replayed half-applied.
- **Generation pairing**: each full checkpoint bumps a generation written to both `checkpoint.json` and the log header. A crash between checkpoint rename and log reset leaves mismatched generations, so the stale log is ignored rather than replayed on top of a checkpoint that already contains it.
- **Batch sequence numbers**: every appended batch carries a monotonic seq. A gap (e.g. main crashed between an RPC take and the disk append) means the byte stream has a hole — the whole log is rejected and restore falls back to the checkpoint (stale-but-consistent beats corrupt).
- **Atomic take+snapshot**: full snapshots go through `takePendingOutput({includeSnapshot: true})`, which drains and serializes in one synchronous daemon turn — a separate snapshot request would let bytes land in between and replay twice on restore.
- **Revive re-anchoring**: a cold-restored session is a fresh shell whose on-disk files belong to the pre-crash session; its first tick takes a full checkpoint instead of appending to the stale log (covered by a dedicated double-crash test).

## Compatibility

- Protocol bump 12→13; v12 daemons keep working through the existing legacy-adapter mechanism and stay on the old full-snapshot checkpoint path (`supportsIncrementalCheckpoints` gate, mirroring the v4 `supportsCheckpoints` pattern).
- Checkpoints written before this change (no `generation` field) restore exactly as before; logs are ignored for them.
- Downgrade-safe: older readers ignore `output.log` and the new JSON field entirely.
- Legacy `scrollback.bin` fallback unchanged.

## Tests

- 33 new tests: codec round-trip/torn-tail/seq-gap/orphan-frame, manager+reader end-to-end (no-base replay, base+tail, generation mismatch, pre-generation checkpoints, torn append, resize/clear replay, alt-screen crash skip, checkpoint log reset, log-cap compaction, stale-log cleanup on session reuse, warm-relaunch continuation), session drain semantics (ordering, coalescing, overflow recovery, atomic snapshot take, dispose), adapter re-anchor on revive.
- Updated adapter tests assert the new contract: periodic ticks append increments and never call full `checkpoint()`; concurrency cap preserved.
- Full daemon suite: 520 passing. Full `src/main` suite: 7,071 passing (3 pre-existing load-flaky tests in unrelated areas pass in isolation). Typecheck + lint clean.
- Both typing-latency e2e specs green.

## Follow-ups (out of scope)

- Renderer-side `SerializeAddon` call-site audit (a full serialize at the 50k-row default scrollback blocks the renderer ~1.2s wherever triggered).
- Windows + long-session soak per the verification plan.

Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) 🐋

records.title: [Feature]: Open a workspace's app URL in the browser from a button, without spawning a terminal
records.body:
### Problem or use case

Hi, and thanks for Orca! The per-workspace worktree flow has been great for us.

We run several Orca workspaces in parallel for a Laravel app, and each one serves the app at its own URL, set as `APP_URL` in that workspace's `.env`. We hop over to a workspace's running app in the browser many times a day, so we would love a one-click, per-workspace button that opens that URL.

There is no built-in action that just opens a URL, so we have to route it through other features, and every option we found has a small downside (below).

### Proposed solution

A first-class "open URL" action that does not spawn a terminal would be wonderful. Ideally both of:

1. A new Command action type (for example `open-url`) so a button on the Commands bar opens a URL directly, with a choice of system browser or Orca's embedded browser.
2. Env variable interpolation in the URL, for example `${env:APP_URL}`, so one shared, repo-scoped button resolves each workspace's own URL without a script.

The dream would be an `open-url` button whose URL can reference `${env:APP_URL}`, with no terminal and no script.

### Alternatives or additional context

We tried two approaches so far. Both work, and both have a small downside.

**Option A: a Command (the Commands bar).** We added a command to open the app URL, using `orca tab create --url <APP_URL>` (embedded) and the OS opener (system browser). Commands only support the `terminal-command` action, so clicking it spawns a terminal pane that then runs the command to open the browser. That leaves a stray terminal tab we would rather not have.

**Option B: "Open in applications" + a wrapper script.** A custom entry under Settings > "Open in applications" pointing at a script. Orca runs it detached (no terminal) and passes the worktree path, so the script reads `.env` and opens the URL:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# $1 = worktree path, passed by Orca's "Open in applications"
url=$(grep -E '^APP_URL=' "$1/.env" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2-)
exec orca tab create --worktree "path:$1" --url "$url"   # embedded browser
# or: exec open "$url"                                    # system browser
```

Downsides:

- It sits in the "Open in..." menu, which means "open the folder in an app" rather than "open a URL", so it is an extra click and a slightly odd fit.
- It needs a script we maintain, and ours uses macOS-only `open`. A built-in action could pick the right opener per platform (`open` / `xdg-open` / `start`) and work on remote and SSH workspaces, where a local script would not.

Either of these would make our day-to-day noticeably smoother. Thanks for considering it!

records.title: Fix markdown preview links routing to system browser instead of Orca
records.body:
## Summary

In the markdown preview, a plain (or Cmd/Ctrl) click on an http/https link called `window.api.shell.openUrl()` directly, which always routes to `shell.openExternal` (the OS default browser). It bypassed `openHttpLink`, so a plain click could **never** reach the Orca built-in browser, regressing the behavior from #987. The Cmd/Ctrl+Shift escape hatch was already correct.

Intended behavior, now restored:
- **plain / Cmd-click** routes to the Orca built-in browser (honoring the "open links in Orca" setting).
- **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift-click** routes to the system default browser.

## Root cause

`MarkdownPreview.tsx` had two http click paths. The Cmd/Ctrl+Shift branch correctly called `openHttpLink(url, { forceSystemBrowser: true })`, but the plain path called `window.api.shell.openUrl()` directly and never went through `openHttpLink`, the only place that decides Orca-vs-system routing. This dates back to the original preview feature and was never migrated when `openHttpLink` was introduced.

## Fix

- New `resolveMarkdownPreviewHttpOpenOptions(event, isMac, worktreeId)` helper centralizes the cross-platform modifier decision (Cmd on Mac, Ctrl on Linux/Windows per `AGENTS.md`):
  - plain / Cmd-click maps to `{ worktreeId }`, routing to the Orca browser, falling back to the system browser when the setting is off, no worktree is known, or a remote runtime is active.
  - Cmd/Ctrl+Shift-click maps to `{ forceSystemBrowser: true }`, routing to the system browser.
- Both http call sites in `MarkdownPreview.tsx` now route through this helper plus `openHttpLink`.

## SSH / remote-runtime

Handled inside `openHttpLink`: with an active remote runtime, http links route to the client system browser rather than an Orca tab. `file://` blocking behavior is unchanged.

## Verification

- New happy-dom interaction test renders the **real** `MarkdownPreview`, lets react-markdown produce a real anchor, and fires **real** `metaKey`/`shiftKey` click events:
  - plain Cmd-click invokes `createBrowserTab(...)` (Orca), with no system-browser call.
  - Cmd+Shift-click routes to the system browser, with no Orca tab.
  - Confirmed to fail against the pre-fix code (regression guard).
- Full Mac/Linux/Windows x plain/Cmd/Shift matrix coverage for the helper.
- Existing `http-link-routing` tests cover the `openHttpLink` destination mapping (including remote-runtime to system browser).
- `typecheck:web` and `oxlint` clean.

Closes #987

records.title: Apply remote ACK recovery snapshots on desktop clients
records.body:
## Summary

- stop marking the `ack-pending-overflow` recovery snapshot `truncated: true`; it is only truncated when serialization failed (matching the requested-snapshot and mobile recovery paths, where `truncated` means "unusable")
- trim retained ACK-pending chunks covered by the recovery snapshot's output seq before the post-recovery flush, so applied snapshots are not followed by duplicate bytes
- teach the desktop multiplexer to classify an unsolicited post-initial snapshot as `recovery`: it is applied through `onSnapshot` with a clear-screen/scrollback prefix, does not re-fire `onSubscribed`, and cannot steal a pending snapshot request

## Why

#4996 added the 256 KiB ACK-pending cap with a recovery snapshot so a stalled remote desktop client cannot grow unbounded memory. But the recovery snapshot was sent with `truncated: true`, and the desktop multiplexer discards truncated snapshots — so the snapshot meant to cover the dropped output was thrown away, leaving a permanent ≥256 KiB gap in a visible remote terminal. The server tests asserted frame ordering only, never client-side application, which is how this escaped.

Pre-stack behavior had no caps and therefore no data loss; this makes the cap loss-free again: dropped middle is covered by an applied snapshot, retained tail is seq-trimmed against it, and newer output resumes live.

## Validation

- New server test `trims recovery-covered ACK pending output instead of replaying it`: recovery snapshot is `truncated: false`, fully covered retained chunks are not replayed, fresh post-recovery output flows
- Updated `caps stalled ACK output…` test asserts the recovery SnapshotStart is not truncated
- New client test `applies mid-session recovery snapshots without re-subscribing`: recovery data is delivered via `onSnapshot` with the `\x1b[2J\x1b[3J\x1b[H` clear prefix and `onSubscribed` is not re-fired
- All three fail against the previous product code and pass with the fix
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/runtime/rpc/terminal-multiplex.test.ts src/renderer/src/runtime/runtime-terminal-stream.test.ts` passed: 25 tests
- Adjacent suites passed: terminal-subscribe-buffer, mobile-subscribe-integration, remote-runtime-pty-transport, runtime-rpc (117 tests, 2 skipped)
- `pnpm exec oxlint` on touched files passed; `pnpm run typecheck` passed; `git diff --check` passed

records.title: Deliver subscribe overflow recovery as resized snapshot
records.body:
## Summary

- send the binary `terminal.subscribe` pending-output-overflow recovery snapshot as `kind: 'resized'` instead of a second `kind: 'scrollback'` frame
- omit the output-byte `seq` from that wire frame (it is still used server-side for trimming covered pending chunks)
- skip the recovery snapshot entirely when the serialized snapshot has no output seq (renderer-source fallback), keeping the pre-existing bounded replay instead

## Why

The shipped mobile client — the consumer of this stream — unconditionally drops a second `scrollback` event for an initialized handle, but applies a `resized` event carrying `serialized` by re-initializing xterm with fresh scrollback. With the old `scrollback` kind, the recovery snapshot introduced in #5025 was discarded client-side while the server had already trimmed the pending chunks it covered — making the visible gap strictly larger than the pre-#5025 behavior (which replayed the retained tail). Omitting `seq` also keeps output-byte sequences out of the client's layout-seq staleness filter.

For renderer-source snapshots there is no output seq, so covered chunks cannot be trimmed exactly — and under backpressure the renderer view may lag the queued chunks, so "serialized later" does not prove coverage. That path now keeps the bounded replay rather than applying an unverifiable snapshot.

## Validation

- Updated recovery test asserts the recovery frame is `kind: 'resized'`, `reason: 'pending-output-overflow'`, with no `seq` on the wire; new test `keeps bounded replay when overflow recovery has no output seq` proves the seq-less path replays the retained tail with no recovery frame
- Both tests fail against the previous server behavior and pass with the fix
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/runtime/rpc/terminal-subscribe-buffer.test.ts src/main/runtime/mobile-subscribe-integration.test.ts` passed: 50 tests, 2 skipped
- `pnpm exec oxlint` on touched files passed
- `pnpm run typecheck` passed
