records.title: fix(daemon): checkpoint-based history persistence to reduce memory
records.body:
## Summary
- Replace per-chunk `appendFileSync` disk writes with periodic checkpoint-based persistence (serialize HeadlessEmulator state every 5 seconds)
- Eliminates unbounded disk I/O that macOS cached as "App Memory" (reported as 140 GB RAM usage by users running TUI-heavy workflows)
- Removes ~150 lines of CSI 3J detection, partial escape buffering, and byte counting logic

## Problem
The daemon history manager wrote every PTY data chunk to disk synchronously for crash recovery. TUIs (vim, lazygit, claude-code) emit CSI 3J on every redraw, resetting the 5 MB byte counter and making total writes unbounded. macOS caches these writes in the unified buffer cache, reporting them as application memory.

## Solution
The HeadlessEmulator already maintains a fully-parsed, deduplicated terminal state. Instead of streaming every byte to disk, we now:
1. Serialize emulator state every 5 seconds via a new `getSnapshot` RPC
2. Write checkpoints atomically (tmp+rename) to `checkpoint.json`
3. Write final checkpoints daemon-side in `TerminalHost.dispose()` for zero data loss on graceful shutdown
4. Fall back to `scrollback.bin` for backward compatibility during the upgrade transition

Key changes:
- `types.ts`: Add `GetSnapshotRequest`/`GetSnapshotResult`, bump `PROTOCOL_VERSION` 3→4
- `terminal-host.ts`: Add `getSnapshot()` method, `onFinalCheckpoint` callback in dispose
- `daemon-server.ts`: Add `getSnapshot` RPC routing
- `history-manager.ts`: Rewrite — `checkpoint()` replaces `appendData()`
- `history-reader.ts`: Read `checkpoint.json` first, fall back to `scrollback.bin`
- `daemon-pty-adapter.ts`: Remove per-chunk writes, add 5s checkpoint timer + `activeSessionIds`

## Test plan
- [ ] All 285 daemon tests pass (24 test files)
- [ ] Verify checkpoint.json is written every 5 seconds with correct snapshot data
- [ ] Verify graceful shutdown writes final checkpoint (zero data loss)
- [ ] Verify cold restore from checkpoint.json works correctly
- [ ] Verify cold restore falls back to scrollback.bin for pre-upgrade sessions
- [ ] Verify no disk I/O on individual PTY data events
- [ ] Verify protocol version bump forces stale daemon replacement
- [ ] Test with TUI-heavy workflows (vim, lazygit, build logs) to confirm memory stays bounded

records.title: [Feature]: Cmd/Ctrl+click on http links opens in OS default browser (plain click stays in built-in browser)
records.body:
### Problem or use case

When I click an `http(s)` link inside Orca (markdown preview, agent output, terminal, sidebar comment, etc.) I usually want to keep context inside the app — the built-in browser tab is perfect for that. But a non-trivial slice of the time I want the link in my OS default browser instead, because that's where my logged-in sessions, extensions, password manager, and tab history live (GitHub, internal SSO dashboards, Linear, etc.).

Today the modifier-aware behavior is **inconsistent across surfaces and requires an awkward three-key chord**:

- **Markdown preview** (`src/renderer/src/components/editor/MarkdownPreview.tsx:256-329`, modifier logic at lines 284-321) — plain click opens in the built-in browser; opening externally requires **Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + click**.
- **Terminal links** (`src/renderer/src/components/terminal-pane/terminal-link-handlers.ts:219-282`, hints at lines 31-46) — Cmd/Ctrl+click opens per the `openLinksInApp` setting, Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+click forces the system browser.
- **Sidebar comments** (`src/renderer/src/components/sidebar/CommentMarkdown.tsx:18-27`) — hardcoded `target="_blank"`, no modifier awareness at all.
- **Main-window + browser-guest `setWindowOpenHandler` / `will-navigate`** (`src/main/window/createMainWindow.ts:196-202, 252-272`, `src/main/browser/browser-manager.ts:409-441, 443-490`) — no modifier awareness, link destination is fixed by the surface.

Muscle memory from every other app (browsers, VS Code, Slack, macOS Finder) is **Cmd/Ctrl-click = "open somewhere else"** — no Shift required. The current Shift requirement is both non-discoverable and uncomfortable to hold with one hand on a laptop trackpad.

### Proposed solution

Make **Cmd/Ctrl+click** (no Shift) the universal "open in OS default browser" gesture across every link surface in Orca. Plain click keeps its existing behavior of opening in the built-in browser (or whatever the surface currently does for in-app navigation). Shift-variants, if kept, can be repurposed or left as aliases.

Concretely:

1. **Shared helper.** Introduce one shared `resolveLinkClickTarget(event): 'in-app' | 'external'` helper (renderer-side) that encapsulates the platform check the repo already uses (`navigator.userAgent.includes('Mac')` → `metaKey`, else `ctrlKey` — same pattern as `terminal-link-handlers.ts:27-46` and per AGENTS.md cross-platform section). Use it everywhere an `<a>` click is intercepted so behavior is identical across markdown, composer output, agent messages, comments, terminal URL links, and any future surface.
2. **Markdown preview.** In `MarkdownPreview.tsx:284-321`, change the external-browser branch from `modKey && event.shiftKey` to just `modKey`. Keep `Shift` as an optional alias for now, or drop it.
3. **Terminal link addon.** In `terminal-link-handlers.ts:219-282`, decouple "modifier = external" from the `openLinksInApp` setting: Cmd/Ctrl+click → `window.api.shell.openUrl()` regardless of the setting; plain click → honor `openLinksInApp`. Update the hint strings at lines 31-46 to `"⌘+click to open in system browser"` / `"Ctrl+click to open in system browser"`.
4. **Sidebar comments.** Replace the hardcoded `target="_blank"` in `CommentMarkdown.tsx:18-27` with a click handler that uses the shared helper — plain click → built-in browser tab, Cmd/Ctrl+click → `shell.openExternal`.
5. **Electron-level handlers.** In `createMainWindow.ts:196-202, 252-272` and `browser-manager.ts:409-441`, forward the click modifier state (available via `details.disposition === 'foreground-tab'` for Cmd-click on web content, or via a custom IPC channel for renderer-originated clicks) so the main process routes the request the same way.
6. **Labels / tooltips.** Update any link tooltip copy to mention the new gesture, following the repo's `⌘` / `Ctrl+` convention (`isMacPlatform()` from `terminal-link-handlers.ts:27-29`).

### Alternatives or additional context

- **Related issue:** #854 ("Open in host browser") is scoped to the Stably hosted-workspace context (in-workspace browser vs. host browser) — different product surface. This request is the Orca-desktop case: which surface inside the same app opens the link.
- **Related issue:** #378 (closed) added the built-in browser itself; this is a natural usability follow-up now that both destinations coexist.
- **Workaround today:** remembering Cmd/Ctrl+**Shift**+click in markdown / agent output, and toggling the global `openLinksInApp` setting for the terminal — neither of which survives context switches between surfaces.

Relevant code:
- `src/renderer/src/components/editor/MarkdownPreview.tsx:256-329` — markdown preview link handler (modifier logic at 284-321)
- `src/renderer/src/components/terminal-pane/terminal-link-handlers.ts:27-46, 219-282` — terminal link modifier logic + hint strings
- `src/renderer/src/components/sidebar/CommentMarkdown.tsx:18-27` — comment link rendering (no modifier awareness)
- `src/main/window/createMainWindow.ts:196-202, 252-272` — main-window `setWindowOpenHandler` + `will-navigate`
- `src/main/browser/browser-manager.ts:409-441, 443-490` — browser guest `setWindowOpenHandler` + navigation guard
- `src/main/ipc/shell.ts:20-33` — `shell:openUrl` IPC (external browser entry point)
- AGENTS.md "Cross-Platform Support" — metaKey/ctrlKey platform convention

records.title: fix(browser): stop webview reload when moving tab between groups
records.body:
## Summary

Moving a browser tab between tab groups (or splitting/dragging a group containing a browser) was reloading the `<webview>` — destroying auth state, scroll position, form input, and mid-request network calls. Electron `<webview>` tears down its guest process whenever the host DOM element is reparented, so the old tree of "BrowserPane lives inside TabGroupPanel" could not survive a group-level remount.

## Approach

Adopt VS Code's `OverlayWebview` pattern, adapted for a React tree:

- A single worktree-level `BrowserPaneOverlayLayer` renders one `<BrowserPane>` per browser tab, keyed on `browserTab.id` only. The React tree never reparents it.
- Each `TabGroupPanel` body tags itself with a per-group CSS `anchor-name` (`--orca-browser-slot-<groupId>`).
- Each overlay slot pins itself to the owning group's anchor via `position-anchor` / `anchor()` / `anchor-size()`. Moving a tab between groups just changes which anchor-name the overlay targets — the browser does all layout tracking with zero JS measurement state.
- Tabs that are transiently orphaned (present in `browserTabs` but not in any group's unified-tab list, e.g. mid-move) render as `display: none` at 0×0 so the DOM parent stays stable and the webview guest survives until reassigned or explicitly destroyed.

## Architectural tradeoffs

- **Complexity**: +1 component layer and +1 small CSS-slot helper module (~150 LoC total).
- **Platform dependency**: CSS anchor positioning requires Chromium 125+. We ship Electron 41 (Chromium 134+), so this is safe today.
- **Focus sync**: The old tree relied on pointer/focus events bubbling through `TabGroupPanel`'s `onPointerDown={focusGroup}`. The overlay is a sibling of `TabGroupSplitLayout`, not a descendant, so we re-implement focus sync explicitly via `onPointerDown` / `onFocusCapture` on each overlay slot. Without this, clicking browser chrome in a split view would leave `activeGroupIdByWorktree` stale.
- **Perf**: Each overlay slot is `memo`'d so unrelated worktree mutations (terminal keystrokes, editor updates) don't cascade into `BrowserPane` re-renders. `BrowserPaneOverlayLayer` and `WorktreeSplitSurface` are also memoized.

## Test plan

Manually verified by @brennanb2025 — tested moving browser tabs in all the ways users do it:

- [x] Split — split a group containing a browser tab
- [x] Split-then-split — splitting again after already having a split
- [x] Move between groups — dragging a browser tab from one group to another
- [x] Move by dropping into a split — dragging a browser tab onto a drop zone in a different split
- [x] Move between worktrees
- [x] Multiple browser tabs open in each worktree

In all cases: webview does not reload, scroll position / form input / auth state survives the move.

### Suggested additional smoke tests before merge

- [x] **Page state survival** — sign into a site, scroll partway, type into a form, then move between groups. Verify nothing resets.
- [x] **Drop-zone visibility** — drag a tab over a group whose active tab is a browser. Confirm the drop indicator is visible (Electron webview occlusion is a known pre-existing footgun; just verifying no regression from the old architecture).
- [x] **Split-group focus after clicking browser chrome** — click inside a browser pane's URL bar in one of two split groups; global shortcuts (new terminal, new markdown) should target the group you clicked into.
- [x] **Worktree switch round-trip** — switch away from a worktree showing a browser tab and back; webview should not reload.

records.title: fix(browser): make address bar Enter match typed intent, not Google Search
records.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #893. The address bar was dispatching Enter to **Google Search** for URL-like inputs (e.g. `www.example.com`), which is the opposite of how Chrome/Firefox omniboxes behave. This rewires the dropdown so the top row always mirrors what `normalizeBrowserNavigationUrl` will actually do on submit.

## Repro on #893

1. Clear history (or type a query that doesn't match any history entry).
2. Type `www.example.com` in the address bar.
3. Press Enter.
4. **Before:** navigates to `https://www.google.com/search?q=www.example.com`.
5. **After:** navigates to `https://www.example.com`.

## Root cause

#893 built the suggestion list like this:

```ts
if (looksLikeSearchQuery(trimmed)) {
  return [searchSuggestion, ...historySuggestions]
}
return [...historySuggestions.slice(0, MAX - 1), searchSuggestion]
```

For URL-like input, a synthetic "[input] — Google Search" row was appended **as a fallback** at the end of the list. If history had no matches, that fallback became `suggestions[0]`, and the existing auto-select-first effect (`setSelectedValue(suggestions[0]?.url ?? '')`) highlighted it. `handleKeyDown`'s Enter branch then resolved to the highlighted row and called `onNavigate(googleSearchUrl)` — bypassing `submitAddressBar` / `normalizeBrowserNavigationUrl` entirely.

Two independent bugs combined:

1. **Semantic mismatch.** `looksLikeSearchQuery` already classifies `www.example.com` as a URL, but the dropdown still offered a search row. Adding "just in case you meant to search" is fine; *defaulting to it on Enter* is not.
2. **Divergent commit paths.** Typing Enter with nothing highlighted went through `submitAddressBar` → `normalizeBrowserNavigationUrl` (correct). Typing Enter with a highlighted row went through `handleSelect(match.url)` (direct navigate). Those two paths can disagree, and here they did.

## The fix

Make the top row always be **the canonical commit action** — the exact URL that `submitAddressBar` would navigate to. That's what Chrome and Firefox do: the first row is always "what Enter does right now."

- URL-like input → top row is `{ title: input, url: normalizeBrowserNavigationUrl(input) }` with a globe icon and no subtitle.
- Query-like input → top row is `{ title: input, subtitle: "Google Search" }` with a search icon.
- If a history row already targets the same URL, suppress the synthetic top row (the history row has a real page title, so it's strictly better).

Now whether the user presses Enter cold or after arrow-keying, both paths land on the same URL, and that URL matches what `normalizeBrowserNavigationUrl` resolves — the single source of truth.

## Notes for future address-bar work

- **Never have two code paths decide what Enter does.** If the dropdown's first row and the form's submit handler can disagree, they eventually will. Keep them routed through one normalizer.
- **Fallbacks aren't free.** A synthetic "search fallback" row looks harmless until auto-select-first makes it the default. Fallback rows belong last *and* must not be auto-highlighted.
- `looksLikeSearchQuery` is already the arbiter of search-vs-URL; lean on it instead of building parallel logic in the suggestion builder.

## Test plan

- [x] Type `www.example.com` → top row is "www.example.com" (globe icon), Enter navigates to `https://www.example.com`.
- [x] Type `example.com/path` → navigates to `https://example.com/path`.
- [x] Type `react hooks` → top row is "react hooks — Google Search" (search icon), Enter hits Google.
- [x] Type `localhost:3000` → navigates to `http://localhost:3000`.
- [x] Type a substring of a visited URL → history row wins (no duplicate synthetic row).
- [x] Change default search engine in settings → subtitle updates ("DuckDuckGo Search", "Bing Search").
- [x] Empty address bar on focus → shows history only, no synthetic row.

records.title: fix(browser): improve Cloudflare Turnstile compatibility
records.body:
## Summary
- Fix blob: URL blocking in navigation guard that prevented Turnstile from loading challenge resources in iframes
- Fix anti-detection script injection timing — switch from broken `executeJavaScript` on `did-start-navigation` (runs on old page) to CDP `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` (persists across navigations, runs before page JS)
- Expand anti-detection signals: `chrome.csi()`, `chrome.loadTimes()`, `Notification.permission`, `navigator.languages`
- Mask CDP proxy identifiers (`Orca/CdpWsProxy` → `Chrome/Headless`)
- Strip Electron/app tokens from default UA even without imported sessions
- Widen passive permission checks so bot detectors see a normal browser fingerprint
- Extract UA/Client-Hints helpers to `browser-session-ua.ts`

## Context
Cloudflare Turnstile challenges fail with error 600010 ("bot behavior detected") in Orca's embedded browser (issue #107). This was caused by multiple detection vectors: blocked blob: URLs, missing anti-detection overrides due to injection timing, leaked Electron identifiers, and suspicious permission fingerprints.

Note: Turnstile uses deep runtime fingerprinting that no public Electron app has reliably bypassed. These fixes address the most impactful detection vectors but may not fully resolve all Turnstile challenges — the error may also be influenced by site-side Turnstile configuration (e.g., PropelAuth's security level).

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify User-Agent does not contain "Electron" or app name

records.title: feat: computer use via agent-browser CDP bridge
records.body:
closes #728 

## Problem
- Orca needed first-class browser automation through the CLI so agents could drive the embedded browser panes through the running app instead of an external browser.
- The initial browser flow still depended too much on ambient active-tab state, which made concurrent CLI workflows brittle:
  - commands in the same worktree could act on whichever browser tab happened to be active
  - hidden or inactive browser guests could time out during screenshots
  - concurrent screenshot and session-lifecycle operations could interleave and restore the wrong UI state or destroy newly recreated sessions

## Solution
- Added full browser automation support via the `agent-browser` daemon and a CDP WebSocket proxy for Orca webview guests.
- Added broad browser CLI coverage, including navigation, DOM interaction, tab management, cookies, viewport control, screenshots, eval, PDF export, uploads, and input events.
- Added explicit stable page targeting for multi-process safety:
  - `tab list --json` now returns a stable `browserPageId`
  - browser commands accept `--page <browserPageId>`
  - bare commands keep the current worktree-scoped active-tab fallback for backward compatibility
  - `skills/orca-cli/SKILL.md` now tells agents to prefer `tab list --json` -> `browserPageId` -> `--page`
- Hardened browser concurrency and lifecycle behavior:
  - queue commands per browser page/session
  - route `tab switch` through the queue
  - serialize screenshot/full-page screenshot prep across sessions
  - wait for pending session destruction before recreating a session after close or process swap
- Made screenshot capture more reliable:
  - map guest page ids to owning browser workspace ids before temporarily activating the browser pane
  - restore the previous worktree/tab state after capture
  - call `webContents.invalidate()` before `Page.captureScreenshot`
  - fall back to `capturePage()` if CDP screenshot still stalls for a guest
- Added unit and integration coverage for bridge routing, runtime/RPC targeting, screenshot fallback, process swaps, and concurrency cases.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm vitest run src/main/browser/agent-browser-bridge.test.ts src/main/runtime/orca-runtime.test.ts src/cli/index.test.ts src/main/browser/cdp-bridge-integration.test.ts`
- [x] `pnpm vitest run src/main/browser/cdp-screenshot.test.ts src/main/browser/cdp-ws-proxy.test.ts`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck:cli`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck:node`
- [x] Live verify explicit page targeting against a dev Orca process
  - `tab list --json` exposes stable `browserPageId`
  - `snapshot --page <id>` targets the requested tab without changing the active tab
  - `goto --page <id>` updates a background tab
  - `tab switch --page <id>` changes the active tab for the current worktree
  - `tab close --page <id>` closes only the targeted page
- [x] Live verify screenshot behavior against a dev Orca process
  - reproduce hidden-tab screenshot timeout
  - confirm the browser workspace activation fix resolves the hidden-tab case
  - confirm a previously failing `screenshot --page <id>` succeeds after the repaint/fallback fix

records.title: Add "Open in host browser" option for links (or provide Orca CLI)
records.body:
## Problem

When working inside an Orca workspace, clicking a link opens it in an in-workspace browser that doesn't share sessions with my host machine. This means I'm logged out of everything — GitHub, internal dashboards, SSO-gated docs, Slack web, etc. — and have to re-auth inside the workspace or copy-paste URLs manually to my host browser.

## Expected behavior

Either (or both) of:

1. **"Open in host browser"** option on links / URL previews — pops the URL out to the host machine's default browser so it uses existing logged-in sessions. Similar to how VS Code Remote forwards `Cmd+Click` URLs to the local browser.

2. **Orca CLI on the host** — a CLI I run on my laptop that connects into a workspace, so I can keep browsing/auth in my host browser and drive the workspace from the outside (e.g. ask "how do I do X in this workspace" without leaving my logged-in host environment).

## Use case

Most of my day involves checking GitHub PRs, internal dashboards, and SSO-gated tools while coding. Re-logging in to every service inside the workspace (and re-doing it each time the workspace is rebuilt) is painful. #1 would unblock the common case; #2 would be the ideal long-term setup.

When a file is modified by Claude Code (or any other process) running inside Orca's own integrated terminal, Orca should detect the change and show the updated content when the file is selected in the file browser. ## Use case

When using Claude Code inside Orca to edit config/JSON files, the edits are invisible in the Orca editor. This breaks the core workflow of using AI coding agents within the IDE — you can't verify changes without switching to an external editor.

records.title: fix: prevent window re-maximize when opening browser tab
records.body:
## Summary
- **Root cause**: Electron 41 on macOS re-emits `ready-to-show` on the same BrowserWindow after webview guest creation. The non-idempotent handler re-ran `maximize()` from the persisted `savedMaximized` flag, snapping the window back to full-screen after the user already resized it.
- **Fix**: One-shot guard (`handledInitialReadyToShow`) around the `ready-to-show` handler so duplicate emissions are ignored.
- **Bonus**: Persist window bounds and maximized state so the app restores to the user's last position/size on relaunch, instead of always maximizing.

## Changes
- `createMainWindow.ts` — one-shot `ready-to-show` guard, bounds/maximize persistence via resize/move/maximize/unmaximize events, default bounds from primary display work area
- `createMainWindow.test.ts` — regression test for duplicate `ready-to-show`, titleBarStyle assertion fix, removed 3 experiment-only tests
- `configure-process.ts` — added `ORCA_DEV_USER_DATA_PATH` override for repro isolation, removed GPU experiment flag guard
- `configure-process.test.ts` — tests for the above, removed GPU experiment test
- `types.ts` — added `windowBounds` and `windowMaximized` to `PersistedUIState`
- `package.json` — added `repro:browser-tab-maximize` script
- `repro-browser-tab-maximize.mjs` — new end-to-end smoke test with `--expect no-maximize` support

Experiment scaffolding removed: `ORCA_EXPERIMENT_DISABLE_MAIN_PROCESS_GPU_FEATURES`, `ORCA_EXPERIMENT_DEFER_GUEST_POLICY_ATTACH_UNTIL_REGISTER`, `ORCA_EXPERIMENT_DISABLE_MAIN_WINDOW_SANDBOX`, `ORCA_EXPERIMENT_SKIP_GUEST_WEB_PREFERENCES_HARDENING`, attach-time resize guard.

Closes #591

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm vitest run` — 31 tests pass (3 test files)

records.title: feat: add Windows support for browser cookie import
records.body:
## Summary

- Adds Windows support for one-click cookie import from Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Arc
- Replaces `sqlite3` CLI dependency with `better-sqlite3` (Node.js native module) on all platforms
- On macOS, the existing import flow is preserved — only the SQLite I/O layer changed

### Windows-specific additions
- Cookie paths via `%LOCALAPPDATA%` with Chrome 96+ `Network/Cookies` fallback
- DPAPI encryption key retrieval from `Local State` via PowerShell
- AES-256-GCM cookie decryption (vs macOS AES-128-CBC)
- User-Agent detection via Windows registry `BLBeacon` keys
- Platform-specific encryption version tag validation (`v10`/`v11` macOS, `v10`/`v20` Windows)

### Cross-platform improvements
- `better-sqlite3` eliminates shell-escaping issues, hex-encoding round-trips, and the implicit `sqlite3` CLI dependency
- WAL/SHM journal files are now properly copied alongside cookie databases and cleaned up
- DB handles are explicitly closed in all error paths (prevents file locks on Windows)
- Chromium 127+ HMAC prefix stripping applied on both platforms
- `integritySkipped` cookies now included in `skippedCookies` summary count
- Corrupt DB errors suggest closing the source browser

records.title: Refactor browser manager internals and fix grab shortcuts
records.body:
## Problem
`src/main/browser/browser-manager.ts` had grown into a large mixed-responsibility file that combined guest lifecycle ownership, grab-session state management, screenshot capture, payload sanitization, and guest shortcut wiring. That made the browser security boundary harder to audit and left two grab-mode bugs in place: bare `c`/`s` could be swallowed while typing in editable browser chrome, and hover `S` did not work when the focused webview consumed the key before the renderer saw it.

## Solution
Keep `BrowserManager` as the privileged facade, but extract its internal subsystems into dedicated modules for payload sanitization, screenshot capture, guest UI wiring, and grab-session orchestration. Add regression coverage around load-failure replay, listener cleanup, timeout and late-settlement races, screenshot behavior, and same-tab guest replacement. Fix grab shortcuts by guarding editable targets in the renderer and forwarding bare `c`/`s` from the focused guest during an active grab op so hover copy/screenshot actions work consistently without breaking typing in the address bar.

records.title: Add browser context grab feature
records.body:
## Summary
- Adds a grab mode to the in-app browser that lets users hover over or click on any page element to capture its DOM structure, computed styles, accessibility metadata, and a cropped screenshot
- Captured context can be copied to clipboard via a right-click-style dropdown menu or keyboard shortcuts (C for contents, S for screenshot)
- Dual-layer security: guest-side pre-clamp + main-side re-validation with attribute allowlist, secret pattern redaction, and URL sanitization

## Implementation
- **Shared types** (`browser-grab-types.ts`): payload shape, budget constants, attribute allowlist, secret patterns
- **Guest overlay** (`grab-guest-script.ts`): self-contained JS strings injected via `executeJavaScript` — shadow DOM overlay with closed mode, full-viewport click catcher, hover tracking, element extraction
- **Main process** (`browser-manager.ts`): grab lifecycle (arm/await/cancel/teardown), `clampGrabPayload` re-validation, screenshot capture with empirical DPI scale derivation, `extractHoverPayload` for keyboard shortcut support
- **IPC layer** (`browser.ts`): 5 grab handlers with sender authorization + guest authorization checks
- **Renderer hook** (`useGrabMode.ts`): state machine (idle → armed → awaiting → confirming → idle/armed)
- **UI** (`BrowserPane.tsx`): toolbar button, instruction bar with shortcut hints, context menu dropdown at selection location, keyboard shortcuts (C/S) that work both while hovering and after clicking
- **Clipboard** (`attach-main-window-services.ts` + preload): `writeClipboardImage` via `nativeImage.createFromDataURL`

## Test plan

- [ ] "Copy Contents" — verify clipboard contains formatted element context
- [ ] "Copy Screenshot" — verify clipboard contains cropped PNG of the element
- [ ] Press C while hovering (without clicking) — verify content copied directly
- [ ] Press S while hovering — verify screenshot copied directly
- [ ] Press Esc to cancel grab mode

records.title: Add in-app browser tabs
records.body:
## Problem
Orca did not have a worktree-scoped in-app browser, so local previews and web flows always had to leave the IDE. The browser UX also needed to fit Orca's mixed terminal/editor tab model without weakening the Electron security boundary.

Closes #378

## Solution
Add browser tabs as a first-class worktree surface backed by isolated Electron webviews, plus the main-process plumbing to manage guest policies, browser IPC, and browser-specific context menus/devtools. Tighten the browser URL policy, restore/session behavior, mixed tab-state fallbacks, and sidebar activity handling, then add regression coverage for the browser lifecycle, session hydration, and worktree activity states.
